docs.title: lumnik — defrost the enterprise
docs.text:
Documentation

lumnik reads the data in your ERP, LIMS and exports — read-only. It fuses the data, shows it to the right team, and answers questions in plain language (Pro). An answer shows its sources, or declines.

Read-only first

Your source system is never written to. Ingest first, risk nothing.

Fuse, conflicts kept

Conflicts are preserved in a _conflicts ledger, never silently resolved away.

Ask with guards

Answers cite their sources — or decline. The guards refuse to invent.

Not a migration, not BI

The ERP stays. lumnik reads it, and puts its data to work beside it.

Deploy lumnik See the WOW Follow the guided path

docs.title: Admin tasks — lm and the API behind it
docs.text:
Day-to-day administration of a running hub: webhooks, deliveries, runs, secrets, migrations, modules, hooks, tenants. Every task below starts from an lm command or a TUI screen (lm ui); raw HTTP appears only where no lm command exists.

No admin web console ships with lumnik.

docs.title: Who can call what
docs.text:
Roles are matched literally, with no hierarchy: lm_superadmin alone does not open an lm_admin door, and the reverse.

Task Gesture Roles needed Wire webhooks lm integration · :integrations lm_integrator + lm_admin, no scope:* role (or lm_admin alone over /api/tenants/{tid}/integrations) Read and replay deliveries lm outputs · :outputs lm_integrator + lm_admin (or lm_superadmin), no scope:* role Runs and dead letters lm run, lm dlq · :runs, :dlq lm_integrator Read secrets (metadata) lm secret list, describe lm_integrator Create, rotate, delete secrets lm secret set, rm lm_integrator + lm_admin Migrations, modules, hooks list, event catalog lm migration, lm module, lm hook list, GET /api/platform/events lm_integrator Declared workflows lm workflow lm_integrator Live event stream the TUI, or GET /api/platform/events/stream lm_integrator, no scope:* role Toggle a hook for a tenant, read one hook POST /api/platform/hooks/{id}/toggle, lm hook get lm_integrator + lm_admin Tenants /api/tenants lm_superadmin Orgs, users, tenant roles /api/tenants/{tid}/… lm_admin, own tenant only

A scope-bound integrator sees only the runs and dead letters of connectors whose scopes it holds (Scopes).

No lm command prints your roles. Ask the hub (needs lm_user):

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/bff/v1/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '{tenant: .tenant.id, roles}'
{
  "tenant": 1,
  "roles": [
    "lm_integrator",
    "lm_admin",
    "lm_user"
  ]
}

tenant is the {tid} the /api/tenants/{tid}/… paths want. Getting a token for curl: Test the API.

docs.title: Send events out to another system
docs.text: Register, test and remove a webhook target with lm integration: Outputs — wire a webhook. In lm ui, :integrations: n registers, T tests, Del removes, d shows recent deliveries.

docs.title: Settings lm does not expose
docs.text:
lm integration add always registers an enabled target in HMAC mode. For another mode, or to change a registration, use the HTTP door /api/platform/integrations:

Field Values Default name unique within the tenant required targetUrl the receiver's URL required eventTypes exact types or .* prefixes required authMode HMAC (X-Lumnik-Signature: sha256=…), BEARER (Authorization: Bearer <secret>), NONE HMAC secret the HMAC key or the bearer token; never returned (hasSecret: true) none platform generic, make, zapier, n8n — a label only (lm integration add --platform) generic enabled true / false true

Rotate a target's secret (a PUT applies only the fields present; a blank secret is ignored):

$ curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/platform/integrations/1001 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"secret":"the-new-shared-secret"}' | jq
{
  "id": 1001,
  "name": "ops-hook",
  "targetUrl": "http://localhost:18955/hook",
  "platform": "generic",
  "authMode": "HMAC",
  "eventTypes": [
    "connector.run.*"
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "hasSecret": true
}

Change the receiver's copy in the same window: the next delivery is signed with the new secret.

docs.title: Watch deliveries and replay a failure
docs.text:
$ lm outputs list
ID    INTEGRATION  EVENT                    STATUS       WHEN              ERROR
1006  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
1005  ops-hook     connector.run.started    no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
1001  (deleted)    connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:44  endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped
1000  (deleted)    connector.run.started    no response  2026-10-19 01:44  endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped
1003  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:45
1002  ops-hook     connector.run.started    ok           2026-10-19 01:45
1004  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:44

Failures come first. A failed delivery is retried automatically, 3 attempts in all, about 30 s apart. After the third, replay it once the receiver is back:

$ lm outputs replay 1006
replayed: delivery 1006 — a new attempt is on record

$ lm outputs list
ID    INTEGRATION  EVENT                    STATUS       WHEN              ERROR
1006  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
…
1007  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:46

The replay is a new row (1007); the original row stays as it was, still listed as failed. In lm ui, :outputs shows the same list; ^R replays the selected delivery.

ERROR column Meaning Gesture connection failed (ConnectException) the receiver did not answer bring it back, then lm outputs replay ID endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped the target was removed, disabled, or no longer subscribes to that event re-enable or re-subscribe, then replay; a removed target accepts no replay (404)

docs.title: Find the event types you can subscribe to
docs.text:
No lm command lists the catalog; the running hub serves it:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/platform/events -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq -r '.[].type'
org.created
org.updated
org.moved
org.archived
connector.run.started
connector.run.completed
connector.run.partial
connector.run.cancelled
connector.run.failed
platform.secret.created
platform.secret.updated
platform.secret.deleted
platform.secret.read
data.row.changed
annotation.decision.acked

Each entry also carries its module, a description and the payload fields. decision.* types are not in this list: each kind:Process and kind:Workflow names its own, and a decision.* subscription matches them when they fire. What each type means: the event registry.

docs.title: Watch ingestion: runs, dead letters, live events
docs.text:
Runs and dead letters, step by step: Diagnosing a failed run.

In lm ui, :runs, :dlq, :sources and :endpoints update by themselves while runs happen. They follow the live event stream, which your own tooling can read too:

Door GET /api/platform/events/stream?topic=connector.run.* (Accept: text/event-stream) topic repeatable; * is a wildcard over the event type; none = every event Each element {"topic": "<type>", "payload": "<JSON as a string>", "capturedAt": "<ISO-8601>"} Order an event shows once the transactions older than it have ended, so a late commit is never missed Scope-bound caller refused (scope not granted); in lm ui the views then refresh only when opened

docs.title: Keep a connector credential: the secret store
docs.text:
Connector manifests name a secret (*_env fields); lm secret stores its value, encrypted. No command returns a value.

$ lm secret set ERP_DB_PASSWORD --description "ERP read account"
Value for ERP_DB_PASSWORD:
Created secret "ERP_DB_PASSWORD"

$ lm secret list
NAME                           ROTATED_AT                     DESCRIPTION
ERP_DB_PASSWORD                -                              ERP read account

$ lm secret rm ERP_DB_PASSWORD
Type 'delete' to confirm removal of "ERP_DB_PASSWORD": delete
Deleted secret "ERP_DB_PASSWORD"
  • The value is typed at the prompt and not shown. From a script: lm secret set NAME - reads stdin.
  • set on an existing name rotates the value (Updated secret "…", ROTATED_AT filled). Without --description, the description stays; --description "" clears it.
  • lm secret describe NAME shows metadata only; lm secret rm --force skips the prompt.
  • Which connectors read the store, and which read the hub's environment instead: REST, CSV, JDBC.

docs.title: Trace a citation back to its source row
docs.text:
lm data row <HASH>

Takes the row_hash of a chat citation and prints the raw source row (all values as text). It answers 404 when the hash resolves to nothing in your tenant. A scope-bound caller reads the row only if every connector writing its table carries one of its scopes.

docs.title: Check migration drift
docs.text:
$ lm migration status
SCHEMA    VERSION  PENDING  LAST APPLIED
core      75       0        2026-10-19 01:36
identity  18       0        2026-10-19 01:36
rag       6        0        2026-10-19 01:36

Migrations apply when the hub starts; there is nothing to run by hand. PENDING 0 on every schema means the database matches this hub build. After an upgrade: Upgrade.

docs.title: Turn a hook on or off, and read declared workflows
docs.text: Gesture What it does lm hook list · lm hook get NAME the hooks this hub loaded lm workflow list · lm workflow get NAME the tenant's declared kind:Workflow manifests (Workflows) POST /api/platform/hooks/{hookId}/toggle?tenantId=… turns one hook on or off for one tenant; other hub threads see it within 60 s

docs.title: Manage tenants, orgs and users
docs.text:
No lm command manages identity; use the HTTP doors. Deletes archive, never erase. The gestures in context (onboarding, offboarding): Identity administration.

The doors, under /api/tenants and /api/tenants/{tid}/…: tenants (lm_superadmin), orgs, users and tenant roles (lm_admin, your own tenant). Their full contract is in your hub's /q/openapi (Test the API).

Org changes emit org.created, org.updated, org.moved, org.archived. lumnik stores no passwords: users sign in through Keycloak or your IdP. On Pro, a user's hub record is created at first login.

docs.title: Act on behalf of a tenant (impersonation)
docs.text:
• Impersonation is a JWT claim minted by your IdP: acting_as_tenant: <tid>, on a token that carries lm_superadmin. There is no hub endpoint that mints it.
  • It switches the tenant, never the roles: the roles in the token are the ones checked.
  • A token carrying the claim without lm_superadmin is refused: 403 {"error": "lm_superadmin required to impersonate a tenant"}.

docs.title: Harden the deployment
docs.text: Concern What the hub does What you do Secrets encrypted at rest, never returned by any door protect the .env that holds the keys; key rotation is not supported (RLS & credentials) Impersonation honoured only for lm_superadmin grant lm_superadmin to as few accounts as possible; an impersonated write is audited in the target tenant under the superadmin's user id, with nothing marking it as impersonation; the impersonation itself shows only in log lines Dev bypass grants every role to every caller never set lumnik.security.dev-bypass=true outside development Platform doors /api/platform/* requires lm_integrator restrict /api/platform/* and /q/* at your proxy if the hub faces the internet

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on /api/platform/* the token expired or was not sent lm login again API error 403: missing role lm_integrator the token lacks lm_integrator read your roles (above), then have it granted API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server — your account may lack the required role (raw HTTP: 403, empty body) a role the door needs is missing — often lm_admin read your roles, then have it granted access refused (403): scope not granted on lm integration, lm outputs (raw HTTP on the event stream: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}) your account holds a scope:* role; these doors are tenant-wide use an account with no scope:* role 403 on /api/tenants/{tid}/… while you hold lm_admin {tid} is not your token's tenant use tenant from /api/bff/v1/me 400 {"error": "Unknown event type: …"} on lm integration test --event … the type is not in the catalog — decision.* never is test with a catalog type; verify decision.* with a real decision API error 400: HMAC mode needs a secret … on lm integration add no --secret-stdin pass the secret on stdin — see Send events out A failed delivery is no longer retried it used its 3 attempts lm outputs replay ID lm outputs replay ID answers 404 for an id in your list the target was removed with lm integration rm register the target again; new events reach it

docs.title: If none of that is it
docs.text:
• Your hub serves its live API contract at /q/openapi and a try-it console at /q/swagger-ui/: Test the API.
  • Security reports: contact@lumnik.fr (acknowledged within 72 hours). It is not a support channel.

docs.title: Architecture — the why
docs.text: Every other page describes a what. This one lists the design commitments everything else hangs from — the page to read when evaluating lumnik.

docs.title: Read-only first
docs.text:
Ingestion is one-way: there is no write path back to your systems — not behind a flag, not for administrators. The hub lands data in its own PostgreSQL, and fusion, chat, apps and events work on that copy. Your system of record stays the sole owner of its data.

The same posture extends downstream: the SQL that answers a chat question executes on a separate, physically read-only database connection — see the next commitment.

docs.title: Isolation lives in the database
docs.text:
Multi-tenant isolation is not application code you have to trust; it is PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, enforced by the layer that cannot be bypassed by a bug in the layer above. Three database roles carry three trust levels:

  • the request path runs RLS-enforced, and owns nothing;
  • LLM-generated SQL runs on a role that can only read, with an empty search_path;
  • deliberate cross-tenant work (migrations, purges) runs on a separate role that every code path must use explicitly.

The full mechanics — policies, the tenant GUC, what RLS does and does not protect against — are on RLS & database roles.

docs.title: Refusal over guessing
docs.text:
The system prefers a refusal to a plausible guess:

  • on the way in, a run's arithmetic always closes — a row is written, benignly skipped, or quarantined with its reason (seeing what was ingested);
  • on the way out, deterministic guards stand between a question and its answer, and an empty result is never phrased as a confident "there are none" (its guards);
  • disagreements between sources are preserved in a ledger instead of silently resolved (entities).

docs.title: Declared over inferred
docs.text: Where meaning enters the system, a human declares it: connectors, entities, views, processes and lifecycles are all manifests an integrator applies — validated, refusable, versionable in git. A workflow even records how its lifecycle is known (provenance: declared), so the day something is inferred instead, the difference will be citable — not retrofitted.

docs.title: One hub, optional extensions
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph core["the hub — runs on its own"]
    ing["connectors"] --> raw[("raw tables")]
    raw --> ent["entities"]
  end
  subgraph ext["extensions — discovered at boot"]
    rag["search · chat"]
    llm["LLM providers"]
  end
  ent -.->|"if present"| rag
  rag -.-> llm

A hub without the chat extension still ingests, fuses and serves. What needs a model says so:

$ lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
Error: API error 400: generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one

Ready to verify any of this against a running system? Deploy is one command, and the cheat sheet is the minimum you need to poke at it.

docs.text: The minimum that operates lumnik, on one page. Unknown word: glossary.

docs.title: Stand it up
docs.text:
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build   # first run writes .env with fresh secrets — BACK IT UP
curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/health   # UP, or DOWN with the failing check named
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub     # follow the hub (see: Reading the logs)

Full walkthroughs: Deploy · Reading the logs.

docs.title: The ten commands
docs.text:
# Command What it does 1 lm login authenticate once; lm remembers the context 2 lm validate -f FILE dry-run a kind: Connector manifest — errors field by field. The other kinds have no dry-run: their apply checks first and refuses rather than half-writes 3 lm apply -f FILE apply a connector manifest (upsert) 4 lm connector run NAME run it now 5 lm run list --connector NAME the run ledger — records in/out/skip at a glance 6 lm dlq list --run ID exactly which rows fell out, and why 7 lm entity apply -f FILE fuse sources into one canonical entity (lm entity delete NAME removes it, and frees a connector it blocked) 8 lm workflow apply -f FILE declare a lifecycle — lists the status values your data holds and the manifest does not declare 9 lm ask --scope S "question" ask the data — prints the answer, the rows and the SQL that ran (-o json for the whole result). lumnik Pro 10 lm secret set NAME store a secret — prompted, not echoed (NAME - reads stdin instead, for a multi-line key or a script); values are never returned

The full surface (sources, endpoints, mappings, tags, observations…) is in the CLI & TUI reference.

Command 5 is the screen you will read most. On every row, IN = OUT + SKIPPED:

$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
30b078c6  customers     default   Completed  12  12   0        0             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
f0466804  orders        default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
3ccd21eb  products      default   Failed     0   0    0        0             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
852771fa  crm-contacts  default   Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-09-05 05:39  2026-09-05 05:39
  • Failed is the run itself (source unreachable, bad credentials): lm run get 3ccd21eb prints the reason.
  • DEAD-LETTERS are rows set aside with their reason: lm dlq list.
  • Stop a running run: lm run cancel ID. It ends after the current batch of rows.

Every -f also takes -f - (stdin), and every listing takes -o json: Integration as code. Command 9 answers Error: API error 404 (no details from the server) on the open edition — see which edition you installed.

docs.title: The TUI in six keys
docs.text:
lm with no arguments opens the TUI:

Key Does : command palette — :sources :runs :dlq :ask :inbox :outputs … r refresh d describe the selected row y yank the row to the clipboard ? help q quit

:runs, :dlq and :inbox live-update — you can watch a run while it happens.

docs.title: When it refuses
docs.text: You see It means Where to look Error: access refused (403): scope not granted your user holds scope roles, and this resource is in none of them Scopes Je ne peux pas répondre à partir des données disponibles… from lm ask a guard refused rather than guess; the message says what to do next The five guards a run with SKIPPED > 0 rows counted and not written. Duplicates and policy-excluded rows are skipped without reaching the DLQ; DEAD-LETTERS is the part that did Ingestion honesty

docs.title: Choosing what your hub offers
docs.text:
The same hub can show a warehouse team two tabs and a sales team four, run with the AI switched off for a client who forbids a model, or carry Search when it was built in. Four questions, asked in order, decide what a business app shows — and each has one gesture.

Who the integrator installing or tuning a hub Gestures the image you deploy, one environment variable, one line in a kind: App manifest — and, for Search, a kind: SearchIndex See the result lm module list, then the app itself Edition both — what differs is which answers are possible (Open vs Pro)

docs.title: The four questions
docs.text:
Questions 1 to 3 decide whether a tab is on an app. Question 4 decides whether it is worth showing: Search checks it before it appears, while Records opens anyway and says what is missing. Read them top to bottom; the first no is your answer when something is missing.

flowchart LR
  a["1. Is it in the build?"] --> b["2. Is it switched on?"] --> c["3. Does the app ask for it?"] --> d["4. Is it ready to be used?"]
  d --> tab(["the tab is there"])
# Question Who decides Your gesture Where you look 1 Is it in the build? the image you deploy pick Open or Pro; add a Search provider when you build the hub lm module list 2 Is it switched on? the operator LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false turns the AI family off; absent means on lm module list 3 Does the app ask for it? the app's kind: App manifest spec.tabs: [...]; leave it out to take everything the hub offers lm app apply 4 Is it ready to be used? the feature itself for Search, declare a search index the user may read the tab, and lm search status

The tabs and who brings them:

Tab Shown as Brought by Needs fiches Records every hub a saved view for the app's scope (without one the tab opens and says so) inbox Inbox every hub — chat Chat Pro (rag + llm) the AI switched on search Search a Search provider (search_pg or search_opensearch) a search index the user may read

docs.title: 1. Is it in the build?
docs.text:
What the image carries is fixed when the hub is built; no setting adds a module that is not there. Ask the hub what it carries:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      ACTIVE
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        ACTIVE

That is a Pro hub: llm and rag are there, together. An Open hub lists core and identity only — it has no Chat tab to offer, and nothing to switch on:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE

Search is added when you build the hub: the published image never carries a provider. See Deploy (up.sh --search or --search-cluster, closed edition) and choosing a provider. The provider then appears in the list:

$ lm module list
NAME       VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core       0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity   0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm        0.1.0    Model provider      ACTIVE
rag        0.1.0    Platform RAG        ACTIVE
search_pg  0.1.0    PostgreSQL search   ACTIVE

No lm command prints which tabs each module brings; the platform API does (integrator token). The hub offers the tabs of the active modules — here a Pro hub with the AI switched off:

$ curl -s "$LUMNIK_URL/api/platform/modules" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    | jq -c '.modules[] | select((.tabs|length)>0) | {id, active, tabs}'
{"id":"core","active":true,"tabs":["fiches","inbox"]}
{"id":"rag","active":false,"tabs":["chat"]}

A Search provider adds {"id":"search_pg","active":true,"tabs":["search"]}.

docs.title: 2. Is it switched on?
docs.text:
One setting switches off the whole AI family — chat, ask, view generation, embeddings — without rebuilding: LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false. The gesture per install is in Deploy — switch the AI off. It must be exactly true or false; anything else stops the hub at startup. What you see, and what keeps running: Switching the AI off.

The module list tells the difference between switched off and not there:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE    
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE    
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
  • Inactive (Pro, switched off): the data is kept, the images are the same, and putting the setting back restores what you had. Content that needed indexing while the AI was off is not there when it returns — re-apply the workflow or re-ingest the file (what comes back).
  • Absent (Open): the module is not in the build, so it is not in the list at all.

Either way the Chat tab is gone from every app. Search is not part of this switch: turning the AI off leaves Search exactly as it was.

docs.title: 3. Does the app ask for it?
docs.text:
Each business app is a kind: App manifest. Without tabs it shows everything the hub offers (and whatever a later release adds). To show fewer tabs, or to change their order, list them:

kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: stock
spec:
  title: Stock
  scope: stock
  icon: stock
  tabs: [fiches, inbox]        # no Chat for the warehouse

$ lm app apply -f stock.yaml
Applied app "stock" → scope stock
  tabs: fiches, inbox

A tab the hub does not offer is kept, and shows up the day the hub offers it. The apply warns without failing — here tabs: [fiches, inbox, chat] on a hub without Chat:

$ lm app apply -f stock.yaml
Applied app "stock" → scope stock
  tabs: fiches, inbox, chat
! stock.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.tabs[2]
          tab 'chat' is not offered by this hub; the declaration is kept and takes effect when a module offering it is active
          → offered here: [fiches, inbox]

The last line is the hub's offer. Order, the opening tab and what is refused: Choosing the tabs.

Hiding a tab hides it, nothing more: who may read what is still decided by roles and scopes.

docs.title: 4. Is it ready to be used?
docs.text:
Tab Ready when Check Records a saved view exists for the app's scope (otherwise the tab opens and says so) lm view list --scope <app scope> Search the user may read a search index (otherwise the tab is not shown) lm search status

Search's full checklist: Enabling Search for an app.

Whether Search is installed: the TUI's :search page says so in its banner, and a query on a hub without a provider is refused, never answered with an empty list:

$ lm search query "Lyon"
Error: search is not installed on this hub — no Search provider is built into it, so there is nothing to query (this is not an empty result). The published hub image never carries one: build it from source with deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search (PostgreSQL) or --search-cluster (OpenSearch), both closed edition

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A warehouse app with no Chat, on a Pro hub. Question 3 only: tabs: [fiches, inbox] in the app's manifest, then lm app apply -f. The other apps keep their Chat.

A client who forbids a model on their hub. Question 2: switch the AI off. Every app loses its Chat tab at once, no manifest changes, and the rest of the hub (including Oracle, SCIM and Search) is untouched.

Search in one app, but not the others (questions 3 and 4, here for the stock app):

  1. In the stock app's manifest, list search in tabs; lm app apply -f.
  2. In each kind: Entity to search, set scopes: [stock] (the entity's scopes list — not the app's scope, not the users' scope:<tag> role); lm entity apply -f.
  3. Declare a search index over those entities: lm search apply -f.
  4. Give every other app a tabs list without search. An app that leaves tabs out shows Search to any user who may read some index.

No results on every search

An app whose scope has nothing indexed still shows Search when its users can read another scope's index — and every search answers No results. Check lm search status when a team expects hits.

docs.title: When a tab is missing
docs.text:
Go down the questions; stop at the first one that answers no.

What you see Look at Likely answer No Chat tab on any app lm module list llm and rag missing: this is an Open build. Listed INACTIVE with disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled: switch the AI back on. No Search tab on any app lm module list no search_pg / search_opensearch: the hub was built without a Search provider. No Search tab, yet search_pg is ACTIVE lm search status no kind: SearchIndex is declared yet (the list is empty), or the users may read none of the entities the indexes cover. Search missing on one app only that app's manifest tabs leaves out search; or its users hold scopes that read none of the indexed entities (compare each entity's scopes with their scope:<tag> roles). Search there, but always No results lm search status the index is not built yet (STATUS, DOCUMENTS). … and STATUS reads invalid lm search status an entity re-apply removed a column the index declares — re-apply the index. … and STATUS reads withheld lm search status an index re-apply removed or changed a field — it serves again once rebuilt. … and the index is ready lm search status no index covers the entities of the app's scope. A tab listed in tabs does not show lm app apply -f again the hub does not offer it (question 1 or 2): the apply warns. The warning reflects the offer when you apply; the tab appears once the hub offers it. Chat tab present, answers fail lm rag status the tab shows whenever rag and llm are active; a model that is not reachable is a different problem (models).

docs.title: Deploy on Windows
docs.text:
Your Windows PC can run all of lumnik — the hub, the database, the login server, even the AI. This page walks you there step by step: each one says where to type, what to type, and what you should see before moving on.

Total time: about an hour, most of it downloads. You need Windows 10 (version 21H2 or later) or Windows 11, and around 20 GB of free disk.

docs.title: The two windows you will type into
docs.text:
Everything below happens in one of two command windows — worth telling apart before starting:

  • PowerShell — Windows' own command window. Open it from the Start menu: type powershell, click the result. You'll use it for Windows-side things (installing tools, running lm.exe).
  • Ubuntu — a small Linux that lives inside Windows (installed in step 1). Open it from the Start menu: type ubuntu. lumnik itself runs here.

Three habits that save an hour

  • Paste with a right-click. In these windows Ctrl+V often does nothing; copy the command here, then right-click inside the window — it pastes.
  • One command, then Enter, then wait. The command is done when the prompt (the line ending in > or $) comes back.
  • Passwords are typed blind. When Ubuntu asks for a password, nothing appears while you type — no dots, no stars. That's normal: type it and press Enter.

docs.title: Step 1 — Install WSL2, the Linux inside Windows (~10 min, one restart)
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell as administrator: Start menu → type powershell → right-click the result → Run as administrator → answer Yes.
  2. Type: 
    wsl --install
    Windows downloads WSL2 and Ubuntu. When it asks, restart the PC.
  3. After the restart, an Ubuntu window opens on its own (if not: Start menu → ubuntu). It asks you to pick a username and a password — this is a new, Linux-side account, not your Windows one. Remember the password: Ubuntu asks for it whenever a command starts with sudo.
  4. Check it worked — in a normal PowerShell window: 
    wsl --status
    You should see Default Version: 2.

It complains about virtualization or the BIOS?

Your PC's virtualization switch is off. Check: Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Performance → CPU → look for Virtualization: Enabled. If it says Disabled, it must be enabled in the BIOS (usually F2/Del at power-on, then an option named VT-x, SVM or "Virtualization Technology"). A search for "enable virtualization + your PC model" gives the exact keys.

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Docker Desktop (~10 min)
docs.text:
Docker runs lumnik's services in containers — you never have to install Java, a database, or anything else by hand.

  1. Download Docker Desktop for Windows from docker.com and run the installer. Keep every default. Restart if it asks.
  2. Open Docker Desktop. It suggests creating an account — you don't need one: look for the small Continue without signing in link.
  3. Two settings to verify (gear icon ⚙, top right):
    • General → Use the WSL 2 based engine — should already be checked.
    • Resources → WSL integration → turn the Ubuntu switch on → Apply & restart.
  4. Prove it — in the Ubuntu window: 
    docker run --rm hello-world
    You should see Hello from Docker! in the output. If instead you get docker: command not found, revisit the WSL-integration switch above.

docs.title: Step 3 — Get lumnik (in Ubuntu, ~5 min)
docs.text:
From here on, work in the Ubuntu window. One rule to know: keep the code in Ubuntu's own home folder (~), never under /mnt/c — the Windows disk seen from Ubuntu is slow and mangles scripts.

  1. Install the small tools lumnik's installer uses (Ubuntu arrives almost empty): 
    sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git curl python3 openssl gawk jq
    (sudo asks for your Ubuntu password — typed blind, see above.)
  2. Fetch the code: 
    cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open

Which edition you just cloned

This is the open edition: every step on this page applies to it except step 5. It has no chat and no natural-language ask. See also the Deploy page.

docs.title: Step 4 — Start the stack (one command; ~10–20 min the first time)
docs.text:
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build

This single command builds and starts everything inside Docker — nothing else to install on your PC. The first run compiles lumnik from source: it's the long one, a coffee's worth. Later runs take seconds.

What the end must look like — the last lines, in this order:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)

Those two password set lines matter: they create your login accounts, with passwords unique to your install (stored in a file named .env).

The script stopped straight away, naming missing tools?

That's its preflight doing its job — run the sudo apt install line from step 3, then run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build again. It's safe to re-run as often as you like.

If instead the very end says !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token, the login server was slow to finish its first start — simply re-run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build; the passwords get set on the next pass.

See it live: in your normal Windows browser, open http://localhost:8080/q/health. It starts like this (Windows sees Ubuntu's services on its own localhost — nothing to configure):

{
    "status": "UP",
    "checks": [
        {
            "name": "Database connections health check",
            "status": "UP",

docs.title: Step 5 — The AI, on the Windows side (~20 min, ~8 GB of downloads)
docs.text:
Ingestion and the REST API work without this step. The chat and the natural-language "ask" need a local AI runtime: Ollama, installed on Windows itself.

On the open edition, skip this step entirely

The modules that call Ollama are not in the tree you cloned at step 3, so nothing in your install will ever reach it — the ~8 GB of downloads below buy you nothing. Come back to this step only on a build that carries the chat extensions.

Graphics drivers first — the trap that looks like nothing

If your PC has an NVIDIA card, update its drivers before the first model run (GeForce Experience, or your PC maker's support page). Ollama uses the graphics card, and outdated drivers make the model silently fail to load — lumnik's ask then errors after ~20 seconds with no useful message.

  1. Download and run the Ollama for Windows installer from ollama.com. No settings to change.
  2. In PowerShell, download the three models lumnik uses at runtime (the names must be exactly these): 
    ollama pull nomic-embed-text
ollama pull llama3.2
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
  3. Prove it: 
    ollama run llama3.2 "say hello"
    A slow-ish sentence back means everything works. The hub finds Ollama on its own — nothing to wire.

16 GB of RAM or less? Give Windows room to breathe

Ubuntu/WSL grabs up to half your RAM by default, and the AI model needs ~6 GB free on the Windows side. Cap WSL once: in PowerShell, notepad $env:USERPROFILE\.wslconfig (say Yes to create the file), put exactly this in it, save and close: 

[wsl2]
memory=6GB
Then wsl --shutdown in PowerShell, reopen Docker Desktop, and wait a minute for the stack to come back.

docs.title: Step 6 — lm, the control room, on Windows
docs.text:
lm.exe is lumnik's command-line and terminal UI for Windows. Download the Windows x86-64 .zip from the Releases page and unpack lm.exe anywhere, e.g. your Downloads folder.

Windows protected your PC?

The first launch may show a blue SmartScreen box — the file is not signed. Click More info, then Run anyway.

In PowerShell, from the folder holding the file:

.\lm.exe config set-context selfhost --server http://localhost:8080 --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
.\lm.exe config use-context selfhost
.\lm.exe login

lm login shows a web address and a code — open the address in your browser, enter the code, and sign in as integrator. The password was minted for your install at step 4; read it in the Ubuntu window with:

grep INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD ~/lumnik-open/.env

Then just:

.\lm.exe

— the full terminal UI. Press ? inside for help, : for the command palette.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
Walk The WOW — ingest two fake legacy systems, watch lumnik fuse them, and ask the result a question in plain language. One habit to take along: after every lm connector run …, check lm run list — "run scheduled" is not "run succeeded", and the list is where the truth lives.

  • A phone on this stack: http://localhost:8080 is reachable from your PC only. Put the TLS proxy in front.
  • Another port, an external PostgreSQL: see How to… — the port stays, use the proxy; an external database is not an option on this path.

docs.title: Troubleshooting, Windows edition
docs.text:
Symptom What it means → what to do wsl --install is "not recognized" Windows too old — run Windows Update until version 21H2+, or install WSL from the Microsoft Store. WSL complains about virtualization / BIOS The VT switch is off — see the note in step 1. docker: command not found in Ubuntu The WSL-integration switch for Ubuntu is off — step 2, setting 3. !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token at the end of up.sh The login server was still starting. Re-run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build: the passwords get set on the next pass. http://localhost:8080 suddenly unreachable (often after the PC slept) WSL's plumbing went stale — in PowerShell wsl --shutdown, reopen Docker Desktop, wait a minute. Logins fail with 401 after the laptop slept Ubuntu's clock drifted during sleep — same cure: wsl --shutdown, reopen Docker Desktop. The ask/chat errors after ~20 s The model failed to load on the Windows side: update your NVIDIA drivers (the classic), then check the RAM note in step 5. SmartScreen blocks lm.exe Expected: the file is not signed — More info → Run anyway (step 6).

For everything not Windows-specific: Troubleshooting, by symptom.

docs.title: Deploy lumnik
docs.text:
Installation

Get the hub running: one command on a single host, or the Helm chart on Kubernetes.

Fastest path

Self-host with Docker Compose and ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build.

What you get

Hub, Postgres, Keycloak, per-install secrets, and real OIDC.

Then do this

Point lm at the hub and log in.

Read this first

Back up the generated .env. Losing LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY makes stored secrets unrecoverable.

Before anything: the prerequisites checklist.

docs.title: Choose the path
docs.text:
• Self-host — one command, one machine. Start here.
  • One HTTPS origin — add it when phones must reach the hub.
  • Kubernetes / Helm — the cloud edition, for a cluster.

docs.title: Self-host — one command
docs.text:
On a Windows PC?

Follow Deploy on Windows instead. It starts from zero, WSL2 and Docker Desktop included. The commands below are for Linux or macOS.

git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build

Which edition you get:

You run You get up.sh --build in a lumnik-open clone lumnik Open: ingestion, entities, views, processes, workflows, outputs, the PWA. No chat, no lm ask, no Ollama. up.sh without --build, with access to the published image lumnik Pro: Open plus chat and lm ask. Prepare Ollama first.

The published image is private: the pull works only if your GitHub account was granted access. Check what runs with lm module list (The two editions).

The stack you get:

flowchart LR
  lmop["lm — the integrator"] --> hub
  phone["a business user's phone"] -.->|"https, via the TLS proxy"| caddy
  subgraph machine["one machine — docker compose"]
    caddy["caddy — one https origin<br/>(optional TLS proxy)"]
    hub["hub :8080<br/>API + PWA at /app/"]
    kc["keycloak :8180<br/>realm lumnik"]
    pg[("postgres<br/>internal")]
    caddy -->|"/*"| hub
    caddy -->|"/realms/*"| kc
    hub --> pg
    hub -.->|"OIDC"| kc
  end

What the launcher does:

1 2 3

Stop the stack: deploy/selfhost/down.sh. Follow its logs: deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub. Re-run up.sh with the same flags at any time: your data and .env are kept.

The bundled Keycloak

  • It serves one machine. backup.sh saves it: Backup & restore.
  • The client's own directory (Keycloak, Okta, Entra ID): Bring your own IdP.

docs.title: Generate secrets safely
docs.text: It writes your passwords and keys into .env, at the root of the clone. Only you can read it. It never overwrites an existing .env. Back it up.

docs.title: Build and start the stack
docs.text: It builds the hub image (--build) or pulls it, starts hub + Postgres + Keycloak, and waits for the hub to be healthy. The first boot can take a minute.

docs.title: Mint per-install passwords
docs.text:
It sets the hubadmin and integrator passwords in Keycloak and prints the URLs.

You know it worked when: the launcher ends like this:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)
  Keycloak:  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
  Next:      point lm at the hub — server http://localhost:8080, OIDC http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik

docs.title: One HTTPS origin — the TLS proxy
docs.text:
A phone installs the PWA only from one https address. The proxy gives it one: the hub at /, Keycloak under /realms/*. Layer it on after up.sh:

LUMNIK_TLS_HOST=erp.example.com \
  docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml up -d
  • A public name gets a Let's Encrypt certificate by itself. Ports 80 and 443 must be reachable.
  • A LAN IP or localhost gets a local certificate, for testing.
  • The proxy listens on every interface, so phones on the LAN reach it. LUMNIK_TLS_BIND=127.0.0.1 restricts it.
  • up.sh keeps the proxy: a later run re-applies the overlays the stack was started with.
  • Choose the address once. Changing it changes who signs the tokens: users created through the old address must be migrated (Keep the same public address).

docs.title: Trust the local certificate on a phone
docs.text:
With a LAN IP, the phone warns and refuses to install the PWA. Copy the certificate out:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml \
  cp caddy:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt ./lumnik-local-ca.crt

Install lumnik-local-ca.crt on the phone. On iOS: AirDrop the file, then Settings → General → VPN & Device Management, then turn on full trust under Certificate Trust Settings.

docs.title: Point lm at the hub
docs.text:
Install lm, then give it the server and the OIDC issuer — nothing else:

lm config set-context selfhost \
     --server http://localhost:8080 \
     --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context selfhost
lm login        # prints a URL + device code — open it, sign in as integrator
User Tenant Password in .env integrator 1 INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD — change it before anything real hubadmin (superadmin) 11 HUBADMIN_PASSWORD

--oidc-client-id defaults to lm-cli, the bundled realm's client; set it only for your own IdP. Check the login — on a fresh hub, headers only:

$ lm connector list
NAME  TYPE  TENANT  SCHED  WINDOW  STATUS  LAST RUN

docs.title: Point the hub at an Ollama on another machine
docs.text: Pro only. Uncomment OLLAMA_BASE_URL=… in .env, then re-run up.sh with your flags. Left unset, the hub looks for Ollama on the machine running Docker.

docs.title: Switch the AI off
docs.text:
The chat, the ask and the embeddings stop; the data is kept, and the PWA drops its Chat tab. The value is exactly true or false.

Install Gesture Self-host LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false in .env, then re-run up.sh with the flags you installed with (--build, --search…). It pulls the hub image: pin LUMNIK_VERSION first, or it is also an upgrade. A plain docker compose restart keeps the old setting. Helm (cloud edition), first install LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false ./deploy/helm/up.sh (chart value ai.enabled) Helm (cloud edition), running cluster helm upgrade <release> deploy/helm/lumnik --reuse-values --set-string ai.enabled=false, then kubectl rollout restart deployment/<release>-hub. up.sh refuses to run on a running cluster — see Kubernetes / Helm

Check it with lm module list: rag and llm read INACTIVE disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled. What a switch back on restores: Switching the AI off.

docs.title: Turn on email delivery
docs.text:
Until you set two lines, the hub only pretends to send mail. In .env:

LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
# optional: LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=587  LUMNIK_SMTP_USERNAME=…  LUMNIK_SMTP_PASSWORD=…
#           LUMNIK_SMTP_FROM=lumnik@example.com  LUMNIK_SMTP_STARTTLS=REQUIRED

Re-run up.sh with your flags. Then check the hub's log:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs hub | grep 'email delivery'

You want a line holding "message":"email delivery live via smtp.example.com". If you set the host but not LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false, every start logs LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST is set but delivery is still mocked. With neither set, the hub stays mocked and logs nothing about email. To switch email back off, comment the host line out: an empty LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST= stops the hub at startup.

Rehearse without a mail provider. Start the bundled test mailbox, point .env at it, restart the hub:

docker compose --profile mailpit -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d
# .env: LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=mailpit  LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=1025  LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d hub

On a TLS install, run the proxy command instead of the last line. Mail then shows at http://127.0.0.1:8025. A failed send is not retried: Email notifications.

docs.title: Offer Kotlin scripts to the integrators
docs.text:
A csv-file connector or a REST endpoint can run a Kotlin script by naming it, script: hooks:<name>.kts (Kotlin hooks). The scripts come from you: copy the .kts files into deploy/selfhost/hooks/.

cp ean-check.kts deploy/selfhost/hooks/
What How The hub sees the directory read-only. Git ignores the files there. A new or replaced script used from the next run, without a restart The integrator checks lm hook scripts lists name, size and SHA-256; lm apply refuses a script that is missing or does not compile File names lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, ending in .kts. Another name is not offered.

A script runs with all of the hub's rights. Install only scripts you have read. On Helm, the scripts come from a ConfigMap.

docs.title: Reach the hub from another machine
docs.text: The hub (8080) and Keycloak (8180) listen on 127.0.0.1 only. Two ways in: an SSH tunnel, or the TLS proxy — the one a phone needs to install the PWA.

docs.title: Run against a managed or external PostgreSQL
docs.text: Not on this path: self-host always runs its own Postgres. An external database is a job for the Kubernetes / Helm path, below.

docs.title: Kubernetes / Helm
docs.text: The cloud edition (commercial) ships a Kubernetes/Helm path — hub + Postgres + Keycloak with real OIDC, sealed secrets, and a managed-PostgreSQL mode. It is not part of this repository.

docs.title: The two editions
docs.text:
lumnik ships as two builds:

Build Licence What it does lumnik-open Apache-2.0, public repository ingest, fuse, react, serve the business apps lumnik Pro commercial adds Ask (natural-language chat over your data), model providers and the external-identity loop

The open hub has no chat and no Ask: no stub, no licence key. lm is one binary for both editions; on an open hub its Ask commands (lm ask, lm chat, lm rag search, lm scopes) say so:

$ lm ask "how many customers?"
Error: this hub's build has no Ask: lumnik Open has no chat, no lm ask and no semantic search (lm module list shows no rag module); Ask ships in lumnik Pro

lumnik Open is the build behind the free Hub tier. lumnik Pro is the build behind both paid tiers — see Three tiers, two builds.

docs.title: Feature by feature
docs.text:
lumnik Open lumnik Pro Connectors: CSV (SFTP/S3), JDBC, REST + GraphQL/SOAP shapes ✓ ✓ Connector: kafka — ✓ JDBC dialect: Oracle (driver included) — ✓ Fusion: entities, _conflicts ledger ✓ ✓ Apps ladder: views, processes, workflows, inbox, PWA ✓ ✓ Outputs: webhooks (signed, journaled, replay), email notifications ✓ ✓ lm CLI / TUI, manifests, the whole integrator surface ✓ ✓ Multi-tenancy & RLS, audit trail, backup ✓ ✓ Search: declare an index (kind: SearchIndex). Querying needs a provider: without one, lm search query answers not installed ✓ ✓ Search provider: PostgreSQL (up.sh --search) or OpenSearch / Elasticsearch (up.sh --search-cluster). Never in the published image. It also brings the PWA's Search tab — ✓ opt-in build Ask: chat and lm ask, semantic search, lm view generate (the AI writes a view) — ✓ Model providers (Ollama & friends) — ✓ JIT provisioning for external IdPs — ✓ SCIM deprovisioning — ✓

Switched off is not absent. A Pro hub can run with the AI switched off (LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false): the data is kept, and lm module list shows rag and llm as INACTIVE. An Open hub does not list them at all. Neither shows a Chat tab. How to switch it: Choosing what your hub offers.

docs.title: Which edition am I running?
docs.text:
$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE    
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE    
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
What you see Build core + identity only lumnik Open plus rag + llm (always together) lumnik Pro — INACTIVE means the AI is switched off, as above plus search_pg or search_opensearch a build with a Search provider

The hub's boot log lists the installed modules too. More: the full answer.

docs.title: Three tiers, two builds
docs.text:
The commercial ladder has three tiers; the builds are two:

Tier Runs the build Who operates it Hub — free, installed on your own machines lumnik Open your integrator, exploring and tooling up Pro lumnik Pro your integrator, running it for a client Enterprise — on quote lumnik Pro your own IT, in your own world

Enterprise is the Pro build, sold with your identity directory (external IdP, SCIM), a Kubernetes delivery and service commitments. These pages mark a capability "not in the open edition" — the build you can check with lm module list, not the tier.

Prices: contact@lumnik.fr. The open edition is the same hub, so an evaluation can start there.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• How lumnik works · How lumnik breathes
  • Deploy — the same one-command stack for either build
  • Choosing what your hub offers — which tabs and features a hub shows, and the gesture for each
  • Security overview — every edition-dependent answer, marked

docs.title: Email notifications
docs.text: A rule routes matching events to a recipient — one mail per event, rendered through a template you choose. Needs the lm_admin role. For tools rather than people, use a webhook.

docs.title: Route events to a mailbox
docs.text:
# Business alerts: send every decision to the sales administration inbox
lm notify add --events 'decision.*' --to adv@example.com --template decision-alert

# The ops case: failed runs, to the integrator, raw payload included
lm notify add --events 'connector.run.failed' --to integrator@example.com

lm notify list
lm notify rm <ID>

$ lm notify add --events 'connector.run.failed' --to integrator@example.com
rule 1000: connector.run.failed → integrator@example.com
$ lm notify list
ID    EVENTS                RECIPIENT               TEMPLATE            ENABLED
1000  connector.run.failed  integrator@example.com  event-notification  true
  • --events takes an exact type or a prefix ending in .* — see the event registry.

  • Narrow a rule to one table (HTTP only): no lm flag does it. Post the rule with entityFilter and the table's full name (mint $TOKEN):

    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/notifications -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"eventPattern":"data.row.changed","entityFilter":"connector.t_customers","recipient":"adv@example.com"}'

    A misspelt key is refused with 400, naming it and the accepted keys:

    {"error":"unknown key: entity_filter — accepted keys: enabled, entityFilter, eventPattern, recipient, template"}

    For data.row.changed, a name that is not a connector table is refused.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates are Qute HTML files at templates/email/<name>.html inside the hub. The rule picks one by name (--template), in kebab-case only; an unknown name is logged and the mail skipped.

$ lm notify add --events 'decision.*' --to adv@example.com --template '../x'
Error: API error 400: template must match [a-z0-9-]+ (a template name, not a path)

Two ship with the hub:

Template Voice Body event-notification (default) ops subject + source/entity/time line + the payload as JSON in a <pre> decision-alert business the process message as headline ("Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €"), entity & key, the referenced fields as a table

docs.title: The variables a template sees
Add your own template
docs.text: Templates ship inside the hub image: the published image cannot take your own. Put the file at lumnik-hub/src/main/resources/templates/email/<kebab-name>.html, then rebuild with ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build. Rehearse against the Mailpit drill before pointing rules at it.

docs.title: Delivery — what to expect
docs.text:
• A mail leaves within about 5 seconds.
  • Mocked until the deploy sets the SMTP knobs (turn on email delivery).
  • Best-effort: a failed send is logged and skipped — no retry, no journal. One broken recipient does not block the others.
  • A hub crash can lose a batch of mails; it never sends one twice.

When delivery must be provable, wire a webhook as well.

docs.title: Mail the ADV every time an order lands in dispute
docs.text:
The demo desk's litige-ouvert process already writes the sentence the ADV reads (Processes). Route it to a mailbox:

lm notify add --events decision.litige-ouvert --to adv@example.com --template decision-alert

Result: the next run that lands an order in dispute sends one mail. Its headline is the process's sentence, as lm inbox shows it: Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €. Below it, the referenced fields as a table.

docs.title: Rehearse without a mail provider
docs.text:
docker compose --profile mailpit -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d
# .env: LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=mailpit  LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=1025  LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build    # re-run with the flags you installed with
# then browse to http://127.0.0.1:8025

Result: every rule-matched event lands in Mailpit's inbox, rendered exactly as your provider would send it — templates included.

docs.title: Show only the fields that matter
docs.text:
A template is ordinary HTML around the variables — this one renders two columns and nothing else:

<!-- templates/email/commande-courte.html -->
<h2>{payload.message ?: eventType}</h2>
<p>N° <strong>{payload.fields.order_no ?: '—'}</strong> · {payload.fields.amount ?: '—'} €</p>

Rebuild the hub (templates ship in the image), then point the rule at it: lm notify add --events decision.litige-ouvert --to adv@example.com --template commande-courte.

docs.text:
• Outputs — the roads out — the full wiring manual, registry included
  • Processes — react — where decision.* and its message are declared
  • Deploy — turn on email delivery — SMTP knobs & Mailpit

docs.title: Entities — joins
docs.text: A product references its category. A join brings the category's fields onto each product, without merging products and without adding a row.

docs.title: Fuse or join
docs.text:
Fuse (match + sources[]) Join (joins[]) The question several systems describe the same object one object references another Example the ERP's customer and the CRM's customer a product and its category Rows merged into one per match key never merged, never multiplied Disagreement kept in _conflicts none: a lookup is not an opinion

match: [category_id] is not a join: it would merge every product of a category into one row.

docs.title: The case
docs.text:
Four products, and a category table with a gap and a duplicate:

m_product_id,m_product_category_id,name
P1,C1,Pump 50
P2,C1,Pump 80
P3,C9,Spare gasket
P4,C2,Valve DN15

m_product_category_id,name,description
C1,Pumps,Centrifugal and gear pumps
C2,Valves,Ball valves
C2,Valves (old),Superseded listing

The entity declares the category table as a lookup:

kind: Entity
name: ProductWithCategory
description: One row per product, enriched with its category — a join, not a fusion.
match: [product_id]
scopes: [catalogue]
sources:
  - table: t_products
    map:
      m_product_id: product_id
      m_product_category_id: category_id
      name: product_name
joins:
  - table: t_product_categories   # the lookup: it fuses nothing and adds no row
    from: category_id             # a canonical column of the fused entity
    to: m_product_category_id     # a physical column of the lookup table
    map:
      name: category_name
      description: category_description

Land and apply (the manifests read /tmp/acme-catalogue/ on the hub's disk):

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml cp docs/apps/demo/data/. hub:/tmp/acme-catalogue
lm apply -f docs/apps/demo/sources/40-products.yaml
lm apply -f docs/apps/demo/sources/50-product-categories.yaml
lm connector run products && lm connector run product-categories
lm entity apply -f docs/apps/demo/entities/30-product-with-category.yaml

Wait for both runs to read Completed in lm run list before the entity apply.

docs.title: The result
docs.text:
$ lm entity get ProductWithCategory
PRODUCT_ID  CATEGORY_ID  PRODUCT_NAME  CATEGORY_NAME  CATEGORY_DESCRIPTION        _CONFLICTS
P1          C1           Pump 50       Pumps          Centrifugal and gear pumps  {}
P2          C1           Pump 80       Pumps          Centrifugal and gear pumps  {}
P3          C9           Spare gasket                                             {}
P4          C2           Valve DN15                                               {"category_name": [{"src": "t_product_categories", "value": "Valves"}, {"src": "t_product_categories", "value": "Valves (old)"}], "category_description": [{"src": "t_product_categories", "value": "Ball valves"}, {"src": "t_product_categories", "value": "Superseded listing"}]}
The lookup has, for the key The joined columns _conflicts no row (P3, category C9) empty; the product is kept nothing: an absence is not an opinion exactly one row (P1, P2) that row's values nothing several rows (P4, category C2 listed twice) empty, even when the rows are identical every row, per column: the ambiguity is shown, never guessed

lm view shows a lookup ambiguity under Ambiguïtés et divergences, and lm conflicts list lists it with the source conflicts.

docs.title: The manifest's joins[]
docs.text:
Field Meaning table the lookup's table in the connector schema; not also a source from a column of the fused entity: the value looked up to a column of the lookup table: the key it is matched on map lookup column: new column; a new name must not collide with another column
  • Joined columns are readable, filterable, askable and exportable like any other.
  • A join reads only the fused entity's columns: joins cannot chain.
  • On a resolution: entity, joins read the resolved rows.
lm entity apply refuses When 400 from is not a column of the entity, a joined name collides, or the lookup is also a source 400 naming the table and column to or a map key is not in the lookup table 409 run the source connectors first the lookup table does not exist yet How keys are compared

Keys match as written. A plain number matches by value: 1000021 = 1000021.0, 1.5 = 1.50. Nothing else is folded: 01 ≠ 1, C1 ≠ c1. When both sides are dates or times, a date matches every time of its day.

docs.title: Deliver it
docs.text: A joined entity exports like any other: Exports. The demo ships one, docs/apps/exports/30-product-catalogue-s3.yaml.

docs.title: kind: Entity — resolve
docs.text:
When two systems share no key, resolution: gives each real customer one identity. It matches rows rule by rule, keeps what it cannot decide for you to review, and takes your correction over any rule.

Kind Entity, with a resolution: block instead of match: Apply lm entity apply — lm_admin Resolve, correct lm entity resolve, lm entity assert-same, lm entity assert-distinct — lm_admin Review lm entity ambiguous, lm entity history — lm_user, scope-bound Edition Open

Use match: when every system carries the same customer code. Use resolution: when they don't: the ERP knows C-003, the CRM knows contact 9003, and only the email address ties them together.

docs.title: Quickstart — land, apply, resolve
docs.text:
Two small exports. The ERP has four customers. Two of them share one mailbox (compta@groupe-rhone.example). The CRM has five contacts with no ERP code, and one of them has no email at all.

code,name,email
C-001,Hydraulique Lyon,contact@hydraulique-lyon.example
C-002,Fixations Milano,ventes@fixations-milano.example
C-003,Filtration Lyon,compta@groupe-rhone.example
C-004,Levage Lyon,compta@groupe-rhone.example

contact_id,company,mail
9001,HYDRAULIQUE LYON,Contact@Hydraulique-Lyon.example
9002,Fixations Milano,ventes@fixations-milano.example
9003,Groupe Rhône,compta@groupe-rhone.example
9004,Transmission Aarhus,
9005,Pneumatique Porto,geral@pneumatique-porto.example

The manifests read the files from /tmp/acme-resolution/ on the hub's filesystem; no lm command places a file there. Copy them in, then land both sources:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml cp docs/entities-resolution/. hub:/tmp/acme-resolution
lm apply -f docs/entities-resolution/10-erp.yaml
lm apply -f docs/entities-resolution/20-crm.yaml
lm connector run res-erp
lm connector run res-crm

$ lm run list --connector res-crm
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
3139233c  res-crm    default   Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-19 01:47  2026-10-19 01:47

The entity declares one rule: same email address, compared in lower case.

# 30-customer.yaml — one Customer across the ERP and the CRM, which share no key.
# The two are matched on the email address, compared in lower case.

kind: Entity
name: Customer
scopes: [sales]
sources:
  - table: t_res_erp
    map:
      code: code
      name: name
      email: email
  - table: t_res_crm
    map:
      contact_id: crm_id
      company: name
      mail: email
resolution:
  identity:               # the column that identifies a row in each source
    t_res_erp: code
    t_res_crm: crm_id
  cascade:
    - id: email
      exact:
        fields: [email]
        normalize: [lower]

Apply it, then resolve it once. After that, every source run that ends Completed or Partial resolves the rows it wrote. A Failed or Cancelled run is covered by the next lm entity resolve.

$ lm entity apply -f docs/entities-resolution/30-customer.yaml
Applied entity "Customer" → connector."v_customer"

$ lm entity resolve Customer
rows seen: 9
resolved: 7
ambiguous: 1
unresolved (no rule): 1
unresolved (provider): 0
newly minted: 5
provider calls: 0
provider failures: 0
rule hits:
  customer:email: 8

$ lm entity get Customer
CODE   NAME                 EMAIL                             CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-001  Hydraulique Lyon     contact@hydraulique-lyon.example  9001    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Hydraulique Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "HYDRAULIQUE LYON"}], "email": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "contact@hydraulique-lyon.example"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Contact@Hydraulique-Lyon.example"}]}
C-002  Fixations Milano     ventes@fixations-milano.example   9002    {}
C-003  Filtration Lyon      compta@groupe-rhone.example               {}
C-004  Levage Lyon          compta@groupe-rhone.example               {}
       Groupe Rhône         compta@groupe-rhone.example       9003    {}
       Pneumatique Porto    geral@pneumatique-porto.example   9005    {}
       Transmission Aarhus                                    9004    {}
  • 9001 joined C-001 even though the CRM writes the address in capitals: the rule compares in lower case. Where the two systems still disagree on a value, the row says so in _conflicts, exactly as with match:.
  • 9003 stayed on its own. Its address belongs to two ERP customers, and the rule cannot choose between them. It is ambiguous, and an ambiguous row is never merged.
  • 9004 stayed on its own. It has no email, so no rule could even try. Nothing is lost: the row is still there, waiting for a better rule or a correction.
  • 9005 is a new customer known only to the CRM. It gets an identity of its own.

A row already resolved is never moved silently. If a later pass would join it to a different customer (the data changed, or so did a rule), the row becomes ambiguous and waits for you. Only a correction moves it.

docs.title: Review what it could not decide
docs.text:
$ lm entity ambiguous Customer
IDENTITY_REF                          SOURCE     SOURCE_ID  CANDIDATES                                                                 DECIDED_BY  OCCURRED_AT
410ca39f-f788-4696-b9c4-82ef9a21e774  t_res_crm  9003       8b2d2706-be5c-44d3-a70f-14523d9a68df,a653a6a7-6d2f-488e-99f0-772d5b462d7b  automatic   2026-10-24 23:12

The two candidates are the identities of C-003 (8b2d2706…) and C-004 (a653a6a7…).

lm entity history NAME SOURCE ID explains any decision, one line per pass:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9003
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME    RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                                                                 SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID  ASSERTED_BY  REASON
2026-10-24 23:12:05  AMBIGUOUS  email            8b2d2706-be5c-44d3-a70f-14523d9a68df,a653a6a7-6d2f-488e-99f0-772d5b462d7b             automatic

C-004 shares C-003's mailbox but comes from the same ERP. One customer never holds two rows of the same source, so C-004 got its own identity, and its history shows the one it was set aside from:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_erp C-004
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME   RULE  PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                            SET_ASIDE                             DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID  ASSERTED_BY  REASON
2026-10-24 23:12:05  RESOLVED                  a653a6a7-6d2f-488e-99f0-772d5b462d7b  8b2d2706-be5c-44d3-a70f-14523d9a68df  automatic

docs.title: Correct it
docs.text:
You know that Groupe Rhône is the billing name of Filtration Lyon. Say so, naming each row as SOURCE:ID, then resolve:

$ lm entity assert-same Customer --left t_res_crm:9003 --right t_res_erp:C-003 --reason "Groupe Rhône is Filtration Lyon's billing name"
recorded: t_res_crm:9003 and t_res_erp:C-003 are same

$ lm entity resolve Customer
rows seen: 9
resolved: 8
ambiguous: 0
unresolved (no rule): 1
unresolved (provider): 0
newly minted: 0
provider calls: 0
provider failures: 0
rule hits:
  customer:email: 7

$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9003
CODE   NAME             EMAIL                        CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-003  Filtration Lyon  compta@groupe-rhone.example  9003    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Filtration Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Groupe Rhône"}]}

The history records the correction as asserted, with who made it and why:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9003
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME    RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                                                                 SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID  ASSERTED_BY  REASON
2026-10-24 23:12:05  AMBIGUOUS  email            8b2d2706-be5c-44d3-a70f-14523d9a68df,a653a6a7-6d2f-488e-99f0-772d5b462d7b             automatic
2026-10-24 23:12:05  RESOLVED                    8b2d2706-be5c-44d3-a70f-14523d9a68df                                                  asserted            integrator   Groupe Rhône is Filtration Lyon's billing name
  • A correction outranks every rule and survives every later run and resolve.
  • It takes effect at the next resolve: a run of one of the sources, or lm entity resolve.
  • Two rows of the same source can't be the same customer: such an assertion is refused (400).

To undo it, assert the opposite, then resolve. C-003 stops being a candidate for 9003; only C-004 is left, so the pass joins 9003 to C-004:

$ lm entity assert-distinct Customer --left t_res_crm:9003 --right t_res_erp:C-003
recorded: t_res_crm:9003 and t_res_erp:C-003 are distinct
$ lm entity resolve Customer
…
$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9003
CODE   NAME         EMAIL                        CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-004  Levage Lyon  compta@groupe-rhone.example  9003    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Levage Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Groupe Rhône"}]}

If that is wrong too, assert it distinct as well.

A row is named as the history names it. A mistyped one is refused:

$ lm entity assert-same Customer --left t_res_crm:9030 --right t_res_erp:C-003
Error: API error 404: entity 'Customer' has no row t_res_crm:9030 — check it with lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9030, or run lm entity resolve Customer if the row is new

docs.title: Every run resolves on its own
docs.text:
Add C-005,Pneumatique Porto,geral@pneumatique-porto.example to the ERP file and run the ERP again. The new row joins the CRM's 9005 with no other gesture:

$ lm connector run res-erp
run scheduled: ada9937e-9dc1-4444-adae-fda4c29b9afb

$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9005
CODE   NAME               EMAIL                            CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-005  Pneumatique Porto  geral@pneumatique-porto.example  9005    {}

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_erp C-005
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME   RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                            SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID                                ASSERTED_BY  REASON
2026-10-24 23:12:13  RESOLVED  email            643566ff-d862-4748-95bf-61dca428bcd1             automatic   ada9937e-9dc1-4444-adae-fda4c29b9afb

Run lm entity resolve NAME yourself after applying the entity, after changing its rules, and after a correction.

docs.title: In the TUI
docs.text:
Type :ambiguous, then the entity name and Enter: the screen lists the same rows as lm entity ambiguous.

  • Enter on a row loads its history.
  • Ctrl-R resolves the entity again.
  • r refreshes the list.

Corrections are made in :entities: Enter on the entity, m marks a row, = (same) or ! (distinct) on another, then Ctrl-R to resolve — see The TUI.

docs.title: With joins and Search
docs.text:
• joins[] work on a resolution: entity too. They are read on top of the resolved customers: each row gets the lookup's value. A key that the lookup holds more than once leaves the joined column empty and lists those rows in _conflicts; it never picks one.
  • A SearchIndex finds a customer once it is resolved. A row still ambiguous, or with no rule, is not searchable yet.

docs.title: The manifest
Operating it
docs.text:
• LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_HMAC_SECRET is required: the hub does not start without it. deploy/selfhost/up.sh generates it; with Helm, set secrets.entityResolutionHmacSecret. Changing it forces a full re-resolve at the next lm entity resolve and breaks open view page links. Back it up with your other secrets.
  • After upgrading the hub, apply each resolution: entity again with the same manifest, then run lm entity resolve NAME.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• kind: Entity — fuse — match:, the _conflicts ledger, joins[]
