docs.title: Guided path — the guided path
docs.text:
Guided onboarding

From an empty machine to a running hub, a fused entity, scoped chat that cites its sources, and a workflow that flags what stopped moving — in three half-days.

Audience

An integrator or tester discovering lumnik — nothing assumed beyond Docker and a terminal.

Format

Three half-days. Every step gives a goal, the page to follow, and a checkpoint.

The spirit

Do the steps — don't just read them.

Before you start

Docker, a terminal, and Ollama for the steps marked Pro. Go 1.26+ only if you build lm yourself. The full list: Prerequisites.

The one rule

Run every command from the repository root unless a page says otherwise.

git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open

That repository is the open edition. A step marked Pro needs lumnik Pro with the AI on (the chat, lm ask, the models); on the open edition, read it and skip its checkpoint. See The two editions.

docs.title: The three half-days at a glance
docs.text:
Half-day 1 Defrost reading

Deploy the hub, meet lm, run the WOW, and prove that ingestion stayed read-only and lost nothing.

Six steps, ≈ 3 h

Half-day 2 Defrost reasoning

Understand entities, the ask guards, scopes, models, and the TUI an integrator operates from.

Six steps, 3 h

Half-day 3 Defrost time

Move from a mirror of the source to views, processes, workflows, inbox decisions, and the PWA.

Six steps, ≈ 3 h 15

docs.title: Half-day 1 — defrost reading
docs.text:
Goal of the day: legacy data flows into the hub, read-only, and you can prove nothing was lost.

1 10 min The pitch

Read the Home page: what lumnik is (a read-only defrost of legacy systems) and what it is not (not a migration, not a BI project).

You know it landed when: you can explain why lumnik is neither a migration nor a BI project.

2 30 min Deploy the hub

Decide what the hub carries — The two editions, Choosing what your hub offers. Then follow Deploy lumnik: ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build. Your passwords are in the .env it writes, at the root of the clone.

You know it worked when: the script ends like this:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)
  Keycloak:  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
  Next:      point lm at the hub — server http://localhost:8080, OIDC http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
3 20 min Meet lm

Follow the Quickstart: install lm, log in, put a first file into the hub.

You know it worked when: lm connector list shows the connector your first file registered.

$ lm connector list
NAME         TYPE      TENANT  SCHED  WINDOW  STATUS  LAST RUN
stock_count  csv-file  1
4 60–90 min The WOW

Run The WOW: a SOAP Siebel and a CSV fused into one Customer.

You know it worked when: lm entity get customer lists the fused customers. Pro: a question asked in French answers with the SQL it ran.

5 30 min How a connector is built

Read Connectors overview and CSV & files, the manifest you just used. Every source type follows the same grammar.

You know it landed when: you can explain the relationship between manifest, endpoint, and ingestion report.

6 20 min What was ingested, skipped, quarantined

Read Seeing what was ingested, skipped, and quarantined.

You know it worked when: on the WOW's cust-csv run, you read IN = OUT + SKIPPED. Every skipped row is counted; lm dlq list shows the ones set aside.

$ lm run get 3e9f353a
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
3e9f353a  cust-csv   default   Completed  8   8    0        0             2026-10-24 21:57  2026-10-24 21:57

docs.title: Half-day 2 — defrost reasoning
docs.text:
Goal of the day: the ingested data answers questions — sources shown, and only to the people entitled to ask.

1 40 min Fuse sources into one truth

Read Entities — fuse and read the Customer entity you applied during the WOW.

You know it worked when: you find the _conflicts ledger and can say why C-200 is in it.

$ lm entity get customer --filter customer_code=C-200
CUSTOMER_CODE  NAME   SEGMENT  EMAIL   CITY  _CONFLICTS
C-200          Marie  SILVER   m@x.fr  Lyon  {"name": [{"src": "cust_siebel", "value": "Marie"}, {"src": "t_cust_csv", "value": "MARIE A."}]}
2 30 min When Ask refuses · Pro

Read When Ask refuses: what lm ask says, and what to do.

You know it worked when: you can say what to do when lm ask answers « la question ne correspond pas au schéma déclaré ».

3 30 min Scopes

Read Scopes: a scope is declared on the connector or entity (scopes:) and granted as a Keycloak role scope:<tag>. No scope role = tenant-wide; one or more = bound.

The bundled realm has no scope-bound user: create one in Keycloak with the realm role scope:desk (Add a user, Grant a business scope).

To work as that second user, give lm a second context. Open the login link in a private browser window: a normal window signs you in as integrator again.

lm config set-context desk --server http://localhost:8080 \
    --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context desk
lm login

lm config use-context selfhost switches back to integrator.

You know it worked when: a user holding only scope:desk is refused the customer entity, whose scope is clients.

$ lm entity get customer          # as a user holding scope:desk
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted
4 20 min Models & providers · Pro

Read Models & providers: which model answers, and how to swap it (local Ollama or a remote provider).

You know it worked when: you know whether your install answers from Ollama or a remote provider.

5 40 min The integrator's cockpit

Skim the CLI & TUI reference, then open the TUI with lm ui: type :runs and Enter, pick a run with the arrow keys, press d to describe it. ? lists every key.

You know it worked when: you can find any connector run and its report using only the TUI.

6 20 min Who may do what

Read Roles & permissions and skim RLS & database roles.

You know it worked when: signed in as hubadmin (tenant 11, password HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env), you see none of tenant 1's decisions from the WOW.

Give lm a hubadmin context and sign in as in step 3 (private window), then:

$ lm inbox --all
ID  WHEN  PROCESS  MESSAGE  ENTITY_KEY

docs.title: Half-day 3 — defrost time and the apps
docs.text:
Goal of the day: the hub stops being a mirror and starts finding things — and each team gets an app.

1 30 min Views — see

Read Views and save the WOW's view: lm view apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml.

You know it worked when: lm view list lists it and a user holding scope:clients renders it.

$ lm view list
NAME          SCOPE    TITLE
clients-desk  clients  Clients
$ lm view clients-desk --filter city=Lyon
Clients · city=Lyon

Code client  Nom            Ville  Segment
C-200        Marie          Lyon   SILVER
C-500        Claire Martin  Lyon   
C-800        Albert Camus   Lyon   
C-900        Saint Exupery  Lyon
2 30 min Processes — react

Read Processes: declarative reactions to data.row.changed, always refusable, never writing to the source.

You know it landed when: you can say what emits the event and what may refuse the action.

3 45 min Workflows — declare the lifecycle

Read Workflows: a declared lifecycle over a status column, and a dormancy threshold that turns a document left unmoved into an alert.

You know it worked when: you replayed the WOW's step 9: lm workflow apply reports EN LITIGE as undeclared. Pro: scoped chat answers a lifecycle question from your declared graph.

4 20 min Inbox — decide

Read Inbox: where decision.* events (including decision.dormant.<workflow>) wait for a human, and lm inbox ack that closes them.

You know it worked when: an acked decision leaves lm inbox and shows [acked] in lm inbox --all.

5 30 min The PWA

Read The PWA, then:

  • open https://<your-host>/app/ — cards on a phone, a table on a tablet;
  • a phone cannot reach your laptop's localhost: put the TLS proxy in front first;
  • choose each app's tabs with one line of its manifest: spec.tabs.

You know it worked when: you see the same scope boundary on the phone and on the desktop.

6 40 min Run it for real

Read Backup & restore and Upgrade, and practise both before you need them.

You know it worked when: ./deploy/selfhost/backup.sh ends with ==> done: <folder> and you know where that folder is.

docs.title: If you get stuck
docs.text:
Common stumbles:

  • Wrong directory. Commands assume the repository root. When a relative path fails, check where you are before checking anything else.
  • The first minute is not an outage. Right after the stack starts, the hub can briefly answer 401 or refuse connections. Wait a minute and retry before diagnosing.
  • The ghost binary. After rebuilding lm, run lm version. If it prints an old build, your PATH serves a stale copy.
  • Credentials. Every password is generated at install time into .env, at the root of the clone. If a login page surprises you, the answer is in that file.
  • Ollama pulls one model at a time. One ollama pull <model> per line, and make sure ollama serve isn't already running before starting it again.

If a step does not match what you see, report it — it is a documentation bug.

docs.title: The reference shelf
docs.text:
Everything not on the walk above, for when you need it.

More source types — same manifest grammar as CSV: JDBC · REST · GraphQL · SOAP · Kafka inbound · Transform at ingestion

Integrations & API — HTTP API for ask · Admin API

Enterprise identity — Bring your own IdP · SCIM deprovisioning

Day-2 operations — Observability · Rate limits · Sizing & load tests

Deploying at scale — the cloud edition (commercial) ships a Kubernetes/Helm path; not part of this repository.

docs.title: How lumnik breathes — from frozen rows to decisions
docs.text: What happens when something changes in the source, and who is told.

docs.title: The moment this page is about
docs.text: A commande slips into EN LITIGE in the 02:00 batch. The row lands, a declared rule turns it into a decision seconds later, and your webhook pings the team's phone at 02:01 — before the client calls at 9:04.

docs.title: The chain, end to end
docs.text:
The chain in one picture:

flowchart LR
  erp[("legacy source")] -->|"your ingestion cron"| row["a new row lands<br/>(mirror table)"]
  row -->|"same transaction"| ev["an event —<br/>new rows only"]
  ev -->|"≤ 5 s"| proc["your declared rule<br/>when: statut=EN LITIGE"]
  proc --> dec["decision.litige"]
  dec --> inbox["Inbox tab<br/>lm inbox"]
  dec -->|"≤ 5 s, retried"| hook["your webhook →<br/>the tool that pings phones"]
  sweep["dormancy sweep<br/>every 15 min"] -->|"a document that STOPPED moving"| dec2["decision.dormant.*"]
  dec2 --> inbox
  dec2 --> hook
  inbox -->|"✓ Acknowledge"| ack["acked — an event,<br/>timestamped, with who"]
  • Only new rows emit. A re-ingested, unchanged row emits nothing. A table emits only once a rule, a webhook or a notification subscribes to it.
  • jdbc, CSV and kafka connectors emit. Tables ingested over REST, GraphQL or SOAP emit no event: a rule on them never fires.
  • Every rule emits decision.<your-name> — the prefix is enforced at apply.
Clock Value rule, webhook and email consumers every 5 s webhook retry sweep every 30 s, 3 attempts in total; journal in lm outputs list dormancy sweep every 15 min your ingestion the connector's own spec.schedule — the slow clock

docs.title: Where a human meets it — the channels
docs.text:
Channel What it does Mode Inbox tab (PWA, phone & desktop) the pile, newest first, badge on open; a treated decision stays visible, dimmed ✓ acknowledged pull — it waits for you to open it lm inbox / TUI inbox page the same pile for keyboard people (untreated only, by default) same pull Your webhook (n8n, Make, your own endpoint) every subscribed event, in seconds, retried, journaled, replayable — the road to a Teams message or an SMS push. lm integration add; forwards from registration onward, never retroactively Email (lm notify add) one mail per matching event, payload included live once the deploy sets the SMTP knobs (Email notifications); a failed send is not retried

The inbox is per scope, not per person. Everyone holding a scope sees all of its decisions; a user with no scope:* role sees every decision. There is no assignment, escalation or out-of-office.

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN   PROCESS             MESSAGE                             ENTITY_KEY
8   10min  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon  ff1027320a1acbe2646ce1b2d1e4a42111868a75bb30825dc4609d785e6aaa7f
$ lm inbox ack 8
acked.
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN  PROCESS  MESSAGE  ENTITY_KEY

docs.title: The gesture: what ✓ Acknowledge is, and is not
docs.text:
• It clears the decision from everyone's untreated pile and shows who took it.
  • It is an event — annotation.decision.acked, timestamped, with who — that a webhook can forward.
  • It never writes to your source system (Reversibility): the correction itself is made in the legacy screen.

docs.title: Silence also emits
docs.text:
Rules catch what happens. The dormancy sweep catches what stopped happening: a declared workflow watches every document, and one that sits non-terminal past its threshold becomes decision.dormant.<workflow>.

  • The threshold counts from lumnik's first observation of the document, not from the source's history.
  • lm workflow apply names every status value your manifest missed, with its row count. An undeclared status is watched too.
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW            WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
commande-lifecycle  7        5        900

MEDIAN_DETECTION_S is the median time, in seconds, from a document's observed last move to its alert.

docs.title: What remains, three months later
docs.text:
Events — decisions and acks — are kept 30 days by default (LUMNIK_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS). Three things outlive that window:

What Where to look the observation tape: every watched document — first seen, in its state since, alerted when lm observations list (--workflow NAME for one); per workflow: lm observations stats your webhook target: forward decision.* and annotation.* to the tool that keeps your proof your tool, on your retention the ingested tables themselves lm entity get, lm view

Wire the webhook on day one

It forwards from registration onward, never retroactively. If an auditor may ask "prove this alert was handled", register it the day you deploy.

docs.title: Named limits, in one place
docs.text:
• No push to user surfaces — the tab and the CLI are pull; the webhook is the road to tools that push. (An event stream does exist for integrators, on the platform API.)
  • The inbox is per scope, time-ordered, without assignment or severity.
  • ✓ Acknowledge never writes to the source.
  • Webhooks forward from registration onward, never retroactively.
  • REST/GraphQL/SOAP-ingested tables emit no events — only jdbc, CSV and kafka ingestion does.
  • Declared status aliases (encours/EC…) serve the dormancy watch and the chat's background knowledge, not the chat's SQL or view filters: those match the literal values in the column.
  • Email is best-effort — a failed send is logged and skipped: no retry, no journal. Delivery stays mocked until the deploy sets the SMTP knobs. Webhooks retry and journal.
  • No usage/adoption dashboard — operational metrics (/q/metrics) are the only proxy, per endpoint, if your ops scrape them.

docs.text: Outputs — the roads out — the wiring manual for every channel on this page · Processes — react · Inbox — decide · Workflows — declare · The PWA · The WOW, step by step — Act 2 runs this whole chain on the demo dataset, EN LITIGE included.

docs.title: Reversibility & exit
docs.text: If you stop using lumnik in two years, what do you get back, in what format — and what was never at risk in the first place?

docs.title: What was never at risk
docs.text:
Your source system. Stopping lumnik changes nothing in it:

  • databases — the connection account needs SELECT only, and there is no write path back (Architecture → Read-only first);
  • file sources — a CSV connector's after_process: move|archive|delete moves or deletes files on the drop zone you declared, nothing else (CSV & files).

No vendor copy to reclaim. Self-hosted, the data never left your infrastructure; the exit below runs on your own machines.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
Asset Format How you take it The ingested mirror Plain PostgreSQL 16 tables in schema connector — ordinary columns, no application-layer encryption (what is and isn't encrypted) Any PostgreSQL client, or the dump below Fused entities SQL views over those tables (connector.v_*) Query the views, or lm entity export NAME -o FILE (CSV) while the hub runs The whole database A standard pg_dump -Fc — the same artifact the backup script produces (nightly once you install the documented cron; nothing schedules it for you) pg_restore into any PostgreSQL 16+ with the pgvector extension available (the rag schema needs it — or exclude that schema on restore), with or without lumnik Your configuration The YAML manifests In your repository for the files you applied; everything else is in the dump, and fetchable as YAML while the hub runs — see below The RAG corpus rag.chunk rows: chunk text in clear + pgvector embeddings The text is portable; see the embeddings caveat below

Fetch the configuration back as YAML while the hub runs:

Kind Command Connector lm connector get NAME — its stored definition, in the hub's own field names Entity no lm command returns the manifest; it is in the dump View lm view get NAME -o FILE Workflow lm workflow get NAME App lm app get NAME Export lm export get NAME Process no lm process get — the TUI's :processes, e on the row, opens the stored manifest SearchIndex no lm command returns the manifest; it is in the dump 
$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o customers.csv
AcmeCustomer: 1099 bytes written to customers.csv (sha256 afa5c455ceaf9a2c6e0fae54b2fbc9b671893f22220c2c2c6a685969c0deceb5)

User accounts and the audit journal are in the same database, so the same dump carries them. Ask/chat history is not stored server-side (the trace is in each response). The exit artifact is the backup you already take.

docs.title: Two caveats to plan around
docs.text:
• Stored secrets die with the master key. Connector/webhook credentials and tenant secrets are pgcrypto-encrypted under LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY / LUMNIK_CRYPTO_SECRET_KEY; individual secrets can be re-entered (rotated) at any time, but the master keys have no rotation or re-encryption tooling, and a lost key makes the stored values unrecoverable (the warning). For an exit this is usually irrelevant — the credentials point at your systems and you hold the originals — but export anything you'd miss before decommissioning.
  • Embeddings are model-bound. The vectors in rag.chunk only mean something to the embedding model that produced them (Models). Treat the chunk text as the portable asset; a future system re-embeds it with its own model.

docs.title: What leaving looks like, concretely
docs.text:
1. ./deploy/selfhost/backup.sh one last time — lumnik.dump is your data, complete.
  2. Keep the manifests you version in git where they live; guided-flow config is in the dump (or fetch it back as YAML while the hub still runs).

  3. Restore the dump wherever your next tool reads PostgreSQL, or keep it as the archived record of what the mirror held. Without lumnik's database roles there, skip them:

    pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges -d <your-database> lumnik.dump
    4. Decommission the stack. Your source system never noticed lumnik arriving; it will not notice it leaving.

docs.title: Where lumnik stands
docs.text:
beta. Nobody outside the lumnik team has run lumnik in production yet.

What each release adds: the release notes.

docs.title: What is deliberately not there
docs.text:
Each line is a decision, declared on the page of its surface and gathered here.

Surface What is not there Declared in GraphQL mutations, subscriptions, schema-introspection discovery, persisted queries, query batching, per-endpoint header overrides, on_error: warn GraphQL — Not yet supported REST mode: api_cursor — declaring it behaves like full; per-endpoint headers, which belong at spec.headers REST SOAP SOAP 1.1 envelopes only — a service that requires SOAP 1.2 (application/soap+xml) is refused SOAP Kafka (Pro) JSON only — no Avro, Protobuf or Schema Registry; one topic per connector, no filtering by key or header; no mapping block, so no hooks at ingestion; no pre-flight test; SASL/SCRAM, mTLS and OAuth Kafka — Limitations Transformers validate-row after split-row, and aggregator on a csv-file run — both refused at lm apply, with the arithmetic reason Transformers Events REST-, GraphQL- and SOAP-ingested tables are event-silent — the respiration rides jdbc, CSV and kafka ingestion How lumnik breathes Chat declared status aliases feed the dormancy watch and the chat's background knowledge, not the chat's SQL or a view's filters — the chat matches the literal values in the column How lumnik breathes Workflows the transition journal's retention is unbounded, and the dormancy sweep costs the database a full pass over the source table every tick Workflows Exports CSV only, one entity per export, mode: snapshot only (no delta, no resume); SFTP and S3 only; four formatters, a row filter with equals/in only; no back-fill of missed slots, no automatic retry Exports — Not in this version Search a row deleted straight from an ingested table — or by lm endpoint purge on a connector-schema hybrid target — stays searchable until the index is rebuilt SearchIndex — Rows deleted directly in the database SCIM (Pro) no /Groups; no bulk, sorting, etags or changePassword; no pagination beyond the two eq filters; not the full PATCH path grammar; no /Schemas or /ResourceTypes SCIM — Not supported Identity SAML-only IdPs are not supported by direct trust — front them with a broker and point lumnik at the broker Bring your own IdP Encryption rotating the master key. Rotating one secret's value is supported, and stamps rotated_at RLS and encryption

Kafka and SCIM are in the Pro build only: see The two editions.

docs.title: What is not finished
docs.text: Nothing known today. A defect found from here on is listed here until it is fixed.

docs.title: When beta goes away
docs.text: When someone outside the lumnik team has run lumnik in production, with this list still empty. To be that first outside run, start with the guided path.

docs.text:

  • Guided path — the three half-days
