docs.title: Proposal dossiers
docs.text: A business person describes a problem on lumnik.fr and downloads a proposal dossier. You draft the workflow from it, then check the dossier against your data.

docs.title: Check a dossier against your data
docs.text:
Ask the hub what it can establish on your data, against a workflow you already applied. No lm command does this: call the hub over HTTP.

curl -X POST "$HUB/api/proposal/check?workflow=<name>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --data-binary @dossier.md > dossier-checked.md

It needs lm_integrator. Mint $TOKEN as in Test the API. The answer is the same file, checked; nothing is applied, and the original answers are untouched. Without workflow=, the dossier is only recomputed.

Point Confirmed when Refuted when a status column exists the comparison read the column the table is there and the column is not an identifier column exists the table has the spec.on.key column the table is there and does not have it (judged only if the status column exists) the target is accepted by the watch validation the workflow is stored never
  • What only a person can establish (the column describes the lifecycle, the identifier is stable) stays to be established.
  • A table not ingested yet, a timeout or a missing grant leave a point unchanged.
  • The proof is about your data today.
  • A dossier for another catalogue version is returned recomputed, unverified.
  • A malformed dossier is a 400 with the reason (duplicate-key); a file that is not UTF-8 is a 400 malformed-header.

docs.title: Draft a workflow from a dossier
docs.text:
lm proposal draft writes the start of the manifest a dossier proposes. It does not contact the hub:

lm proposal draft dossier.md \
  --name orders-lifecycle --scope sales \
  --table connector.t_commandes --column statut --key n_commande --after 14d \
  -o orders-lifecycle.yaml
  • Every flag is optional; a value you leave out is left out of the file, with a comment saying where it goes.
  • States and transitions are never generated: you write them before lm workflow apply.
  • --after without --key is accepted here and refused at apply.
  • The header comments list each point, refuted first, then missing, unverified, confirmed; what no tool can check is marked to establish yourself.
  • -o never overwrites a file; without it the draft goes to stdout. The dossier can come from stdin (lm proposal draft -).
  • A dossier with no stalled-documents@1 lead, or two, is refused; other leads are named on stderr.

The loop: draft → complete and lm workflow apply -f → check the dossier against the stored workflow (the curl above) → draft again from the checked dossier, to a new file.

docs.title: The PWA — your data in your pocket
docs.text: The hub rendered on a phone. /app/ is served by the hub itself: no app store, no build step. It installs from the browser like any PWA. One hub can serve several teams; ?m= selects the app. The demo app uses French labels, but the app definition is language-neutral.

docs.title: Declare a business app
docs.text:
A business app is a kind: App manifest: a title, a scope, an icon. The demo desk's:

# 20-desk.yaml — the demo desk as a business app: Clients ACME, for anyone holding scope:desk.
# Open it at /app/?m=desk once the desk's views are applied.
kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: desk
spec:
  title: Clients ACME
  scope: desk
  icon: clients
  default: true

$ lm app apply -f docs/apps/demo/apps/20-desk.yaml
Applied app "desk" → scope desk
  default app — "clients" is no longer the default
$ lm app list
NAME     TITLE         SCOPE    ICON     ACCENT   BACKGROUND  DEFAULT  TABS
clients  Clients       clients  clients  #8b7ff0  #14121f              (all)
desk     Clients ACME  desk     clients  #8b7ff0  #14121f     yes      (all)
stock    Stock         stock    stock    #8b7ff0  #14121f              (all)

Then two more gestures, or the app opens empty:

  1. Apply the views that the app reads: lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml (Views).
  2. Grant the users the scope:desk role in Keycloak (Tenants, users & scopes).

The PWA reads the apps at every login: no rebuild, no redeploy.

Field Says icon one of clients, stock, generic, event, alert, contract. No upload. theme accentColor and backgroundColor, both optional. The accent is checked for contrast: it is also the chat bubble's background. default the app an address without ?m= opens. At most one. To move it, apply another app with default: true. tabs which tabs, in which order. Absent: every tab the hub offers. Choosing the tabs.
  • Change an app: lm app get desk > desk.yaml, edit, lm app apply -f desk.yaml.
  • Remove it: lm app rm desk.

docs.title: Open it on a phone
docs.text:
https://<your-host>/app/            # the app declared default: true
https://<your-host>/app/?m=desk     # the desk app

A phone installs a PWA only from an https address. The self-host stack has a TLS proxy for that; on a LAN address, the phone must trust its certificate first (how).

  1. Open https://<host>/app/?m=desk and sign in.
  2. iOS Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen. Android Chrome: the install prompt, or ⋮ → Add to Home screen.
  3. The icon and name are the app's own. Each app is its own home-screen icon.

For a fleet of phones, push the proxy's certificate and the app's address through your MDM.

An unknown ?m=, or an app of a scope the user does not hold:

docs.title: What the business user sees
docs.text: The screens below are the desk app on a phone, against the demo desk.

docs.title: Records — the saved views
docs.text:
• One view for the app's scope: it opens directly. Several: a picker. None: an amber message asking for one.
  • A view opens on its first 50 rows. Next › and ‹ Previous move a page.
  • Filters are built, not typed: a column, an operator, a value. A text column offers contains and =; a number or a date also offers < and >; declared values use a list. Each filter is a chip; tap it to remove it.
  • Tap a row: its record opens, ending with its conflicts and ambiguities — here, the city of P-1008: Lyon in the ERP, Villeurbanne in the CRM.
  • The data age is the time since the last run that fed the scope.

docs.title: Inbox — decisions
docs.text:
• Newest first. ✓ Acknowledge is the same ack as lm inbox ack. Acknowledged decisions are dimmed.
  • The badge on the tab counts the open decisions.
  • It shows decisions from every scope the user holds, not only the open app's scope (who sees which decision).

docs.title: Chat — ask your data (Pro)
docs.text:
• The same guarded ask as lm ask, bound to the app's scope. The SQL is folded under the answer.
  • When the answer filters on a disputed value, an amber block names the record and the value used.
  • A follow-up such as And in Paris? continues the previous question. lumnik shows the full question it answered; read it before trusting the figure.
  • The context chip shows the question that the next message continues. Tap it to ask on its own. New conversation clears the thread. A reload forgets it; nothing is stored.
  • A phrase such as the second one points at a result row that lumnik does not keep. The chat asks for an explicit value instead.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Present on a hub with Search, for a user who may read an index. A word or two, then Search: ranked results, matched words highlighted.

  • It searches only the app's scope.
  • Counted values (a city, a segment) appear as chips: tap one to narrow.
  • A result opens its record, read-only, with each source's value where they disagree.

docs.title: Choosing the tabs
docs.text:
Tab Shown Records always Inbox always Chat on lumnik Pro, AI on Search on a hub with Search, for a user who may read an index

To show fewer, or reorder them, list them in the app's manifest:

spec:
  tabs: [fiches, inbox]
  • The manifest names are fiches, inbox, chat, and search.
  • The app opens on the first tab of the list that the hub has.

  • A tab the hub does not have is accepted, with a warning. It appears the day the hub has it, so the same manifest works on Open and on Pro:

    $ lm app apply -f desk-app.yaml
Applied app "desk" → scope desk
  tabs: fiches, inbox, search
! desk-app.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.tabs[2]
          tab 'search' is not offered by this hub; the declaration is kept and takes effect when a module offering it is active
          → offered here: [fiches, inbox]

  • Hiding a tab locks nothing: who may read what is still decided by roles and scopes.

  • What a hub offers in the first place: Choosing what your hub offers.

docs.title: Enabling Search for an app
docs.text:
1. A Search provider in the hub (choosing a provider).
  2. Entities carrying the app's scope.
  3. A search index over them: lm search apply -f index.yaml (declare one). The hub builds it within a minute.
  4. The tab in the app's list, if the app lists its tabs: add search.

lm search status shows whether each index is built and fresh.

docs.title: On a tablet, on a display
docs.text: Width Records Navigation Record phone cards bottom tabs bottom sheet tablet (≥ 640 px) table bottom tabs bottom sheet display (≥ 900 px) table left rail side panel

docs.title: Sign-in, offline
docs.text:
• Users sign in with their Keycloak account. Closing the tab ends the session.
  • A refused scope shows the amber refusal, never a broken screen.
  • Your own IdP: its client for the app needs the audience lumnik-backend (Bring your own IdP).
  • Offline, the app reports that data will return with the network and offers Retry. It never shows stale rows: only the app shell is kept on the phone.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• kind: View — the lists the Records tab shows.
  • Inbox — the decisions behind the Inbox tab.
  • Scopes — the boundary the whole app lives within.

docs.title: kind: View — see
docs.text:
The first rung of the app ladder: a declarative, read-only list over a scope's table, rendered by the hub and displayed by lm, the TUI or the PWA. One YAML says which columns; a filter it cannot apply is refused instead of showing an empty table.

Kind View — apps.lumnik.io/v1 Over any table of a scope's card: a raw connector.t_*, or a fused connector.v_* Renders lm view -f FILE or lm view NAME (list, filters, one record's detail); the TUI's :view; the PWA's Records tab Store lm view apply / lm view rm — lm_integrator, scope-bound; reads lm_user Bounds 1 000 rows and a 5-second statement timeout per read, read-only, tenant-isolated; when more rows match, lm view ends with first 1000 rows shown; more match — narrow with --filter (-o json: "truncated": true) Edition Open

A view is a title, a table and the columns worth looking at. Over an entity it uses the entity's labels, and a record's detail ends with the sources' disagreements on it. The file is the app — hand-written, or drafted by the AI.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Over a raw table or a fused entity. A freshly landed export is viewable as it is; an entity's view carries its labels and its _conflicts ledger.
  • A filter grammar that refuses. An unknown column, a column the view does not show, a malformed filter or a value outside a declared domain is refused.
  • One record's detail, disagreements included. lm view KEY prints a record and, under Ambiguïtés et divergences, which source said what.
  • A store the PWA discovers. lm view apply publishes a manifest; anyone holding the scope finds it on their phone.
  • Drafted by the AI, gated like a render. The model picks table, columns and filters; the hub validates them and writes the YAML.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the demo desk that ships with the repo

Land the three sources as The demo desk shows, then apply the customer entity: lm entity apply -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml.

# 10-customers.yaml — the desk's customer list, over the fused entity.
#
# Column headers are the labels the entity manifest declares; the detail of one record ends
# with its _conflicts ledger when the sources conflict on it.
#
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter city=Lyon
#   lm view P-1000 -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
kind: View
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: acme-customers
spec:
  scope: desk
  table: connector.v_acmecustomer
  title: Clients ACME
  columns: [code, name, city, segment, credit_limit]

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
Clients ACME

Code client  Raison sociale             Ville      Segment  Encours autorisé
P-1000       Hydraulique Lyon 1000      Lyon       GOLD     500
P-1001       Roulements Bruxelles 1001  Bruxelles  SILVER   637
P-1002       Fixations Milano 1002      Milano     BRONZE   774
P-1003       Pneumatique Porto 1003     Porto      GOLD     911
P-1004       Étanchéité Kraków 1004     Kraków     SILVER   1048
P-1005       Transmission Aarhus 1005   Aarhus     GOLD     1185
P-1006       Outillage Valencia 1006    Valencia   BRONZE   1322
P-1007       Levage Bristol 1007        Bristol    SILVER   1459
P-1008       Filtration Lyon 1008       Lyon       GOLD     1596
P-1009       Soudure Bruxelles 1009     Bruxelles  BRONZE   1733
P-1010       Hydraulique Milano 1010    Milano     SILVER   1870
P-1011       Roulements Porto 1011      Porto               2007
P-1012       Levage Aarhus 1012         Aarhus              
P-1013       Filtration Valencia 1013   Valencia

The headers are the entity's labels. Fourteen rows, ordered by the first declared column. Narrow it — filters are repeatable and ANDed, and the title lists them:

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter segment=GOLD --filter 'credit_limit>1000'
Clients ACME · segment=GOLD · credit_limit>1000

Code client  Raison sociale            Ville   Segment  Encours autorisé
P-1005       Transmission Aarhus 1005  Aarhus  GOLD     1185
P-1008       Filtration Lyon 1008      Lyon    GOLD     1596

One record — the first declared column is the key:

$ lm view P-1008 -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
Clients ACME / P-1008

  Code client        P-1008
  Raison sociale     Filtration Lyon 1008
  Ville              Lyon
  Segment            GOLD
  Encours autorisé   1596

  (!) Ambiguïtés et divergences
  Ville   t_acme_desk_erp «Lyon» · t_acme_desk_crm «Villeurbanne»

Ambiguïtés et divergences is the entity's _conflicts ledger for that record: the ERP (listed first) won with Lyon, and the CRM's Villeurbanne is kept. A record both sources agree on:

$ lm view P-1005 -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
Clients ACME / P-1005

  Code client        P-1005
  Raison sociale     Transmission Aarhus 1005
  Ville              Aarhus
  Segment            GOLD
  Encours autorisé   1185

  ✓ aucune ambiguïté ni divergence

docs.title: The manifest
Linking views
docs.text:
A cell can lead somewhere: to another view, or to a page of your ERP. Declare it on the view the user starts from:

# 40-customers-links.yaml — the desk's customers, with two cells that lead somewhere.
#
# Tap a customer's name: the orders view opens, already filtered on that customer.
# Tap a customer's code: the customer's page in the ERP opens in a new tab.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: View
metadata:
  name: acme-customers-linked
spec:
  scope: desk
  table: connector.v_acmecustomer
  title: Clients ACME — liens
  columns: [code, name, city, segment]
  links:
    - column: name
      targetView: acme-orders
      filters:
        code: "{code}"
    - column: code
      url: "https://erp.example.com/customers/{code}"
  • Tap a name: the acme-orders view opens, already filtered on that customer. The filter shows in the filter bar, and removes like one the user typed.
  • Tap a code: https://erp.example.com/customers/P-1008 opens in a new tab.
  • {code} is the value of that column on the row tapped. It must be one of the view's columns.

What the tap on Filtration Lyon 1008 opens is this list:

$ lm view acme-orders --filter code=P-1008
Commandes · code=P-1008

order_no   code    status     amount   ordered_on
SO-000006  P-1008  EN LITIGE  4100.00  2026-08-07

Apply the target first, or later. A link to a view that does not exist yet is kept, with a warning. It works once the target is applied:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/40-customers-links.yaml
applied: acme-customers-linked (scope desk)
! 40-customers-links.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.links[0].targetView
          targetView 'acme-orders' is not a view of scope 'desk' (yet); the declaration is kept, and following the link is refused until that view is applied

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml
applied: acme-orders (scope desk)
  • One destination per link: targetView with at least one filter, or url.
  • The target must be a view of the same scope. If it refuses the filter, the user stays where they are and reads why.
  • An external link is https:// only. The other system receives the value: link only to systems you trust with it.
  • Limits: one link per column, 16 links, 8 filters per link.

The same rules apply to a search result's link to your ERP.

docs.title: A view over a raw table
docs.text:
No entity is needed: a view can point straight at a raw table the scope's connectors land — here the order book, as the ERP exported it:

# 20-orders.yaml — a view straight over a raw ingest table, no entity needed.
#
# A scope's card lists the raw tables as well as the fused views, so a freshly landed export
# is viewable as it is. The status column is shown exactly as the ERP spells it.
#
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'status~litige'
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'amount>1000'
kind: View
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: acme-orders
spec:
  scope: desk
  table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
  title: Commandes
  columns: [order_no, code, status, amount, ordered_on]

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'status~litige'
Commandes · status~litige

order_no   code    status     amount   ordered_on
SO-000006  P-1008  EN LITIGE  4100.00  2026-08-07
SO-000010  P-1004  EN LITIGE  77.00    2026-08-12

The headers are the raw column names, because nothing declared a label. A kind: Workflow is what declares what the status values mean.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
lm view -f FILE                                # the list, from a manifest file
lm view -f FILE --filter city=Lyon             # filtered; repeatable, ANDed
lm view KEY -f FILE                            # one record — KEY matches the first declared column
lm view NAME [KEY]                             # the same, from a view saved in the store

A saved view renders without a file:

$ lm view acme-customers --filter segment=GOLD
Clients ACME · segment=GOLD

Code client  Raison sociale            Ville   Segment  Encours autorisé
P-1000       Hydraulique Lyon 1000     Lyon    GOLD     500
P-1003       Pneumatique Porto 1003    Porto   GOLD     911
P-1005       Transmission Aarhus 1005  Aarhus  GOLD     1185
P-1008       Filtration Lyon 1008      Lyon    GOLD     1596

Rendering needs lm_user and stays inside the business-scope boundary: a view whose spec.scope you do not hold answers Error: access refused (403): scope not granted.

  • Rows are sorted by the first declared column.
  • lm view shows at most 1 000 rows. Past that it says first 1000 rows shown; more match — narrow with --filter.
  • A render that takes more than 5 seconds is refused, and says so. Narrow it with filters.
  • The PWA reads a view 50 rows at a time.

In the TUI, :view opens the same file interactively:

Key Action f add a filter F clear the filters r re-render Enter one record's detail o open another manifest g generate a manifest from a sentence a apply the rendered view to the store

docs.title: Filter grammar
docs.text:
Form Meaning col=value exact match; a date against a date or timestamp column is equal as an instant (due=2026-07-01 is midnight UTC); a number against a number column by value (amount=1500.00 finds 1500); on a column with declared values, an out-of-domain value is refused col~text substring, case-insensitive col>v col<v col>=v col<=v ordering — v must be a number or an ISO-8601 date; a row whose value has neither shape is not matched

The ordering forms work on the text columns a CSV or a fusion produces — credit_limit>1000 above, and on the order book:

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'ordered_on>2026-08-10'
Commandes · ordered_on>2026-08-10

order_no   code    status     amount   ordered_on
SO-000009  P-1010             120.00   2026-08-11
SO-000010  P-1004  EN LITIGE  77.00    2026-08-12
SO-000011  P-1006  BROUILLON  3000.00  2026-08-12
SO-000012  P-1011  En cours   55.00    2026-08-13
Filter details
  • Ordering works on numbers and dates, and on text that holds them. money, time, interval, boolean and uuid columns refuse it, naming the column: use = or ~.
  • A date without an offset is read as UTC: ordered_on>2026-08-10 starts at midnight UTC. A process reads a date the same way.

docs.title: Refusal rules
docs.text:
Each refusal names the fix:

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/60-refused-unknown-column.yaml
Error: API error 400: column 'phone' is not in the 'desk' schema for table connector.v_acmecustomer — fix the column name or add it to the scope's entity
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter email~example
Error: API error 400: cannot filter on 'email' — the view does not show it; declare it in spec.columns to filter on it
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter 'city~'
Error: API error 400: filter 'city~' needs a column and a value — col=value, col~text, or col>value
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter segment=PLATINUM
Error: API error 400: 'PLATINUM' is not an allowed value for segment (allowed: GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter "city='Lyon'"
Error: API error 400: filter value 'Lyon' is quoted; a value here is a bare literal, so the quotes would be compared to city too — write city=Lyon

A zero-row result is then meaningful: the filter is valid and matches nothing.

docs.title: The saved-view store
docs.text:
A manifest can also live in the hub, where the PWA at /app/ finds it under its scope:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
applied: acme-customers (scope desk)
$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml
applied: acme-orders (scope desk)
$ lm view list
NAME            SCOPE  TITLE
acme-customers  desk   Clients ACME
acme-orders     desk   Commandes
$ lm view get acme-customers -o acme.yaml
manifest written to acme.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f acme.yaml

lm view get NAME without -o prints the stored YAML, comments included, byte for byte.

Command Effect Role lm view apply -f FILE validate-then-upsert: a view that cannot render is never saved; re-applying a name overwrites lm_integrator lm view list [--scope TAG] NAME · SCOPE · TITLE — a scope-bound user sees only the granted scopes' views lm_user lm view get NAME [-o FILE] the manifest YAML verbatim lm_user lm view rm NAME removes the view for good, no prompt lm_integrator 
$ lm view rm acme-orders
view acme-orders deleted
$ lm view rm acme-orders
Error: API error 404: no saved view named 'acme-orders'
  • There is no disable: a saved view is live from apply until rm.
  • apply and rm are scope-bound: a scope-bound integrator cannot publish or remove a view outside their grants.
  • Every apply and removal is recorded in the audit trail.
  • A saved view is visible to every tenant of the hub. Each one sees only its own rows.

A user holding only scope:stock sees nothing of the desk:

$ lm view list
NAME  SCOPE  TITLE
$ lm view list --scope desk
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted

The stored name must be a URL-safe slug, and four names are reserved:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/62-refused-reserved-name.yaml
Error: API error 400: metadata.name must be a URL-safe slug ([a-z0-9_-], starting with a letter or digit) and not one of [detail, render, apply, generate]

docs.title: Generate a view with the AI
docs.text:
Describe the need; the hub's model selects the table, the columns and the filters, the hub validates them like a render, and writes the YAML. The manifest is yours to review and keep.

$ lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
manifest written to lyon.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f lyon.yaml
$ cat lyon.yaml
# asked for: les clients de Lyon
# kept: city=Lyon — a condition of that description not listed here is NOT enforced
# lm view -f lyon.yaml --filter 'city=Lyon'
apiVersion: "apps.lumnik.io/v1"
kind: "View"
metadata:
  name: "clients_of_lyon"
spec:
  scope: "desk"
  table: "connector.v_acmecustomer"
  title: "Clients of Lyon"
  columns:
  - "code"
  - "name"
  - "city"
  - "segment"
  - "credit_limit"
Header line Tells you # asked for: your sentence, on one line # kept: the filters the view enforces — anything else in your sentence is not enforced # lm view -f … a ready-to-run render of your -o file

Within generate, -o is the output file, not the output format.

  • Generation is rate-limited per tenant: lumnik.ratelimit.view-generate.rpm, default 10 per minute; past it, lm prints rate limited (429): rate limit exceeded, retry in Ns.

docs.title: Generation contract
docs.text:
Case Answer The scope cannot serve the description ("les commandes" over a scope with no orders) the model abstains; you get its reason, never invented columns No card for the scope no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first No chat model on the hub generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one

Nothing checks that the model kept everything you asked for — read the # kept: line:

$ lm view generate desk "les commandes en litige de plus de 500 euros" -o litiges.yaml
manifest written to litiges.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f litiges.yaml
$ head -3 litiges.yaml
# asked for: les commandes en litige de plus de 500 euros
# kept: amount>500 — a condition of that description not listed here is NOT enforced
# lm view -f litiges.yaml --filter 'amount>500'

Two conditions asked, one kept: en litige was dropped. Add the filter by hand, or rephrase.

"Run discovery first": lm source rediscover --scope <tag> rebuilds the schema card (needs lm_integrator and lm_admin, and a scope you hold). lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what the card holds.

docs.title: Show one team a filtered list on their phone
docs.text:
lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml

Result: anyone holding scope:desk finds Clients ACME under the Records tab of the PWA at /app/. On the phone, a text column offers contient and =; ordering (>, <) needs a column typed at the source (parse-number, parse-date).

docs.title: Let the AI draft a view, then check it before anyone else sees it
docs.text:
lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
cat lyon.yaml                                             # review it — the third line is the suggested render
lm view -f lyon.yaml --filter city=Lyon                   # test it yourself
lm view apply -f lyon.yaml                                # only once it looks right

Result: only apply writes to the store. Nobody else sees the draft before that.

docs.title: Look at an export before any entity exists
docs.text: Point spec.table at the raw connector.t_* table — 20-orders.yaml above. Result: the export's own columns, unlabelled, filterable the same way.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture apply refused: unknown key(s) in the manifest: … a misspelled field (titel:) the message lists what kind:View honors — fix the spelling render or apply refused: column is not in the '…' schema for table … spec.columns names a column the scope's card does not have fix the column name, or add it to the scope's entity render refused: column '…' is not in … — the entity changed since this view was written the entity lost that column, but the scope's card still lists it: in another tenant than the one that applied, for the moment it takes to rebuild the card; for good, if that rebuild failed (the hub log says so) drop the column from spec.columns, or put it back in the entity; lm source rediscover --scope <tag> refreshes the card filter refused: cannot filter on '…' — the view does not show it filtering on a column not listed in spec.columns add the column to spec.columns filter refused: '…' is not an allowed value for … the entity declares a values domain for that column one of the listed values — or fix the domain in the entity filter refused: '…' is not a number or ISO date — > needs an ordered value an ordering filter with a value that is neither a number, or YYYY-MM-DD apply answers with a warning on spec.links[…].targetView the target view is not applied yet in that scope apply the target; the link then works apply refused: spec.links[…].url: an external link is https://… http:, a relative address, or a host that is not written out write the full https://host/path/{column} following a link answers Lien refusé : … the target refused the filter fix the filter in links[].filters, or the target's columns 403 … scope not granted you do not hold the spec.scope role ask for that scope: role apply refused: metadata.name must be a URL-safe slug … the name is not a lowercase slug, or is apply/render/detail/generate rename metadata.name rate limited (429): rate limit exceeded, retry in Ns on generate over 10 lm view generate calls per minute for the tenant wait the seconds it names, then retry 404 … no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first discovery has never run for that scope lm source rediscover --scope <tag> (lm_integrator + lm_admin) generation abstained: … / generation failed: … the card cannot serve the description, the selection failed twice, or the hub has no chat model rephrase, or write the filter by hand; lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what the card has the title reads like a table name no spec.title, and the entity declares no label: set spec.title, or give the entity a label: a list stops at exactly 1 000 rows the render cap narrow it with filters API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server you lack the role: lm_integrator for apply and rm, lm_user for the rest ask your administrator; no lm command lists your roles (GET /api/bff/v1/me returns them under roles)

docs.title: kind: Workflow — declare
docs.text:
The fourth rung: a declarative document lifecycle over a status column ingestion already landed — states, aliases for the spellings the source really uses, the transition graph, and a threshold past which a document that has not moved is a decision.

Kind Workflow — apps.lumnik.io/v1 Over one column of one table: a raw connector.t_*, or a fused connector.v_* (dormancy there needs spec.on.order) Declares states with aliases, transitions, provenance: declared; optionally a business key and a dormancy threshold Produces a report at apply on what the data holds, and after each import when asked (workflow.undeclared.<name>); answers in the chat (Pro); decision.dormant.<name> and decision.overdue.<name> alerts, and an observation tape, when watched Commands lm workflow apply · list · get · disable · enable · rm — lm_integrator, scope-bound; one lifecycle per column Edition Open

Legacy exports carry dirty statuses — En cours, encours, fini, TERMINE with a trailing space. A workflow declares what they mean, so the chat answers lifecycle questions from a declared graph instead of inventing one.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dirty values resolve to declared states. Alias matching is trim and case-insensitive.
  • A data-truth report that never blocks. Apply compares the declaration with the column — undeclared values, unobserved codes, blanks — and stores the manifest either way.
  • The same check after each import. spec.check.trigger: ingestion re-checks the column when a run writes it, and a value no report named raises workflow.undeclared.<name>.
  • Grounded answers (Pro). The chat answers lifecycle questions from the declared graph.
  • Dormancy. A key and a threshold turn the declaration into a watch: a document unmoved in a non-terminal state past the threshold is a decision.dormant.* in the inbox.
  • A tape that outlives the alert. Every watched document's state, since when, and whether it alerted.
  • One column, one lifecycle. A second lifecycle on the same column is refused, naming the first.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the demo desk that ships with the repo

An order book whose status column carries seven spellings and one blank, under docs/apps/demo/. Land it first — The demo desk has the commands and the hand count. The screens below start on day 1.

# 10-order-lifecycle.yaml — the lifecycle the orders' status column already has.
#
# Four declared states with aliases for the spellings the export really carries, a
# transition graph, and a dormancy threshold that turns the declaration into a watched one.
# `ANNULE` is declared and never seen; `EN LITIGE` and `Terminé` are seen and never declared.
# Apply reports both — and refuses neither: a fact about the data is not a contradiction in
# the declaration.
#
# Expect: 200, dataTruth.undeclared = EN LITIGE (2 rows) + Terminé (1), unobserved = [ANNULE],
#         nullOrBlank = 1, keyNullOrBlank = 0.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: acme-order-lifecycle
spec:
  scope: desk
  provenance: declared
  on:
    table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
    column: status
    key: order_no
  dormancy:
    after: 30d
  states:
    - code: BROUILLON
      label: "Brouillon"
      initial: true
    - code: EN_COURS
      label: "En préparation"
      aliases: [en cours, encours]
    - code: TERMINE
      label: "Terminée"
      aliases: [fini]
      terminal: true
    - code: ANNULE
      label: "Annulée"
      terminal: true
  transitions:
    - { from: [BROUILLON], to: EN_COURS }
    - { from: [BROUILLON, EN_COURS], to: ANNULE }
    - { from: [EN_COURS], to: TERMINE }

The same manifest, as the graph it declares:

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> BROUILLON
  BROUILLON --> EN_COURS
  BROUILLON --> ANNULE
  EN_COURS --> ANNULE
  EN_COURS --> TERMINE
  TERMINE --> [*]
  ANNULE --> [*]
  note right of EN_COURS
    «En préparation»
    aliases: "en cours", "encours"
    dormancy: unmoved 30d → alert
  end note
  note right of TERMINE
    alias: "fini" — terminal
  end note

lm workflow apply prints what it stored, then the report: one line per disagreement between the declaration and the data. With -o json, the hub's answer: the report is under dataTruth.

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
Applied workflow "acme-order-lifecycle" → connector.t_acme_desk_orders.status, scope desk
  in the data, not declared: EN LITIGE (2 rows), Terminé (1 row)
  declared, not in the data: ANNULE
  status null or blank: 1 row
$ lm workflow list
NAME                  TABLE                         COLUMN  SCOPE  ENABLED
acme-order-lifecycle  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  status  desk   true

One 200, stored and indexed, with what the declaration and the data disagree on:

  • EN LITIGE sits on two orders and nobody declared it; Terminé (with its accent) on one;
  • ANNULE is declared and no order has reached it;
  • one order has no status at all.

EN LITIGE is deliberately not in the graph: it stays visible in the report, and the dormancy sweep still watches it.

docs.title: The manifest
The scope must exist, the table need not
docs.text:
spec.scope must be a discovered scope; an unknown one is a 404, as for a process:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/65-refused-unknown-scope.yaml
Error: API error 404: no schema for scope 'dsk' — run discovery first

The table is not checked: you may declare a lifecycle before ingesting the data. The report then says the table is not there yet.

docs.title: Names the source chose
docs.text:
on.column and on.key are the names your source uses, copied as they are — a Kafka message's JSON keys become columns verbatim:

on:
  table: connector.t_Commandes
  column: "Statut Commande"
  key: "N° Commande"

Quote them in the YAML if they contain spaces or punctuation; the hub adds the SQL quotes.

on.table must be a table ingestion owns — connector.t_<table>, or connector.v_<entity> — spelled the way the hub created it (a connector's target keeps your capitals, a fused view is lower case, neither contains a space). Anything else is refused, the hub's own tables included:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/66-refused-foreign-table.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.on.table is required and must name a table in the 'connector' schema that ingestion owns (connector.t_<table>) or a fused entity view (connector.v_<entity>, always lower-case), spelled the way the hub created it (letters, digits and underscores — a space is a typo): identity.app_user

A fused view carries a taxonomy as it is. A dormancy on one needs spec.on.order, because a view has no ingest order: the current version.

docs.title: One column, one lifecycle
docs.text:
A different name declaring an already-declared on.table + on.column is refused, naming the holder:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/64-refused-same-column.yaml
Error: API error 400: column connector.t_acme_desk_orders.status already has a declared lifecycle: workflow 'acme-order-lifecycle' — a column has exactly one lifecycle; re-apply under the name 'acme-order-lifecycle' to update it

apply on the same name is the update. The rule is per tenant.

docs.title: Alias semantics
docs.text:
Alias and code matching is trim + case-insensitive: "TERMINE ", "fini", "En cours" all resolve. On the demo desk, day 1:

Status as written Rows Resolves to En cours, encours 4 EN_COURS fini, TERMINE 2 TERMINE BROUILLON 2 BROUILLON EN LITIGE 2 undeclared Terminé 1 undeclared — an accent is not an alias anyone declared (empty) 1 nullOrBlank

Contradictions in the declaration are refused:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/61-refused-alias-collision.yaml
Error: API error 400: alias 'en_cours' on state BROUILLON collides with state code
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/60-refused-two-initial.yaml
Error: API error 400: exactly one state must be initial: true (found 2)
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/62-refused-terminal-outgoing.yaml
Error: API error 400: terminal state 'TERMINE' has an outgoing transition
  • an alias that collides with a state code;
  • an alias declared on two different states;
  • not exactly one initial: true;
  • a terminal: true state with an outgoing transition.

docs.title: The data-truth report — never blocks
docs.text:
apply stores the manifest first, then compares it with what the column contains. The comparison never becomes a refusal. Read three lines:

Line -o json field Means On the demo desk (day 1) in the data, not declared undeclared values in the data that no state declares, each with its row count EN LITIGE ×2, Terminé ×1 declared, not in the data unobserved declared states never seen in the data ANNULE <column> null or blank nullOrBlank rows with no status status null or blank: 1 row

Nothing to report: the data matches the declaration.

The other lines Line -o json field Means the table is not there yet tableMissing the table does not exist yet spec.on.key: the table has no such column keyColumnMissing spec.on.key names a column the table does not have key null or blank keyNullOrBlank rows with no key: the dormancy watch skips them spec.due.column … dueProblem why spec.due.column cannot give a deadline; null when it can spec.on.order: N rows with no valid order, their documents are never watched invalidOrderValues rows whose order value cannot place them; null without spec.on.order N keys hold several rows: declare spec.on.order to pick one keysWithSeveralRows a due date over a view without spec.on.order: the sweep reads every one of those rows not verified until the table exists: … columnsUnverified the declared columns an absent table left unchecked the data could not be checked checkUnavailable, unavailableReason the comparison could not run: the other fields are empty, not "the data agrees". Re-apply once fixed

The comparison reads the 200 most frequent values: a rare undeclared value can be missed.

docs.title: After each import — spec.check
docs.text:
The report above is computed when you apply. Without more, a spelling that the next night's export brings stays unseen until someone re-applies. spec.check.trigger: ingestion runs the same comparison after each completed run that writes spec.on.table:

spec:
  on:
    table: connector.t_orders
    column: status
  check:
    trigger: ingestion
  • A value that no earlier report named raises one workflow.undeclared.<name> event.
  • What the last apply reported is not said again: you have read it. A value still undeclared on the next run is not said twice.
  • A re-apply resets what is known to its own report. A value the new declaration covers is forgotten, and is news again if a later declaration drops it.
  • A failed or cancelled run checks nothing. A fused view (connector.v_*) is checked after a run that writes a table its entity fuses or looks up.

The event reaches what you subscribe to it, like any other: lm integration add --events 'workflow.undeclared.*' or an e-mail rule (Outputs). It never appears in the inbox, which holds decision.* only. Its payload:

Field Meaning message 1 new value of connector.t_orders.status matches no state of workflow orders-status — declare it as an alias, or correct the source. It counts the values and never quotes them workflow, table, column what was checked values the new values, each {value, rows} undeclared how many undeclared values the column holds now, new or not null_or_blank rows with no status run_id the run that triggered the check

The comparison costs one GROUP BY on the column per completed run of the table. On a large table imported every minute, that is one aggregate a minute.

docs.title: What the chat answers from it
docs.text:
lumnik Pro. Two gestures, two kinds of answer:

You ask with It answers about lm chat, then :scope desk the lifecycle: states, aliases, transitions lm ask --scope desk "…", the PWA's Chat tab the rows: a document's current status

The lifecycle, asked in the chat:

$ lm chat
[corpus=* scope=default topK=10] > :scope desk
scope → desk

[corpus=* scope=desk topK=10] > quels sont les états d une commande et quelles transitions sont autorisées ?
Les états d'une commande sont :

* Brouillon
* En cours
* Terminée (ou finie)
* Annulée

 Les transitions autorisées entre ces états sont :

* Du brouillon vers l'état en cours ou l'état annulé
* De l'état en cours vers l'état annulé ou le terme

Every transition it names is declared. The wording varies from one run to the next; the states and transitions must match the manifest. The chat does not know which state an order is in. lm ask does:

$ lm ask --scope desk "Dans quel statut est la commande SO-000004 ?"
La commande SO-000004 est en statut "BROUILLON".
  data as of: 2026-10-16T08:43:46.474408Z (last completed run)

  STATUS
  BROUILLON
  1 row returned

  SQL: SELECT status FROM "connector"."t_acme_desk_orders" WHERE order_no = 'SO-000004'
LIMIT 500

docs.title: Dormancy — the memory of the breathing
docs.text:
A legacy status is overwritten in place: the raw table says an order is EN_COURS, not since when. A scheduled sweep records each document's state from the moment lumnik starts watching, and alerts when one has sat unmoved, in a non-terminal state, past the declared threshold.

  • Two fields switch it on: spec.on.key (order_no — links a document's successive rows) and spec.dormancy.after (30d, any [0-9]+[mhd]).
  • The sweep runs every 15 minutes (lumnik.workflow.sweep.every, Observability).
  • The clock starts at lumnik's first sighting, not at the real stall: declare after: 14d today over orders stuck for weeks, and the earliest alert is in fourteen days.
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/63-refused-dormancy-no-key.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.dormancy requires spec.on.key (dormancy is per-document; the key links a document's versions)

The tape after the first sweep that saw the desk (day 1):

$ lm observations list
WORKFLOW              DOC        STATE      SINCE             ALERTED
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000001  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000002  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000003  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000004  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000005  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000006  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000007  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000008  Terminé    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000010  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW              WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
acme-order-lifecycle  11       0        -

SO-000009 is absent: it has no status, so there is no state to watch. The states are the resolved codes where an alias matched (fini reads TERMINE), the raw value where none did.

For the next screens the threshold was shortened to after: 1m and the manifest re-applied under the same name (the shipped file keeps 30d). Then day 2 was loaded:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml cp docs/apps/demo/data/acme-orders-day2.csv hub:/tmp/acme-desk/acme-orders.csv
lm connector run acme-desk-orders

Two ticks later:

$ lm observations list
WORKFLOW              DOC        STATE      SINCE             ALERTED
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000001  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000002  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000003  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000004  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000005  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000006  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000007  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000008  Terminé    2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000010  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 02:06  2026-10-19 02:21
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW              WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
acme-order-lifecycle  12       10       900
  • Ten alerts: nine at the first tick past the threshold, then SO-000013 — new on day 2, first seen at 02:06 — one tick later.
  • The two TERMINE orders never alert: a terminal state is excluded.
  • SO-000008 does alert: Terminé, with its accent, matched no alias, and an undeclared value can never be terminal.
  • The median detection delay is 900 s — one sweep interval, the floor.

What each alert says, in the inbox:

$ lm inbox --limit 3
ID  WHEN      PROCESS                        MESSAGE                                                                                                                                  ENTITY_KEY
47  just now  workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013: observed unmoved in "EN LITIGE" since 2026-10-19 (first observed 2026-10-19) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013
46  15min     workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012: observed unmoved in "EN_COURS" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle   SO-000012
45  15min     workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011: observed unmoved in "BROUILLON" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011
note: result hit the limit of 3 — there may be more

ENTITY_KEY is the business key. The wording names the date lumnik started watching, the date it first saw the document and the declared threshold — never how long the order sat in the ERP. The message's dates are UTC, while lm observations list shows your terminal's time zone: the 01:51 (Paris) sighting was 23:51 UTC the day before.

docs.title: Due date — a deadline the data carries
docs.text:
Dormancy counts from the day lumnik first saw a document. A due date counts from a date the data carries: a delivery promised for 20 October, still on the road on the 24th, is late.

The desk's carrier export holds a promised date per delivery:

delivery_no,status,promised_on
DL-1,EN_ROUTE,2026-10-20
DL-2,LIVREE,2026-10-20
DL-3,EN_ROUTE,2030-01-15
DL-4,EN_ROUTE,

Type the date at the door. A CSV column is text, and a due date must be a date. The connector types it with parse-date:

  mapping:
    cell:
      - parse-date: { column: promised_on, formats: ["yyyy-MM-dd"] }

Without it, the apply says so, and no alert is ever raised:

  spec.due.column promised_on is text, not a date: no deadline can be read from it

The workflow declares the deadline:

# 20-delivery-lifecycle.yaml — a delivery promised for a date and still on the road is late.
#
# Expect: one decision.overdue.acme-delivery-lifecycle, for DL-1 (promised 2026-10-20, EN_ROUTE).
#         DL-2 is delivered; DL-3 is promised for 2030; DL-4 has no date.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: acme-delivery-lifecycle
spec:
  scope: desk
  provenance: declared
  on:
    table: connector.t_acme_desk_deliveries
    column: status
    key: delivery_no
  due:
    column: promised_on
    states: [EN_ROUTE]
    zone: Europe/Paris
    message: "Livraison {doc_key} promise pour le {due}, toujours {state_label}"
  states:
    - code: EN_ROUTE
      label: "en route"
      initial: true
    - code: LIVREE
      label: "livrée"
      terminal: true
  transitions:
    - { from: [EN_ROUTE], to: LIVREE }

$ lm connector run acme-desk-deliveries
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/20-delivery-lifecycle.yaml -o json | jq -r .dataTruth.dueProblem
null
$ lm inbox --type decision.overdue.acme-delivery-lifecycle
ID  WHEN      PROCESS                           MESSAGE                                                       ENTITY_KEY
66  just now  workflow:acme-delivery-lifecycle  Livraison DL-1 promise pour le 2026-10-20, toujours en route  DL-1
  • DL-1 is late: promised for 20 October, still EN_ROUTE. DL-2 is delivered. DL-3 is promised for 2030. DL-4 has no date. None of them alerts.
  • The check runs every 15 minutes, like dormancy: the alert lands in the inbox within that time.
  • One alert per deadline. A date moved to another past day alerts again; a date moved to the future waits.
  • zone says where the deadline falls: a date passes at the end of that day in zone. Without zone, UTC.
  • A fused entity view is accepted. With several rows per key, declare spec.on.order: without it the sweep reads every row, and the apply report counts the keys concerned.
  • Files: data/acme-deliveries.csv, sources/80-deliveries.yaml, workflows/20-delivery-lifecycle.yaml, landed like the demo desk.

docs.title: The current version — spec.on.order
docs.text:
A sweep needs one version per document. On an ingest table it takes the last one ingested. That is wrong when the source sends events out of order, as Kafka can, and impossible on a fused view, which has no ingest order and may hold one row per event. spec.on.order names the column that orders a document's versions:

spec:
  on:
    table: connector.v_freezerdoorevent
    column: door_state
    key: door_incident_id
    order: occurred_at
  dormancy:
    after: 1m
Watched Without order With order connector.t_* the last version ingested the greatest order value; ingestion breaks a tie connector.v_*, dormancy refused at apply the greatest order value; a tie follows the rule below connector.v_*, due date every row, as before the greatest order value; a tie follows the rule below

The column. A date, a timestamp or a number orders as itself, when it is finite: NaN and infinity are no position. Text must be an ISO 8601 instant with an explicit offset, and is compared as an instant, never as text:

  • read: 2026-10-26T10:00:00Z, 2026-10-26T10:00:00.123Z, 2026-10-26T11:00:00+01:00;
  • never read: 2026-10-26T10:00:00 (no zone), 2026-10-26 (a date, not an instant), 01/07/2026, a blank.

2026-10-26T12:00:00+03:00 is 09:00Z: it comes before 2026-10-26T10:00:00Z. Two offsets of one instant are a tie.

A tie on a view. When the latest rows of one document disagree on the state, or on the deadline for a due date, the document is ambiguous: nothing is decided about it. When they agree, one row is picked by the view's canonical key. That pick is deterministic, not "the latest".

Unreadable documents. A document with one version whose order value is invalid or empty is not watched: lumnik cannot tell which version is current, and a bad date must never make an older state current. It raises nothing, its SINCE restarts on every sweep while it stays unreadable, and its history stays on the tape. When it is readable again, its clock runs from there.

On an ingest table, a later valid version does not clear the bad one: the table keeps every version.

OPEN    2026-10-26T10:00:00Z
CLOSED  not-a-date
CLOSED  2026-10-26T10:05:00Z     ← the document stays unreadable

Correct or remove the malformed source row, or rebuild the table from a corrected full export. The hub log names the documents: dormancy: 1 documents of tenant 1 workflow … are not watched: a version has no valid spec.on.order value — correct or remove the malformed source rows (e.g. DOOR-17). It says so again only when their number changes.

What it costs. At apply, the report reads the whole table to count the invalid values. On a fused view, every sweep computes the view once and ranks it: about 2 seconds for 100,000 documents, on top of the observations it writes.

docs.title: What a decision carries
docs.text:
A dormancy or due decision can say where the document is and who must act. A {name} its message does not reserve is a column of spec.on.table, read from the very version the decision is about; on a fused view, that includes the columns its entity joins. fields lists columns the payload carries and the sentence does not:

spec:
  on:
    table: connector.v_freezerdoorevent
    column: door_state
    key: door_incident_id
    order: occurred_at
  dormancy:
    after: 1m
    message: "{freezer_id} ({laboratory}): door {state} since {since}. Owner: {owner}"
    fields: [owner_email]

FZ-17 (Cryobiology Lab): door OPEN since 2026-10-26. Owner: Dr. Lina Moreau

The payload keeps its usual keys and gains fields: each cited or declared column, once, with its value.

  • A reserved name wins in the sentence. With message: "{doc_key} is still {state}" and fields: [state], {state} is the workflow's resolved state (OPEN) and fields.state is the raw value of a source column named state (open). The two differ by design.
  • An empty value renders as nothing in the sentence and stays null in fields. A timestamp is its UTC instant in both. A number loses its trailing zeros in the sentence (-67.4); fields keeps it as the column holds it (-67.4000). A Process decision does the same.
  • The order of the keys in fields is not part of the contract: the event log stores the payload as jsonb.
  • Without a cited column or fields, the payload is exactly what it was before.
  • At apply, a cited or declared name the table lacks is refused, naming it. A sentence's refusal also lists the reserved names, in case one was misspelt ({sinse}). A table not ingested yet is not checked: the report says not verified until the table exists, with the names.
  • A cited column the table no longer has, after an entity re-apply, renders empty: the alert still fires, and the hub log says so once (… cites owner, which … no longer has: it renders empty). Stop citing it and cite it again while it is still missing: the log says it again. So does a workflow disabled or deleted, then applied again.

Who receives fields

Fields included in a decision payload can leave the hub through tenant-wide webhooks, e-mail rules and the administrative event stream. Declare only the columns those outputs may receive. The inbox shows a decision to the workflow's scope; the event itself carries no scope.

docs.title: Applying it
docs.text:
lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
lm workflow list
lm workflow get acme-order-lifecycle      # the stored manifest, verbatim, comments included
lm observations list                      # the tape: what has not moved, stillest first
lm observations stats                     # per workflow: watched, dormant, median detection delay
lm inbox                                  # where decision.dormant.<name> lands

Turn it off, or remove it:

$ lm workflow disable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=false
$ lm workflow list
NAME                  TABLE                         COLUMN  SCOPE  ENABLED
acme-order-lifecycle  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  status  desk   false
$ lm workflow enable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=true
$ lm workflow rm acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle deleted
$ lm workflow rm acme-order-lifecycle
Error: API error 404: unknown workflow: acme-order-lifecycle

disable stops the sweep (no new alerts) and removes the lifecycle from chat, keeping the manifest and the tape; enable restores both. rm removes it for good, with no prompt — its tape too (lm observations stats no longer lists it). Each gesture, and every apply, is recorded in the audit trail.

Command Role Scope-bound lm workflow apply, list, get, disable, enable, rm lm_integrator yes — outside your grants, 403 scope not granted; list shows only your scopes lm observations list, stats lm_integrator and lm_admin (or lm_superadmin) yes — they list only the workflows of your scopes

docs.title: Declare the lifecycle a legacy status column already has
docs.text:
lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
lm workflow get acme-order-lifecycle

Result: the manifest is stored and indexed in one 200, with the data-truth report. The semantic chat in that scope now answers transition questions from the declared graph.

docs.title: Get told when a document stops moving
docs.text:
The demo manifest already carries spec.on.key and spec.dormancy.after: applying it switches the sweep on. Alerts land in lm inbox (and the PWA's Inbox tab) for users holding the workflow's scope and for users with no scope: role. To push them to an external system, lm integration add (Processes).

Don't treat the inbox as a register of everything asleep. A document alerts once per stall, and the alert ages out with the event log (30 days by default). The tape keeps it — see Re-alert semantics.

docs.title: Add the value the report says nobody declared
docs.text: The report named EN LITIGE (in the data, not declared). Add it as a state (or an alias of one) and re-apply under the same name. Result: the report no longer lists it, the chat knows what it means, and the sweep watches it as a declared state. The documents the tape held as EN LITIGE, and the source still holds, read the declared code from the next tick; a meaning is not a movement, so their SINCE, their alert and the transition journal stay as they were.

docs.title: Get told when a new spelling arrives
docs.text: Add check: { trigger: ingestion } under spec and re-apply. Result: the apply reports what is undeclared today; each later run that brings a value nobody declared raises workflow.undeclared.<name>, once.

docs.title: From a proposal dossier
docs.text: A business person can describe a problem on lumnik.fr and download a proposal dossier. Turning it into a workflow, and checking it against your data: Proposal dossiers.
