docs.title: Advanced: the sweep in detail
docs.text: What the sweep skips, the alert's wording, re-alerts, the tape, and scale

docs.title: What the sweep does not see
docs.text: A document with a NULL or blank key, or a NULL or blank status, is skipped — permanently: there is nothing to follow it by, or no state to watch (SO-000009 on the demo desk). The apply report counts both: key null or blank and status null or blank.

docs.title: The alert, verbatim
docs.text:
From the demo desk, with dormancy.after shortened to 1m:

SO-000004: observed unmoved in "BROUILLON" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle

The default shape — <key>: observed unmoved in "<state>" since <date> (first observed <date>) — declared threshold <after> in <workflow> — never asserts how long the document sat in the source. It is emitted as decision.dormant.<workflow> and appears in the inbox as workflow:<workflow>.

A workflow writes the sentence in the team's language with spec.dormancy.message:

dormancy:
  after: 14d
  message: "{doc_key} : immobile en « {state_label} » depuis le {since} — seuil {threshold}"

{state_label} is the state's declared label (its code when the state is undeclared); dates are the UTC day. Any other {name} is a column of the watched table: what a decision carries.

docs.title: Re-alert semantics
docs.text:
A document alerts once per stall. It alerts again only after it moved (a new state resets its clock) and then sat unmoved past the threshold once more.

A permanently stuck document alerts once; the alert leaves lm inbox with the event retention (lumnik.events.retention-days, 30 by default) What to do ack the alert into your own tracker, or raise lumnik.events.retention-days beyond your review cadence What stays the tape: lm observations list keeps ALERTED until the document moves

docs.title: Reading the tape
docs.text:
lm observations list — the watched documents of every workflow in your scopes, stillest first (--workflow, --limit: default 200, at most 1000). SINCE is when lumnik started observing that state; ALERTED is empty until the sweep alerts. lm observations stats sums it up per workflow. The TUI's :observations screen shows the same, with humanized ages. Both need lm_admin (or lm_superadmin) on top of lm_integrator.

lm observations transitions reads the journal: every observed move, newest first (--workflow, --doc, --limit). IN_FROM_S is the seconds the document spent in FROM, from ENTERED — its previous move, or its first observation for its first one (a lower bound, like SINCE). Moves are seen at sweep granularity: a document that moved twice between two ticks shows one move.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text:
• On a table with millions of documents, lengthen lumnik.workflow.sweep.every (15 minutes by default).
  • The tape is kept until lm workflow rm.
  • A workflow whose table is gone is skipped, and comes back by itself when the table returns. The other workflows are never affected. The hub log names the workflow.

docs.title: An undeclared value can never be terminal
docs.text: EN LITIGE is not declared, so it cannot be terminal: true: a document sitting in it is watched like any non-terminal state. The apply report names the value; the sweep names the documents asleep in it.

docs.title: lm — CLI & TUI reference
docs.text:
lm is the integrator's single binary: a kubectl-style CLI plus a k9s-style TUI. This page maps the whole surface; every command also documents itself with lm <cmd> --help.

Every command takes the global flags:

$ lm --help
…
Flags:
      --context string   Override the current context from ~/.lm/config.yaml
  -h, --help             help for lm
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --server string    Override the server URL
      --token string     Override the auth token (sent as-is; the context's refresh is not run)
  -v, --verbose          Verbose output (debug logs)
  • --token skips the context's stored session and its refresh, so a token from elsewhere works even when the stored one has expired.
  • Five commands use -o for an output file instead: lm source rest from-openapi, lm view get, lm view generate, lm entity export and lm proposal draft.

A command that only groups others (lm connector, lm entity, lm module…) prints its subcommands when typed alone. A word that is not one of them is an error with a non-zero exit:

$ lm connector lst; echo "exit=$?"
Error: unknown command "lst" for "lm connector"
exit=1

docs.title: Context & auth
docs.text:
Command What it does lm config set-context NAME --server URL --oidc-issuer URL create/update a context (--oidc-client-id defaults to lm-cli, the bundled realm client) lm config set-context NAME --server URL --tenant ID --user ID a context for a dev-bypass hub (make k8s-up): the ids are sent as X-Tenant-ID / X-User-ID; an OIDC hub ignores them lm config use-context NAME switch context (the default for every later command; inside lm ui, :context switches the session only) lm config view print ~/.lm/config.yaml with each credential shown as REDACTED — safe to paste into a ticket; --raw prints the tokens in clear lm login OIDC device flow: prints a URL + code, stores tokens in the context lm version binary version

First run? The deploy page walks through standing up a hub and pointing lm at it.

docs.title: Environment & TLS
docs.text:
Setting Where Effect LUMNIK_URL env var replaces the current context's server, per run LUMNIK_TOKEN env var the Bearer token, per run — for CI. Sent as is, ahead of a stored lm login session, never refreshed or saved; --token wins over it ca-file: /path/to/root.crt ~/.lm/config.yaml, by hand trust an internal CA (the TLS proxy's LAN certificate) insecure-skip-verify: true ~/.lm/config.yaml, by hand disable TLS verification; ca-file wins when both are set tenant: / user: ~/.lm/config.yaml dev-bypass hubs only; a real hub ignores them

The env vars need an existing current context: create it once with lm config set-context ci --server … && lm config use-context ci.

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text:
Command What it does lm validate -f FILE validate a kind: Connector manifest without applying it — field-by-field errors, exit code 1 on error. Other kinds are checked by their own apply lm apply -f FILE apply a kind: Connector manifest — upserts by metadata.name, so re-applying an edited file updates it. Prints Applied connector "NAME" — 1 endpoint; -o json prints the hub's answer, the connector id included. Not lm connector apply, which takes the flat stored fields lm entity apply -f FILE apply a kind: Entity fusion manifest lm entity delete NAME remove an entity and its view (lm_admin). Names the view and the search indexes over it, then asks you to type delete (--force skips the question). This is what frees a connector blocked by the 409 below lm entity list the entities you may read — name, sources, scopes, match or resolution lm entity get NAME [--filter COLUMN=VALUE]… [--limit N] [--offset N] one page of an entity's canonical rows (Read API). --filter is an exact match — a date on a date column is equal as an instant — repeatable; --limit is 1..1000 (default 100); a full page is announced on stderr lm entity resolve NAME resolve a resolution: entity over every row now (lm_admin); prints what was resolved, ambiguous and unresolved lm entity ambiguous NAME [--limit N] [--offset N] the rows a resolution: entity could not decide, with their candidates lm entity history NAME SOURCE ID every decision about one source row: outcome, rule, candidates, automatic or asserted lm entity assert-same\|assert-distinct NAME --left SOURCE:ID --right SOURCE:ID [--reason TEXT] a correction that outranks every rule, applied at the next resolve (lm_admin) lm entity export NAME -o FILE [--force] download the entity's canonical CSV through the one-shot door. An existing file is refused without --force; -o - streams to stdout lm app apply -f FILE declare a kind: App business app — title, scope, icon and theme lm app list / lm app get NAME the declared apps; one app as an applyable manifest (lm app get NAME > app.yaml, edit, re-apply) lm app rm NAME delete a declared app for good (no prompt); the last default app is refused lm view apply -f FILE / lm view list / lm view get NAME / lm view rm NAME saved kind: View manifests: store, list, fetch, delete (no prompt) lm process apply -f FILE / lm process list apply/list kind: Process notify rules lm process enable/disable NAME start or stop a process firing — the manifest stays stored lm process rm NAME delete a process for good (no prompt) lm workflow apply -f FILE apply a kind: Workflow lifecycle — prints the data-truth report lm workflow list / lm workflow get NAME declared lifecycles (name, table, column, scope, enabled); one manifest's YAML on stdout lm workflow enable/disable NAME serve a workflow again, or stop serving it — the manifest stays stored lm workflow rm NAME delete a workflow for good (no prompt) lm export apply -f FILE declare a kind: Export lm proposal draft DOSSIER write a draft kind: Workflow from a proposal dossier (- for stdin); flags --name --scope --table --column --key --after -o. Offline, never applies; -o FILE refuses an existing file lm describe connector-type KIND field reference for a connector kind 
$ lm validate -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml
✗ 10-customer.yaml — 4 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    apiVersion
          apiVersion is required
          → Use: apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1

  ERROR    kind
          kind must be "Connector"
…
$ lm workflow disable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=false
$ lm app rm clients
Error: API error 400: cannot remove the last default app — apply a different app with default: true first, which demotes this one automatically
$ lm app rm lumilait
app lumilait deleted

docs.title: Connectors, endpoints, sources
docs.text:
Command What it does lm connector list / get NAME the connector instances; one connector's flat stored fields lm connector apply -f FILE edit a connector from the file lm connector get prints — Editing a connector's stored fields lm connector delete NAME erases the connector's data: tables, run history, RAG chunks (erasure). Says what goes, then asks you to type delete. --dry-run stops there; --force skips the question. A table an entity reads blocks it (capture below) lm connector run NAME trigger an immediate run lm connector pause/resume NAME stop/restart scheduling; lm connector list shows a paused connector's cron followed by (paused), and lm connector run still runs it lm connector scope ls/set/add/rm/sync manage the connector's business scopes; sync re-stamps its already-indexed chunks lm endpoint enable/disable/reset-cursor C/E per-endpoint scheduler and cursor lm endpoint purge C/E delete one endpoint's rows after stating how many and asking you to type purge (--dry-run only counts, --force skips the question). For rest-generic endpoints and one-shot lm csv ingest tables; refused for jdbc-generic, csv-file and kafka — see Emptying one endpoint lm source rest test C pre-flight every enabled endpoint — the request a run would send, nothing written; non-zero exit if one fails lm source rest probe C --endpoint PATH sample one path with the connector's connection and credential; drafts the endpoint fragment to paste under spec.endpoints lm source rest from-openapi URL --name N generate a manifest (--scope repeatable, -o FILE, --apply upserts it) lm source jdbc test/discover/add open a JDBC source directly; the password is prompted without echo, or piped with --password-stdin. There is no --password lm source jdbc list-tables NAME the tables registered under a source the hub already holds lm source schema --scope TAG / lm source rediscover --scope TAG show / rebuild the scope's schema card (--scope is required) lm csv ingest FILE\|sftp://…\|s3://… one-shot CSV ingest into an ext.* table, no run recorded — flags on CSV & files. lm source csv ingest is the same command 
$ lm connector delete orders --dry-run
Would delete connector orders (csv-file) — 8 rows of connector.t_orders, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)
$ lm connector delete acme-desk-erp --dry-run
Error: API error 409: table connector.t_acme_desk_erp feeds entity acmecustomer — remove the entity first (lm entity delete acmecustomer)

A one-shot ingest:

$ lm csv ingest stock.csv --scope retail --name stock-count
Ingested stock.csv into ext.stock_count
  • rows written:    3
  • promoted cols:   4
      - sku (text)
      - label (text)
      - qty (bigint)
      - warehouse (text)

  • askable:         scope 'retail' — try: lm ask --scope retail "how many rows are in ext.stock_count?"
A dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

With the AI off, the askable line is replaced by: A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat.

docs.title: Editing a connector's stored fields
docs.text:
lm connector get NAME prints the connector as the hub stores it. Edit that file and apply it back:

lm connector get erp-clients > c.yaml     # keep the id: line, it names the connector to update
lm connector apply -f c.yaml
  • Create a connector with lm apply -f and its kind: Connector manifest. lm connector apply creates only csv-file and hello-world; for another type it says to use lm apply -f.
  • A file without id: under a name already taken is refused, naming the id to add.

docs.title: Data, runs & answers
docs.text:
Command What it does lm run list / lm run get ID connector runs, one row per endpoint (records in/out/skipped); list is newest first, --connector NAME, --limit N. An EVALUATED column appears once the tenant has an enabled Process: whether it has evaluated the rows the run wrote. get --wait-evaluated [--timeout D] [--interval D] waits for it, and exits 1 when the hub cannot say (no enabled Process, processes changed since the run started, or a run from before the hub recorded it) lm run cancel ID stop a run. A Running run stops at its next chunk; a Queued one ends at once. Refusals: Stopping a run lm dlq list / lm dlq get ID dead-letter entries (reason + offending row); --run RUN, --connector NAME, list --limit N lm dlq replayed ID --new-run-id RUN / lm dlq discard ID close an entry: carried again by that run, or dropped — the rules lm conflicts list fused-entity rows with a source conflict or a lookup ambiguity (--limit N) lm observations list the workflow tape: watched documents, stillest first (--limit N); --workflow NAME narrows the hub's read to one workflow lm observations transitions the journal: each observed move, newest first, with the seconds spent in the state it left (IN_FROM_S, counted from the first observation for a document's first move); --workflow NAME, --doc KEY, --limit N lm observations stats the tape per workflow: watched, dormant, median detection delay (seconds; - when nothing is dormant) lm integration add NAME --url U --secret-stdin [--events T] register a webhook target. The signing secret is required and read on stdin. --events defaults to decision.*; --platform is a label only lm integration list / describe ID registered targets; the table shows scheme and host only, -o json\|yaml the full URL lm integration test ID [--event T] fire a catalog event at the target and report the delivery; decision.* events cannot be fired here lm integration rm ID remove a target — delivery history is kept lm notify add --events T --to EMAIL [--template N] / list / rm ID email rules (needs the deploy's SMTP settings — see the self-host guide) lm outputs list what was sent out and whether it arrived, failures first (--limit N) lm outputs replay ID re-send one failed delivery as a new attempt lm data tables / lm data row HASH dynamic tables with your row count (unknown when it could not be counted); the raw row behind a citation, a timestamp as its UTC instant lm secret set/list/describe/rm encrypted secrets; values never returned. set NAME prompts without echo, set NAME - reads stdin, set NAME VALUE warns (shell history). --description, rm --force. rm does not check references: a connector naming the secret fails at its next run

The two tables you will read most:

$ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
884f487d  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
$ lm dlq list --run 884f487d
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
b6bc9601  orders     884f487d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/orders.csv:9 — Record has 2 values but 5 column…
b4176d39  orders     884f487d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 c…

The ID columns are abbreviated — and the abbreviation works

lm run list and lm dlq list show the first 8 characters of each id. get, discard, replayed and --run accept those 8 characters; an ambiguous prefix is refused. -o yaml prints every id in full.

A full page says so

Lists answer in pages. Each takes --limit N, up to a cap:

Command Default Cap lm run list 50 200 lm dlq list 100 200 lm inbox 50 200 lm export runs NAME 20 200 lm outputs list 200 500 lm conflicts list 200 1000 lm observations list / transitions 200 1000 lm entity get NAME / lm entity ambiguous NAME 100 1000

A full page prints note: result hit the limit of N — there may be more on stderr, so pipes and -o json stay clean. Raise --limit to see further back. --connector filters on the hub, so a quiet connector's old runs are still found.

docs.title: Ask your data
docs.text:
lumnik Pro

lm ask, lm chat, lm rag and lm scopes need the AI. On lumnik Open, or with the AI off, they answer Error: API error 404 (no details from the server).

Command What it does lm ask [--scope S] [--lang XX] [--previous "question"] "question" analytic text-to-SQL over the fused hub: the answer, a data as of line, any disputed rows, the rows the query returned and the SQL that ran (the guards). --lang sets the answer language (default: from LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG). Without --scope, asks your default scope. --previous names the question this one continues: "Et SUP-004 ?" is answered as the full question, shown on an understood as line. -o json\|yaml for a script lm chat interactive REPL chat — in-REPL commands: :corpus NAME (or all), :scope TAG (or default), :topK N (1 to 50), :clear, :help, :exit lm scopes / lm scope / lm scope set TAG list scopes (a scope-bound user sees only granted ones); show/set your default (404 no user record on this hub…: see Tenants, users & scopes) lm rag search/status/reindex semantic search (--top-k N, 1 to 50, default 5); corpus status; re-index of the platform corpus (manifests, API, hooks)

docs.title: The rows under the answer
docs.text:
lm ask prints the rows its query returned under the answer, then how many there are, then the SQL. When the hub withholds a phrased answer, these rows are the answer. Played on the demo desk:

$ lm ask --scope desk "Quels clients GOLD sont à Lyon ? Donne leur code et leur nom."
Il y a 2 clients GOLD à Lyon :

- Code : P-1000, Nom : Hydraulique Lyon 1000
- Code : P-1008, Nom : Filtration Lyon 1008

Total de clients : 2
  data as of: 2026-10-16T08:50:37.235585Z (last completed run)

  disputed — a source disagrees on a value this answer filtered on:
    P-1008  city = 'Lyon'  counted  t_acme_desk_erp: Lyon · t_acme_desk_crm: Villeurbanne

  CODE    NAME
  P-1000  Hydraulique Lyon 1000
  P-1008  Filtration Lyon 1008
  2 rows returned

  SQL: SELECT v.code, v.name
FROM connector."v_acmecustomer" v
WHERE v.segment = 'GOLD' AND v.city = 'Lyon'
LIMIT 500

  try: lm conflicts list  — where this scope has source conflicts or lookup ambiguities, row by row
  • The query stops at 500 rows; every row returned is printed. A line break inside a value shows as \n.
  • no rows returned when the query found nothing; no table when the answer ran no query.

For a script, ask for JSON (or -o yaml): one document, nothing else on stdout.

$ lm ask -o json --scope desk "Quels clients GOLD sont à Lyon ? Donne leur code et leur nom." | jq -r '.rows[] | .code + "  " + .name'
P-1000  Hydraulique Lyon 1000
P-1008  Filtration Lyon 1008
Field Holds answer the sentence abstained true for a refusal. Test this, never the wording of answer sql, columns, rows, rowCount the query and what it returned; numbers stay numbers dataAsOf the last run that fed the scope understoodAs the full question, when --previous was used disputed, disputedTruncated the disputed rows, and whether the list was cut otherDoors the try: suggestions printed under the answer

docs.title: The apps ladder
docs.text: Command What it does lm view -f FILE [--filter …] render a kind: View list — filters col=v · col~text · col>v (>= < <=, number/ISO date), repeatable (AND). The value is a bare literal: --filter 'city=Lyon'; city='Lyon' is refused lm view KEY -f FILE one record's detail (with the _conflicts ledger) lm view NAME [KEY] [--filter …] the same for a saved view of lm view list. A view named like a subcommand (list, get, apply, generate, rm) runs the subcommand instead lm view generate SCOPE "DESCRIPTION" [-o FILE] ask the AI to write a kind: View manifest over a scope; review it, then render with lm view -f lm view list [--scope S] the saved views you may read lm view get NAME [-o FILE] one saved view's manifest YAML — to stdout, or to a file lm view apply -f FILE / lm view rm NAME store a kind: View manifest; delete one (no prompt) lm app apply -f FILE / list / get NAME / rm NAME business apps — see Manifests lm workflow … lifecycles — see Manifests lm export apply -f FILE declare a kind: Export; inline credentials are refused, naming the field lm export list / lm export get NAME the exports your scopes can see; one export's manifest YAML (user:password@ printed as ***@) lm export run NAME [--wait] start a managed run. Without --wait it returns once the run is accepted; --wait follows it to Completed (prints the receipt) or Failed (exit 1). --timeout (default 30m) and an interrupt stop the waiting, never the run lm export retry NAME RUN_ID [--wait] a new attempt of a Failed run, regenerated from byte 0 lm export runs NAME [--limit N] / lm export status NAME [RUN_ID] the export's run ledger, newest first; one run in full (latest by default) lm inbox [--limit N] [--all] [--process NAME] [--type TYPE] recent decision.* events — what needs you; --process/--type narrow the hub's read lm inbox ack ID dispose of a decision (idempotent)

docs.title: Admin & platform
docs.text: Command What it does lm module list installed business modules, with ACTIVE/INACTIVE and the reason lm migration status migration status per schema: version, pending count, last applied (— when none). No apply: the hub migrates at every startup — capture lm hook list / lm hook get NAME the Kotlin platform hooks loaded at startup lm hook scripts the Kotlin scripts a connector manifest can name as script: hooks:<name>.kts: name, size, SHA-256

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Command What it does lm search apply -f FILE declare a kind: SearchIndex — validate, then create or update; -f - reads stdin (integrator) lm search rm NAME delete a declared index and queue the purge of its documents (Deleting); asks you to type delete (--force skips the question; in a script without it: aborted: no confirmation read) lm search query "TEXT" [--entity E] [--facet field=value]… [--limit N] [--cursor C] keyword search over the declared indexes, no model — the full guide lm search status [INDEX] every index (name, status, lag, documents, last rebuild), or one index's detail lm search rebuild INDEX [--wait] full rebuild; without --wait it prints the run id once claimed, --wait follows it to ready/failed/cancelled (--timeout, default 30m) lm search cancel INDEX request cancellation of an index's active rebuild; refused once it has reached publish

The footer lists the keys of the page you are on. The key reference lists them all.

docs.title: Getting around
docs.text:
: opens the palette. Type the start of a page name (:so offers :sources), then Tab or Enter.

Group Pages Your data :sources (alias :connectors) :endpoints :runs :dlq :tables :entities :conflicts :ambiguous Decide :inbox :outputs :observations Explore & ask :ask :view :scopes :search Create & declare :new :processes :views :apps :workflows :exports Admin :modules :hooks :migrations :rag :secrets :integrations :notify

Global keys, from any page:

Key Effect : open the command palette r refresh the current page d toggle the describe panel (full detail on the selected row) Tab with the describe panel open: give it the keys, so ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn scroll a long record; Tab or Esc gives them back to the list / on list pages: filter the table to the rows holding a text (Esc clears) — the key reference lists the pages y copy the current row to your clipboard, through the terminal: works over SSH where the terminal allows it (iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Windows Terminal; not macOS Terminal) q quit ? help screen (the same table, always at hand) Esc close a modal, cancel an input, or back out one level
  • The header names the hub, the page, the session scope and the event stream: [LIVE✓], or [RECONNECTING] with the reason in the footer.
  • :sources, :endpoints, :runs, :dlq and :inbox update live; the cursor stays on your row.
  • Another hub: :context (or :ctx) lists your contexts. Enter switches for this session only; lm config use-context sets the default.
  • Session expired: a window opens. L logs in again, as lm login does, and the TUI resumes.

docs.title: Watch an ingestion
docs.text:
:sources is the home page: one row per connector. /desk above kept the rows holding desk.

  • ^R (or R) runs the selected connector now; ^P pauses or resumes its schedule.
  • e opens its YAML in $EDITOR; t edits its scopes, then offers to re-stamp its chat chunks.
  • Del says what the delete takes, then asks: Delete connector "cust-csv"? Goes with it: 3 rows of connector.t_cust_csv, its run history and RAG chunks. A table an entity reads shows the refusal instead, naming the entity.
  • Enter opens a REST or JDBC source's :endpoints, any other connector's :runs.

Enter on acme-desk-crm, then d on its run:

║CONNECTOR          ENDPOINT      STATUS           STARTED          DURATION      RECORDS      TRIGGER       ║
║acme-desk-crm      default       ● Completed      10-24 23:07      37ms          8/8/0        MANUAL        ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
── describe: cb24e3a8 ──
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│id:              cb24e3a8-c418-4985-8247-d5210ebc0687                                                       │
│connector:       acme-desk-crm                                                                              │
│endpoint:        default                                                                                    │
│status:          ● Completed                                                                                │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 Esc: clear filter  d: describe  D: dead letters  y: yank  s: sort  c: cancel  r: refresh  Tab: scroll the
  • RECORDS is in/out/skip. Every dead letter is counted in skip.
  • d shows the run in full: for a failed or cancelled run, an error: section with the message.
  • D opens the run's dead letters in :dlq.

:endpoints (REST and JDBC sources) shows each endpoint's SCHEDULE, LAST_RUN and STATUS: where to check "did it even fire?". T tests the endpoint, nothing written; P probes a path and drafts its fragment; C resets its cursor (asks first); Del purges its rows, when the type allows it — the question names the count.

docs.title: Stopping a run
docs.text:
Select a Running row in :runs and press c. The chunk in flight finishes; the run ends at the next one. A Queued run ends at once.

Refusal toasted Meaning run … already ended (STATUS) nothing left to stop run … is being started; try again in a moment a Queued run is starting — retry run … is not in flight on this hub the run started a moment ago — retry; refused again, no process runs it, and the hub marks it Failed on its own

docs.title: What a status means
docs.text:
STATUS What happened Look at Queued waiting for a free slot (only with the run queue on) nothing: it starts on its own Running still going d Completed done. Rows in :dlq were set aside; other skip rows were filtered on purpose :dlq, RECORDS Partial read less than the source held; the next run resumes d: the error: section Failed the run failed: source unreachable, bad credentials, refused config d: the error: section Cancelled stopped by a user, or skipped: another run of the endpoint was active d no row at all the schedule has not fired yet :sources, :endpoints

Found the cause? In :sources, e fixes the connector and R runs it again. The full walk: Diagnosing a failed run.

:dlq lists the rows a run set aside, with reason and row. ^R marks one replayed (naming the run that carried it again), ^D discards it.

docs.title: Decide
docs.text:
Four pages answer "what needs me":

  • :inbox — the decisions your processes and workflows raised. a acks the selected one; it leaves the list. A shows the acked ones too:
 lumnik 2026 · lm @ selfhost (localhost:18080) · :inbox · scope: system · 00:34:00  [LIVE✓]
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════ :inbox ══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║ID WHEN PROCESS                          MESSAGE                                                            ║
║66 1h   workflow:acme-delivery-lifecycle Livraison DL-1 promise pour le 2026-10-20, toujours en route [acke…║
║63 1h   litige-ouvert                    Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €           ║
║8  2h   lyon-client-arrive               Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon [acked]                         ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
 a: ack · A: show disposed · d: describe · y: yank · r: refresh
  • :outputs — what was sent out and whether it arrived, failures first. ^R replays a failed delivery.
  • :observations — the workflow tape: documents that have NOT moved, stillest first. The title shows, per workflow, the documents watched, the dormant ones and the median detection time.
  • :conflicts — the fused rows with a source conflict or a lookup ambiguity. Read-only: d shows which source said what; the fix is a source or manifest change.

docs.title: Explore & ask
docs.text:
:ask is analytic chat: a plain-language question comes back as generated SQL, rows and an answer. It asks the session scope shown in the header — your default (lm scope) at startup, changed with :scopes → Enter or :scope <tag>. A question continues the last one answered, as lm ask --previous does: "Et SUP-004 ?" is answered as the full question, shown in the headline after understood as:. An answer that ran no SQL keeps the question it continues; changing the scope starts over.

Key Effect Enter run the question y yank the generated SQL e export the result rows to a CSV file n new question — the next one stands alone r clear the page — the next question stands alone

:view renders a kind: View manifest file. The path field starts on the WOW's docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml, relative to where you started lm: from the repo root, Enter renders it:

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
:new is the authoring loop. Pick a kind; every kind you can apply is offered — the connector types, Entity, Process, Workflow, App, View, Export and SearchIndex — each with a real example from these docs.

Key Effect Enter open the kind's example in $EDITOR; on save it validates and applies, then jumps to where you observe it v edit, then validate without applying; a then applies the buffer you checked e after refusals (shown field by field): re-open the same buffer Esc abandon — your edits are kept in a temp file w guided setup: jdbc-generic (name, JDBC URL, user, password typed masked, schema → test → pick tables → one connector per table) · csv-file (ingest a local file once, then opens :tables) d the kind's example and, for a connector kind, its type's configuration schema (lm describe connector-type)
  • v checks a connector through the hub's validator; any other kind by its YAML and kind only.
  • graphql and soap show rest-generic's schema: they are request shapes of that type.
  • In the JDBC picker, a table of an unsupported shape is listed but cannot be ticked.

:processes lists declared kind: Process rules: e re-opens one in the same edit → validate → apply loop, ^P enables or disables it (the manifest stays), Del deletes it after a confirmation.

docs.title: Admin corner
docs.text:
Page What it lists Keys :modules installed business modules — :hooks installed Kotlin hooks (read-only: they load from deployment manifests at startup) d the binding: handler, events, priority (lm hook get) :migrations migration status per schema; a pending one is applied at the hub's next start — :rag chunks indexed per scope (connectors, last indexed); the title shows the platform corpus R reindex the platform corpus (asks first) :tables the t_* tables your connectors landed, with your row count Enter the raw rows in landing order, a timestamp as its UTC instant (2026-10-19T21:20:04.123456Z) (n/p page, d whole row, Esc back) :entities the entities you may read see :entities keys :ambiguous the identities one entity's resolution could not settle Enter type an entity name / load a row's history · ^R re-run the pass · d the row :views the saved views the hub serves the PWA Enter render in :view · e edit in :new · Del delete (asks first) :apps the business apps (title, scope, default, tabs) e edit in :new (rebuilt from the app's fields) · Del delete (asks first) :workflows the declared document lifecycles e edit in :new · ^P enable/disable · Del delete (asks first) :exports kind: Export manifests: entity, schedule, destination, last run (integrator role only) Enter its runs · R run now · ^R retry a Failed run · e edit in :new :search whether this hub has a Search provider, then the declared indexes (status, documents, last rebuild) / query, bound to the session scope · R rebuild · c cancel the rebuild · Del delete (asks first) :secrets the credentials connectors refer to by name (values never shown) n store one (typed masked) · e rotate its value · Del delete (asks first) :integrations the webhook targets :outputs delivers to, with recent delivery health; URLs shown to the host only n register (URL and secret typed masked) · T fire a test event · d registration and latest deliveries · Del remove (asks first; history kept) :notify the email rules n add one (events, recipient, entity filter, template) · Del remove (asks first) :scopes the tenant's business scopes Enter set the active scope

What the pages show when a feature is absent:

  • :rag with the AI switched off says so (the module stays installed, its chunks are kept); in an Open build it says the module is not in the build.
  • :search on a hub without a Search provider says not installed.
  • :exports for an lm_user says the page needs the integrator role.

  • Connectors overview — what a source, an endpoint and a run are.
  • Inbox — the decisions :inbox surfaces.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text: Connectors ingest your legacy sources — files, databases, APIs, event topics — into hub tables, read-only and declaratively: one YAML manifest, three commands — validate, apply, run.

docs.title: Which connector for which source?
docs.text:
Your source Connector Page CSV exports — dropped locally, on SFTP, or in S3 csv-file CSV & files A live database — PostgreSQL; Oracle (Pro) jdbc-generic JDBC An HTTP/JSON API (Stripe, HubSpot, …) rest-generic REST A GraphQL API rest-generic, GraphQL shape GraphQL A SOAP middleware (Siebel, SAP PI, …) rest-generic, SOAP shape SOAP An event broker (Kafka, Redpanda, Event Hubs) kafka — Pro Kafka

There are five connector types: csv-file, jdbc-generic, rest-generic, kafka and hello-world (a smoke-test connector with no page of its own). GraphQL and SOAP are not types: they are request shapes of a rest-generic endpoint, with the same auth, retry and rate limits.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  src["legacy source"] --> t["transport / engine"] --> p["parser"]
  p --> m["mapping & transforms"] --> tbl["hub table"] --> rag["RAG chunks"]

Every connector reads the source and writes a hub table. Each tenant sees only its own rows.

  • A csv-file connector can repair the data on the way: Transformers.
  • On lumnik Pro with the AI on, the table also feeds the scoped chat.

docs.title: The lifecycle — every connector, same three commands
docs.text:
Assumes a deployed hub and an authenticated lm — see Quickstart.

  1. Write a manifest (kind: Connector) — every connector uses the same envelope:

    apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: <kebab-case-name>
  connector_type: <csv-file|jdbc-generic|rest-generic|kafka>
  scopes: [<scope>]                    # the scope(s) this connector's tables are askable in
spec:
  # type-specific — see your connector's page
  ...

  2. lm validate -f manifest.yaml — check it without touching anything.

  3. lm apply -f manifest.yaml — register or update the connector (safe to re-run).

  4. lm connector run <name> — run it now. Or schedule it:

    • spec.schedule: "0 6 * * *" — cron, evaluated in UTC (here: daily at 06:00 UTC).
    • spec.window: "22:00-07:00" — scheduled runs start only inside this UTC window; the end is exclusive, so 07:00 keeps the 06:00 slot inside.

    What the three commands print, on a small orders export:

    $ lm validate -f orders.yaml
✓ orders.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f orders.yaml
Applied connector "orders" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run orders
run scheduled: 6806802f-ed3c-46d6-8eeb-a0f7cff94e77

    "Scheduled" is not "done" — the result lands in the run ledger a few seconds later:

    $ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
6806802f  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
$ lm dlq list --run 6806802f-ed3c-46d6-8eeb-a0f7cff94e77
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  RESOLUTION  MESSAGE
7c863b7a  orders     6806802f  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/sales-orders.csv:10 — Record has 5 values but o…
004c3b56  orders     6806802f  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/sales-orders.csv:7 — Record has 4 values but on…

    Ten rows read, eight written, two set aside in the dead-letter queue with their reason.

    lm connector run prints one run id. A connector with several endpoints starts one run per endpoint: lm run list --connector <name> shows them all. 5. Watch it in the TUI (CLI & TUI): :sources (connectors), :runs (history), :dlq (rejected rows).

docs.title: Several runs at once
docs.text:
• A hub runs at most 4 scheduled endpoints at once. The others wait; a waiting endpoint has no run in lm run list yet.
  • lm run cancel <id> stops a run after its current batch of rows.
  • Raising the limit, and queuing manual runs: Turning on the run queue.

docs.title: Freshness follows the schedule
docs.text:
A change in the source appears at the next run that reads it.

  • A row deleted at the source stays in the hub table. One exception: a csv-file connector reading one local file, where the table follows the file (full refresh).
  • A JDBC watermark connector re-reads only the rows whose watermark moved.

docs.title: Validate before apply
docs.text: Command Purpose lm validate -f manifest.yaml Validate without applying. Exit 0 if valid (warnings allowed), 1 if errors. lm apply -f manifest.yaml Apply. The server runs the same checks: on errors nothing is written and you get the same report. Warnings do not block the apply. lm describe connector-type <kind> Show the schema (fields, types, required/optional, docs) of a connector type.

docs.title: Valid
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f stripe.yaml
✓ stripe.yaml — valid

docs.title: Errors only
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f bad.yaml
✗ bad.yaml — 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.auth.token_env
          bearer auth requires token_env (or inline token_value)
          → Use `lm secret set <NAME> ...` then reference via token_env: <NAME>

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].id
          must match kebab-case identifier

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 2 error(s)

docs.title: Warnings only (still valid, exit 0)
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f noscopes.yaml
! noscopes.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     metadata.scopes
          no scopes declared — a user bound to a scope will not see this connector, its runs or its dead letters
          → Add: scopes: [compta]  (a user must hold the role scope:compta)

lm apply prints the same warnings, and applies. A warning never fails lm validate or lm apply.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Exit Meaning 0 No errors (warnings allowed) 1 Validation errors, and every other failure (file not found, unparsable YAML, hub unreachable)

docs.title: One file, one command — lm csv ingest
docs.text: Load one export in one command, to look at it before writing a connector. Nothing is scheduled, nothing is transformed.

docs.title: Load it
docs.text:
$ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv --name quick-look --scope demo
Ingested ./clients.csv into ext.quick_look
  • rows written:    2
  • promoted cols:   3
      - row_id (bigint)
      - email (text)
      - signup_date (text)

  • askable:         scope 'demo' — try: lm ask --scope demo "how many rows are in ext.quick_look?"
A dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.
  • The rows land in ext.<name>. --name quick-look gives ext.quick_look: every - becomes _.
  • Numbers and true/false become typed columns. Dates stay text, like signup_date above.
  • The file is askable at once in the scope you pass (Pro, AI on). Without --scope, it goes to system.
  • On lumnik Open, or with the AI off, the last lines read A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat. and The rows are in ext.quick_look, and a dormant connector is registered.

A dormant connector is registered under the same name. It never runs on its own. Inspect it, turn it into a manifest, or remove it with lm connector delete quick_look.

docs.title: Where the file can be
docs.text:
lm csv ingest ./clients.csv                                       # a file on your machine, uploaded
lm csv ingest sftp://user@host/export/clients.csv --key-secret ACME_SFTP_KEY \
    --host-key-fingerprint "SHA256:…"                             # or --password-secret NAME
lm csv ingest s3://acme-exports/billing/ --region eu-west-3 --suffix .csv
  • An uploaded file is limited to 10 MB. A larger one: put it on SFTP or S3.
  • A remote file is limited to 500 MB, and stays where it is.
  • A folder holds several files: each lands in its own ext.<filename>. --name takes one file only, and is refused on a folder.

docs.title: Load it again
docs.text:
The same name refreshes the table. Rows are deduplicated, new columns added:

$ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv --name quick-look --scope demo
Re-ingested ./clients.csv into ext.quick_look — refreshed, rows deduplicated by key
  • rows written:    3
  • promoted cols:   3
      - row_id (bigint)
      - email (text)
      - signup_date (text)

A different --scope moves the table to that scope.

docs.title: What it does not do
docs.text:
A csv-file connector lm csv ingest Runs on a schedule yes no Repairs the data (transformers) yes no A malformed row set aside, the run continues the whole load is refused, nothing written Moves or deletes the source file sftp/s3: yes no Lands in connector.t_<name> ext.<name>

To make it recurring, write a csv-file connector under the registered name, then wake it: Make it nightly.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Do this Error: API error 400: malformed CSV row at line 3 — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared Fix line 3 of the file, load it again. Error: API error 413 (request too large): the hub accepts a request body up to 10 MB … Put the file on SFTP or S3, and load it from there. Error: API error 409: the name 'articles' belongs to a configured connector … Pass another --name. name 'clients' would ingest 3 files into one dataset … Drop --name (one table per file), point at one file, or write a connector with a glob. A second connector appears after lm apply -f The manifest's metadata.name differs from the registered name. Delete the duplicate.

docs.title: CSV & files (SFTP/S3)
docs.text:
Ingest CSV files — dropped locally, on an SFTP server, or in an S3 bucket — into a hub table on a schedule, with per-row error isolation.

Type csv-file Transports local, sftp, s3 Target connector.t_<name> Schedulable cron Edition Open

docs.title: Quickstart — one local file, three commands and a look at the ledger
docs.text:
# 10-local-simple.yaml — the simplest CSV ingest: one local file, full load.
#
# Apply and run:
#   lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
#   lm connector run csv-local-simple
#
# A file that has not changed since its last run is skipped; one that has changed
# (replaced in place, or grown) is read again in full, and the table then holds
# exactly what the file holds: rows the file no longer has are removed — a run that
# would shrink the table by more than 30% fails instead, unless refresh.max_removed
# says otherwise (docs/connectors/csv.md, full refresh). Suitable for reference
# files fully replaced on each load cycle. after_process: none means the source is
# never moved or deleted.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: csv-local-simple          # unique connector name within the workspace
  connector_type: csv-file        # selects the CSV-file connector implementation
  scopes: [demo]                  # the scope(s) this table is askable in — a scope-bound user needs scope:demo

spec:
  transport:
    kind: local                   # no remote fetch — the path below is on the HUB's filesystem,
                                  # not on yours (mount a volume, or use sftp/s3 / lm csv ingest)
    path: docs/connectors/csv/data/customers.csv   # plain path = single file

  parser:
    has_header: true              # first row holds column names; they drive target column mapping

  after_process: none             # leave the source file untouched after ingestion

The hub reads the manifest's path:, on its own disk. On the self-host stack, copy the sample file into the hub's container, then set path: /tmp/customers.csv in your copy of the manifest:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml cp docs/connectors/csv/data/customers.csv hub:/tmp/customers.csv

A hub in dev mode reads the repository path as it is. From the repository root:

$ lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
✓ 10-local-simple.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
Applied connector "csv-local-simple" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run csv-local-simple
run scheduled: 2e37cb12-0a66-4c4c-a4c2-b796b2d40540

"Scheduled" is not "done" — the result lands in the run ledger a second later:

$ lm run get 2e37cb12
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2e37cb12  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39

STARTED / ENDED are in your terminal's time zone (these screens: Paris, UTC+2); schedule is evaluated in UTC.

What landed in connector.t_csv_local_simple — the header row became the columns:

lumnik=> select row_id, email, signup_date from connector.t_csv_local_simple;
 row_id |    email    | signup_date
--------+-------------+-------------
 1      | alice@x.com | 02/06/2026
 2      | bob@x.com   | 15/01/2026
(2 rows)

Run it again on the unchanged file, then once more after a third line is appended:

$ lm run list --connector csv-local-simple
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2565ea5a  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
52d1ac0b  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
2e37cb12  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
  • A file already read is not read again — the second run says IN 0, and lm run get adds • 1 file(s) unchanged since they were last read — not read again. A file that changed (replaced in place, or grown) is read again in full: the third run says IN 3, even when the copy kept the file's size and date.
  • The table deduplicates: after three runs it holds 3 rows, not 5.
  • SKIPPED and DEAD-LETTERS are explained below.

docs.title: The three transports
docs.text:
The manifest's transport: block picks one:

local sftp s3 files are on the hub's filesystem a remote server a bucket selected by path or glob path or glob prefix + suffix a new run reads one file: when it changed. A glob: new names sorting after the last one read files modified since the last run files modified since the last run after_process none only all four all four credentials — key_env or password_env access_key_env / secret_key_env

docs.title: Local — the hub's disk, not yours
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: local
  path: /imports/*.csv        # glob OK
  • The path is on the hub's filesystem. The self-host stack mounts nothing: mount a volume, use sftp/s3, or upload one file with lm csv ingest.
  • Glob: * and ? only, in the final filename segment — /imports/*/x.csv never matches, and there is no **.
  • No name is excluded implicitly — use *.csv to keep .tmp files out.
  • A path that matches nothing is not an error: the run completes with IN 0.
  • A path without * or ? names one file, and that file is the whole table — see full refresh.

A drop folder, run by run. A 1 200-row export 2026-09-01-orders.csv, then two more files:

$ lm run list --connector orders-drop
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b159e727  orders-drop  default   Completed  0     0     0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
393a2729  orders-drop  default   Completed  10    10    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
165a4c6d  orders-drop  default   Completed  0     0     0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
ff5b8f80  orders-drop  default   Completed  1200  1200  0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
run the folder holds IN why 1 2026-09-01 (1 200 rows) 1 200 first read 2 the same file 0 already read in full 3 plus 2026-09-02 (10 rows) 10 only the new file — it sorts after the last file read 4 plus 2026-08-31 (5 rows) 0 it sorts before the last file read — never read

Drop-folder contract: names must grow lexically

A run resumes after the last file it read, in name order. Name incoming files monotonically (date-prefixed: 2026-07-25-orders.csv), or use sftp/s3, which track modification time instead.

  • Have the producer write under a name the glob does not match (.tmp), then rename it.
  • Archive a file only after its run is Completed.

docs.title: SFTP — a remote folder, a secret, a fingerprint
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: sftp
  host: sftp.example.com
  port: 22                    # optional, default 22
  user: lumnik
  path: /erp-export/*.csv     # glob OK
  password_env: SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD           # OR key_env (the PEM private key) — one is required
  host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc"  # required unless strict_host_key: false
  # strict_host_key: true     # the default — refuses unless the fingerprint above matches
# spec level, next to transport:
after_process: archive
archive_path: /archive/       # default /archive/; required when after_process: move

Credentials are never inline. key_env / password_env name a secret stored with lm secret; an OS env var of that name is the fallback:

$ lm secret set SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD
Value for SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD:
Created secret "SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD"

A manifest with neither credential is refused:

$ lm validate -f sftp-nocred.yaml
✗ sftp-nocred.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.transport
          SFTP transport requires key_env or password_env
          → Use `lm secret set <NAME> ...` then reference via key_env: <NAME>

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f sftp-nocred.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

One session per run. Your server sees one SSH connection per running endpoint, for the whole run. Mind its idle timeout and its limit on concurrent sessions.

The host key is verified. With strict_host_key: true (the default), host_key_fingerprint must match what the server presents. Here a wrong fingerprint is declared:

$ lm run get b31b1efe
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b31b1efe  sftp-badkey  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-06 22:13  2026-09-06 22:13
✖ run failed: SFTP host key refused for sftp.example.com:22 — the server presented SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc, and it does not match the declared SHA256:0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000. Confirm that fingerprint out of band (ssh-keyscan -p 22 sftp.example.com | ssh-keygen -lf -), then set host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc" in the transport block. Setting strict_host_key: false connects without checking at all — which accepts an impostor as readily as the real server.
  • Confirm the presented fingerprint out of band (the ssh-keyscan | ssh-keygen -lf - line, from a machine you trust), then paste it.
  • strict_host_key: false skips the check: an impostor would receive the password and feed rows. Use it only for a throwaway container whose key changes at every restart — as the demo manifest 30-sftp-key.yaml does.

A wrong password, or a user who cannot read the folder:

$ lm run get 22957eeb
ID        CONNECTOR                    ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
22957eeb  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-04 14:23  2026-09-04 14:23
✖ run failed: SFTP error (SSH_FX_PERMISSION_DENIED): Permission denied

A file is read once while it is unchanged; one rewritten later (newer modification time) is read again, even under the same name and at the same size. Oldest first; a run that finds nothing new reads nothing. Zero-byte files are never listed — never ingested, never archived:

$ lm run list --connector sftp-c-bpartner-credentials
ID        CONNECTOR                    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN     OUT    SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a9533cb5  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  0      0      0        0             2026-09-06 22:09  2026-09-06 22:09
80032250  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  6      5      1        1             2026-09-04 15:27  2026-09-04 15:27
8358fb91  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  19009  19009  0        0             2026-09-04 14:40  2026-09-04 14:41

docs.title: S3 — a prefix in a bucket (AWS, MinIO, R2, GCS S3-compat)
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: s3
  bucket: acme-exports         # required
  prefix: billing/             # optional key prefix filter, default ""
  suffix: .csv                 # optional filename filter, default "" (no filter)
  region: eu-west-3            # optional, default eu-west-3
  endpoint: http://minio:9000  # optional — only for non-AWS S3
  access_key_env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID       # optional, default AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  secret_key_env: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   # optional, default AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  archive_bucket: acme-archive # optional, for after_process archive|move (default: source bucket)
  archive_prefix: archive/     # optional, default archive/
  • billing/ + .csv reads billing/2026-09-01.csv and ignores billing/2026-09-01.csv.tmp.
  • Same rule as SFTP: an object is read when new or rewritten, oldest first; zero-byte objects are skipped.
  • access_key_env / secret_key_env are secret names (lm secret set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID). A rotated key takes effect at the next run.

One export, archived after commit — the manifest of the S3 how-to:

$ lm run list --connector s3-c-bpartner
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN     OUT    SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ee860da1  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  10     5      5        5             2026-09-06 16:30  2026-09-06 16:30
dda81fcb  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  0      0      0        0             2026-09-06 16:21  2026-09-06 16:21
7329d11d  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  19009  19009  0        0             2026-09-06 16:03  2026-09-06 16:03
  • 16:03 — the 19 009-row export, read and archived.
  • 16:21 — nothing new under billing/ (the file is in the archive bucket now): IN 0.
  • 16:30 — a 10-record file, half malformed on purpose: 5 rows in, 5 dead-lettered.

docs.title: Parser
docs.text:
parser:
  delimiter: ","                # optional, auto-detected if absent
  encoding: UTF-8               # optional, auto-detected if absent
  has_header: true              # default true
  bom_strip: true               # default true
  null_values: ["", "NULL", "null", "#N/A"]  # default as shown
  columns: [code, name, email]  # REQUIRED when has_header: false; ignored otherwise
  lines: false                  # true: one line = one row, one column `line` (fixed width, logs)
  • The encoding and the delimiter are guessed per file. Declare delimiter or encoding when the guess is wrong.

  • Headerless files need names, in file order ("\t" is a tab in YAML):

    parser:
  delimiter: "\t"
  has_header: false
  columns: [c_bpartner_id, name, created, isactive]

    Without columns:

    $ lm validate -f hl.yaml
✗ hl.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.parser.columns
          columns is required when has_header: false — headerless rows need names
          → Add parser.columns: [code, name, ...] in file order

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f hl.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

  • A fixed-width file (positions, not separators: mainframe extracts, bank or payroll files) is read one line per row with lines: true. Each line lands in one column, line. Then regex-extract cuts it by position. The file:

    E00001Martin Claire                 0003250.00
E00002Dupont Jean                   0002980.50
E00003Nguyen Linh                   0004100.00

    The manifest's parser and mapping:

      parser:
    lines: true
  mapping:
    cell:
      - regex-extract:                     # employee 6, name 30, salary 10
          column: line
          pattern: "^(.{6})(.{30})(.{10})"
          groups: { 1: employee, 2: name, 3: salary }
      - clean: { columns: [employee, name, salary], strip: true }
      - parse-number: { column: salary, decimal-separator: "." }

    What lands:

    lumnik=> select employee, name, salary from connector.t_payroll;
 employee |     name      |  salary
----------+---------------+-----------
 E00001   | Martin Claire | 3250.0000
 E00002   | Dupont Jean   | 2980.5000
 E00003   | Nguyen Linh   | 4100.0000
(3 rows)

    lines: true refuses delimiter and has_header. Full example: docs/connectors/csv/73-lines-fixed-width.yaml.

  • An empty value is a present column. 1, against two columns is written, the second value null (because "" is in null_values; override the list to keep "").

docs.title: Malformed rows — the per-row DLQ
docs.text:
A malformed row never fails the file. It goes to the dead-letter queue (DLQ), reason MalformedSource, and the run continues. A 6-row file with two bad rows:

"c_bpartner_id","name"
1004194,"DUPONT SARL"
1019809,"MARTIN"
BADROW,"trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch"
1030001,"LAMBERT & FILS"
BADROW2
1030002,"NAUTILUS SAS"

$ lm run get 0a4af97d
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
0a4af97d  csv-malformed  default   Completed  6   4    2        2             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
⚠ 2 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
$ lm dlq list --run 0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
ID        CONNECTOR      RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  RESOLUTION  MESSAGE
556c4da1  csv-malformed  0a4af97d  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:6 — Record …
a2867c28  csv-malformed  0a4af97d  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:4 — Record …

The entry keeps every raw value, with the file and line:

$ lm dlq get a2867c28
ID:        a2867c28-0424-44f7-86dd-77f3a0d86872
Connector: csv-malformed (434507c6-df49-4a09-a59f-dfb5df0589e9)
Run:       0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:4 — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared
Detail:    {"file":"/tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv","line":4,"message":"Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared"}
Payload:   {"raw":["BADROW","trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch"],"file":"/tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv","line":4}
Resolution: open

Malformed = the value count differs from the declared columns, in either direction:

the row against 2 declared columns result BADROW,"trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch" 3 values DLQ — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared BADROW2 1 value DLQ — Record has 1 value but 2 columns are declared 1, 2 values, one empty written, name is null 1,2, 3 values — a trailing delimiter is one column too many DLQ 3,"open (unclosed quote) swallows the rest of the file DLQ — one entry; the lines after it are never rows
  • An extra value is never dropped to make the row fit.
  • A trailing delimiter on every line sends the whole file to the DLQ — strip it producer-side.
  • SKIPPED and DEAD-LETTERS move together for malformed rows.
  • Fix the export, run again, then close each entry: Diagnosing a failed run.
  • Rows a validate-row hook drops land here too, reason ValidationFailed.

docs.title: One file is the table — full refresh
docs.text:
A local path with no * or ? names one file, and that file is the table's whole state. A run that reads it to the end and succeeds removes the rows the file no longer holds.

transport:
  kind: local
  path: /imports/articles.csv    # one file: full refresh
after_process: none
refresh:
  max_removed: 30%               # the default — off, or 100%, lifts the guard

Ten articles, then A07 deleted from the file:

$ lm run get 2a1c346f
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2a1c346f  articles   default   Completed  9   9    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
• 1 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them

The removed count sits outside IN = OUT + SKIPPED: the run never read those rows.

Four guards: the run fails and nothing is removed. The next run reads the whole file again.

  • The table would shrink by more than refresh.max_removed (30% unless declared). A truncated export looks exactly like a purge. Here the file is cut to 4 lines; the purge is real, so the threshold is raised:
$ lm run get d4fa0d53
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
d4fa0d53  articles   default   Failed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
✖ run failed: 5 of 9 rows would be removed: the file holds 4 where the table held 9, more than refresh.max_removed (30%) allows — nothing was removed. If the file really lost them, raise refresh.max_removed (or set it to off) and run again.
$ tail -3 articles.yaml
  after_process: none
  refresh:
    max_removed: 60%
$ lm apply -f articles.yaml
Applied connector "articles" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run articles
run scheduled: 54de3ded-1939-449a-bd99-73eb36813a1d
$ lm run get 54de3ded
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
54de3ded  articles   default   Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
• 5 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them
  • A row of the file went to the dead letters while rows would be removed: its last good version stays. A row a validate-row hook drops counts the same way.
$ lm run get 08cb8fb5
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
08cb8fb5  articles   default   Failed  4   3    1        1             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 08cb8fb5-286b-4fe0-84bd-eafec50d10f5
✖ run failed: 1 row(s) of the file went to the dead letters this run (lm dlq list --run 08cb8fb5-286b-4fe0-84bd-eafec50d10f5): a full refresh removes nothing while a row of the file is in the dead letters, whatever its reason (unreadable, dropped by validate-row…) — nothing was removed. Fix the cause each dead letter reports (lm dlq get <id>) and run again.
  • An empty file (a header and no rows) never empties the table:
$ lm run get 4f61dcf3
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
4f61dcf3  articles   default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
✖ run failed: the file is empty: a full refresh never empties a table from an empty file — nothing was removed. If the source really is empty, delete the connector's data instead (lm connector delete).

The guards speak only when rows would be removed. A dead letter on a new row, with nothing to remove, completes as usual (IN 5 OUT 4 DEAD-LETTERS 1).

A changed row is not a removed row. The run writes its new version and drops the old one. The file still holds the row, so the run does not count it as removed, and the guard sees no shrink. Ten articles, then the price of A03 changed:

$ lm run get dd0a52c4
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
dd0a52c4  articles   default   Completed  10  10   0        0             2026-10-25 11:17  2026-10-25 11:17  yes

The removed count is how much the table shrank. The rows have no key, so a row lost while another is added looks like a changed row, and is not counted.

What never removes a row:

the run why finds the file unchanged it is not read again reads a glob (*.csv) a drop folder only adds reads an sftp or s3 transport each file is read when new or rewritten; nothing is compared

A refresh block on a drop folder is flagged:

$ lm validate -f drop.yaml
! drop.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.refresh
          refresh is read only for one local file (transport kind: local, a path without * or ?): this source is a drop folder and never removes rows, so the block does nothing here
          → Remove the refresh block, or point transport.path at the one file that holds the table

A removed row also leaves the entities fused from it, lm ask, and any Search index over them.

docs.title: Scheduling & lifecycle
docs.text:
• schedule — optional cron, 5 fields, in UTC (0 6 * * * = daily at 06:00 UTC), checked at apply. The hub fires it — no OS cron. A re-apply without schedule unschedules the connector. window: "22:00-06:00" (UTC, end exclusive) fences scheduled runs.
  • after_process — required. What happens to a file once its rows are committed:
none archive move delete does leaves the file in place relocates it relocates it — same action, archive_path mandatory removes it sftp ✓ → archive_path (default /archive/) → archive_path ✓ s3 ✓ → archive_bucket/archive_prefix (defaults: source bucket, archive/) same ✓ local ✓ refused refused refused
  • The archived name carries the file's modification time: livraisons.csv read with its mtime at 16:35:44 UTC on 22 October 2026 is archived as livraisons.20261022T163544Z.csv. An export that drops the same name every night keeps one archive per night; none replaces another. A source with sub-second times keeps them: on s3, livraisons.20261022T163544.047Z.csv.
  • Only the version that was read is archived. Have the producer write under a name the glob does not match, then rename it in.
  • A file that cannot be archived is said on the run — an archive folder the user cannot write, say. The file was read; it stays in the source folder, and lm run get says so:
• 1 file(s) read but not archived — still in the source folder (after_process failed; see the hub log)

On a local transport, only after_process: none is accepted.

A file is archived only after its rows are in the table (sftp/s3).

A misspelled key is flagged, and the manifest still applies. Inside mapping, a misspelt tier is refused.

$ lm validate -f typo.yaml
! typo.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.windo
          unknown key — ignored by the runtime
          → Remove it, or check the spelling

docs.title: Target table
docs.text:
• One table per connector, connector.t_<name>, columns from the header (or parser.columns).
  • Reserved column names: id, _row_hash, _ingested_at, _source, _run_id, _mapping_version, tenant_id, and _seen_run on a one-file table. A source column with one of these names is refused: rename it with map-columns.
  • Two identical lines are one row. OUT counts the lines; the table holds distinct rows.

  • target.indexes declares Postgres indexes — { columns: [...], unique: <bool> } (unique defaults to false); a malformed entry fails validation:

    target:
  indexes:
    - { columns: [email], unique: true }
    - { columns: [bpartner_id, dateordered] }

  • The business scope is on the connector: metadata.scopes (see Scopes); the validator warns when none is declared.

  • lm connector delete removes the connector's rows, its run history and its RAG chunks (the table goes with the last connector writing into it):

    $ lm connector delete csv-local-simple --dry-run
Would delete connector csv-local-simple (csv-file) — 3 rows of connector.t_csv_local_simple, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)

  • lm endpoint purge refuses a csv-file endpoint. Delete the connector instead.

docs.title: Transform at ingestion
docs.text:
An optional mapping block repairs legacy data as it flows in — dataset → row → cell hooks, in that order, on every connector run:

mapping:
  cell:
    - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name, city] }      # "BÃ©nÃ©dict" → "Bénédict"

Every hook, by business problem: Transformers. A value a hook cannot read is emptied, the row is still written, and the run counts it in cell_errors.

docs.title: One file, one command: lm csv ingest
docs.text: To look at one export before writing a manifest, lm csv ingest loads it in one command. It does not schedule, transform or set rows aside: One file, one command.

docs.title: Ingest an SFTP folder nightly
docs.text:
1. Store the secret the manifest names:

    $ lm secret set CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD
Value for CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD:
Created secret "CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD"

  2. Apply the manifest — this one targets the docker-compose demo server:

    # 30-sftp-key.yaml — pull CSVs from an SFTP server into the hub.
#   lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/30-sftp-key.yaml
#   lm connector run csv-sftp
#
# Credentials are never inline: `password_env` names a secret stored with `lm secret set`.
# Use `key_env` instead for an SSH key (the value is the private key).
#
# Each run reads only the files that are new or rewritten since the last run.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: csv-sftp
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [demo]

spec:
  transport:
    kind: sftp
    host: localhost
    port: 2222                       # the dev compose 'sftp' service; from a hub in Docker,
                                     # use host.docker.internal
    user: csvuser
    path: /upload/seed/*.csv         # glob on the remote side (seed/ subdir from the read-only mount)
    password_env: CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD  # the secret's name, never the password itself
    strict_host_key: false           # DEMO ONLY: this test server gets a new host key at every
                                     # restart. Against a real server, drop this line and declare
                                     # host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:…" instead. Without the check,
                                     # an impostor server would receive the password.

  parser:
    has_header: true

  after_process: none              # archive | delete | move | none (leave the file in place)

  3. lm connector run csv-sftp reads every file under /upload/seed/*.csv. Once it looks right, add schedule: "0 6 * * *", and after_process: archive with an archive_path.

Watch it in the TUI (CLI & TUI): :runs for the run's status, :dlq for rejected rows.

docs.title: Ingest a headerless export under an S3 prefix, and archive it
docs.text:
# 45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml — a headerless, tab-separated ERP export under an S3 prefix,
# archived to another bucket once its rows are committed.
#   lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml
#   lm apply    -f docs/connectors/csv/45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml
#   lm connector run s3-c-bpartner
#
# No `endpoint:` → real AWS; set `region` to the region the bucket lives in (the default is eu-west-3).
# `access_key_env` / `secret_key_env` name secrets stored with `lm secret set`, never the values.
# `has_header: false` makes `parser.columns` mandatory — the names, in file order.
# `after_process: archive` moves each file to `archive_bucket`/`archive_prefix` once its rows are
# in the table; the next run then finds nothing new and reads 0 rows.
# Walk-through: docs/connectors/csv.md.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: s3-c-bpartner
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [s3-scenario]

spec:
  transport:
    kind: s3
    bucket: lumnik-exports
    prefix: billing/
    region: us-east-1
    suffix: .csv
    access_key_env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    secret_key_env: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    archive_bucket: lumnik-archive
    archive_prefix: archive/

  parser:
    delimiter: "\t"
    has_header: false
    columns: [c_bpartner_id, name, created, isactive]

  after_process: archive

Result: the run ledger above — 19 009 rows on the first run, IN 0 on the next because the file is in lumnik-archive now. Column 1 lands as c_bpartner_id, column 2 as name, and so on. For MinIO or another S3-compatible store, add endpoint: — see 40-s3-prefix.yaml in docs/connectors/csv/.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix SFTP host key refused for host:22 — the server presented SHA256:… host_key_fingerprint absent or wrong, with strict_host_key: true (the default) confirm the presented fingerprint out of band (ssh-keyscan -p 22 HOST \| ssh-keygen -lf -), paste it into host_key_fingerprint SFTP error (SSH_FX_PERMISSION_DENIED): Permission denied wrong password/key, or the user cannot read path lm secret list, then lm secret set <NAME> (a private key is many lines — pipe it with <NAME> -); check the folder's rights SFTP transport requires key_env or password_env neither credential declared lm secret set <NAME>, then password_env: <NAME> or key_env: <NAME> S3 403 Forbidden invalid S3 credentials check the secrets named by access_key_env / secret_key_env columns is required when has_header: false a headerless parser without names parser.columns: [a, b, …] in file order after_process: archive is not executed on local connector runs a relocation on a local transport after_process: none, or an sftp/s3 transport … is not read by connector runs file_filter, pre_process, post_process or max_file_size in a connector manifest drop the key run Failed: connector.t_… is already written by connector '…' another connector of the tenant already writes the table named after this one apply it under another metadata.name, then lm connector delete the refused one — see JDBC run completes with IN 0 nothing new — or the local path matches nothing on the hub's disk lm connector get NAME shows the path (config.transport.path); check it exists on the hub a file dropped in a local folder is never read its name sorts before the last file read (drop-folder contract) name incoming files monotonically, or switch to sftp/s3 run Failed: The cursor's file … is gone, but files sorting after it are waiting a file was archived before the run that read it completed lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint>; archive only after Completed DEAD-LETTERS > 0, reason MalformedSource value count differs from the declared columns — trailing delimiter, unclosed quote lm dlq get ID shows the raw values, file and line; fix the export or parser: rows missing, DLQ empty filter-where / skip-empty-rows excluded them (counted in SKIPPED) see Transformers § Troubleshooting a mapped column is blank for some rows a parse-* or lookup hook nulled a value it could not read cell_errors on lm run get <id> — see the reference run Failed: N of M rows would be removed: the file holds … the one local file lost more rows than refresh.max_removed allows check the file; for a real purge raise refresh.max_removed (or off), re-apply, run again — see full refresh run Failed: the file is empty: a full refresh never empties a table the one local file holds a header and no row fix the export; to empty the table, lm connector delete run Failed: N row(s) of the file went to the dead letters this run a line of the one local file could not be read lm dlq list --run <id>, fix the export, run again run Failed: the file changed while this run was reading it the producer rewrote the file mid-run run again; have the producer write elsewhere and rename the file in rows gone from a local table after a run the file no longer holds them lm run get <id> says N row(s) removed; to keep history, ingest a folder (*.csv) a source column shares a reserved column name one of the reserved columns rename it with map-columns
