docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
Ingest a GraphQL API by putting the query in the manifest — a request shape on the REST engine (connector_type stays rest-generic), with Relay pagination required.

Type rest-generic (shape graphql) Protocol GraphQL over POST Target ext.* hybrid Schedulable cron Edition Open

Auth, retry, rate limiting and the hybrid JSONB + typed storage are all shared with REST. This page covers what is different: the query, Relay pagination, and what happens when the server answers 200 and still says no.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The screens below read the demo API that ships with the repo — the same one the REST page uses, under its POST /graphql shape. Start it, and put its key in the registry:

python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/acme-api.py
lm secret set ACME_API_KEY        # demo-key

# 70-graphql-relay.yaml — GraphQL is a request shape of the REST connector.
#
# `connector_type` stays rest-generic. The request is a POST carrying {"query", "variables"} to
# one URL; the cursor rides in `variables`.
#
# A graphql endpoint must declare `kind: relay` with `cursor_binding: variable`. Both are refused
# at apply otherwise.
#
# Relay puts the rows under edges[].node and the paging state under pageInfo:
#   cursor_path    → $.data.partners.pageInfo.endCursor
#   has_more_path  → $.data.partners.pageInfo.hasNextPage
#   response_path  → $.data.partners.edges[*].node
#   cursor_var     → after — the name of $after in the query, without the $
#
# Page size lives in the query (`first: 500`).
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in ext.acme_graphql_partners.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-graphql
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099
  graphql_path: /graphql

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          partners(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id name city credit_limit } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.partners.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.partners.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.partners.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_graphql_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name,         path: "$.name",         type: text }
          - { name: city,         path: "$.city",         type: text }
          - { name: credit_limit, path: "$.credit_limit", type: bigint }

$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/rest/demo/70-graphql-relay.yaml
Applied connector "acme-graphql" — 1 endpoint
$ lm source rest test acme-graphql
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
partners  POST    200     500    ok

The pre-flight sends the request a run sends (POST): one page, 500 nodes, nothing written.

$ lm connector run acme-graphql
run scheduled: f26868f0-641e-471a-8719-e6c4c2957fee
$ lm run list --connector acme-graphql
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
f26868f0  acme-graphql  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
Field Where Required Notes graphql_path spec no The single POST endpoint; requests go to base_url + graphql_path (default /graphql) kind: graphql endpoint no An endpoint carrying a query is treated as GraphQL either way — the examples declare it for readability query endpoint yes The query document; declare the cursor variable it expects (e.g. $after) variables endpoint no Static variables sent with every request; the relay cursor is injected on top pagination endpoint yes Hard rule: kind: relay with cursor_binding: variable — anything else is refused at apply cursor_var pagination yes The variable that receives endCursor (e.g. after) cursor_path, has_more_path, response_path pagination yes JSONPaths to endCursor, hasNextPage and the node list target endpoint yes The same hybrid target as REST: table, unique_key, promote incremental endpoint no mode: watermark sends the mark as the variable named by param — see Incremental

path and method are implicit — the request is always a POST to graphql_path.

  • In the query the variable carries its sigil ($after); cursor_var: after names it without.

  • There is no page-size field: page size is in the query itself (first: 500 above).

  • The rows that land are the nodes, without the edges wrapper.

  • A graphql endpoint must declare kind: relay with cursor_binding: variable. lm apply refuses anything else, and shows the block to write.

docs.title: The two ways a GraphQL server says no on HTTP 200
docs.text:
A GraphQL server may answer 200 with an errors array, or with "data": null. Both are refused — by lm source rest test before any run:

$ lm source rest test acme-graphql-errors
ENDPOINT      METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
errors-array  POST    200     0      GraphQL response carried 1 error(s); first: Cannot query field 'boom' on type 'Query'
null-data     POST    200     0      GraphQL response has no errors and null/absent data (malformed envelope): {"data": null}
Error: 2 of 2 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data

and by a run, with the same message:

# 80-graphql-errors.yaml — the two ways a GraphQL server says no on HTTP 200.
#
# GraphQL does not use status codes to report a failed query. A server that cannot resolve a
# field answers 200 with an `errors` array; one whose resolver blew up answers 200 with
# `"data": null`. Read as transport, both are successes — and a run that reads them as data
# ingests nothing and completes green.
#
# Both endpoints below must FAIL, and `lm source rest test acme-graphql-errors` must refuse
# them before any run is started.
#
# The demo API triggers them from the query text: a query mentioning `boom` gets the errors
# array, one mentioning `nullData` gets the null envelope.
#
# Expect: both endpoints Failed, each naming what came back.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-graphql-errors
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099
  graphql_path: /graphql

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY

  endpoints:
    - id: errors-array
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          boom(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.boom.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.boom.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.boom.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_gql_errors
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

    - id: null-data
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          nullData(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.nullData.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.nullData.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.nullData.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_gql_nulldata
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-graphql-errors
ID        CONNECTOR            ENDPOINT      STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2ca12c44  acme-graphql-errors  null-data     Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45
84f519e9  acme-graphql-errors  errors-array  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45

$ lm run get 84f519e9
ID        CONNECTOR            ENDPOINT      STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
84f519e9  acme-graphql-errors  errors-array  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45
✖ run failed: GraphQL response carried 1 error(s); first: Cannot query field 'boom' on type 'Query'

Nothing is ingested and nothing is dead-lettered. Fix the query, or the permission it needs, and run again.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: spec.headers[] applies to every request, as for REST request headers.

docs.title: Incremental: the mark rides in a variable
docs.text:
On a graphql endpoint, incremental.param names a GraphQL variable. The stored mark is sent in the request's variables, on every page of the run:

endpoints:
  - id: partners
    kind: graphql
    query: |
      query($after: String, $updated_since: String) {
        partners(first: 500, after: $after, updatedSince: $updated_since) {
          edges { cursor node { id name updated_at } }
          pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
        }
      }
    incremental:
      mode: watermark
      param: updated_since              # the variable, without the $
      watermark_path: "$.updated_at"
  • The query must declare the variable. lm apply refuses a param the query does not declare.
  • Declare it nullable (String, not String!). The first run has no mark yet and sends none.
  • The server filters on it. The demo API reads $updated_since and returns the partners changed at or after it.

The demo's acme-graphql with this incremental block (and updated_at added to the node), run twice:

$ lm run get 0e15e816
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
0e15e816  acme-graphql-inc  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-25 11:16  2026-10-25 11:16  yes
$ lm run get beb5aab8
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
beb5aab8  acme-graphql-inc  partners  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-25 11:16  2026-10-25 11:16  yes

The second run asks only from the mark. It reads a little before it, by the length of the previous run: a change during a run.

docs.title: Not yet supported
docs.text: Mutations, subscriptions, schema-introspection discovery, persisted queries, query batching, per-endpoint header overrides.

docs.title: Send static variables with every request
docs.text:
endpoints:
  - id: partners
    kind: graphql
    variables: { locale: fr-FR }   # merged into every request

Result: every request carries locale: fr-FR in its GraphQL variables, beside the relay cursor.

docs.title: Read a second collection from the same API
docs.text: Add a second endpoint with its own query, its own pagination paths (they name the collection: $.data.<collection>.pageInfo.endCursor) and its own table. One connector, one API, one credential; the ledger records one run per endpoint.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture Run fails though the HTTP status was 200 an errors[] array, or data: null with no errors read the message in lm run get — it carries the server's first error verbatim Run completed with IN 0 response_path does not match the envelope lm source rest test <connector> prints the item count it read from one page cursor_binding: variable refused at apply that binding is only valid on relay on a graphql endpoint use query or header binding on a plain REST endpoint Pagination never ends cursor_path resolves to a value that does not change it must point at pageInfo.endCursor, the opaque cursor the server hands back

docs.title: JDBC
docs.text:
Read tables from a live PostgreSQL or Oracle database into hub tables — the whole table once, then only what changed, on a schedule.

Type jdbc-generic Dialect postgres — Open; oracle — Pro only Target connector.t_<table>, or connector.t_<target> Schedulable cron Edition Open for PostgreSQL. Oracle ships only in lumnik Pro — see Oracle

The connection is read-only: every query this connector issues is a SELECT.

docs.title: Quickstart — one table, three commands, a look at the ledger
docs.text:
# 10-full-dump.yaml — the whole table, once, then only what is inserted after it.
#
# `mode: full` pages through the table by primary key and remembers the last key it read.
# The next run continues past that key: new rows arrive, rows changed in place do not.
# Switch this same connector to `20-watermark.yaml` to pick up changes too.
#
# The source tables are created by data/demo-source.sql in the hub's own PostgreSQL, so the
# page can be replayed with nothing but the self-host stack. LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD is
# already exported where the hub runs; a real base names its own variable.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-invoices
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  defaults:
    schema: demo

  source:
    tables:
      - name: invoices
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [invoice_id]

The screens on this page read a demo source in the hub's own PostgreSQL — four tables and a view — so they replay on the self-host stack alone. Create it first:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec -T postgres psql -U lumnik -d lumnik < docs/connectors/jdbc/data/demo-source.sql
What that script creates 
-- demo-source.sql — the source tables the JDBC page's screens read.
--
-- They live in the hub's OWN PostgreSQL so the page can be replayed with nothing but the
-- self-host stack (`deploy/selfhost/up.sh`). A real integration points at the ERP instead;
-- nothing else in the manifests changes.
--
--   docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec -T postgres psql -U lumnik -d lumnik < docs/connectors/jdbc/data/demo-source.sql
--
-- The two GRANTs are the only ones a lumnik connection user ever needs: USAGE on the schema,
-- SELECT on the tables. Nothing in the jdbc connector writes to a source.

CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS demo;

-- The view goes first: it reads demo.invoices, and Postgres refuses to drop a table a view
-- depends on — so a second run of this script would stop here.
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS demo.v_open_invoices;

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS demo.invoices;
CREATE TABLE demo.invoices (
    invoice_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    customer   text           NOT NULL,
    total      numeric(12,2)  NOT NULL,
    status     text           NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamp      NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO demo.invoices VALUES
    (1001, 'Northwind Ltd', 1250.00, 'paid',    '2026-09-01 09:15:00'),
    (1002, 'Contoso SA',     480.50, 'open',    '2026-09-01 11:40:00'),
    (1003, 'Fabrikam Oy',   2310.75, 'open',    '2026-09-02 08:05:00'),
    (1004, 'Adventure BV',   199.90, 'draft',   '2026-09-02 16:20:00');

-- A table whose primary key is called `id` — one of the seven names the hub reserves on its
-- own tables. See "Reserved column names" on the page.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS demo.price_list;
CREATE TABLE demo.price_list (
    id    bigint PRIMARY KEY,
    sku   text    NOT NULL,
    price numeric(10,2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO demo.price_list VALUES
    (1, 'PUMP-075', 349.00),
    (2, 'HOSE-32M',  59.90),
    (3, 'FILT-A1',  129.50);

-- Two more tables for the guided flow: `warehouses` is the one it adds, `audit_log` has no
-- primary key, which is what the guided add refuses.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS demo.warehouses;
CREATE TABLE demo.warehouses (
    warehouse_id integer PRIMARY KEY,
    code         text      NOT NULL,
    city         text      NOT NULL,
    updated_at   timestamp NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO demo.warehouses VALUES
    (1, 'W-LYS', 'Lyon',      '2026-09-01 08:00:00'),
    (2, 'W-MRS', 'Marseille', '2026-09-03 08:00:00');

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS demo.audit_log;
CREATE TABLE demo.audit_log (
    at     timestamp NOT NULL,
    actor  text,
    action text
);

INSERT INTO demo.audit_log VALUES ('2026-09-01 06:00:00', 'system', 'boot');

-- A COMPOSITE primary key: 100 orders of seven lines each, 700 rows. `pk_columns` is read
-- whole, so the pair (order_id, line_no) is what the reader orders and resumes on and no
-- order is split by a chunk boundary. See "Per-table keys" on the page.
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS demo.order_lines;
CREATE TABLE demo.order_lines (
    order_id integer NOT NULL,
    line_no  integer NOT NULL,
    sku      text,
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, line_no)
);

INSERT INTO demo.order_lines
SELECT o, l, 'SKU-' || o || '-' || l
FROM generate_series(1, 100) AS o, generate_series(1, 7) AS l;

-- The view the page reads in "Reading a view": the invoices that are not paid.
CREATE VIEW demo.v_open_invoices AS
    SELECT invoice_id, customer, total, updated_at FROM demo.invoices WHERE status <> 'paid';

GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA demo TO lumnik_readonly;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA demo TO lumnik_readonly;
ANALYZE demo.invoices;
ANALYZE demo.price_list;
ANALYZE demo.warehouses;
ANALYZE demo.audit_log;
ANALYZE demo.order_lines;

Then, from the repository root:

$ lm validate -f docs/connectors/jdbc/10-full-dump.yaml
✓ 10-full-dump.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/jdbc/10-full-dump.yaml
Applied connector "demo-invoices" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run demo-invoices
run scheduled: d36a90a0-c658-4335-baa4-d63f685b59e0

"Scheduled" is not "done" — the run ledger is where the result lands:

$ lm run list --connector demo-invoices
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
d36a90a0  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

STARTED / ENDED print in your terminal's time zone (these screens: Paris, UTC+2). schedule is evaluated in UTC.

What landed in connector.t_invoices — every source column:

 invoice_id |   customer    |   total   | status |       updated_at
------------+---------------+-----------+--------+------------------------
       1001 | Northwind Ltd | 1250.0000 | paid   | 2026-09-01 09:15:00+00
       1002 | Contoso SA    |  480.5000 | open   | 2026-09-01 11:40:00+00
       1003 | Fabrikam Oy   | 2310.7500 | open   | 2026-09-02 08:05:00+00
       1004 | Adventure BV  |  199.9000 | draft  | 2026-09-02 16:20:00+00
  • jdbc-generic is a 1:1 dump. There is no column filter; rename: is the only per-column knob. To read fewer columns or rows, read a view.
  • There is no mapping block. Transformers and Kotlin scripts run on a csv-file connector. A mapping: here is refused, so a check you declared cannot be skipped without anyone noticing: spec.mapping — jdbc-generic has no mapping block — rows land as the source holds them, so nothing declared here would run.
  • invoice_id reads 1001, total reads 1250.0000 — see Column types.
  • The password never sits in the manifest. password_env names a variable in the environment where the hub runs (the self-host stack exports the one used here), or an lm secret entry.

docs.title: Two modes — full and watermark
docs.text:
Both modes remember where the last run stopped:

  • mode: full remembers the last primary key it read. The next run continues past it.
  • mode: watermark remembers the last value of a column that moves on every change, plus that row's key. The next run reads everything past that value.
mode: full mode: watermark ordered by primary key watermark column, then primary key a row inserted with a higher key read read a row inserted with a lower key (a backfill) never read read — the insert stamps the column a row updated in place never read again read again a row deleted never noticed never noticed a run with nothing changed 0 rows 0 rows declares pk_columns pk_columns and watermark_column

docs.title: The watermark manifest
docs.text:
The quickstart's connector, read incrementally. mode and watermark_column sit under defaults:, which holds what every table of the connector shares:

# 20-watermark.yaml — the same table, read incrementally on a column that moves on every change.
#
# `updated_at` only ever grows: an INSERT and an UPDATE both arrive, and a run with nothing
# changed reads 0 rows.
#
# Same connector name as 10-full-dump.yaml on purpose. Applied over a table that already ran in
# `full`, it reads the table again once; the hub table does not grow.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-invoices
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  defaults:
    schema: demo
    mode: watermark
    watermark_column: updated_at

  source:
    tables:
      - name: invoices
        pk_columns: [invoice_id]
        indexes:
          - { columns: [customer], unique: false }

  # Uncomment to let the hub poll the source itself. Incremental runs cost one keyset query
  # per table when nothing has changed. Cron times are UTC.
  # schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  # window: "22:00-06:00"

docs.title: The same table, five runs
docs.text:
Runs 1 and 2 use the quickstart manifest; run 3 applies the one above over the same connector.

-- between run 1 and run 2: one insert, one update
INSERT INTO demo.invoices VALUES (1005, 'Tailspin AG', 640.00, 'open', '2026-09-08 07:30:00');
UPDATE demo.invoices SET status = 'paid', updated_at = '2026-09-08 07:45:00' WHERE invoice_id = 1002;

-- between run 3 and run 4: one update
UPDATE demo.invoices SET status = 'paid', updated_at = '2026-09-08 09:10:00' WHERE invoice_id = 1003;

$ lm run list --connector demo-invoices
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
87b4931c  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
5e3330f8  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  1   1    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
772a43f1  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
55bd41b4  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  1   1    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
d36a90a0  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
run mode source change before it IN why d36a90a0 full — 4 first read, no cursor 55bd41b4 full 1 insert, 1 update 1 only the insert — its key sorts past the cursor. The update is invisible to a key cursor 772a43f1 watermark the manifest changed mode 5 the table restarts — see What restarts a table 5e3330f8 watermark 1 update 1 the changed row's updated_at is past the cursor 87b4931c watermark — 0 nothing past the cursor

After run 2 the hub still said invoice 1002 was open while the source said paid: mode: full does not see updates.

docs.title: Which one to declare
docs.text:
• watermark, whenever the source stamps a column that moves on every write. ERPs usually have one: updated_at, updated, modified_at, last_modified.
  • full, for a table that only grows — an append-only ledger, a reference table nobody edits in place.
  • full on a table that is edited in place will not see the edits. Expose a timestamp column on the source, or re-read the table with lm endpoint reset-cursor before each run.

A watermark column that does not move is worse than full

The hub cannot check that the column moves. Two ways to get it wrong, both silent:

  • A column the application forgets to touch on some writes — those changes never reach the hub.
  • A numeric primary key as the watermark. lm source jdbc discover suggests one when it finds no timestamp (see price_list below) — it behaves like mode: full.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
connection:
  url: jdbc:postgresql://db.acme.io:5432/billing   # required
  user: ro_user                                    # required
  password_env: ACME_DB_PASSWORD                   # required — a hub variable, else an lm secret
  dialect: postgres                                # optional, inferred from the url
  zone: Europe/Paris                               # optional, UTC when absent
  • Dialect: PostgreSQL (postgres, alias postgresql) ships with every edition; Oracle (oracle) only with lumnik Pro — see Oracle. A declared dialect that is not installed, or does not accept the URL, fails validation. An absent one is inferred when exactly one installed dialect accepts the URL.
  • Zone: the time zone the database writes its dates-and-times in when it stores no zone with them — see A time without a time zone. An unknown zone fails validation. A connector made by lm source jdbc add has no zone option: it reads such times as UTC.
  • Grants: USAGE on the schema and SELECT on the tables. Nothing more.
  • Reachability is the hub's, not yours. The URL is resolved where the hub runs: a database on your Mac is host.docker.internal for a hub in Docker, not localhost.

docs.title: Where the password comes from
docs.text:
Resolved at run time, first match wins:

Source Notes 1 Attached credential Stored encrypted, created by lm source jdbc add as <source-name>--credential. lm apply never sets one. 2 password in the manifest Plain text, dev and test only. It wins over password_env; lm validate warns. 3 password_env The name of a variable in the hub's environment, else of an lm secret entry. Neither at run time fails the run, naming it.
  • password_env is required by validation even when password is present.
  • Set it with lm secret set ACME_DB_PASSWORD: no hub restart. A variable of the same name in the hub's environment wins.
  • The attached credential is encrypted under LUMNIK_CRYPTO_SECRET_KEY — see Security → Secrets at rest.

The quickstart connector re-applied with password_env: ACME_DB_PASSWORD, a name neither the hub's environment nor lm secret holds:

$ lm connector run demo-invoices
run scheduled: 3570bbf6-29f5-4b1c-99a9-5e6e0aec810e
$ lm run get 3570bbf6
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
3570bbf6  demo-invoices  invoices  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 07:24  2026-10-19 07:24
✖ run failed: password_env 'ACME_DB_PASSWORD' is neither in the server environment nor in lm secret

docs.title: Source — one entry per table
docs.text:
# 40-two-tables.yaml — two tables under one connector, each with its own mode.
#
# Every entry in `source.tables[]` becomes an endpoint, and every endpoint gets its own run
# row in the ledger: one `lm connector run` on this connector produces two rows. `defaults:`
# carries what both tables share; each table overrides what it needs.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-erp
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  defaults:
    schema: demo

  source:
    tables:
      - name: warehouses
        mode: watermark
        watermark_column: updated_at
        pk_columns: [warehouse_id]

      - name: price_list
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [id]
        rename:
          id: price_list_id

Each entry in source.tables[] is an endpoint of the connector:

  • the endpoint name is the table name;
  • one lm connector run runs all of them;
  • each endpoint writes its own row in the run ledger — two rows per run here.
$ lm run list --connector demo-erp
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT    STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
122112a8  demo-erp   price_list  Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
d2eb4159  demo-erp   warehouses  Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
4013a639  demo-erp   price_list  Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
664b8c9b  demo-erp   warehouses  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41

The first run read warehouses (2 rows) and price_list (3); the second found nothing new. ENDPOINT is also the second half of the endpoint commands' address: lm endpoint reset-cursor demo-erp/warehouses.

docs.title: Per-table keys
docs.text:
Key Required What it does name yes The source table. Also names the hub table, connector.t_<name>, unless target does target no Names the hub table connector.t_<target> instead schema yes (here or in defaults) The source schema mode yes full or watermark watermark_column when mode: watermark The column that moves on every change pk_columns yes The paging key and the hub table's key: one row per key. It must be unique together indexes no Postgres indexes to create on the hub table rename no Source column name → hub column name
  • chunk_size is refused; any other key gets a warning, unknown key — ignored by the runtime — see Validation rules.

pk_columns is the paging key, read whole

The reader orders by every entry and resumes on all of them at once. A composite key pages exactly like a single-column one. demo.order_lines is 700 lines over 100 orders, seven each:

# 60-composite-key.yaml — a table whose primary key is two columns.
#
# `pk_columns` must be unique TOGETHER: `order_id` alone is not (700 lines over 100 orders,
# seven lines each). Keep the order of the entries: changing it reads the table again once.
# demo.order_lines is created by data/demo-source.sql.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-lines
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  source:
    tables:
      - name: order_lines
        schema: demo
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [order_id, line_no]

The full read, then a second run that finds nothing:

$ lm run list --connector demo-lines --limit 2
ID        CONNECTOR   ENDPOINT     STATUS     IN   OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a04d56c9  demo-lines  order_lines  Completed  0    0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
17ce005f  demo-lines  order_lines  Completed  700  700  0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
note: result hit the limit of 2 — there may be more
  • The order of the entries is the paging order. Reversing it restarts the table (see What restarts a table).
  • The key must be unique together. lm source jdbc add writes the discovered primary key; a hand-written manifest may not. A run that meets two rows under one key fails, and that read writes nothing. demo.order_lines declared on order_id alone:
$ lm run get 0fdd0a87
ID        CONNECTOR   ENDPOINT     STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
0fdd0a87  demo-lines  order_lines  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
✖ run failed: pk_columns (order_id) does not identify one row of demo.order_lines: two rows share the key where a read ends, and paging past it would skip one — declare the columns of the source table's primary key

docs.title: defaults
docs.text:
defaults: holds fallbacks for every table; a table that declares the same key wins.

  • The merge is per key, not deep: a table's rename: replaces the one in defaults:.
  • mode, watermark_column and schema are the usual ones — see the watermark manifest.

There is no chunk_size setting: lm validate refuses one.

docs.title: The hub table
docs.text:
Rows land in the connector schema as connector.t_<table-name>, one table per source table, created on the first run from the columns the source returned.

The hub table is named after the source table, not the connector

Two connectors of a tenant reading a table of the same name land in the same connector.t_<name>. The second one's run is refused; give it its own hub table with target: — see Two connectors reading a table of the same name.

docs.title: Column types
docs.text:
The hub types each column from the source's declared type:

Source type Hub column smallint, integer, bigint BIGINT real, double precision, numeric, decimal NUMERIC(18,4) timestamp (no time zone) TIMESTAMPTZ, the time read in the connection's zone, UTC without one (below) timestamptz TIMESTAMPTZ, the same instant date DATE boolean, bit BOOLEAN everything else TEXT
  • Oracle has its own list and refuses a column outside it — see Oracle.
  • NUMERIC(18,4) holds at most 14 digits before the point. A wider source column — a 19-digit id declared numeric(20,0) — fails the run with numeric field overflow. Expose it as text through a view: SELECT event_id::text AS event_id, .... A bigint id is not affected.

  • A time without a time zone is read in the connection's zone, UTC when it declares none, wherever the hub runs. A timestamptz keeps its instant. ordered_at is a timestamp at the source, paid_at a timestamptz holding the same instants — read on a hub running in Paris, no zone declared:

     order_id |       ordered_at       |        paid_at
----------+------------------------+------------------------
        1 | 2026-08-02 23:30:00+00 | 2026-08-02 23:30:00+00
        2 | 2026-01-15 23:30:00+00 | 2026-01-15 23:30:00+00

    An ERP that writes Paris time declares it: zone: Europe/Paris under connection. Each time is then read at its own offset, UTC+2 in summer, UTC+1 in winter. A date keeps its day:

     order_id |       ordered_at       |   due_on
----------+------------------------+------------
        1 | 2026-08-02 21:30:00+00 | 2026-08-02
        2 | 2026-01-15 22:30:00+00 | 2026-01-15

    The zone applies to the rows a run reads. On a table already written, re-apply the connector, then read the table again:

    $ lm apply -f erp.yaml
Applied connector "erp" — 1 endpoint
$ lm endpoint reset-cursor erp/orders
$ lm connector run erp
run scheduled: a97e7633-c3d3-43f6-8aac-a3dd0711aed7
$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a97e7633  erp        orders    Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-20 15:33  2026-10-20 15:33

    Each row it reads again is rewritten in place, at the right instant. Without reset-cursor, the run reads only what is new and the old rows keep their time. An unknown zone is refused before anything is written:

    $ lm apply -f erp.yaml
✗ erp.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.connection.zone
          'zone' is not a time zone: "Europe/Pariss" (for example Europe/Paris or UTC)

  • A table the hub already created keeps the types it was created with. To retype it, delete the connector (which drops its tables) and re-ingest, or ALTER the columns yourself.

docs.title: Seven reserved column names
docs.text:
id, _row_hash, _ingested_at, _source, _run_id, _mapping_version, tenant_id — the hub adds these to every table it creates. A source column of one of those names fails the run:

$ lm run get ded8b2ac
ID        CONNECTOR        ENDPOINT    STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ded8b2ac  demo-price-list  price_list  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
✖ run failed: source column 'id' collides with a hub system column (_ingested_at, _mapping_version, _row_hash, _run_id, _source, id, tenant_id); it must reach the hub under another name — jdbc: source.tables[].rename; csv: a map-columns row hook under spec.mapping; kafka: no rename exists, the field must be renamed in the topic payload

rename: is the fix:

# 30-rename-reserved-column.yaml — a source table whose primary key is called `id`.
#
# The hub adds seven columns of its own to every table it creates, `id` among them, so a
# source column of that name is refused at write time rather than silently dropped. `rename:`
# is the fix: the source column lands under another name in the hub table. Nothing is renamed
# on the source — the connection stays read-only.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-price-list
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  source:
    tables:
      - name: price_list
        schema: demo
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [id]
        rename:
          id: price_list_id

$ lm connector run demo-price-list
run scheduled: ee29d37e-843e-4cd3-8972-9422ea54b36e
$ lm run list --connector demo-price-list
ID        CONNECTOR        ENDPOINT    STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ee29d37e  demo-price-list  price_list  Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
ded8b2ac  demo-price-list  price_list  Failed     0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41

 price_list_id |   sku    |  price
---------------+----------+----------
             1 | PUMP-075 | 349.0000
             2 | HOSE-32M |  59.9000
             3 | FILT-A1  | 129.5000
  • The rename applies in the hub table only. Nothing is renamed on the source.
  • lm validate refuses a rename into one of the seven, and two source columns renamed onto the same hub column.

docs.title: One row per key — a changed row replaces its version
docs.text:
The hub table holds one row per pk_columns value:

  • A row read again unchanged is left as it is.
  • A row changed at the source replaces its previous version.

After the five runs above, t_invoices holds five rows for five invoices:

 invoice_id | status |       updated_at
------------+--------+------------------------
       1001 | paid   | 2026-09-01 09:15:00+00
       1002 | paid   | 2026-09-08 07:45:00+00
       1003 | paid   | 2026-09-08 09:10:00+00
       1004 | draft  | 2026-09-02 16:20:00+00
       1005 | open   | 2026-09-08 07:30:00+00

The hub table is the source's current state; it keeps no history.

OUT counts rows delivered, not rows written

Rows skipped because they did not change are counted in OUT too, which is why a re-read that changes nothing still reports a non-zero OUT.

docs.title: Deletes are never propagated
docs.text: A row deleted at the source stays in the hub table, in both modes. To resync from nothing, delete the connector, then apply and run it again.

docs.title: Emptying one endpoint on its own
docs.text:
A jdbc-generic endpoint cannot be purged on its own. lm endpoint purge asks the hub first, so the refusal comes with no prompt:

$ lm endpoint purge demo-invoices/invoices
Error: API error 400: This endpoint writes to a connector table whose rows are not tracked per endpoint, so it cannot be purged on its own. Deleting the connector removes its data, along with its run history.

Delete the connector instead. --dry-run states what goes:

$ lm connector delete demo-invoices --dry-run
Would delete connector demo-invoices (jdbc-generic) — 5 rows of connector.t_invoices, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)
$ lm connector delete demo-invoices --force
deleted: demo-invoices
  • Without --force, lm asks you to type delete first.

  • If an entity (here invoice) is built on the table, it blocks the delete, before any question:

    $ lm connector delete demo-invoices --dry-run
Error: API error 409: table connector.t_invoices feeds entity invoice — remove the entity first (lm entity delete invoice)

  • The connectors lm source jdbc add made share the source's stored credential (<source>--credential). It goes with the last of them, and that one's statement names it: …, credential demo-src--credential, its run history and RAG chunks.

  • Re-apply the manifest and run it to start clean.

The same holds for csv-file and kafka endpoints.

docs.title: Two connectors reading a table of the same name
docs.text:
Two sites, one ERP: erp-north and erp-south differ only by defaults.schema, and both read customers. erp-north ran first and writes connector.t_customers; the run of erp-south is refused, naming the holder:

$ lm run list --connector erp-south
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT   STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
501528ee  erp-south  customers  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
$ lm run get 501528ee
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT   STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
501528ee  erp-south  customers  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
✖ run failed: connector.t_customers is already written by connector 'erp-north'; a second connector cannot write it — give this one its own hub table: jdbc: source.tables[].target; csv: the table is named after the connector, rename it; kafka: the endpoint's name

Name the second one's hub table with target:, apply, run:

  source:
    tables:
      - name: customers
        target: customers_south
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [customer_id]

$ lm apply -f erp-south.yaml
Applied connector "erp-south" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run erp-south
run scheduled: bf0b74c8-6132-4df7-b789-3ac960d069ee
$ lm run list --connector erp-south
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT   STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
bf0b74c8  erp-south  customers  Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
501528ee  erp-south  customers  Failed     0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
$ lm data tables | grep -E '^(MAPPING|jdbc:)'
MAPPING                               SCHEMA     TABLE                      ROWS
jdbc:customers                        connector  t_customers                2
jdbc:customers_south                  connector  t_customers_south          3
  • The endpoint keeps the source table's name — customers in lm run list and in lm endpoint reset-cursor erp-south/customers; only the hub table changes.
  • Another tenant may read a customers table too. Neither sees the other's rows.
  • The rule holds across connector types: a csv-file connector named customers writes connector.t_customers too.

docs.title: Indexes on the hub table
docs.text:
Index a column your views, exports or entities filter on. indexes: is declared per table:

indexes:
  - { columns: [customer], unique: false }     # unique defaults to false

Each entry is { columns: [non-empty strings], unique?: bool }; a malformed entry fails validation.

docs.title: Resume, restart, reset
docs.text:
• An interrupted run continues at the next run, with nothing doubled and nothing skipped.
  • A row inserted while a run reads belongs to the next run.
  • A row whose watermark column is empty is read once, by a first run or after reset-cursor, and never refreshed. Give the column a value, or read the table in mode: full.
  • Changing mode, watermark_column or pk_columns reads the table again once. IN shows the full count; the table does not grow (run 772a43f1 above).

docs.title: Restarting a table on purpose
docs.text:
lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> drops the stored cursor; for jdbc the endpoint is the table name. It prints nothing; the next run's IN is the proof:

$ lm endpoint reset-cursor demo-invoices/invoices
$ lm connector run demo-invoices
run scheduled: 22607df2-5515-425d-af55-46b9b6c26963
$ lm run list --connector demo-invoices --limit 2
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
22607df2  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
87b4931c  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
note: result hit the limit of 2 — there may be more

docs.title: Scheduling
docs.text:
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"   # cron, UTC
  window: "22:00-06:00"      # optional fence, UTC
  • schedule applies to the connector as a whole: all its tables ingest on the same trigger.
  • Both clocks are UTC, not the server's local zone.
  • window fences the schedule: a slot due outside it is skipped, never queued. A window may cross midnight.
  • The end is exclusive. A nightly 0 6 * * * needs a window ending later than 06:00, for instance 22:00-07:00.
  • A manual lm connector run ignores the window.
  • Re-applying without the key lifts it. An absent schedule unschedules; an absent window removes the fence.

On a production database, a window is usually the DBA's condition for granting the SELECT account — see Sizing & load tests.

docs.title: Guided flow — lm source jdbc
docs.text:
Four commands, no YAML: test and discover explore, add creates the connectors, list-tables lists them. They need the lm_integrator and lm_admin roles. The password is never a flag:

You are What happens at a keyboard Password for <user>: is prompted, and what you type is not shown piping, with --password-stdin the first line of stdin is the password piping, without the flag same, plus a warning on stderr naming the flag

Use it to explore a base you do not know, and to stand up a table quickly. Write a manifest for rename, indexes, a view, a composite or undiscoverable key, or config kept in version control.

docs.title: test
docs.text:
$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc test --password-stdin --url jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik --user lumnik_readonly
OK       : true
Dialect  : postgres
Version  : 16.15 (Debian 16.15-1.pgdg12+2)
Latency  : 1 ms
Schemas  : connector, core, demo, ext, identity, information_schema, pg_catalog, platform, public, rag

Schemas lists every schema of the database, granted or not.

docs.title: discover
docs.text:
$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc discover --password-stdin --url jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik --user lumnik_readonly --schema demo
SCHEMA     NAME                            ROWS  COLS PK                   WATERMARK       UNSUPPORTED
demo       audit_log                          1     3                      -               -
demo       invoices                           4     5 invoice_id           updated_at      -
demo       order_lines                      700     3 order_id,line_no     -               -
demo       price_list                         3     3 id                   id              -
demo       warehouses                         2     4 warehouse_id         updated_at      -
Column / flag Meaning --schema defaults to public; an ERP in its own schema names it here ROWS the planner's estimate, -1 when the table was never analyzed PK empty: no primary key — that table needs a manifest or a view WATERMARK a suggestion. Check that the column moves on every write: a numeric key, as price_list suggests id, is not one (above) UNSUPPORTED the columns the dialect cannot read, as COLUMN TYPE (- when none). add refuses such a table by name; the interactive picker marks it [!]. Always - on PostgreSQL --include-views adds views to the listing --skip-pattern replaces the dialect's default exclusions (PostgreSQL: pg_*,information_schema*,t_*) -o json / -o yaml the whole descriptor, unsupportedColumns included

docs.title: add
docs.text:
$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc add --password-stdin demo-src --url jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik --user lumnik_readonly --schema demo --tables warehouses
Created 1 connectors:
  • demo-src--warehouses
$ lm source jdbc list-tables demo-src
TABLE                          CONNECTOR                                STATUS
warehouses                     demo-src--warehouses                     active
$ lm connector run demo-src--warehouses
run scheduled: b2e594a3-bd79-4944-b50b-1642b5edc066
$ lm run list --connector demo-src--warehouses
ID        CONNECTOR             ENDPOINT    STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b2e594a3  demo-src--warehouses  warehouses  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:43  2026-10-19 01:43

What it creates, per requested table:

  • one connector named <source-name>--<table>;
  • one encrypted credential per source, <source-name>--credential — the password never lands in a file;
  • mode: watermark when a watermark column was found, mode: full otherwise. There is no --mode.

Flags:

  • --interactive opens a TUI table picker instead of --tables, pre-filled with the discovered suggestions.
  • --schedule-cron sets the schedule, in the 5-field form schedule: takes, e.g. */30 * * * *. It is checked like the manifest's: anything else is refused with invalid cron expression: … and nothing is created.

What it refuses, by name and reason, before anything is created:

$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc add --password-stdin demo-src ... --tables audit_log
Error: API error 400: table demo.audit_log has no primary key — jdbc-generic pages by primary key; declare pk_columns in a manifest instead
$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc add --password-stdin demo-src ... --tables nope
Error: API error 400: table demo.nope not found among the base tables of that schema — check the schema and the connection user's SELECT grant; a view is declared in a manifest, not through the guided add
  • a table it cannot find in that schema, and a view;
  • a table without a primary key;
  • a table whose name is not a plain identifier;

A table whose connector already exists is skipped, not re-created:

$ printf '%s\n' "$DB_PASSWORD" | lm source jdbc add --password-stdin demo-src ... --tables warehouses
Created 0 connectors:
Skipped 1 (already exist):
  • demo-src--warehouses

docs.title: Oracle
docs.text: lumnik Pro. Oracle 12c and later, with its own names and types: JDBC — Oracle.

docs.title: Reading a view
docs.text:
A view is how a table reaches the hub when the table itself cannot: no primary key, a reserved column name, a value too wide for the hub's numeric type, or more rows than the team needs.

# 50-view.yaml — read a VIEW instead of a table.
#
# A view brings a source table the hub cannot read as it is: no primary key, a column name the
# hub reserves, a column too wide, or more rows than the business needs.
#
# The guided `lm source jdbc add` refuses views: declare `pk_columns` in a manifest. The column
# named there must be unique and stable.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: demo-open-invoices
  connector_type: jdbc-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/lumnik
    user: lumnik_readonly
    password_env: LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD

  source:
    tables:
      # demo.v_open_invoices is created by data/demo-source.sql, with the tables.
      - name: v_open_invoices
        schema: demo
        mode: full
        pk_columns: [invoice_id]

$ lm run list --connector demo-open-invoices
ID        CONNECTOR           ENDPOINT         STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
22356ffd  demo-open-invoices  v_open_invoices  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42

The columns named in pk_columns must be unique together and stable — they are what the reader pages on.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
lm validate refuses before lm apply does, and both name the path:

$ lm validate -f bad-chunk.yaml
✗ bad-chunk.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.source.tables[0].chunk_size
          chunk_size is not a knob — jdbc chunking is fixed at 500 rows per read; remove it
          → The engine reads its chunk size from the connector type, never from the manifest

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad-chunk.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)
Rule Severity Path connection.url matches jdbc:<dialect>:... ERROR spec.connection.url Dialect is installed and accepts the URL ERROR spec.connection.dialect (declared) or spec.connection.url (inferred) A declared dialect matches the URL scheme ERROR spec.connection.dialect connection.user and connection.password_env present ERROR spec.connection.* A plain-text connection.password WARNING spec.connection.password A declared connection.zone is a time zone ERROR spec.connection.zone source.tables[] non-empty ERROR spec.source.tables mode present and in ERROR spec.source.tables[i].mode schema present, on the table or in defaults ERROR spec.source.tables[i].schema mode: watermark declares watermark_column ERROR spec.source.tables[i].watermark_column pk_columns is a non-empty list ERROR spec.source.tables[i].pk_columns chunk_size is refused — chunking is fixed at 500 ERROR spec.source.tables[i].chunk_size No unknown per-table key WARNING spec.source.tables[i].<key> indexes entries are { columns: [...], unique?: bool } ERROR spec.source.tables[i].indexes[j] No duplicate table names ERROR spec.source.tables[i].name target is a plain identifier ERROR spec.source.tables[i].target No two tables of the connector land in one hub table ERROR spec.source.tables[i].name rename targets are plain identifiers ERROR spec.source.tables[i].rename rename targets none of the seven reserved names ERROR spec.source.tables[i].rename No two rename sources hit the same target ERROR spec.source.tables[i].rename schedule is a valid cron ERROR spec.schedule window is HH:MM-HH:MM and not empty ERROR spec.window No unknown key at the root of spec WARNING spec.<key> metadata.scopes declared WARNING metadata.scopes

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture password_env '...' is neither in the server environment nor in lm secret neither the hub's environment nor the tenant's lm secret holds that name lm secret set <NAME>, export it where the hub runs, or attach a credential through the guided flow lm validate: required field missing at spec.source.tables[i].schema no schema on the table nor in defaults add schema: — see Per-table keys source column 'id' collides with a hub system column the source has a column named like one of the seven add rename: { id: source_id } on that table run Failed: connector.t_… is already written by connector '…' another connector of the tenant already writes that hub table add target: <name> on that table — see Two connectors reading a table of the same name numeric field overflow a numeric value wider than 14 digits before the point expose the column as text through a view the run reads 0 rows and nothing is wrong the cursor is already past everything expected — change a row at the source, or lm endpoint reset-cursor updated rows never arrive mode: full, or a watermark column the application does not move switch to watermark on a column that moves the hub log says the cursor was persisted by another configuration mode, watermark_column or pk_columns changed expected once; the table restarts and unchanged rows are skipped a deleted source row is still in the hub table deletes are never propagated delete the connector, then re-apply and run run Failed: could not reach public.workorder (SQLSTATE 08001): host not resolved (UnknownHostException) the hub cannot open a connection to the source: its host is not known any more (host not resolved), nothing answers on the port (connection failed), or the network cuts the attempt. The run ends there: at its start nothing is written, after a chunk what was written stays check the source from where the hub runs; for a source retired on purpose, lm connector pause NAME: what it wrote stays readable a table is in discover but add refuses it no primary key, or it is a view declare pk_columns in a manifest discover lists nothing in a schema test shows the wrong --schema (default public), or no SELECT grant on its tables pass --schema <name>; grant USAGE on the schema and SELECT on its tables run Failed: pk_columns (…) does not identify one row of … the declared pk_columns is not unique declare the whole primary key — see Per-table keys
