docs.title: Kotlin hooks — when no transformer fits
docs.text: A kotlin cell hook runs a .kts script over each row of a csv-file connector, or over each item's promoted columns on a REST endpoint. Use it only when no transformer does the job.

docs.title: Name the script in the manifest
docs.text:
The manifest never holds the script. It names one the hub already has:

mapping:
  cell:
    - kotlin:
        script: hooks:ean-check.kts        # a script of your hub's hooks directory
        context: { defaultCountry: FR }    # optional; the script reads it as `context`
script: Where the script is hooks:<name>.kts The hooks directory of your hub. Its operator copies the files there (how). Write the file name alone: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, ending in .kts. classpath:<path> Built into the hub. One sample ships: classpath:hooks/samples/normalize-date.kts.

A script runs with all of the hub's rights. That is why only the operator installs one, and a manifest can only name it.

docs.title: Check what the hub holds
docs.text:
lm hook scripts lists the scripts of the hooks directory. The SHA-256 tells you which version the hub holds.

lm validate and lm apply check every script:: it must exist and compile. A refusal names the hook (spec.mapping.cell[1].kotlin) and says why:

The refusal says Do this this hub has no hooks directory Ask the hub's operator to set one up. hooks:<name> is not in the hooks directory Check the name with lm hook scripts. hooks: takes a file name of the hooks directory Write the file name alone: no folder, no capital letters. Kotlin script compilation failed for ean-check.kts: … (ean-check.kts:2:14) The script has an error at line 2, column 14. Send that line to its author.

docs.title: Write a script
docs.text:
The script sample that ships with the hub rewrites 31/12/2019 into 2019-12-31:

// normalize-date.kts — a cell hook: rewrite legacy "DD/MM/YYYY" into ISO "YYYY-MM-DD".
// The script reads and changes the row through bindings["cells"].
@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
val cells = bindings["cells"] as MutableMap<String, Any?>
val raw = cells["signup_date"] as? String
if (raw != null && Regex("""\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}""").matches(raw)) {
    val (d, m, y) = raw.split("/")
    cells["signup_date"] = "$y-$m-$d"
}
  • bindings["cells"] is the row. Change it: the next hooks and the table see the change.
  • bindings["context"] holds the manifest's context: values, with their types: lead_days: 3 is a number. Read it as (context["lead_days"] as Number).toInt().
  • Reading a number as String fails the run, naming the script and its line. Use .toString().

docs.title: A value the script cannot read
docs.text:
Do not fail the run: call bindings["unreadable"]. Each call counts one cell_errors, like a built-in hook:

// Reads "12,5 kg" / "3 pce"; a quantity in any other shape is declared unreadable.
@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
val cells = bindings["cells"] as MutableMap<String, Any?>
val m = Regex("(\\d+(?:,\\d+)?) (kg|pce)").matchEntire((cells["quantity"] as String).trim())
if (m == null) {
    (bindings["unreadable"] as Runnable).run()    // "env. 4 kg": counted, not guessed
} else {
    cells["qty"] = m.groupValues[1].replace(',', '.')
    cells["unit"] = m.groupValues[2]
}
  • The kotlin hook takes no column:. So on-error's default decides the row: soft writes it, dlq sets it aside, fail stops the run.
  • A script that throws fails the run, naming the script, the exception and the line: ✖ run failed: kotlin hook hooks:quantity.kts failed: NumberFormatException at line 4.

docs.title: Which version a run used
docs.text:
A script the operator replaces applies at once, without a restart. lm run get names each script the run used, with the SHA-256 lm hook scripts shows:

• script hooks:shipping-fee.kts  sha256 23ba31c1b1827ff86228f4f7f36ffd2b73b7ab77ef155598bf05ef12c4b1273e

A script replaced while a run was going gives two lines: that run used both versions.

Runnable example: docs/connectors/csv/50-kotlin-row-hook.yaml.

docs.title: REST
docs.text:
Ingest any HTTP/JSON API: point at the base URL, declare the endpoints and how they page, apply. The rows land as typed columns plus the untouched JSON payload.

Type rest-generic Protocol HTTP/JSON (+ the GraphQL and SOAP request shapes) Target the table each endpoint declares in target.table (ext.*) Schedulable cron Edition Open

Every endpoint declares its own method; a source usually needs GET. The connector sends only the requests the manifest declares.

A response must be JSON, except on a SOAP endpoint. Any other body, such as XML or an HTML page, fails the run with its Content-Type: the response is not JSON (Content-Type application/xml). The run is never read as an empty page.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads a demo API that ships with the repo

One Python file, no dependencies, 2 400 fictional ACME partners under ten path dialects. Start it in a terminal of its own, and put its three credentials in the hub's registry:

python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/acme-api.py
lm secret set ACME_BASIC_PW        # demo-pass
lm secret set ACME_BEARER_TOKEN    # demo-token
lm secret set ACME_API_KEY         # demo-key

The manifests point at http://host.docker.internal:8099, because the hub runs in a container and localhost inside it is that container. What each dialect imitates, and which ones misbehave on purpose: The demo API.

# 10-quickstart.yaml — one endpoint, a pagination preset instead of a pagination block.
#
# `pagination: {kind: spring-page, size: 500}` fits any API that answers like a Spring `Page`
# (`content`, `totalPages`). Set `size`: the default, 50, turns 2 400 partners into 48 requests.
#
# The password is never in this file. `password_env` names a secret:
#   lm secret set ACME_BASIC_PW        # the demo API answers to demo-user / demo-pass
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in ext.acme_partners.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-partners
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  # The hub runs in Docker: `localhost` there is the hub's own container, not your machine.
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: basic
    username: demo-user
    password_env: ACME_BASIC_PW   # basic takes no inline password: name a secret

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      path: /spring/partners
      method: GET
      pagination: { kind: spring-page, size: 500 }
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name,         path: "$.name",         type: text }
          - { name: city,         path: "$.city",         type: text }
          - { name: credit_limit, path: "$.credit_limit", type: bigint }
          - { name: updated_at,   path: "$.updated_at",   type: timestamptz, transform: parse_iso8601 }

$ lm validate -f docs/connectors/rest/demo/10-quickstart.yaml
✓ 10-quickstart.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/rest/demo/10-quickstart.yaml
Applied connector "acme-partners" — 1 endpoint

Before running anything, send the first request a run would send:

$ lm source rest test acme-partners
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
partners  GET     200     500    ok

ITEMS is the number of records read from that one page (the manifest asks for 500). Nothing is written. Now run it:

$ lm connector run acme-partners
run scheduled: 9deb9cb6-d9bc-427f-ba27-5af060647f19
$ lm run list --connector acme-partners
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
9deb9cb6  acme-partners  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39

STARTED / ENDED print in your terminal's time zone; schedule is evaluated in UTC.

What landed in ext.acme_partners — the promoted columns, beside the whole payload:

lumnik=> SELECT external_id, name, city, credit_limit, updated_at
lumnik->   FROM ext.acme_partners ORDER BY external_id LIMIT 4;
 external_id |           name            |   city    | credit_limit |       updated_at       
-------------+---------------------------+-----------+--------------+------------------------
 1000        | Hydraulique Lyon 1000     | Lyon      |          500 | 2026-01-01 00:00:00+00
 1001        | Roulements Bruxelles 1001 | Bruxelles |          637 | 2026-01-01 00:01:00+00
 1002        | Fixations Milano 1002     | Milano    |          774 | 2026-01-01 00:02:00+00
 1003        | Pneumatique Porto 1003    | Porto     |          911 | 2026-01-01 00:03:00+00
(4 rows)
  • promote is a projection, not a filter. Every field the source returned is in data (JSONB); the promoted ones are also copied into typed columns.
  • A field is shaped by its promote[] entry and its transform:. A rule over the promoted columns — a filter, a Kotlin script — goes in the endpoint's mapping: Run hooks over the promoted columns.
  • unique_key makes a re-run safe. It becomes external_id, unique per tenant, and every write is an upsert — see Storage layout.
  • The password is never in the manifest. password_env names an lm secret entry (or, if none, an environment variable on the hub).

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
spec:
  base_url: https://api.example.com
  auth: { kind: bearer, token_env: EXAMPLE_TOKEN }
  default_rate_limit: 100/s
  schedule: "0 6 * * *"          # optional cron, evaluated in UTC by the hub scheduler
  window: "22:00-06:00"          # optional fence, UTC, end exclusive, may cross midnight
  graphql_path: /graphql         # only for GraphQL endpoints; this is the default
  headers:
    - { name: X-Api-Version, value: "2026-01" }
  endpoints:
    - id: charges                # kebab-case, unique in the connector
      method: GET                # GET | POST | PUT | PATCH | DELETE
      path: /v1/charges
      pagination: { kind: stripe }
      incremental: { mode: full }          # optional, this is the default
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.example_charges
        unique_key: $.id
        promote:
          - { name: amount, path: $.amount, type: bigint }
  • The path-shaped fields (cursor_path, response_path, unique_key, link_path, …) are JSONPath read against the response body: $.data[-1:].id is "the id of the last element of data".
  • A promote entry's type is one of text, bigint, integer, decimal, boolean, date, timestamptz, jsonb.
  • A promote entry copies one value into a typed column. Values sent as text are read as the type says: "2026-10-01T08:01:00Z" as a timestamptz, "12" as a bigint, "true" as a boolean. A value that cannot be read leaves that column empty for the row, and the run counts it in cell_errors; the row is written and keeps the value in its payload.
  • A path with a filter or a wildcard reads one value: $.status.conditions[?(@.type=='Ready')].status reads False, not ["False"]. Nothing matched: the column is empty. Several values: the column is empty and the run counts one cell error. A jsonb column keeps the list; a path without a filter keeps what it points at, an array included.
  • A path the JSONPath library cannot evaluate leaves that row's column empty and counts one cell error; the run goes on. first() after a filter is one: write the filter alone.
  • A promote entry may also carry a transform:, e.g. from_epoch for a number of seconds: the list.
  • Without schedule, the connector runs only on lm connector run. window fences scheduled runs: a slot due outside it is skipped, never queued. A manual run ignores the window.

An unknown key at the connector level of spec comes back as a warning; the manifest still applies:

$ lm validate -f my-api.yaml
! my-api.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.headerz
          unknown key — ignored by the runtime
          → Remove it, or check the spelling

docs.title: Transform a promoted value
docs.text:
A promote entry takes one transform:. A rule over several columns goes in the endpoint's mapping: Run hooks over the promoted columns.

Value Effect from_epoch Unix epoch seconds → timestamp (UTC). Milliseconds are not supported. parse_iso8601 ISO-8601 text → timestamp to_lower / to_upper case trim removes the spaces around the value to_json_string writes the value as JSON text parse_quantity a number with a unit suffix → the number in its base unit: 100m → 0.1, 64Mi → 67108864, 99827146n → 0.099827146. Use type: decimal. last_path_segment a link → its last path segment, percent-decoded: http://erp/products/SKU-00001?projection=full → SKU-00001. A link with no segment reads no value.

parse_iso8601 reads these shapes:

Source text Stored 2008-04-18T00:00:00 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z: no offset means UTC 2008-04-18 00:00:00 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z: a space works too 2008-04-18 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z: a date alone is midnight 2026-08-01T14:30:00+02:00 2026-08-01T12:30:00Z: the offset is applied

Any other shape leaves the column empty for that row and counts one cell error; the row is written and keeps the value in its payload.

parse_quantity reads the notation Kubernetes uses, which many APIs share:

Suffix Factor n u m 10⁻⁹, 10⁻⁶, 10⁻³ k M G T P E 10³ … 10¹⁸ Ki Mi Gi Ti Pi Ei 2¹⁰ … 2⁶⁰ e3, E-3 10 to that power, at most 18

Read from a cluster's metrics.k8s.io — each value promoted twice, as sent and with the transform:

promote:
  - { name: cpu,          path: "$.containers[0].usage.cpu",    type: text }
  - { name: cpu_cores,    path: "$.containers[0].usage.cpu",    type: decimal, transform: parse_quantity }
  - { name: memory,       path: "$.containers[0].usage.memory", type: text }
  - { name: memory_bytes, path: "$.containers[0].usage.memory", type: decimal, transform: parse_quantity }

lumnik=> SELECT pod, cpu, cpu_cores, memory, memory_bytes FROM ext.k8s_usage ORDER BY pod LIMIT 2;
             pod              |    cpu    |  cpu_cores  | memory | memory_bytes
------------------------------+-----------+-------------+--------+--------------
 catalog-api-54b5c97cdf-q9v2g | 99756659n | 0.099756659 | 316Ki  |       323584
 checkout-worker-0            | 44515n    | 0.000044515 | 8544Ki |      8749056

The suffix is case-sensitive: m is milli, M mega. 12 MB or 1mi is not a quantity: the column stays empty and the run counts one cell error, as for any transform.

docs.title: A key read from a link
docs.text:
unique_key takes the same object form when the key needs a transform. Spring Data REST, for example, puts no id in the item: the id is the last segment of its self link.

pagination: { kind: spring-hateoas, items: products }
target:
  kind: hybrid
  table: ext.products
  unique_key: { path: $._links.self.href, transform: last_path_segment }
  promote:
    - { name: sku, path: $._links.self.href, transform: last_path_segment, type: text }
  • Never key on the whole link. It carries the host the hub reached: the day the API moves behind https or another name, every row is written again beside the old one.
  • An item whose key reads no value fails the run, as an item without the key's field does.

docs.title: Run hooks over the promoted columns
docs.text:
transform: changes one value. A rule over the row — keep some items, compute a column from others — goes in the endpoint's mapping. It takes the transformers and Kotlin scripts of a csv-file connector:

# 96-mapping-hooks.yaml — hooks over an endpoint's promoted columns: a filter, then a Kotlin script.
#
# The script is the operator's: docs/connectors/rest/hooks/credit-band.kts, copied into the hub's
# hooks directory (docs/deploy.md#offer-kotlin-scripts-to-the-integrators).
#
# Expect: 300 rows in ext.acme_partner_bands (the French partners), 2 100 skipped.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-partner-bands
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      path: /open/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        total_path: "$.total"
        response_path: "$.data"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_partner_bands
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name,         path: "$.name",         type: text }
          - { name: country,      path: "$.country",      type: text }
          - { name: credit_limit, path: "$.credit_limit", type: bigint }
          - { name: credit_band,  type: text }      # no path: the mapping fills it
      mapping:
        dataset:
          - filter-where: { column: country, equals: FR }
        cell:
          - kotlin: { script: hooks:credit-band.kts }

The script, from the hub's hooks directory:

// A partner's credit band, from its credit limit: A from 20 000, B from 5 000, C below.
@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
val cells = bindings["cells"] as MutableMap<String, Any?>
val limit = (cells["credit_limit"] as Number).toLong()
cells["credit_band"] = when {
    limit >= 20_000 -> "A"
    limit >= 5_000 -> "B"
    else -> "C"
}

The run reads 2 400 partners, keeps the French ones, and says which script it ran:

$ lm run get 0ff895b1-1ba1-4703-a4f4-737203d3325e
ID        CONNECTOR           ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
0ff895b1  acme-partner-bands  partners  Completed  2400  300  2100     0             2026-10-29 20:35  2026-10-29 20:35
• script hooks:credit-band.kts  sha256 eb508f320131cff3ad56cc814743d4af4e7f805ab239f85c0248ab7791baf63d

lumnik=> SELECT external_id, name, credit_limit, credit_band FROM ext.acme_partner_bands
lumnik->   ORDER BY external_id::int LIMIT 2;
 external_id |         name          | credit_limit | credit_band
-------------+-----------------------+--------------+-------------
 1000        | Hydraulique Lyon 1000 |          500 | C
 1008        | Filtration Lyon 1008  |         1596 | C

lumnik=> SELECT data FROM ext.acme_partner_bands WHERE external_id = '1000';
 {"id": 1000, "city": "Lyon", "name": "Hydraulique Lyon 1000", "country": "FR", "updated_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "credit_limit": 500}
  • A hook sees the promoted columns, after their transform:, not the JSON. To read a field, promote it. A field the item lacks is in the row, empty.
  • A value is as the API sent it. "12" stays text and 12 a number: the column's type applies when the row is written. A script reads (cells["credit_limit"] as Number) only when the API sends a number.
  • A column the mapping fills is a promote entry without path. The entry gives its type.
  • data stays what the API returned. The mapping changes the columns, never the payload.
  • An item a hook drops is counted in SKIPPED: IN = OUT + SKIPPED. Under on-error: dlq, the dead letter is the item as the API sent it.
  • One item is one row, mapped on its own. split-row and aggregator are refused: a row lands beside the item it was read from. sort-by and fill-down are refused too: an item mapped alone has nothing around it to order or to carry from.
  • The mapping belongs to its endpoint. spec.mapping and spec.defaults.mapping are refused: each endpoint promotes its own columns.

lm validate knows the columns. In the demo, replace the script with - lower: { columns: [city] }: city is not promoted, and the hook is named by its path:

$ lm validate -f bad-column.yaml
✗ bad-column.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].mapping.cell[0].lower.columns[0]
          column 'city' is not in the row here — the source's columns are known and no earlier hook adds it; the hook would do nothing with it
          → Check the spelling, or add the column in an earlier hook

docs.title: One connector, one API
docs.text:
One connector is one API, whatever number of endpoints it exposes. Two endpoints of the same API may page by different conventions:

# 20-two-endpoints.yaml — one connector is one API, whatever number of endpoints it exposes.
#
# Both endpoints below read the same 2 400 partners from the same server, through two
# conventions that have nothing in common:
#
#   /v1/partners   opaque cursor  — ?starting_after=<id>, $.has_more says whether to continue
#   /drf/partners  follow a link  — $.next carries the whole next URL, until it is null
#
# Preset `stripe` expands to kind: cursor (cursor_param starting_after, cursor_path
# $.data[-1:].id, has_more_path $.has_more, response_path $.data); preset `drf-page` expands to
# kind: body-link (link_path $.next, response_path $.results). Neither sends a page-size
# parameter — see the page-size note in rest.md — so `page_size` rides in the DRF endpoint's
# own `path:`, which the request builder extends with `&`.
#
# The credential is declared once, at connector level, and both endpoints use it.
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in each of the two tables.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-saas
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: bearer
    token_env: ACME_BEARER_TOKEN   # lm secret set ACME_BEARER_TOKEN   → demo-token

  endpoints:
    - id: cursor-partners
      path: /v1/partners?limit=500
      method: GET
      pagination: { kind: stripe }
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_cursor_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }
          - { name: city, path: "$.city", type: text }

    - id: link-partners
      path: /drf/partners?page_size=500
      method: GET
      pagination: { kind: drf-page }
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_link_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }
          - { name: city, path: "$.city", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-saas
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT         STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
9d7a4883  acme-saas  link-partners    Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
3531807d  acme-saas  cursor-partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

The ledger records one run per endpoint. stripe and drf-page are two of the presets.

docs.title: Settings shared by every endpoint
docs.text:
spec.defaults holds what several endpoints would otherwise repeat. An endpoint that does not write a key takes it from there; an endpoint that writes it keeps its own, whole:

spec:
  defaults:
    incremental: { mode: watermark, param: updated_since, watermark_path: $.updated_at }
  endpoints:
    - id: partners               # runs incremental, from defaults
      ...
    - id: countries              # its own block replaces the default
      incremental: { mode: full }
      ...
Key in spec.defaults Taken by incremental every endpoint variables GraphQL endpoints header, soap_action SOAP endpoints

Only these four keys belong in spec.defaults. lm validate names any other, and reports a mistake in a default once.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text:
Kind Config bearer token_env: VAR_NAME (preferred), or token_value: "..." (dev only); optional scheme (Bearer) basic username + password_env: VAR_NAME api-key in: header\|query, name, value_env: VAR_NAME oauth2 token_url, client_id, client_secret_env: VAR_NAME; optional scope, client_auth: basic\|post — below none no credentials (the default when auth: is omitted)

Every auth *_env field names an lm secret entry first, then a variable of that name in the hub's environment. Set the value before lm apply:

lm secret set ACME_BASIC_PW     # prompts at the keyboard; what you type is not shown
  • scheme is the word before a bearer token. An API on Django REST Framework's token authentication, NetBox for one, wants Authorization: Token <key> and refuses Bearer: auth: { kind: bearer, scheme: Token, token_env: NETBOX_TOKEN }. One word that starts with a letter, then letters, digits, - or _, at most 32 characters.
  • basic and api-key have no inline field: the value comes from password_env / value_env, or not at all.
  • bearer: when both are set, token_env wins and token_value is ignored, even if nothing resolves under token_env. Declare one or the other.

If the API writes your credential back into a response — an error that repeats the token it received, for instance — lumnik hides it as <redacted> before showing that response anywhere (lm source rest test, a failed run). The data you ingest is never rewritten. Credentials a source writes back

A credential that does not resolve is named before any run:

$ lm source rest test acme-badauth
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
partners  GET     -       0      Basic password unavailable (env=ACME_NOT_SET_PW)
Error: 1 of 1 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data

docs.title: OAuth2 client credentials
docs.text:
A SaaS that hands out a client id and a secret, and wants a short-lived token on every call:

auth:
  kind: oauth2
  token_url: https://auth.saas.example/oauth/token
  client_id: lumnik-orders
  client_secret_env: SAAS_CLIENT_SECRET
  scope: orders.read            # optional, space-separated
  client_auth: basic            # optional: basic (the default) or post
  • lumnik asks token_url for a token, keeps it as long as it is valid, and asks for a new one shortly before it expires.
  • If the API refuses a token during a run (for example after rotating its keys), lumnik asks for a new one once and repeats the request.
  • client_auth: basic works with almost every server; use post only if the server's documentation asks for it.

With the secret set and the grant accepted, the pre-flight reads the first page:

$ lm source rest test saas-orders
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
orders    GET     200     25     ok

Once the SaaS has revoked that secret, the same command and the next run both say so:

$ lm source rest test saas-orders
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
orders    GET     -       0      OAuth2 token refused by the authorization server: HTTP 401 invalid_client
Error: 1 of 1 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data

What lm source rest test and a failed run say:

Cause Verdict client_secret_env resolves to nothing OAuth2 client secret unavailable (env=SAAS_CLIENT_SECRET) The server refuses the grant OAuth2 token refused by the authorization server: HTTP 401 invalid_client token_url cannot be reached OAuth2 token request failed: host not resolved (UnknownHostException) The answer carries no token OAuth2 token response carries no access_token

invalid_client and similar codes come from the authorization server. The secret and the token are never shown.

docs.title: An internal CA
docs.text:
An API served over HTTPS with a certificate your company's CA signed — an in-house service, a reverse proxy with its own PKI, a Kubernetes API server — is refused at the handshake: lumnik trusts the public CAs only. Name the CA in the connector:

spec:
  base_url: https://kubernetes.default.svc
  tls:
    ca_secret: CLUSTER_CA        # an lm secret holding the CA's PEM certificate(s)

lm secret set CLUSTER_CA - < ca.crt
  • Only the CAs in that secret are trusted for this connector — the public ones no longer are. One connector, one API: its runs, lm source rest test and lm source rest probe all share that trust.
  • A certificate the trust refuses fails at once, as certificate refused (SSLHandshakeException): it is not retried like a network failure, which still reads TLS failure.
  • A secret may hold several PEM certificates (a root and an intermediate): each one is trusted.
  • A secret nothing holds, or one that holds no certificate, fails the run and lm source rest test by the secret's name, never by its content: CA certificate unavailable (secret=CLUSTER_CA), secret CLUSTER_CA holds no PEM certificate.
  • A tls block that names no CA (ca_secret missing or blank) is refused at lm apply, and a run given one fails: a declared trust never falls back to the public CAs.
  • There is no switch to skip the check.
  • An oauth2 token request (token_url) still uses the public trust.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Every endpoint declares how the source hands back its next page. Most APIs follow a named convention, so the usual answer is one line:

pagination: { kind: spring-page }        # Spring Data Page — seven fields under one word

Twelve presets name the framework behind the API (Spring Data, Micronaut, Django REST, FastAPI, NestJS, JSON:API, Sequelize, Stripe). When none fits, write one of seven strategies by hand: cursor, page, offset, link-header, body-link, relay, and none for an answer that holds the whole list.

→ Pagination — the catalogue, the fields of each strategy, where the cursor is injected, page size on the strategies that send none, and kind: custom.

docs.title: Request headers
docs.text:
Connector-level only — spec.headers[] goes out on every request:

spec:
  headers:
    - { name: X-Api-Version, value: "2026-01" }       # static
    - { name: X-Client-Id,   value_env: CLIENT_ID }   # from lm secret or the environment
  • Each entry needs name + exactly one of value / value_env.
  • value_env reads like an auth *_env field: the lm secret entry first, then a variable of that name in the hub's environment.
  • A value_env that resolves to nothing is an error, not a missing header: the run, lm source rest test and lm source rest probe stop before sending the request. The error names the header and the reference, never a value.
  • Headers are applied before auth — an auth-injected header wins a name clash.
  • Endpoint-level headers are refused:
$ lm apply -f bad-headers.yaml
✗ bad-headers.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].headers
          per-endpoint headers are not supported in this release; declare headers at spec.headers
          → Move the headers block up to spec.headers (connector level)

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad-headers.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

lm source rest test and lm source rest probe send the declared headers too. /hdr/partners answers 400 without X-Api-Version; the acme-witness connector (manifest under The declared total) declares it:

$ lm source rest test acme-witness
ENDPOINT    METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
incomplete  GET     200     500    ok
versioned   GET     200     500    ok

The same connector with { name: X-Api-Version, value_env: ACME_API_VERSION }, before and after the secret is stored:

$ lm source rest test acme-witness-env
ENDPOINT    METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
incomplete  GET     -       0      Header X-Api-Version unavailable (env=ACME_API_VERSION)
versioned   GET     -       0      Header X-Api-Version unavailable (env=ACME_API_VERSION)
Error: 2 of 2 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data
$ lm secret set ACME_API_VERSION      # 2026-01
Created secret "ACME_API_VERSION"
$ lm source rest test acme-witness-env
ENDPOINT    METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
incomplete  GET     200     500    ok
versioned   GET     200     500    ok

A run without it fails the same way: ✖ run failed: Header X-Api-Version unavailable (env=ACME_API_VERSION).

docs.title: Incremental sync
docs.text:
incremental:
  mode: full              # re-fetch every page (default)
  # OR
  mode: watermark         # send the stored watermark as a query parameter,
  param: updated_since    #   e.g. ?updated_since=<watermark>
  watermark_path: $.updated_at   # new watermark = MAX of this JSONPath over the items read
  lookback: 10m           # optional — see "A change during a run" below

# 40-watermark.yaml — read only what changed since the last run.
#
# `mode: watermark` sends the last mark on the first request of the run, and the API returns
# only what is newer:  GET /offset/partners?updated_since=2026-01-02T15:59:00Z&offset=0&limit=500
#
# Run 1: no mark yet — a full read, 2 400 rows.
# Run 2: only the rows changed since run 1 (a little before, so nothing changed during run 1 is
#        missed). They replace their earlier version: the table stays at 2 400.
#
# The mark moves only when a run completes: a failed run leaves it where it was.
#
#   lm endpoint reset-cursor acme-incremental/partners     # the next run is full again
#
# Point `watermark_path` at a field the source updates on every change, or every run re-reads
# everything.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-incremental
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: basic
    username: demo-user
    password_env: ACME_BASIC_PW

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      path: /offset/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        response_path: "$.data"
        # No total_path here on purpose: an incremental endpoint returns a filtered slice, and
        # the source's unfiltered $.total is not the number it should be checked against.
      incremental:
        mode: watermark
        param: updated_since        # the query parameter the API filters on
        watermark_path: "$.updated_at"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_incremental_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name,       path: "$.name",       type: text }
          - { name: updated_at, path: "$.updated_at", type: timestamptz, transform: parse_iso8601 }

Run it twice:

$ lm run list --connector acme-incremental
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
17c95cc8  acme-incremental  partners  Completed  2     2     0        0             2026-10-24 22:30  2026-10-24 22:30  yes
f9bc9c64  acme-incremental  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-24 22:30  2026-10-24 22:30  yes

Run 1 has no mark: it reads all 2 400 rows. Run 2 asks only for what changed since, with a small margin (below): 2 rows come back and replace their earlier version. The table still holds 2 400 rows.

  • The mark advances only when the run completes, never page by page.
  • lm endpoint reset-cursor acme-incremental/partners clears it; the next run is a full read. The command prints nothing and exits 0.
  • Point watermark_path at a column the source updates on every change. Otherwise every run re-reads everything.
  • Best: a date and time with a time zone, or a number that only grows.

docs.title: A change during a run
docs.text:
An order that changes while a run is reading could be missed by the next run. So each run asks from a little before the last mark. The few orders read twice are simply updated again.

  • lookback: 10m chooses that margin yourself; lookback: 0s turns it off.
  • It works when updated_at is a date and time with a time zone. With a change number or a date alone, the mark is sent as it is, and such a change can still be missed.

docs.title: Storage layout
docs.text:
Each endpoint's table is created on the first run. Besides the promoted columns, it holds:

Column Holds external_id the unique_key: a re-run replaces the row instead of adding one data the whole payload, as JSON

A re-run rewrites only the rows that changed, yet OUT still counts every row read and SKIPPED stays 0. To check that nothing duplicated, count the table's rows.

A new promote entry adds its column on the next run — see Add a typed column later.

Deleting a REST connector deletes its data

lm connector delete removes the connector's rows from its ext.* tables (a table goes with the last connector writing into it), and every RAG chunk it produced. To empty one endpoint's rows and keep the connector, see Empty one endpoint's rows.

docs.title: When the source misbehaves
docs.text: The engine retries what is worth retrying, refuses to read an error body as data, and — where the source publishes a count — checks the run against it.

docs.title: Retry, page cap, rate limit
docs.text: Guard Behaviour Retry 429, 5xx, timeouts and network errors are retried up to 5 times, with growing pauses. Then the run fails. Other statuses are not retried Page cap 10 000 pages per endpoint per run Rate limit default_rate_limit (default 100/s): count/window, window s, m or h with an optional integer (100/s, 100/5m, 1000/h). One bucket per connector, shared by all its endpoints — set it to the strictest endpoint's limit

docs.title: An outage fails the run
docs.text:
/down/partners answers 500 to everything; /flaky/partners answers 429 then 503 before serving each page:

# 60-source-down.yaml — what a run does when the source is simply down.
#
# `/down/partners` answers 500 to everything. The retry policy spends its five attempts, and
# then the run must FAIL: an outage that lands as a clean empty sync pages nobody, and the
# next run reads a table it believes to be current.
#
# The guard refuses a FINAL non-2xx, not a retried one — `/flaky/partners` below answers 429
# then 503 before serving each page, and its endpoint completes in full.
#
#   curl http://127.0.0.1:8099/admin/reset     # before re-running: the flaky counters persist
#
# Expect: `down` Failed with the upstream status in the message, `flaky` Completed with 2 400.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-outage
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: basic
    username: demo-user
    password_env: ACME_BASIC_PW

  endpoints:
    - id: down
      path: /down/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        response_path: "$.data"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_outage_down
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

    - id: flaky
      path: /flaky/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        response_path: "$.data"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_outage_flaky
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-outage
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b3e0c1db  acme-outage  flaky     Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
a05e8be8  acme-outage  down      Failed     0     0     0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

$ lm run get a05e8be8
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a05e8be8  acme-outage  down      Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
✖ run failed: upstream returned HTTP 500 (transient) — refusing to ingest its body as data: {"error": "this endpoint is down and stays down"}

A final non-2xx fails the run; it is never reported as an empty sync. A status that succeeds on retry does not — the flaky endpoint completes with all 2 400 rows.

The pre-flight sends one request without retry, so a flaky source shows red there:

$ lm source rest test acme-outage
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
flaky     GET     429     0      HTTP 429
down      GET     500     0      HTTP 500
Error: 2 of 2 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data

Every enabled endpoint is tried; the command exits non-zero if any did not answer.

docs.title: The declared total — a witness on the count
docs.text:
A run that loses rows can still end green. Where the source publishes its row count, total_path checks the run against it. /liar/partners serves 2 300 of its 2 400 partners and still declares "total": 2400:

# 50-total-witness.yaml — the row count the source publishes, used as a witness.
#
# `/liar/partners` serves 2 300 of its 2 400 partners and still declares `"total": 2400`. The
# pagination ends the way a complete read ends — no error, no short page the strategy can see —
# so without `total_path` this run lands Completed with 2 300 rows and agrees with itself.
#
# With `total_path` pointed at that number, the run compares what it returned against what the
# source declared, and fails naming both figures. That comparison is exact and reads both ways,
# which is why it must point at a ROW count published by the source — never at a page count,
# never at an estimate.
#
# The second endpoint is the same shape against `/hdr/partners`, which answers 400 to any
# request without `X-Api-Version` — the declarative header at spec level below. Headers are
# connector-level only; a `headers:` key on an endpoint is refused at apply.
#
# Expect: `liar` FAILS on the mismatch, `hdr` completes with 2 400.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-witness
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  headers:
    - { name: X-Api-Version, value: "2026-01" }   # sent on EVERY request of this connector

  auth:
    kind: basic
    username: demo-user
    password_env: ACME_BASIC_PW

  endpoints:
    - id: incomplete
      path: /liar/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        response_path: "$.data"
        total_path: "$.total"       # the witness
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_witness_incomplete
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

    - id: versioned
      path: /hdr/partners
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: offset
        offset_param: offset
        limit_param: limit
        limit: 500
        response_path: "$.data"
        total_path: "$.total"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_witness_versioned
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-witness
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT    STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
03b05ee0  acme-witness  versioned   Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
a368b49d  acme-witness  incomplete  Failed     2000  2000  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

$ lm run get a368b49d
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT    STATUS  IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a368b49d  acme-witness  incomplete  Failed  2000  2000  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
✖ run failed: Endpoint 'incomplete': the source declared 2400 rows but this run returned 2300 — refusing to report a partial extract as a complete one
  • The run fails. The rows already written stay: 2 000 here. The next successful run completes them.

total_path is optional on every strategy; a soap endpoint ignores it. It also lets offset stop once every row is in. The drf-limit-offset and sequelize presets set it for you (total_path: $.count).

  • Point total_path at an exact row count: not a page count, not an estimate.
  • The check does not run on an incremental endpoint, or when the total changes during the read.

A count in a response header. Gitea, GitLab or WordPress send it as a header, beside a body that is just the list: name the header with total_header instead of total_path.

pagination: { kind: link-header, response_path: $, total_header: X-Total-Count }
  • The header's name is matched in any case. A response without it is no witness.
  • Its value must be a whole number from 0: pagination.total_header must read a row count: a whole number from 0 otherwise.
  • total_path and total_header together are refused at lm validate: one witness per endpoint.
  • It checks the count only; the pages are read as without it. On offset, which can also stop on total_path, the read ends on its first short page: one more request when the total is a multiple of the limit.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
lm apply -f <file.yaml>
lm validate -f <file.yaml>
lm connector run <connector>
lm endpoint enable|disable|reset-cursor|purge <connector>/<endpoint>
lm source rest test <connector>                      # pre-flight every enabled endpoint, no write
lm source rest probe <connector> --endpoint <path>   # sample one path, draft its endpoint block
lm source rest from-openapi <url> --name N --scope S -o FILE

docs.title: TUI
docs.text:
• :sources — the KIND column shows rest/jdbc/csv; Enter on a REST connector drills into :endpoints
  • :endpoints — NAME/METHOD/PATH/SCHEDULE/LAST_RUN/STATUS/ENABLED; Enter → :runs filtered

Full reference: CLI & TUI.

docs.title: Check a connector before running it
docs.text:
lm source rest test <connector>

Result: for each enabled endpoint, the hub sends the first request a run would send (same method, path, headers, auth and pagination) and reports what came back. Nothing is written.

  • 200 with 0 items: the response arrived but nothing matched response_path.
  • Disabled endpoints are skipped and counted on stderr.
  • -o json adds the URL called (host and path; the query string is not shown) and an excerpt of the body:
$ lm endpoint disable acme-saas/link-partners
$ lm source rest test acme-saas -o json
note: skipped 1 disabled endpoint(s)
[
  {
    "endpoint": "cursor-partners",
    "method": "GET",
    "url": "http://host.docker.internal:8099/v1/partners",
    "status": 200,
    "ok": true,
    "items": 500,
    "detail": "",
    "sample": "{\"data\": [{\"id\": 1000, \"name\": \"Hydraulique Lyon 1000\", \"city\": \"Lyon\", \"country\": \"FR\", \"credit_limit\": 500, \"updated_at\": \"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z\"}, {\"id\": 1001, \"name\": \"Roulements Bruxelles 1001\", \"…"
  }
]
$ lm endpoint enable acme-saas/link-partners

docs.title: Draft an endpoint from a live path
docs.text:
probe samples one path on an existing connector and prints the endpoint block that would ingest it. The base URL and credential come from the connector:

$ lm source rest probe acme-partners --endpoint /spring/partners
# Drafted by lm source rest probe — review before applying
- id: spring-partners
  method: GET
  path: /spring/partners
  pagination: { kind: page }
  target:
    kind: hybrid
    table: ext.acme_partners_spring_partners
    unique_key: $.id
    promote:
      - { name: id, path: $.id, type: bigint }
      - { name: name, path: $.name, type: text }
      - { name: city, path: $.city, type: text }
      - { name: country, path: $.country, type: text }
      - { name: credit_limit, path: $.credit_limit, type: bigint }
      - { name: updated_at, path: $.updated_at, type: text }

Result: an endpoint fragment — paste it under spec.endpoints:, review it, then lm apply.

  • The pagination kind is a guess from the response envelope; an unknown envelope gives kind: unknown for you to fill in.
  • A list found with no paging signal is drafted as kind: none, with its response_path and a comment that gives the number of items read, such as # 6 items, no paging signal in the answer: if the source pages, declare how. A round count such as 20 or 50 is often one page: declare the pagination.
  • The promote list covers the scalar fields of the first record only.

An upstream error is reported instead of a draft:

$ lm source rest probe acme-partners --endpoint /open/nope
Error: API error 502: upstream returned HTTP 404 (permanent) — refusing to ingest its body as data: {"error": "unknown resource", "known": ["down", "drf", "flaky", "hdr", "liar", "link", "offset", "open", "spring", "v1"], "resource": "/open/nope"}

A connector that is not rest-generic is refused by name.

docs.title: Generate a manifest from an OpenAPI spec
docs.text:
The hub reads the spec and writes a draft manifest. The demo API serves one at /openapi.json:

lm source rest from-openapi http://localhost:8099/openapi.json \
    --name acme-from-openapi -o acme-from-openapi.yaml

The hub fetches the URL itself. From a hub in Docker, use http://host.docker.internal:8099/openapi.json. The draft's base_url is the spec's servers entry; the demo puts there the address you called.

Result: one endpoint per GET path of the spec. The draft writes only what the spec says. A path it cannot page correctly stays in the file, commented out:

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-from-openapi
  connector_type: rest-generic
spec:
  base_url: "http://localhost:8099"
  auth: { kind: bearer, token_env: ACME_FROM_OPENAPI_API_KEY }
  endpoints:
    # auth: this path asks for no credentials, not a bearer token — move it to a connector of its own.
    # pagination: not drafted — limit has no default and no maximum, so the page size is unknown.
    # Declare an offset pagination with a limit the source serves whole, then uncomment (https://docs.lumnik.io/connectors/rest/pagination/).
    # - id: open-partners
    #   method: GET
    #   path: "/open/partners"
    #   incremental: { mode: full }
    #   target: { kind: hybrid, table: ext.acme_from_openapi_open_partners, unique_key: $.id, promote: [] }
    # auth: this path asks for http basic, not a bearer token — move it to a connector of its own.
    # pagination: not drafted — page has no default and no minimum, so where pages start is unknown.
    # Declare a page pagination with its start_page, then uncomment (https://docs.lumnik.io/connectors/rest/pagination/).
    # - id: spring-partners
    #   method: GET
    #   path: "/spring/partners"
    #   incremental: { mode: full }
    #   target: { kind: hybrid, table: ext.acme_from_openapi_spring_partners, unique_key: $.id, promote: [] }
    - id: v1-partners
      method: GET
      path: "/v1/partners"
      pagination: { kind: cursor, cursor_param: starting_after, cursor_path: "$.data[-1:].id", has_more_path: "$.has_more", response_path: "$.data" }
      incremental: { mode: full }
      target: { kind: hybrid, table: ext.acme_from_openapi_v1_partners, unique_key: $.id, promote: [] }

The draft passes lm validate when at least one endpoint is not commented out. Review three things before you apply it:

  • Auth. It comes from the spec's security schemes: http basic, bearer or an API key, or none. Auth is one per connector, so the draft keeps the one most paths ask for. A path that asks for another is marked # auth:: give it a connector of its own. Create the secret the draft names (ACME_FROM_OPENAPI_API_KEY here) with lm secret set. A basic block also needs a real username in place of CHANGE_ME.
  • Pagination. It is drafted only when the parameters and the answer both say how pages work: a Stripe cursor, offset + limit with a declared limit, or page with a declared first number. Otherwise the endpoint is commented out under the key to declare. A guess here could skip a page and still end clean. In the demo, /open/partners takes { kind: offset, offset_param: offset, limit_param: limit, limit: 100, response_path: $.data } and /spring/partners takes { kind: spring-page }.
  • Target. promote is empty: every row lands as JSONB only.

A URL that holds no spec is refused:

$ lm source rest from-openapi http://127.0.0.1:8099/spring/partners --name x --scope billing -o x.yaml
Error: API error 502: no OpenAPI spec could be read at http://127.0.0.1:8099/spring/partners — unreachable, not a spec, or not parseable

docs.title: Reset a stuck cursor
docs.text:
lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint>

Result: the stored watermark is cleared and the next lm connector run is a full read. The command prints nothing.

docs.title: Empty one endpoint's rows
docs.text:
lm endpoint purge deletes the rows one endpoint has landed and keeps the connector, its other endpoints and its run history. --dry-run only counts:

$ lm endpoint purge acme-incremental/partners --dry-run
Would purge 2400 rows (dry run, nothing deleted)
$ lm endpoint purge acme-incremental/partners
Type 'purge' to delete 2400 rows: purge
Purged 2400 rows
$ lm endpoint purge acme-incremental/partners
Nothing to purge: this endpoint has no rows
  • Every rest-generic endpoint can be purged. A jdbc-generic, csv-file or kafka endpoint is refused — see Emptying one endpoint on its own.
  • --force skips the question.
  • Add lm endpoint reset-cursor to re-read the endpoint from scratch on the next run.
  • In lm ui, Del on :endpoints does the same, with the same count and question.

docs.title: Add a typed column later
docs.text:
Add an entry to the endpoint's target.promote list in your copy of 10-quickstart.yaml (here acme-partners.yaml) and re-apply:

promote:
  - { name: city,    path: $.city,    type: text }
  - { name: country, path: $.country, type: text }   # new column

Result: lm apply changes nothing in the database; the next run adds the column and fills it as rows are read again.

$ lm apply -f acme-partners.yaml
Applied connector "acme-partners" — 1 endpoint
$ lm connector run acme-partners
run scheduled: b9a1bf1a-f9dc-403c-a2d4-6cdab8fb7f79
$ lm run list --connector acme-partners
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b9a1bf1a  acme-partners  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 07:25  2026-10-19 07:25
9af1c00d  acme-partners  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 07:25  2026-10-19 07:25

lumnik=> SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE country IS NOT NULL) AS with_country, count(*)
lumnik->   FROM ext.acme_partners;
 with_country | count 
--------------+-------
         2400 |  2400
(1 row)

A full endpoint fills every row on that run; a watermark endpoint fills only the rows that change, unless you lm endpoint reset-cursor first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture Not sure the credential is valid — lm source rest test <connector> — one request per enabled endpoint, nothing written; an unresolved secret is named in VERDICT Run completed, IN is 0 the response arrived but nothing matched response_path lm source rest test <connector> shows 200 with 0 items; check response_path against the body Run failed on the source declared N rows total_path points at a number the run did not match check the source; if total_path points at a page count or an estimate, see The declared total 429 Too Many Requests from the API default_rate_limit exceeds what the API tolerates lower it (100/s → 50/s); it is one bucket for the whole connector Sync stops picking up new rows the stored watermark is stale or points at a column the source does not touch lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> → the next run is a full read A run reads far more pages than expected cursor, body-link and link-header send no size parameter put the size in the endpoint's path: — see the page-size warning lm apply refused with an unknown transform a promote entry's transform: is not one of the supported values see Transformers column 'x' is not in the row here at …mapping… a hook reads a field the endpoint does not promote promote it: a hook sees the promoted columns only path is required … this endpoint has none a promote entry without path, and no mapping to fill it give the entry a path, or the endpoint a mapping Run failed on the mapping writes column 'x', which no promote entry declares a script writes a column the table does not have add { name: x, type: … } to promote, without path Need to wipe an endpoint's rows — lm endpoint purge <connector>/<endpoint> — see Empty one endpoint's rows
