docs.title: Transformers — reference
docs.text: Every hook, its parameters and their defaults, on one page. The guide, by business problem: Transformers.

docs.title: How lm validate checks a mapping
docs.text:
• A misspelt hook or parameter is refused, with the entry's path and the accepted names: spec.mapping.cell[0].upper.colums → upper hook: unknown parameter 'colums' — accepted: columns.
  • A parameter of the wrong shape is refused the same way: a list where one name is expected, "yes" where true or false is expected, an empty list.
  • A column that does not exist is refused when the file's columns are known before it is read: parser.lines: true, or a headerless file with columns: declared. With a header read from the file, the run names the missing column instead.
  • A misspelt key under mapping is refused, naming the four it accepts: spec.mapping.cel → mapping: unknown key 'cel' — accepted: dataset, row, cell, on-error.

docs.title: Cell hooks
docs.text:
Hook Parameters (default) What it does clean columns; strip (false); remove-control-chars (false); normalize-unicode (off; NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD) always strips a leading BOM; then optional trim, control-character removal, Unicode normalization fix-mojibake columns BÃ©nÃ©dict → Bénédict; leaves a value it cannot repair safely as it is, +1 cell_errors decode-html-entities columns & → & replace-smart-quotes columns curly quotes and guillemets → ", dashes → -, ellipsis → ..., non-breaking space → space strip-invisible columns removes invisible characters: zero-width space, soft hyphen, BOM remove-diacritics columns Café → Cafe upper / lower columns case; text cells only titlecase columns DUPONT SARL → Dupont Sarl; also collapses repeated spaces fill-down columns; reset-when: { column, in } (none) an empty cell takes the last value above it, one file at a time; reset-when forgets it first truncate column; length (unlimited) keeps the first length characters regex-replace column; pattern; replacement ("") replaces every match; $1 in replacement is a group regex-extract column; pattern; groups (group number → new column); required (false) writes capture groups into new columns; a miss writes null, counted only with required: true default column; value fills an empty cell; never overwrites lookup column; table (map); on-missing (keep; or null / error / any value) translates a code with the map parse-date column; formats (list of date patterns); zone (UTC) first matching format wins; a pattern with a time gives a timestamp, otherwise a date parse-number column; decimal-separator (auto; or "," / "."); negatives-in-parens (false); integer (false) 1 234,56 € → 1234.56; with integer, a whole number parse-email column; lower (false) trims, optionally lowercases, checks the shape parse-phone column; default-region (US) 06 12 34 56 78 → +33612345678 with FR mask column; keep-first (0); keep-last (0); mask-char (*) masks the middle of the value split column; by (,); into (list) or into-array (false) parts into new columns, or an array to-uuid column; generate (false); generate-from (column); on-invalid (null; or keep / generate) makes the column a UUID — every case kotlin script (hooks:<name>.kts or classpath:<path>); context (map) your own code — Kotlin hooks
  • columns left out applies the hook to every column of the row.
  • A single-column hook takes column:, never columns:.

docs.title: Row hooks
docs.text: Hook Parameters (default) What it does map-columns rename (map old → new); drop (list) renames, then drops — drop uses the new names coalesce column; from (list) an empty target takes the first non-empty column of from defaults a map column: value fills each listed column when empty validate-row required (list) a row with an empty required column goes to the dead letters (ValidationFailed); place it before split-row split-row by (column) and sep (,); escape (one character); position (new column) — or explode (a column holding an array, from split: { into-array: true }) one row per part, the other columns copied; position numbers the parts

docs.title: Dataset hooks
docs.text: Hook Parameters (default) What it does require-headers columns (all must exist); any-of (one must) fails the run when the file has the wrong header skip-empty-rows — drops blank rows; counted in SKIPPED filter-where column; equals; in (list); regex (whole value) keeps the rows matching every criterion; the others count in SKIPPED sort-by columns (list) sorts each block of 500 rows, never the whole file enrich-context a map column: value; ${now} = the moment of ingestion adds a constant column; never overwrites

docs.title: When a hook cannot deliver: cell_errors and on-error
docs.text:
cell_errors counts the cells a hook could not deliver — one per cell:

The cell is Hooks emptied parse-date, parse-number, parse-email, parse-phone, lookup with on-missing: null, to-uuid with on-invalid: null, regex-extract with required: true left as it arrived fix-mojibake declined; split found more or fewer parts than into replaced by a value the source never sent to-uuid with on-invalid: generate overwritten map-columns renamed onto a column the row already had declared unreadable kotlin, by the script

lm run get prints the alert when the count is above zero:

⚠ 1 cell(s) a hook did not deliver as declared — the rows were still written

lm run get <id> -o json (or -o yaml) carries the count as cellErrors. What happens to the row, per column:

on-error mode The row soft (default) is written, the cell emptied; cell_errors counts it dlq goes to the dead letters as it was read (MappingFailed) — example fail stops the run
  • fields names the column: of a single-column hook. Every other hook follows default.
  • dlq is refused beside split-row: it would set aside parts, not source rows.

docs.title: Transformers — repair the data at the door
docs.text:
Legacy exports arrive dirty: broken accents, 31/12/2019 dates, 1 234,56 € amounts, a value written once for a whole block. Transformers repair them as the file is read. You declare them in the connector manifest; no code.

Every parameter, on one page: Transformers — reference.

docs.title: Where it applies
docs.text:
• A csv-file connector reads them in the manifest's spec.mapping block.
  • A REST, GraphQL or SOAP endpoint reads them in its own mapping, over its promoted columns: Run hooks over the promoted columns. One value alone takes transform:.
  • Not lm csv ingest. The one-shot load never transforms. Apply a csv-file connector.
  • A JDBC or Kafka connector writes what it reads. A JDBC table can only rename a column: JDBC: the hub table.
  • Dirty status values (fini, TERMINE) are not repaired here. Declare them as workflow aliases.

Try a manifest on a sample file first, read the result, then point it at the real feed. lm validate checks the manifest, not your data.

docs.title: How a mapping reads
docs.text:
spec:
  mapping:
    dataset:                    # 1 — the whole batch of rows
      - skip-empty-rows: {}
    row:                        # 2 — each row; may drop it or split it
      - map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name } }
    cell:                       # 3 — each value, in place
      - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name] }
  • The three tiers always run in this order: dataset, then row, then cell.
  • Inside a tier, hooks run top to bottom. The order is yours, and it matters.
  • One entry per hook: - hook-name: { parameters }.
  • lm validate refuses a misspelt hook or parameter, and names the entry: spec.mapping.cell[0].upper.colums → upper hook: unknown parameter 'colums' — accepted: columns.
  • It refuses a misspelt tier too: spec.mapping.cel → mapping: unknown key 'cel' — accepted: dataset, row, cell, on-error.

Nothing is dropped silently. A row leaves by one of three doors:

The row Hook Counted in excluded by a declared filter filter-where, skip-empty-rows SKIPPED missing a mandatory field validate-row SKIPPED and the dead letters written, one value emptied a cell hook that cannot read the value cell_errors

docs.title: The file has the wrong shape
require-headers — refuse a file with the wrong shape
docs.text:
dataset:
  - require-headers: { columns: [c_bpartner_id, name], any-of: [created, isactive] }
The file's header Result c_bpartner_id,name,created,isactive passes c_bpartner_id,name,created passes: every columns, one of any-of c_bpartner_id,name fails the run: none of required headers found: [created, isactive] name,created fails the run: required header missing: c_bpartner_id

A headerless file is checked against the parser.columns you declared.

docs.title: skip-empty-rows — blank lines in the export
docs.text:
dataset:
  - skip-empty-rows: {}
In Out C1,Acme Corp kept , dropped, counted in SKIPPED C2,Globex kept

docs.title: filter-where — keep only the rows you asked for
docs.text:
dataset:
  - filter-where: { column: status, in: [ACTIVE, PENDING] }
status in: [ACTIVE, PENDING] equals: ACTIVE regex: "[0-9]+" ACTIVE kept kept dropped PENDING kept dropped dropped 1042 dropped dropped kept 10a dropped dropped dropped: the pattern must match the whole value (empty) dropped dropped dropped
  • Several criteria combine: a row must match them all.
  • A dropped row counts in SKIPPED. It is not a dead letter.

docs.title: map-columns — legacy column names (CUST_NM)
docs.text:
row:
  - map-columns:
      rename: { CUST_NM: name, CUST_CITY: city }
      drop: [internal_flag]
In Out CUST_NM,CUST_CITY,internal_flag name,city Bénédict Martin,Montréal,X Bénédict Martin,Montréal
  • It renames first, then drops: drop uses the new names.

  • Rename a column away from a name the hub keeps for itself (id, tenant_id). lm validate refuses the opposite:

      ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.rename.CUST_ID
          targets 'id', a hub system column (_ingested_at, _mapping_version, _row_hash, _run_id, _source, id, tenant_id) — renaming a source column AWAY from one of these is what the rename is for, renaming into one only recreates the collision

  • Renaming onto a column the file already has overwrites it, and counts one cell_errors per row.

docs.title: coalesce — first non-blank of several columns
docs.text:
row:
  - coalesce: { column: display_name, from: [trade_name, name] }
display_name trade_name name → display_name (absent) Dupont DUPONT SARL Dupont (absent) (blank) DUPONT SARL DUPONT SARL Kept Dupont DUPONT SARL Kept: a filled target is never touched

It copies the value as it arrived, before the cell hooks change it.

docs.title: defaults — fill blanks in several columns
docs.text:
row:
  - defaults: { is_active: "Y", country: FR }
is_active → N N: never overwritten (blank) Y (absent) Y: the column is created

One column, later in the order: default.

docs.title: Rows that must not land incomplete
validate-row — rows missing mandatory fields
docs.text:
row:
  - validate-row: { required: [code, name] }

A file with C1,Acme Corp and C2, (no name):

$ lm run get fc9b4ba6
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
fc9b4ba6  csv-customers  default   Completed  2   1    1        1             2026-10-19 07:19  2026-10-19 07:19
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run fc9b4ba6-5b32-49a3-af64-f96b8c344a2c
  • C1 lands. C2 goes to the dead letters, with the reason required column 'name' is missing or blank.
  • Place validate-row before split-row. lm validate refuses the other order.
  • Fix the source, run again, then close the dead letter: Diagnosing a failed run.

docs.title: An empty amount is a wrong row: on-error: dlq
docs.text:
By default, a value a hook cannot read is emptied, and the row lands. For an invoice, a row without its amount is wrong. Say so for that column. The file:

invoice_no,customer,amount_eur
F-1001,ACME,1250.00
F-1002,Globex,n/a
F-1003,Initech,89.90

The manifest's mapping:

  mapping:
    on-error:
      fields: { amount_eur: dlq }   # this column: set the row aside
      default: soft                 # every other column: write it, count the cell
    cell:
      - parse-number: { column: amount_eur, decimal-separator: "." }

The run sets F-1002 aside, as it was read:

$ lm run get 460efbba
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
460efbba  invoices   default   Completed  3   2    1        1             2026-10-24 22:15  2026-10-24 22:15
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 460efbba-458f-461d-b6d3-45e439415abe
$ lm dlq get 260a6940-0d56-4478-a743-a5b8713660d8
ID:        260a6940-0d56-4478-a743-a5b8713660d8
Connector: invoices (a7487f8c-c3db-4afa-adc5-88e2ab8cb487)
Run:       460efbba-458f-461d-b6d3-45e439415abe
Reason:    MappingFailed
Attempts:  1
Message:   amount_eur: parse-number could not read the value
Detail:    {"field":"amount_eur","message":"parse-number could not read the value"}
Payload:   {"customer":"Globex","amount_eur":"n/a","invoice_no":"F-1002"}
Resolution: open
  • Three modes: soft (the default) writes the row; dlq sets it aside; fail stops the run.
  • fields names the column: of a hook. Full example: docs/connectors/csv/72-on-error-dlq.yaml.

docs.title: clean — BOM, stray whitespace, control characters
docs.text:
cell:
  - clean: { columns: [name, note], strip: true, remove-control-chars: true, normalize-unicode: NFC }
In Out ﻿ hello\t (a BOM, two spaces, a tab) hello Café written as e + a separate accent Café with one é (NFC)
  • A BOM at the start is always removed. The three switches are off by default.
  • Use NFC when two exports spell the same accent two ways and your keys stop matching.

docs.title: fix-mojibake — accents came out as BÃ©nÃ©dict
docs.text:
A Windows export often garbles accents. This hook repairs them, only when it recognizes the pattern:

cell:
  - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name, city] }
In Out BÃ©nÃ©dict Martin Bénédict Martin CAFÃ‰ DU PORT, lâ€™atelier, 10 â‚¬ CAFÉ DU PORT, l’atelier, 10 € Bénédict Martin unchanged: a clean value is never touched BÃ©nÃ©dict € unchanged, +1 cell_errors: repairing it would garble the €

A value it declines lands as it arrived. Re-export it from the source with the right encoding.

docs.title: decode-html-entities — & in text
docs.text: In Out Eau & Soleil Eau & Soleil café café

docs.title: replace-smart-quotes — curly quotes from Word and Excel
docs.text: In Out “Eau & Soleil” – depuis 1998… "Eau & Soleil" - depuis 1998... l’été l'été «bonjour» "bonjour"

docs.title: strip-invisible — a code that "looks equal" but never matches
docs.text: In Out AB​CD (an invisible space inside) ABCD soft­hyphen softhyphen

docs.title: remove-diacritics — ASCII-only identifiers
docs.text: In Out Montréal Montreal

docs.title: upper / lower / titlecase — case
docs.text:
Hook In Out upper sarl SARL lower Montreal montreal titlecase MARTIN DUPONT (two spaces) Martin Dupont

They change text cells only. titlecase also collapses repeated spaces.

docs.title: truncate — hard cut
docs.text:
- truncate: { column: name, length: 60 } keeps the first 60 characters.

All these hooks take columns: [a, b], or every column when columns is left out:

cell:
  - decode-html-entities: { columns: [slogan] }
  - replace-smart-quotes: { columns: [slogan] }
  - strip-invisible: { columns: [code] }
  - remove-diacritics: { columns: [city] }
  - titlecase: { columns: [name] }

docs.title: parse-date — dates are 31/12/2019
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-date: { column: signup_date, formats: ["dd/MM/yyyy", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"] }
In Out 31/12/2019 2019-12-31: a date 2004-10-18 23:42:39 2004-10-18 23:42:39+00: a timestamp 12/31/2019 (empty), +1 cell_errors: no format matched
  • Formats are tried in order.
  • dd is the day, MM the month, yyyy the year. Lowercase mm means minutes: the classic trap.
  • A format with a time (HH:mm) gives a timestamp. Without, a date.

docs.title: Which time zone a time is in
docs.text:
An ERP writes 2026-08-02 23:30:00 without a time zone. Say which one it is:

cell:
  - parse-date: { column: stamp, formats: ["yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"], zone: Europe/Paris }
In zone Stored (shown in UTC) 2026-08-02 23:30:00 (none) 2026-08-02 23:30:00+00: read as UTC 2026-08-02 23:30:00 Europe/Paris 2026-08-02 21:30:00+00: Paris is UTC+2 in summer 2026-01-15 23:30:00 Europe/Paris 2026-01-15 22:30:00+00: UTC+1 in winter 2026-08-02 Europe/Paris 2026-08-02: a date has no time
  • An unknown zone is refused at lm validate.
  • Fusing these dates with an ERP's in an entity: Dates across sources.

docs.title: parse-number — numbers are 1 234,56 € or (123)
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-number: { column: balance, decimal-separator: ",", negatives-in-parens: true }
In Out 1 234,56 € 1234.56 (123) -123 $1,234.50 with decimal-separator: "." 1234.50 n/a (empty), +1 cell_errors

It removes currency signs and spaces. A new column holds decimals: 1024944 reads 1024944.0000.

docs.title: An integer column: integer: true
docs.text:
An identifier or a count is a whole number. Say so:

cell:
  - parse-number: { column: m_product_id, integer: true }
In Out 1024944 1024944: an integer 7.0000 7 7.1 (empty), +1 cell_errors: not a whole number

A column is typed when the table is created. Two consequences:

  • If the first rows leave the column empty, it is created as text, and stays text.
  • Adding parse-date or parse-number to a connector that already ran does not change its column. Create the table again: the four steps.

docs.title: lookup — translate codes with an inline table
docs.text:
cell:
  - lookup: { column: is_active, table: { "Y": "true", "N": "false" }, on-missing: null }
In on-missing: keep (default) null error INACTIVE (any value) Y true true true true ? ? (empty), +1 cell_errors the run fails INACTIVE

The translated values land as text.

docs.title: default — fill one blank column
docs.text:
cell:
  - default: { column: legal_form, value: "NONE" }
In Out SARL SARL: never overwritten (empty) NONE

docs.title: parse-email — trim, lowercase, validate
docs.text:
- parse-email: { column: contact_email, lower: true }

In Out Contact@Example.COM contact@example.com contact at example (empty), +1 cell_errors

docs.title: parse-phone — one format for every phone
docs.text:
- parse-phone: { column: phone, default-region: FR }

In Out 06 12 34 56 78 +33612345678 +1 415 555 2671 +14155552671: a full number ignores the region abc (empty), +1 cell_errors

Set default-region to the source's country. The default is US: French numbers would land wrong.

docs.title: regex-replace — normalise with a pattern
docs.text:
cell:
  - regex-replace: { column: name, pattern: "\\s+", replacement: " " }
In Out DUPONT SARL DUPONT SARL
  • Every match is replaced. Without replacement, the match is deleted.
  • In replacement, $1 is the first group. Write a literal $ as \\$.

docs.title: regex-extract — pull a piece into its own column
docs.text:
cell:
  - regex-extract:
      column: name
      pattern: "\\b(SARL|SAS|EURL|SCI)\\b"
      groups: { 1: legal_form }
name → legal_form DUPONT SARL SARL Standard (empty): no match
  • Each group writes into a new column. lm validate refuses a column the row already holds. To rewrite a value in place, use regex-replace.
  • A miss is not counted: an optional field misses on many rows. A column that is empty on every row means the pattern never matched.
  • Every row must match? Add required: true: a miss then counts one cell_errors.
  • Follow it with default to give the misses a value.

docs.title: split — parts into new columns
docs.text:
cell:
  - split: { column: tags, by: ";", into: [tag1, tag2, tag3] }
tags tag1 tag2 tag3 cell_errors retail;online;b2b retail online b2b — retail;online retail online (empty) +1: fewer parts a;b;c;d a b c +1: d has nowhere to go

The row stays one row. into-array: true writes one array instead.

docs.title: split-row — one row per value of a;b;c
docs.text:
An order line lists its items in one cell:

order_no,items
ORD-1,TSH-BLEU-M|TSH-BLEU-M|CAP-NOIR

split-row makes one row per item. Two identical items would land as one row. Add position: each row then carries its place, and both land.

row:
  - split-row: { by: items, sep: "|", position: item_no }
Without position With position order_no items order_no items item_no ORD-1 TSH-BLEU-M ORD-1 TSH-BLEU-M 1 ORD-1 CAP-NOIR ORD-1 TSH-BLEU-M 2 ORD-1 CAP-NOIR 3
  • The other columns are copied onto each row. IN and OUT still count one source row.
  • position names a new column.
  • A separator written inside a value, such as EDIFACT's ?': add escape: "?".

docs.title: A value written once, for the rows below
fill-down — a value written once, for the rows that follow
docs.text:
A bank statement writes the account number once, on the first row of its block:

account,booked_on,label,amount
FR76-3000-0001,2026-10-01,Solde initial,1200.00
,2026-10-03,Virement client ACME,450.00
,2026-10-05,Prélèvement URSSAF,-320.00
FR76-3000-0002,2026-10-01,Solde initial,800.00
,2026-10-04,Carte bancaire,-42.50

fill-down copies it onto the rows below, until the next account:

  mapping:
    cell:
      - fill-down: { columns: [account] }

$ lm connector run bank-statement
$ lm run get 3df03f1c
ID        CONNECTOR       ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
3df03f1c  bank-statement  default   Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-24 22:15  2026-10-24 22:15

lumnik=> select account, booked_on, label, amount from connector.t_bank_statement;
    account     | booked_on  |        label         | amount
----------------+------------+----------------------+---------
 FR76-3000-0001 | 2026-10-01 | Solde initial        | 1200.00
 FR76-3000-0001 | 2026-10-03 | Virement client ACME | 450.00
 FR76-3000-0001 | 2026-10-05 | Prélèvement URSSAF   | -320.00
 FR76-3000-0002 | 2026-10-01 | Solde initial        | 800.00
 FR76-3000-0002 | 2026-10-04 | Carte bancaire       | -42.50
(5 rows)

Every movement now carries its account. Full example: docs/connectors/csv/70-fill-down.yaml.

Start again at each block: reset-when. An order export writes an H row (the order), then its L rows (the lines). The second order has no customer:

type,order_no,customer,sku,qty
H,SO-1,ACME,,
L,,,PMP-100,2
L,,,VAN-200,1
H,SO-2,,,
L,,,FLT-300,5

Without care, SO-2 would inherit ACME. reset-when forgets what is carried at each H row:

      - fill-down: { columns: [order_no, customer], reset-when: { column: type, in: [H] } }

lumnik=> select type, order_no, customer, sku, qty from connector.t_order_lines;
 type | order_no | customer |   sku   | qty
------+----------+----------+---------+-----
 H    | SO-1     | ACME     |         |
 L    | SO-1     | ACME     | PMP-100 | 2
 L    | SO-1     | ACME     | VAN-200 | 1
 H    | SO-2     |          |         |
 L    | SO-2     |          | FLT-300 | 5
(5 rows)
  • Each file starts with nothing carried.
  • A filter-where runs before: a row it drops is never carried from. Filter the H rows out later, in a view, not here.
  • fill-down follows the file's order. lm validate refuses it beside sort-by.

Full example: docs/connectors/csv/71-fill-down-reset.yaml.

docs.title: to-uuid — an id column holds junk like N/A or 0
docs.text:
Two knobs: generate decides an empty cell, on-invalid a cell holding junk.

cell:
  - to-uuid:
      column: customer_id
      generate: true          # an EMPTY cell gets a new id
      on-invalid: keep        # a cell holding "N/A" is left alone for you to look at
The cell holds generate on-invalid Result cell_errors a valid UUID any any unchanged — nothing false (default) any stays empty — nothing true any a new id — N/A any null (default) emptied +1 N/A any generate a new id in place of N/A +1 N/A any keep N/A, untouched —

A generated id changes at every run. To keep one id per row, derive it from a column:

cell:
  - to-uuid: { column: ext_id, generate-from: code }   # F0004 gets the same id every night

on-invalid: generate invents an identifier

The new id replaces a value your source sent, and joins to nothing elsewhere. Only a few rows dirty? Run once with keep and look at them first.

docs.title: mask — a column holds card/PII data
docs.text:
cell:
  - mask: { column: card_number, keep-last: 4 }
In Out 4556123498761234 ************1234 contact@example.com with keep-first: 2, keep-last: 4 co*************.com 1234 1234: not masked, too short

Two things to know before trusting mask

  • A value not longer than keep-first + keep-last lands unmasked.
  • A dead letter keeps the raw value. A row set aside before the cell tier is shown unmasked by lm dlq get.

docs.title: enrich-context — stamp provenance on every row
docs.text:
dataset:
  - enrich-context: { source_system: siebel, ingested_at: "${now}" }

Every row gains source_system = siebel and the moment of ingestion. An existing value is never overwritten.

docs.title: sort-by — order within the chunk
docs.text: - sort-by: { columns: [c_bpartner_id] } sorts each block of 500 rows, as text, empty values first. It never sorts the whole file.

docs.title: Order matters
docs.text:
Three placements to get right

  • validate-row before split-row. lm validate refuses the other order.
  • regex-extract before mask: after mask, the value is stars.
  • default after the regex-extract whose misses it fills.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Do this Rows missing, and no dead letter A filter-where or skip-empty-rows dropped them. Read SKIPPED in lm run get. DEAD-LETTERS > 0, reason MalformedSource The file itself is broken: wrong column count, unclosed quote. lm dlq get <id> shows the line. Fix the export. A column is empty on some rows, the rows landed A hook could not read those values. lm run get warns with ⚠ N cell(s) a hook did not deliver. A regex-extract column is empty on every row The pattern never matched. Test it on a real value. The mapping seems to do nothing You loaded with lm csv ingest, which never transforms. lm validate: unknown cell hook: … A typo, or the hook is under the wrong tier. The refusal lists the tier's hooks. A run fails and says run lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> The file or the mapping changed while a fill-down run had stopped halfway. Run the command: the next run reads the file again from its start. aggregator is not supported on csv-file connector runs Group the rows in the source export instead. lm validate refuses spec.mapping.cell[N].kotlin Kotlin hooks

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Transformers — reference: every hook and parameter.
  • Kotlin hooks: your own code, when no transformer fits.
  • CSV & files: the connector these hooks run in.
  • docs/connectors/csv/ in the repository: the runnable manifests.

docs.title: JDBC — Oracle
docs.text:
lumnik Pro. The Oracle provider ships in lumnik Pro with its JDBC driver — you drop no jar. The open edition has no Oracle provider: a manifest declaring dialect: oracle there is refused with JDBC dialect 'oracle' is not installed. Available: postgres.

spec:
  connection:
    url: jdbc:oracle:thin:@//erp-db.acme.io:1521/ERP   # by service name
    user: ro_user
    password_env: ACME_DB_PASSWORD
    dialect: oracle                                    # optional, inferred from the url
  defaults:
    schema: ERP                                        # the OWNER, exactly as Oracle stores it
  source:
    tables:
      - name: ORDERS                                   # exactly as `lm source jdbc discover` prints it
        mode: watermark
        watermark_column: UPDATED_AT
        pk_columns: [ID]
        rename:
          ID: order_id                                 # optional: land a column under another name
  • Versions. Oracle 12c and later; tested on Oracle 23ai Free only. Oracle 11g is not supported.
  • Connect by service name: @//host:1521/SERVICE, @host:1521/SERVICE, or a full @(DESCRIPTION=…) descriptor (quote it in YAML). The SID form (@host:1521:SID) works on a non-multitenant database only; on a multitenant one it fails with ORA-01017. TCPS and wallets are not tested.
  • lm needs --schema. lm source jdbc discover and add default to --schema public; for Oracle pass the owner, e.g. --schema ERP, or the listing is empty.
  • Names are exact, never folded. Write schema, table and column names exactly as lm source jdbc discover lists them (ORDERS, not orders).
  • The hub columns keep that spelling — quoted upper-case ("ID", "UPDATED_AT"), next to the hub's lower-case system columns. Quote them in a query, or rename: them.
  • Empty string is NULL. Oracle stores '' as NULL; the hub receives NULL.
  • Index (watermark, key) on every Oracle table you page. Without it every page scans the whole table. A very large group of rows sharing one watermark value still pages more slowly.
  • Watermark ties and NULLs behave as on PostgreSQL — see A run reads what the table held when it started.
Oracle type Lands as NUMBER, FLOAT, BINARY_FLOAT, BINARY_DOUBLE by the Column types table VARCHAR2, NVARCHAR2, CHAR, NCHAR, CLOB, NCLOB TEXT DATE, TIMESTAMP (no time zone) TIMESTAMPTZ, read in the connection's zone, UTC without one: DATE '2026-01-02' lands as 2026-01-02 00:00:00+00 TIMESTAMP WITH [LOCAL] TIME ZONE TIMESTAMPTZ, the same instant — usable as a watermark BLOB, RAW, LONG, LONG RAW, XMLTYPE, BFILE, ROWID, object types refused: discover lists the column under UNSUPPORTED, add refuses the table by name

docs.title: Writing a JDBC provider
docs.text:
jdbc-generic reads one database per connector. The database it speaks is decided by a provider: a module that owns that database's SQL dialect and its JDBC driver. PostgreSQL ships with every edition, Oracle with lumnik Pro; any other database is one more provider.

This page is for a Java developer adding a database. Using an installed provider needs no code — see JDBC → Connection.

docs.title: What a provider is
docs.text:
• A Maven module io.lumnik:lumnik-jdbc-<db>, classes under the package io.lumnik.jdbc.<db>.
  • It depends on lumnik-jdbc-spi and on its own driver, even when the hub already carries it.
  • It exposes one CDI bean implementing JdbcDialect. The hub never imports a provider class; it collects every installed bean.

Two build details decide whether the hub sees the provider at all:

  • the module builds a jandex index (jandex-maven-plugin) — without it the hub boots with that dialect missing, and says nothing;
  • the hub depends on it with runtime scope.

Providers add up: several live in one image, and each connector picks its own.

docs.title: What each method owes
docs.text:
Method Contract id() The lowercase name used in dialect:. Unique across installed providers. aliases() Other accepted spellings (PostgreSQL: postgresql). Unique too. acceptsUrl(url) Whether this provider recognises the JDBC scheme. Used to infer a missing dialect:. driverClass() The driver the pool loads. A provider installed without its driver fails with JDBC driver 'X' of dialect 'Y' is not on the classpath. quoteIdentifier(id) Quote one identifier. The query builder never concatenates a raw name. keyComparison(columns, comparison) The > (cursor) or <= (run ceiling) comparison over the quoted key columns, and the bind plan. No default. limitClause(n) The row limit appended after ORDER BY (LIMIT 100, FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY, …). No default. defaultSkipPatterns() Table-name globs excluded from discovery when the request gives none. unsupportedReason(column) Why this provider cannot read a column, or empty. Discovery lists the table with the column named; the guided add refuses it. Default: every column is readable. readColumn(rs, index) The value of a cell. Default getObject; override for a LOB locator or a driver-specific timestamp class, and throw to refuse a type you cannot read. isWallClock(metadata, index) Whether the column holds a date and time written with no time zone, which the hub then reads in the connection's zone, UTC without one. Default: the column's JDBC type is TIMESTAMP. Override it when your driver reports a zoned type under that same code. sessionInitSql() A statement run on every new connection of this dialect's pool — for a database whose session settings (sort order, number format) change what a query means. Default: none. introspection listTables, tableExists, listColumns, listPrimaryKey, listForeignKeys, estimateRowCount, inferWatermarkColumn.

keyComparison and limitClause have no default so that a provider cannot compile while emitting SQL its database rejects, or reads differently.

docs.title: The bind plan
docs.text:
keyComparison returns a KeyComparison(sql, parameterIndexes). The i-th ? of the SQL takes the value of key column parameterIndexes[i].

Dialect SQL for (a, b) > cursor Plan PostgreSQL (row value) ("a", "b") > (?, ?) [0, 1] a database without tuple comparison (("a" > ?) OR ("a" = ? AND "b" > ?)) [0, 0, 1]
  • The SQL is one self-contained, parenthesised predicate: the builder joins it with AND, and for a watermark ceiling with OR <watermark> IS NULL.
  • The builder refuses a plan that is empty for a non-empty key, or that names a column that does not exist.

docs.title: How a connector picks its provider
docs.text:
Manifest Result dialect: names an installed provider, URL accepted that provider dialect: names a provider that is not installed refused: JDBC dialect 'X' is not installed. Available: … dialect: set, URL not accepted by it refused, naming the dialect and the URL scheme dialect: absent, exactly one provider accepts the URL that provider dialect: absent, none accepts it refused, listing the installed providers dialect: absent, several accept it refused as ambiguous
  • Names are compared trimmed and lowercased.
  • Two providers claiming the same id or alias stop the hub at startup, naming both.
  • A connection pool is kept per URL, user, tenant, driver and dialect: two providers that accept the same URL never share one.

docs.title: Build it in, and check it
docs.text:
1. Add your module to the hub as a runtime dependency, in a Maven profile, like the Oracle one in lumnik-hub/pom.xml.
  2. Rebuild the hub image with that profile.

  3. Point lm at a database of your kind:

    lm source jdbc test --url jdbc:<db>://host:port/base --user ro_user

    The answer names your provider on its Dialect : line. A hub built without it refuses the URL, listing the providers it has.

docs.title: The demo broker
docs.text:
One Redpanda in a container and one Python file that fills it with ten topics, plus one name kept absent on purpose, over the same 2 400 fictional ACME partners the REST demo API serves — the source every screen of the Kafka page reads.

It ships with the repo. Two commands start and fill it:

docker compose -f docs/connectors/kafka/demo/docker-compose.yml up -d
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py

  ▸ created acme.partners
  ▸ created acme.orders
  ▸ created acme.partners-drift
  ▸ created acme.partners-poison
  ▸ created acme.partners-compacted
  ▸ created acme.partners-reserved
  ▸ created acme.partners-raw
  ▸ created acme.partners-trimmed
  ▸ created acme.empty
  ▸ created acme.live
  ✓ filled
  ✓ eleven topics as declared (acme.absent is absent)

The script needs the Kafka client for Python: python3 -m pip install confluent-kafka.

docs.title: The topics
docs.text:
A partner has the same name and city here and on the REST demo. Each topic serves one section of the Kafka page:

Topic Shape Used by acme.partners 2 400 JSON objects, one partition Quickstart acme.orders 24 000 orders, keyed by partner over six partitions Partitions and the cursor acme.partners-drift 2 400, and two new fields appear at message 1 201 Schema evolution acme.partners-poison 1 000, of which 143 are not a JSON object Poison messages acme.partners-compacted cleanup.policy=compact; 1 000 rows then 300 tombstones Tombstones acme.partners-reserved 500, each carrying a top-level id — the REST record verbatim Seven reserved names acme.partners-raw 500 with Partner Name, credit.limit, MONTANT_€, an object and an array Names the producer chose acme.partners-trimmed 5 000, and trim moves its log start on demand A log that moved under the cursor acme.empty created, zero messages An empty poll acme.live empty until feed writes to it while a run reads The head is the target acme.absent never created A topic that does not exist

The poison is placed deterministically (every index where i % 7 == 3: a truncated object, a JSON array, a JSON scalar), so every fill gives the same counts.

docs.title: The three gestures that change the broker
docs.text:
These three write to the broker; the Kafka page says when to use each:

python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py feed --rate 200 --seconds 30     # a producer racing the run, on acme.live
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed --rate 500 --seconds 2
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py trim 5500                        # acme.partners-trimmed: offsets 0..5499 are gone

trim moves the partition's log start at once, as retention would over days. It runs rpk in the container lumnik-demo-redpanda; set KAFKA_DEMO_CONTAINER to use another one.

docs.title: Checking it before you blame the manifest
docs.text:
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py verify

It checks every topic's count and partitions, and that acme.absent does not exist. After trim, or feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed, verify reports acme.partners-trimmed: expected. reset drops the topics and fills them again:

python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py reset

Reset the hub's cursors too. With the old cursor, a run on a refilled topic reads nothing and completes. After reset, for each connector to read from the start:

lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/default

host.docker.internal:29092, not localhost:19092

  • Your shell (and acme-topics.py) reaches the broker at localhost:19092.
  • The hub, in its container, reaches it at host.docker.internal:29092 — what the manifests carry. The wrong listener ends in the broker timeout after about 60 s.

Check both:

docker exec lumnik-demo-redpanda rpk cluster info --brokers localhost:9092
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec hub bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/host.docker.internal/29092 && echo REACHABLE'

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• Automatic topic creation is off, so acme.absent stays absent.
  • Authenticates nobody. Every topic is plaintext. The sasl-plain manifest on the Kafka page shows its refusals, not a successful handshake.
  • A throwaway rig. One node, no replication, no persistence to count on.

docs.title: Kafka — when the topic misbehaves
docs.text: lumnik Pro. A bad message, a deletion, a missing topic, a log that moved, a broker that does not answer. Each case replays on the demo broker.

docs.title: Poison messages — the per-message DLQ
docs.text:
acme.partners-poison holds 1 000 messages of which 143 are not a JSON object — a truncated object, a JSON array, a JSON scalar:

# 40-poison.yaml — messages that are not JSON objects go to the dead letters.
#
# acme.partners-poison holds 1 000 messages; 143 are not a JSON object: a truncated object, a
# JSON array, a JSON scalar.
#
# Expect: Completed, in=1000 out=857 skipped=143, 143 dead letters under MalformedSource,
#         857 rows in the table.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-kafka-poison
  connector_type: kafka
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  name: acme_partners_poison
  # The hub runs in Docker: `localhost` there is the hub's own container, not your machine.
  brokers: host.docker.internal:29092
  topic: acme.partners-poison
  format: json

$ lm run get 4337fffd
ID        CONNECTOR          ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
4337fffd  acme-kafka-poison  default   Completed  1000  857  143      143           2026-10-24 22:35  2026-10-24 22:35
⚠ 143 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 4337fffd-5654-41a2-b32a-447a583e48ad
$ lm dlq list --run 4337fffd-5654-41a2-b32a-447a583e48ad
ID        CONNECTOR          RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  RESOLUTION  MESSAGE
9b85fe53  acme-kafka-poison  4337fffd  MalformedSource  1                     acme.partners-poison:0:997:997 — message value is not a JSON…
66e84e95  acme-kafka-poison  4337fffd  MalformedSource  1                     acme.partners-poison:0:990:990 — invalid JSON: Unexpected en…
9edf38bb  acme-kafka-poison  4337fffd  MalformedSource  1                     acme.partners-poison:0:983:983 — message value is not a JSON…
$ lm dlq get 9b85fe53-7f0a-4228-a645-0e88843c7d88
ID:        9b85fe53-7f0a-4228-a645-0e88843c7d88
Connector: acme-kafka-poison (9abf52e2-55a4-491d-82b6-4bde61d469b1)
Run:       4337fffd-5654-41a2-b32a-447a583e48ad
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   acme.partners-poison:0:997:997 — message value is not a JSON object
Detail:    {"file":"acme.partners-poison:0:997","line":997,"message":"message value is not a JSON object"}
Payload:   {"raw":["[1, 2, 3]"],"file":"acme.partners-poison:0:997","line":997}
Resolution: open
  • IN 1000 = OUT 857 + SKIPPED 143, and the table holds 857 rows.
  • Each entry names topic:partition:offset and keeps the raw value.
  • A bad message is set aside once, and never read again. A long run of them stops the run early, Partial; the next run continues after them.
  • The producer sent a fixed message? Once a run has read it, close the old entry: lm dlq replayed <id> --new-run-id <run>. Otherwise: lm dlq discard <id>.

docs.title: Tombstones — a deletion is not garbage
docs.text:
On a compacted topic, a record with a null value is how a producer says "this key is deleted"; log compaction keeps it as the deletion marker. acme.partners-compacted holds 1 000 partners, then 300 tombstones:

# 45-compacted.yaml — a compacted topic carrying tombstones.
#
# 1 000 partner records, then the producer deletes the first 300 keys — on a compacted topic
# a deletion is a record with a NULL value, the tombstone log compaction keeps as the marker.
# The hub's ingestion is append-only: a tombstone is dead-lettered under a reason naming the
# key, never applied as a DELETE on the table.
#
# Expect: Completed, in=1300 out=1000 skipped=300, 300 dead-letters each naming its key,
#         1 000 rows in the table.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-kafka-compacted
  connector_type: kafka
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  name: acme_partners_compacted
  # The hub runs in Docker: `localhost` there is the hub's own container, not your machine.
  brokers: host.docker.internal:29092
  topic: acme.partners-compacted
  format: json

$ lm run get f1005a9a
ID        CONNECTOR             ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
f1005a9a  acme-kafka-compacted  default   Completed  1300  1000  300      300           2026-10-24 22:37  2026-10-24 22:37
⚠ 300 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run f1005a9a-9121-45bf-be57-b9a8ddb454e6
$ lm dlq get b931b145-2503-4ceb-be26-cd759d1d7b7b
ID:        b931b145-2503-4ceb-be26-cd759d1d7b7b
Connector: acme-kafka-compacted (845c4dc6-8ec2-429d-bf39-3fe004be76c7)
Run:       f1005a9a-9121-45bf-be57-b9a8ddb454e6
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   acme.partners-compacted:0:1299:1299 — Kafka tombstone (key '1299'): the message value is null — the producer deleted that key, and append-only ingestion dead-letters the marker rather than applying it as a delete
Detail:    {"file":"acme.partners-compacted:0:1299","line":1299,"message":"Kafka tombstone (key '1299'): the message value is null — the producer deleted that key, and append-only ingestion dead-letters the marker rather than applying it as a delete"}
Payload:   {"raw":[],"file":"acme.partners-compacted:0:1299","line":1299}
Resolution: open
  • A tombstone does not delete the row. It becomes a dead letter naming the deleted key.
  • A deletion that must reach the table travels as data: a field the producer sets, such as deleted: true.

docs.title: A topic that does not exist
docs.text:
# 60-absent.yaml — a topic the broker does not have.
#
# acme.absent is never created, and the consumer the hub builds is forbidden to create it
# (a read must not write to its source). The refusal names the topic and says which of two
# situations it is: a first read (check the name) or an endpoint that had read this topic
# before (the broker lost it, or the name was edited).
#
# Expect: Failed — `kafka topic 'acme.absent' does not exist on the broker`.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-kafka-absent
  connector_type: kafka
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  name: acme_absent
  # The hub runs in Docker: `localhost` there is the hub's own container, not your machine.
  brokers: host.docker.internal:29092
  topic: acme.absent
  format: json

$ lm run get c1008671
ID        CONNECTOR          ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
c1008671  acme-kafka-absent  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-13 02:21  2026-09-13 02:21
✖ run failed: kafka topic 'acme.absent' does not exist on the broker: it reports no partition for that name, so there is nothing to read. Check spec.topic for a typo, or create the topic on the broker. The hub never creates one (an ingestion run must not write to its source).
  • The hub never creates a topic, even on a broker that allows automatic creation.
  • On an endpoint that already has a stored position, the message says the topic was read before: it was deleted or renamed on the broker, or the manifest's topic was edited.

docs.title: A log that moved under the cursor
docs.text:
Retention, compaction or a trim moves a partition's log start forward, past a stored position. Replay it on the demo broker:

# 70-trimmed.yaml — the broker deletes what the cursor still points at.
#
# Retention, compaction or an administrative trim moves a partition's log start forward. A
# stored position below it names messages that no longer exist. Replay it in three gestures:
#
#   lm connector run acme-kafka-trimmed                              # run 1: 5 000, cursor at 5 000
#   python3 …/acme-topics.py feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed --rate 500 --seconds 2   # ~600 more
#   python3 …/acme-topics.py trim 5500                               # offsets 0..5499 are gone
#   lm connector run acme-kafka-trimmed                              # run 2
#
# Expect: run 2 ends `Partial`, its error names offsets 5000..5499 as unreadable, and the
#         hub log carries the same sentence at WARN.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-kafka-trimmed
  connector_type: kafka
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  name: acme_partners_trimmed
  # The hub runs in Docker: `localhost` there is the hub's own container, not your machine.
  brokers: host.docker.internal:29092
  topic: acme.partners-trimmed
  format: json

$ lm connector run acme-kafka-trimmed                                    # run 1
$ python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed --rate 500 --seconds 2
  ▪ fed 607 messages at 500.0/s into acme.partners-trimmed
$ python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py trim 5500
  ✓ acme.partners-trimmed now starts at offset 5500 (high watermark 5607): offsets 0..5499 are gone
$ lm connector run acme-kafka-trimmed                                    # run 2
$ lm run list --connector acme-kafka-trimmed
ID        CONNECTOR           ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
49b90bd6  acme-kafka-trimmed  default   Partial    107   107   0        0             2026-09-13 02:22  2026-09-13 02:22
c30cf76f  acme-kafka-trimmed  default   Completed  5000  5000  0        0             2026-09-13 02:22  2026-09-13 02:22
$ lm run get 49b90bd6 > /dev/null
• run partial: acme.partners-trimmed[0]: the stored position is offset 5000 but the broker's log now starts at 5500 — offsets 5000..5499 are no longer on the broker (retention, compaction or a trim removed them) and can never be read; resuming at 5500
  • Run 2 read the 107 messages left and ended Partial, naming the lost range (5000..5499). Those messages cannot be recovered.
  • A first run (or one after lm endpoint reset-cursor) on a topic whose start moved completes normally: nothing was lost for this connector.
  • When it repeats: raise the topic's retention, or run more often.

docs.title: An empty poll, and what it does not prove
docs.text:
A run ends when a poll returns nothing. On a slow link with a short poll_timeout_ms, a poll can time out before the first fetch and end the run with less than the topic holds.

  • The run stays Completed. A green run that read less than expected: raise poll_timeout_ms. The hub log names the topic with a warning.

An empty topic, with no such line:

$ lm run list --connector acme-kafka-empty
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2b7a9ee6  acme-kafka-empty  default   Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-13 02:21  2026-09-13 02:21

docs.title: A broker that does not answer
docs.text:
An address that does not answer, or refuses the connection, fails the run after about 60 s — here brokers: 10.255.255.1:9092:

$ lm run get ffb91ec8
ID        CONNECTOR        ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ffb91ec8  acme-kafka-down  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 07:28  2026-10-19 07:29
✖ run failed: the kafka broker did not answer within the client's metadata timeout (10.255.255.1:9092, topic acme.partners) — check the broker is up and reachable from the hub

A broker that comes back is picked up by the next scheduled slot.

A host name the hub cannot resolve (brokers: no-such-host:9092) fails at once, and every slot repeats it until the manifest is fixed:

$ lm run get 38327a21
ID        CONNECTOR          ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
38327a21  acme-kafka-nohost  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 07:28  2026-10-19 07:28
✖ run failed: Failed to construct kafka consumer — No resolvable bootstrap urls given in bootstrap.servers

docs.title: The demo API
docs.text:
One Python file, no dependencies, 2 400 fictional ACME partners served under ten path dialects, a GraphQL endpoint and eight SOAP services — the source every screen of the REST, GraphQL and SOAP pages reads.

It ships with the repo. Start it in a terminal of its own and leave it running:

python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/acme-api.py

ACME Partners API on http://0.0.0.0:8099 — 2400 partners, dialects: down, drf, flaky, hdr, liar, link, offset, open, spring, v1 + POST /graphql + GET /openapi.json
SOAP services (POST /<service>/start.swe): fault, fault200, flaky, mute, sap, session, siebel, tail

It logs one line per request on stdout: the query string a pagination strategy composed, the watermark a run sent.

docs.title: The ten dialects
docs.text:
The first path segment picks the envelope; the data is the same under every dialect.

Path What it imitates Used by /spring/partners Spring Data Page — $.content + $.totalPages Quickstart /v1/partners Stripe-style opaque cursor — ?starting_after= One connector, one API /drf/partners Django REST — $.results + a whole next URL in $.next One connector, one API /link/partners an RFC 5988 Link: …; rel="next" header Pagination /offset/partners offset + limit with a published $.total Incremental sync /open/partners the same, with no auth wall at all try it with curl /hdr/partners 400 to any request without X-Api-Version Request headers /liar/partners serves 2 300 rows while declaring 2 400 The declared total /down/partners 500, forever When the source misbehaves /flaky/partners 429 then 503 before each page, then 200 When the source misbehaves POST /graphql Relay edges / pageInfo GraphQL GET /openapi.json an OpenAPI 3 document for /open, /spring and /v1 Generate a manifest from an OpenAPI spec

/openapi.json describes three paths; the server never reads it. Its servers entry is the address you called it on.

docs.title: The eight SOAP services
docs.text:
One POST path per service; the operation and the row offset are in the XML body. Same partners, in XML, with ns: prefixes on every payload element.

Path What it imitates Used by POST /siebel/start.swe Siebel QueryPage — LastPage, and a SOAPAction it checks Quickstart POST /sap/start.swe SAP PI — a MoreRecords flag instead Where the loop stops POST /mute/start.swe a service that announces nothing at all Where the loop stops POST /tail/start.swe 201 rows, so the last page holds one element Where the loop stops POST /fault/start.swe <soap:Fault> on HTTP 500 A Fault fails the run POST /fault200/start.swe the same Fault on HTTP 200 A Fault fails the run POST /flaky/start.swe two 500s without a Fault, then the page The same 500, retried POST /session/start.swe 401 unless a token rides in <soap:Header> A credential inside the envelope

/tail ends on a page holding a single element: a correct run ingests 201 rows, not 200.

docs.title: Its four credentials
docs.text:
Put them in the hub's secret registry; the manifests name them:

lm secret set ACME_BASIC_PW        # demo-pass   — /spring, /offset, /hdr, /liar, /down, /flaky and every SOAP service
lm secret set ACME_BEARER_TOKEN    # demo-token  — /v1 and /drf
lm secret set ACME_API_KEY         # demo-key    — /link and /graphql
lm secret set ACME_SESSION_TOKEN   # demo-session-42 — /session, inside the SOAP envelope

host.docker.internal, not localhost

The manifests point at http://host.docker.internal:8099. The hub runs in a container, and localhost inside it is that container — the address above is how it reaches your machine. The demo API listens on every interface for the same reason; pass it an address (acme-api.py 8099 127.0.0.1) to keep it to your own shell.

docs.title: Checking it before you blame the manifest
docs.text:
python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/selftest.py

It walks every dialect and SOAP service to its last page and checks that the 2 400 ids arrive exactly once, /flaky answers 429, 503, 200, /tail yields 201 rows and both fault services carry a <soap:Fault>. It exits non-zero when something is off.

Reset the flaky counters between retry tests

/flaky fails twice per query string, then serves that page for good: a second run retries nothing. curl http://127.0.0.1:8099/admin/reset puts it back.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• Not a GraphQL or SOAP engine. It answers fixed shapes; what is under test is the connector.
  • A throwaway rig. /open/ has no auth wall, and the credentials are fixed test values: run it on loopback or a developer machine only.

docs.title: The manifests that read it
docs.text:
Fourteen manifests live beside it, each transcluded into the page that explains it:

File Reads Page 10-quickstart.yaml /spring Quickstart 20-two-endpoints.yaml /v1 + /drf One connector, one API 30-link-header.yaml /link Pagination 40-watermark.yaml /offset Incremental sync 50-total-witness.yaml /liar + /hdr The declared total 60-source-down.yaml /down + /flaky When the source misbehaves 70-graphql-relay.yaml POST /graphql GraphQL 80-graphql-errors.yaml POST /graphql GraphQL 90-soap-querypage.yaml /siebel SOAP 91-soap-stop-signals.yaml /sap + /mute + /tail Where the loop stops 92-soap-fault.yaml /fault + /fault200 A Fault fails the run 93-soap-retry.yaml /flaky The same 500, retried 94-soap-session.yaml /session A credential inside the envelope 95-soap-watermark.yaml /siebel Incremental

docs.text:

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
How an endpoint asks for the next page. Most APIs follow a convention that already has a name: declare its preset. When none fits, write one of seven strategies.

This page serves REST and GraphQL: both are the same engine, and relay is what a GraphQL endpoint declares.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Declare the preset that matches the API's framework:

Preset For Same as spring-page Spring Data Page, serialized as is page ($.content, $.totalPages, 0-indexed) spring-paged-model Spring Data Page under VIA_DTO (PagedModel) page ($.content, $.page.totalPages, 0-indexed) spring-slice Spring Data Slice (no total) page + last_path: $.last spring-hateoas Spring Data REST body-link ($._links.next.href, $._embedded.{items} — needs items) micronaut Micronaut Data Page page ($.content, $.totalPages, 0-indexed) drf-page Django REST PageNumberPagination body-link ($.next, $.results) drf-limit-offset Django REST LimitOffsetPagination offset ($.count, $.results) fastapi fastapi-pagination page ($.items, $.pages, 1-indexed) nestjs nestjs-paginate body-link ($.links.next, $.data) json-api JSON:API body-link ($.links.next, $.data) sequelize Node/Sequelize offset ($.count, $.rows) stripe Stripe-style cursor cursor ($.has_more, $.data) 
pagination: { kind: spring-page }                       # 7 lines → 1
pagination: { kind: spring-page, size: 500 }            # override any expanded field
pagination: { kind: spring-hateoas, items: products }   # {items} → $._embedded.products

A Spring Page comes in two shapes. Look at one response:

{"content":[…],"totalPages":65,"totalElements":130,…}               → spring-page
{"content":[…],"page":{"size":50,"number":0,"totalPages":65,…}}     → spring-paged-model

The second is the shape Spring recommends since Spring Data 3.3 (@EnableSpringDataWebSupport(pageSerializationMode = VIA_DTO)). Read with spring-page, it still loads every row, but asks for one empty page after the last.

nestjs and json-api expand identically. Only spring-hateoas requires an override: items fills its $._embedded.{items} placeholder.

Spring Data REST puts no id in its items: key them on their self link's last segment, a key read from a link.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
When no preset fits, write the strategy out. Each one below shows what the API answers, then the block that reads it.

cursor — the next page starts after the last item:

{ "data": [ {"id": "cus_41"}, {"id": "cus_42"} ], "has_more": true }

pagination:
  kind: cursor
  cursor_param: starting_after      # sent as ?starting_after=cus_42
  cursor_path: $.data[-1:].id       # the id of the last item
  has_more_path: $.has_more
  response_path: $.data

An API whose cursor is the "more" signal — a token that is empty or absent on the last page, like the Kubernetes API's metadata.continue — needs no has_more_path:

{ "metadata": { "continue": "eyJ2IjoibWV0YS5rOHMuaW8vdjEi" }, "items": [ … ] }

path: /api/v1/pods?limit=500
pagination:
  kind: cursor
  cursor_param: continue            # sent as ?continue=eyJ2…
  cursor_path: $.metadata.continue  # empty on the last page: the read stops
  response_path: $.items
  • With has_more_path, the flag decides, and it must read a boolean: a string there is refused as pagination.has_more_path must read a boolean, not a string. A flag saying "more" on a page whose cursor is empty is refused too (… says more pages, but cursor_path reads no cursor): the rest of the source would otherwise go unread with the run reported complete.
  • Without it, the cursor decides: an empty or absent cursor ends the read, and so does an empty page, whatever cursor it carries. lm validate says which mode the endpoint is in.
  • A source that sends back the cursor it was just given, while saying there is more, fails the run: Endpoint 'events': the source sent back the cursor it was given while saying more pages — the cursor is not reaching it (check cursor_binding, and cursor_param or cursor_var). The usual cause is a cursor sent where the API does not read it: in the query when it expects a header, or under another variable name for a GraphQL relay (Cursor binding).
  • A path reads one value. A slice such as $.data[-1:].id is fine — empty on an empty page; a path that reads several values ($..endCursor across nested connections) is refused rather than one of them picked.
  • total_path and total_pages_path read a number, or its digits sent as text ("1234").

page — page numbers:

{ "content": [ … ], "number": 0, "totalPages": 5 }

pagination:
  kind: page
  page_param: page                  # ?page=0, ?page=1, …
  size_param: size
  size: 500
  start_page: 0                     # the default is 1
  total_pages_path: $.totalPages
  response_path: $.content

page stops at total_pages_path, has_more_path or last_path (whichever you declare), and on the first empty page.

offset — a row offset and a limit:

{ "data": [ … ], "total": 2400 }

pagination:
  kind: offset
  offset_param: offset              # ?offset=0&limit=500, then ?offset=500…
  limit_param: limit
  limit: 500
  response_path: $.data

body-link — the answer carries the next page's URL:

{ "results": [ … ], "next": "https://api.example.com/partners?page=2" }

pagination:
  kind: body-link
  link_path: $.next
  response_path: $.results

The link is a URL, or a link object carrying it as href — JSON:API allows both, and Drupal writes the object ("next": { "href": "…" }): link_path: $.links.next reads either. Anything else is refused, naming the JSON type it read: pagination.link_path must read a URL or a link object with href, not an object for an object without href, … not a number for a number.

none — the answer holds the whole list, and there is no next page. Older applications often answer this way, such as Spring PetClinic before Spring Boot:

{ "vetList": [ {"id": 1, "lastName": "Carter"}, {"id": 3, "lastName": "Douglas"} ] }

pagination:
  kind: none
  response_path: $.vetList

One request, every row it holds. If the source does page, none reads the first page only: check the count against the application, or declare total_path.

link-header — the next URL is in the Link header (GitHub style). Only response_path is needed: the example below.

relay — GraphQL Connections: GraphQL.

total_path is accepted by every strategy. It checks the run's row count against what the API declares: The declared total. When the API sends that count in a response header (X-Total-Count), name it with total_header instead.

Page size is a knob on page and offset only

cursor, body-link and link-header send no size parameter: the server's default page size governs the run.

To ask for a larger page, put it in path:, as 20-two-endpoints.yaml does with path: /drf/partners?page_size=500. relay takes its size from first: in the query.

docs.title: A full example: link-header
docs.text:
The next page is in the response's Link header, and the API wants a key:

# 30-link-header.yaml — the next page is in a HEADER, and the credential is an API key.
#
# RFC 5988: the response body says nothing about paging; `Link: <url>; rel="next"` does. The
# strategy follows that URL until the header stops carrying a `next` relation. `rel` defaults
# to next and is spelled out here for readability; `response_path` is what unwraps the rows.
#
# Where the key goes is declarative — `in: header` + `name:`. Use `in: query` and the key rides
# the query string instead, which is what APIs that pre-date bearer tokens tend to want.
#
#   lm secret set ACME_API_KEY        # the demo API answers to demo-key
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in ext.acme_header_partners.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-header
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY   # api_key takes no inline value: name a secret

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      path: /link/partners?limit=500
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: link-header
        rel: next
        response_path: "$.data"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_header_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-header
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
539d998f  acme-header  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

docs.title: Cursor binding
docs.text:
For cursor and relay, cursor_binding says where the cursor goes:

Binding Cursor goes into Needs query (default) a query parameter cursor_param header an HTTP header cursor_param (the header name) variable the POST body's variables.<name> cursor_var — relay on a graphql endpoint only

An API that wants the cursor in a header:

pagination:
  kind: cursor
  cursor_binding: header
  cursor_param: X-Next-Cursor       # the header's name
  cursor_path: $.next_cursor
  has_more_path: $.has_more
  response_path: $.items

variable anywhere else than a GraphQL relay is refused at lm apply.

A pure GraphQL API (POST a query, cursor in variables): see GraphQL.

docs.title: Every field
docs.text: Strategy Required fields Optional fields (default) cursor cursor_param, cursor_path, response_path has_more_path (none: a non-empty cursor means more), cursor_binding (query), total_path or total_header page page_param, response_path size_param, size (50), start_page (1), total_pages_path, total_path or total_header, has_more_path, last_path, empty_check (true) offset offset_param, limit_param, response_path limit (100), total_path or total_header link-header response_path rel (next), total_header or total_path body-link link_path, response_path total_path or total_header none response_path total_path or total_header relay cursor_path, has_more_path, response_path; plus cursor_param or cursor_var cursor_binding (query), total_path or total_header
