docs.title: Backup & Restore (self-host)
docs.text:
A hot pg_dump for PostgreSQL and a briefly-stopped copy for Keycloak. A restore drops and recreates the database. .env is not covered.

The self-host stack holds customer data in two stores:

Store Contents Backup method PostgreSQL (selfhost_pg volume) ALL hub data: ingested tables, RAG chunks, saved views, identities, audit hot pg_dump -Fc — no downtime Keycloak dev-file H2 (selfhost_kc volume) realm changes made at runtime: users created by hand, password hashes cold copy — Keycloak stops ~15 s

During the Keycloak stop, new logins fail; issued tokens keep working.

docs.title: Take a backup
docs.text:
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh              # keeps the newest 7
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh --keep 30
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh --no-keycloak

Each step prints a ==> line; the last ones are ==> done: backups/<UTC-stamp> and a reminder to back up .env. The snapshot lands at the repo root:

File Present when backups/<UTC-stamp>/lumnik.dump always backups/<UTC-stamp>/keycloak-data.tgz unless you passed --no-keycloak

Not covered — back these up separately, off-machine:

  • .env — it holds LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY; without it, secrets stored in the hub are unrecoverable. Copy it once; it changes only when you rotate keys.
  • Host-level config (reverse proxy, cron entries).

The dump grows with the unpurged mirror; --keep N is the only retention on backups themselves.

docs.title: Cron example
docs.text:
# nightly at 03:10, keep 14 days
10 3 * * *  cd /opt/lumnik && deploy/selfhost/backup.sh --keep 14 >> /var/log/lumnik-backup.log 2>&1

Ship backups/ to another machine (rsync, restic, object storage): a backup on the database's own disk is only half a backup.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
Same machine (roll back data):

deploy/selfhost/restore.sh backups/<UTC-stamp>

The script asks first and waits for Enter:

!! This OVERWRITES the hub database (and Keycloak store, if present in the snapshot)
   with backups/<UTC-stamp>. Press Enter to continue, Ctrl-C to abort.
  • The hub is stopped for the whole restore, and Keycloak while its store is swapped.
  • The lumnik database is dropped and recreated, then the dump is restored into it: anything created after the snapshot is gone.
  • It ends with ==> done. and the hub started again.

Fresh machine (disaster recovery):

  1. Install Docker, clone the repo, put your saved .env at the repo root.
  2. deploy/selfhost/up.sh — creates the roles and an empty database.
  3. deploy/selfhost/restore.sh backups/<UTC-stamp>.

Check it worked:

lm migration status     # every schema at the snapshot's version, PENDING 0
lm run list             # your last runs, as they were at the snapshot

Restore onto the same public address: another one turns every user into a new account (why, and the fix).

docs.title: What this does NOT give you
docs.text:
• Point-in-time recovery: it is a nightly snapshot, not WAL archiving.
  • Kubernetes (cloud edition): use your cluster's volume snapshots; only the pg_dump part carries over. The chart's bundled Keycloak keeps nothing between restarts (Tenants, users & scopes): there is no Keycloak store to back up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix backup.sh exits: !! --keep must be a positive integer >= 1 (got: 0) --keep 0 or a non-numeric value Pass a positive integer. backup.sh exits: !! pg_dump produced an empty file the dump captured nothing (database unreachable, stack down) Check the stack (docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps) and retry. Logins fail for ~15 seconds, then work again, at a fixed hour a backup.sh run (cron or manual) stopped Keycloak to copy its store Expected; issued tokens keep working. Move the cron to a low-traffic window if needed. restore.sh appears to hang it waits for Enter (Press Enter to continue, Ctrl-C to abort) Press Enter to proceed. After a restore, Keycloak serves reads but every login fails with H2 error 90097 "The database is read only" the store was restored by hand (e.g. docker cp), not by restore.sh Restore again with restore.sh. Users who logged in before a restore show up as brand-new accounts the public origin/issuer changed between backup and restore Keep the same public address.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: Health probes and Prometheus metrics, live on every boot; OpenTelemetry tracing, off until you point it at a collector. No dashboards, alert rules or RAG/chat metrics ship with them.

docs.title: What's exposed out of the box
docs.text:
Endpoint What it answers Auth GET /q/health overall UP/DOWN, all checks (the database connections) none GET /q/health/live "the process is alive" — watched by the selfhost compose healthcheck none GET /q/health/ready "I can serve traffic" — the Helm chart's startup and readiness probe none GET /q/metrics Prometheus text format: JVM, HTTP server, and the domain metrics below none lm module list each installed module, its version and whether it is active lm_integrator 
$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled

The /q/* endpoints sit on the application port (8080):

  • They carry no authentication, and /q/metrics names your connectors in its labels.
  • The TLS proxy forwards them: it sends everything except /realms/* and /resources/* to the hub. On a public origin, block /q/* at your proxy or firewall.

GET /api/platform/health returns the same module data plus the Search provider's state, for a monitoring probe. It needs an lm_integrator token — except on a Helm install set to dev-bypass, where every endpoint answers without one (Security).

docs.title: Scraping with Prometheus
docs.text:
Point a scrape job at /q/metrics:

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: lumnik-hub
    metrics_path: /q/metrics
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["your-hub-host:8080"]

No push gateway, no agent.

docs.title: Domain metrics
docs.text:
Besides the JVM and HTTP meters, the hub emits:

Metric Tags When it moves lumnik_runs_total status (Completed, Partial, Failed, Cancelled) a connector run reaches a terminal status lumnik_rate_limited_total bucket a request is refused 429 by rate limiting; the tenant is in the WARN log line lumnik_dead_letters_total reason a row is quarantined to the DLQ — real losses only; benign skips (duplicates, policy-excluded) do not count csv_filesource_list_total transport, connector files listed on a remote source csv_filesource_list_duration_seconds transport, connector time spent listing csv_filesource_open_total transport, connector, result (ok/error) a file open attempt csv_filesource_bytes_read_total transport, connector bytes downloaded from a remote file csv_filesource_after_process_total transport, action, result a post-ingest file action (move/delete/…) lumnik_search_projection_lag_seconds — age of the oldest change not yet in a search index lumnik_search_projection_lagging_indexes — how many search indexes have a pending change lumnik_search_rebuild_total outcome a search index rebuild ends lumnik_search_rebuild_duration_seconds outcome how long that rebuild took lumnik_search_catchup_failures_total — a search index catch-up attempt failed 
$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/metrics | grep '^lumnik_'
lumnik_runs_total{status="Failed"} 1.0
lumnik_runs_total{status="Completed"} 5.0
lumnik_dead_letters_total{reason="MalformedSource"} 2.0
  • A meter appears once its event has happened on this process: absence means "not yet", not "broken". The lumnik_search_* meters appear only on a hub built with a Search provider.
  • The run record (lm run get) is the reference. A counter may count a run twice.
  • csv_filesource_* moves only for lm csv ingest. Scheduled CSV connector runs do not emit it: watch lumnik_runs_total and the DLQ for them.

docs.title: What to alert on
docs.text:
• Partial runs, more than Failed. A failed run is loud. A partial one wrote what it read, but did not read everything. lm run get <id> says why, on its • run partial: line.
  • Per-connector history is in the run ledger, not in Prometheus:
$ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
9c64afbf  orders     default   Completed  9   9    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
8778809f  orders     default   Completed  10  10   0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
6e52921c  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38

docs.title: Scheduled background work
docs.text:
Each hub runs these jobs. A job still busy at its next turn skips that turn.

Job Cadence What it does Connector scheduler every 1 min starts each connector whose spec.schedule is due; marks runs left Running by a dead process as Failed Export scheduler every 1 min starts each export whose schedule is due Connector run queue every 5 s² starts queued manual connector runs (run queue) Export run queue every 5 s² starts queued on-demand export runs Workflow dormancy sweep every 15 min¹ flags documents sitting unmoved past their dormancy threshold Workflow due-date sweep every 15 min¹ flags documents whose due date has passed in a due state Webhook delivery every 5 s delivers new events to the tenant's integrations (lm integration) Webhook retry every 30 s re-attempts failed deliveries with backoff — the failure journal (lm outputs) Email delivery every 5 s mails events matching notification rules (lm notify); a failed send is logged and skipped; mocked until the SMTP settings are set Search projection every 1 min brings search indexes up to date (Search provider builds only) Event retention purge daily 04:30 trims the event outbox — never past what the slowest consumer has seen Audit retention purge daily 04:45 trims the audit trail past its window (default 365 d; 0 disables) Webhook journal purge daily 05:00 trims the webhook delivery journal (default 90 d)

The retention windows are in sizing.

¹ lumnik.workflow.sweep.every (env LUMNIK_WORKFLOW_SWEEP_EVERY). A shorter interval notices an overdue document sooner; the threshold itself is spec.dormancy.after, per workflow.

² LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL, passed through by both the selfhost compose file and the Helm chart (runQueue.pollInterval).

To change it: self-host, set it in the root .env and recreate the hub; Helm (cloud edition), pass it through hub.extraEnv. Both gestures are in rate limits.

docs.title: Traces to a collector
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry is off in the shipped stacks:

  • The dev profile disables it.
  • The selfhost compose file defaults QUARKUS_OTEL_SDK_DISABLED to true (no collector ships).
  • The Helm chart (cloud edition) sets QUARKUS_OTEL_SDK_DISABLED: "true" in the hub ConfigMap, for the same reason. Check what your release renders:

$ helm template lumnik deploy/helm/lumnik -f my-values.yaml -s templates/hub-configmap.yaml | grep OTEL
  QUARKUS_OTEL_SDK_DISABLED: "true"
- Only traces are exported — no OTel metrics or logs.

To send traces, run a collector (OTLP/gRPC) and set on the hub container:

QUARKUS_OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=false
OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT=http://your-collector:4317   # default: http://localhost:4317

Self-host: set both in the root .env and recreate the hub. Helm (cloud edition): pass both through hub.extraEnv — an entry there wins over the ConfigMap's default. Both gestures are in rate limits.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: Every console line carries the tenant id (blank outside a tenant's request). The prod profile writes JSON lines, ready for your log shipper. Recipes: logs.

docs.title: What does not exist
docs.text:
• No dashboards or alert rules — bring your own Grafana.
  • No per-connector tag on lumnik_runs_total — use lm run list --connector.
  • No row-count or duration metric per run — those are on the run record (lm run get).
  • No RAG/chat metrics — token usage, ask-to-SQL verdicts and abstentions are not metered.
  • No OTel metrics or logs export — traces only.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix lumnik_runs_total / lumnik_dead_letters_total absent from /q/metrics on a fresh boot nothing has happened yet on this process Trigger a run, or read the run record (lm run get). A scheduled CSV connector shows nothing under csv_filesource_* those meters move only for lm csv ingest Watch lumnik_runs_total and the DLQ instead. No traces reach the collector OTel is disabled in the shipped stacks See Traces to a collector. GET /api/platform/health returns 401/403 it needs an lm_integrator token Use an lm_integrator account (then lm module list), or /q/health for up/down only. Set LUMNIK_WORKFLOW_SWEEP_EVERY in .env, cadence unchanged the hub reads it at startup only Recreate the hub; see Scheduled background work.

docs.title: On-call runbook — 2 a.m., by symptom
docs.text:
What is safe to restart, what each restart costs, and the exact commands.

Scope. The self-host compose stack. SSH to the host and run every command from the repo root (where docker-compose.selfhost.yml and .env live). On Kubernetes the costs below still hold; the gestures are your cluster's (kubectl rollout restart …).

At 2 a.m., restart — never a bare docker compose up

docker compose up -d on the base file alone recreates hub and keycloak without the overlays. On a TLS-proxy install, the hub then refuses tokens from the https origin. restart <svc> touches one container and keeps its settings. up.sh keeps the overlays, but it pulls the hub image: unless LUMNIK_VERSION pins a release, that is an upgrade. Leave it for the morning.

docs.title: Step 0 — health before logs
docs.text:
lm has no health command; ask the hub directly:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/health
{
    "status": "UP",
    "checks": [
        {
            "name": "Database connections health check",
            "status": "UP",
            "data": {
                "readonly": "UP",
                "<default>": "UP",
                "admin": "UP"
            }
        }
    ]
}
What you see What it means "status": "DOWN" a database connection is down; data names which one no answer at all during a boot the hub is still starting — migrations run first (Migrating schema … lines in the hub log) UP, but chat or ask fails /q/health checks only the database: a down Ollama or Keycloak still shows UP

Then: which log to read, by symptom.

docs.title: "The chat is down" — the short path
docs.text:
1. /q/health (above) — rules out the database.
  2. ./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub — the log recipes have the jq one-liners.
  3. The ask and the model: the symptom table, with the fix for each.

docs.title: The nightly login mystery, pre-solved
docs.text: Logins fail for ~15 seconds at a fixed night hour: your backup cron is stopping Keycloak to copy its store (the example schedules it at 03:10). Issued tokens keep working. Check your crontab's hour before opening an incident.

docs.title: The restart matrix — cost and command
docs.text:
Container Safe? Command (repo root) What it costs hub yes docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml restart hub see below keycloak yes, briefly docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml restart keycloak New logins fail during the window; issued tokens keep working. The store survives on its volume. postgres be gentle docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml restart postgres A full outage while it lasts. Expect a failed request or two right after. Interrupted runs resume on their cursor. Ollama (host) yes Linux: systemctl restart ollama · macOS/Windows: the Ollama app The first ask after the restart is a cold load (tens of seconds). OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 keeps the model resident (the trap list). caddy (proxy) yes docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml restart caddy A blip on the https origin. Certificates and the internal CA survive on the tls_caddy_data volume (docker volume ls shows <project>_tls_caddy_data).

What a hub restart costs:

  • Rate-limit counters reset (rate limits) — harmless.
  • A jdbc or CSV run in flight stops and resumes on its cursor at the next trigger (how jdbc cursors resume).
  • A REST run in flight restarts its pagination from page one.
  • The boot window: the compose healthcheck allows up to ~210 s before unhealthy; a restart on an already-migrated database is much faster.

docs.title: After a hard kill: the run marks itself failed
docs.text:
• What you see: a run killed mid-flight stays Running, and its connector's schedule waits.
  • How long: at most a minute after the hub is back: it marks the run Failed.
  • What to do: nothing. The connector resumes on its cursor at its next scheduled run, or now with lm connector run <name>.

lm run get prints the reason:

$ lm run get ff03ad75
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN   OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ff03ad75  acme-desk-erp  default   Failed  500  500  0        0             2026-10-19 01:48  2026-10-19 01:52
✖ run failed: reaped: the hub process running it restarted or died while it was in flight

A reaped run's ENDED is when the hub noticed, not when the run died: its duration includes the outage.

docs.title: What waits for morning
docs.text:
• Anything touching the database's disk — nothing purges the mirror (storage).
  • Credential rotation.
  • Any lm connector delete — it purges the connector's data.
  • Any up-shaped gesture — see the red box above.

docs.title: Inbound rate limits
docs.text: Five endpoints are throttled, per tenant, in a fixed 60-second window. Everything else is unlimited. The counters live in the hub process.

docs.title: What is limited
docs.text:
Bucket Endpoint Used by Default rpm Edition view-generate POST /api/views/generate lm view generate 10 all search GET /api/search lm search query, the PWA Search tab 60 all platform-chat POST /api/platform/rag/chat lm chat, lm ask 60 Pro user-chat POST /api/rag/chat the PWA chat 60 Pro platform-search POST /api/platform/rag/search lm rag search 60 Pro
  • A bucket without its own setting uses lumnik.ratelimit.default.rpm (60).
  • On the open edition the three Pro endpoints do not exist, and neither do their limits.
  • Counting is per (bucket, tenant): one tenant cannot exhaust another's budget, and buckets are independent. Requests with no resolved tenant share one system budget.

docs.title: The 429 contract
docs.text:
When a window is exhausted the request is refused before it runs:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: <seconds until the window resets>

{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}

Waiting Retry-After seconds always lands in a fresh window. lm prints:

Error: rate limited (429): rate limit exceeded, retry in 17s

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Property form (per bucket, falling back to default):

lumnik.ratelimit.default.rpm=60
lumnik.ratelimit.view-generate.rpm=10

Environment form (non-alphanumerics become underscores):

LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_DEFAULT_RPM=120
LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_VIEW_GENERATE_RPM=20
LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_USER_CHAT_RPM=0    # 0 disables that bucket

0 disables a bucket: no counting, no 429. A misspelt bucket name is ignored.

Self-host. Set the variables in the root .env, then recreate the hub alone — it reads them at startup:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d hub
  • Name every overlay the stack runs with (-f docker-compose.tls.yml…). The hub lists them: docker inspect $(docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps -q hub) --format '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.config_files"}}'. With the TLS proxy, LUMNIK_TLS_HOST must be set too, as when you started it.
  • up.sh keeps the overlays by itself, but pulls the hub image: pin LUMNIK_VERSION in .env first, or the change becomes an upgrade.

Before that, check what the hub container will receive. With LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_USER_CHAT_RPM=0 in .env:

$ docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml config hub | grep RATELIMIT
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_DEFAULT_RPM: "60"
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_PLATFORM_CHAT_RPM: ""
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_PLATFORM_SEARCH_RPM: ""
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_SEARCH_RPM: ""
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_USER_CHAT_RPM: "0"
      LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_VIEW_GENERATE_RPM: "10"

An empty value is the same as unset: that bucket uses default.

Helm (cloud edition). The chart has no value per bucket; pass them through hub.extraEnv, then restart the hub. On the kind cluster up.sh built:

helm --kube-context kind-lumnik upgrade lumnik deploy/helm/lumnik --reuse-values \
  --set 'hub.extraEnv[0].name=LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_DEFAULT_RPM' --set-string 'hub.extraEnv[0].value=120'
kubectl --context kind-lumnik rollout restart deployment/lumnik-hub

--set on a list replaces the whole list: name every hub.extraEnv entry you want to keep.

docs.title: Observing 429s
docs.text:
Every refusal shows twice on the hub side:

  • A WARN log line: rate limit exceeded: bucket=user-chat tenant=42 rpm=60 retryAfter=17s
  • A counter: lumnik_rate_limited_total{bucket="…"} in /q/metrics (domain metrics). No alert ships; wire one on its rate.

A spike on one bucket from one tenant (the WARN lines name it) tells an attack from a busy Monday. Both reset when the hub restarts.

docs.title: Single-node caveat
docs.text:
• Counters are per hub process, in memory. Both shipped deploy paths run one hub replica, so the limits are exact there.
  • N replicas behind a balancer count independently: the effective limit is up to N × the configured rpm.
  • A hub restart resets every window.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Set LUMNIK_RATELIMIT_* in .env, the limit did not move the hub reads it at startup only, or the bucket name is misspelt (an unknown bucket is ignored) Recreate the hub (up -d hub) and check the name against the bucket list (see Tuning). The chat or RAG search endpoints never return 429 open edition: they do not exist Expected; view-generate and search are limited there. A request seems to share its budget with unrelated callers requests with no resolved tenant share the system budget Check why the tenant did not resolve. 429 Too Many Requests in a connector run, not from an API client the source system throttling lumnik's outbound calls Lower default_rate_limit in the connector YAML (REST).

docs.title: The short answer
docs.text:
Measured on Load Result a VPS, 4 vCPU / 16 GB / NVMe, self-host + TLS proxy 50 concurrent users on the read surface p95 ≈ 11 ms, 0 errors, ~112 requests/s a laptop (Docker VM, 10 CPU / 7.6 GB), PostgreSQL Search provider search alone, 50 000 rows per index p95 87–140 ms
  • Not measured: ask, chat and RAG search. The model is the cost there: size its machine on its own.
  • Not measured: ingestion. It is a batch; its cost shows in each run.
  • Disk is your own question: see Storage.

docs.title: Storage — the sizing question this page does NOT answer
docs.text:
The load tests below measure throughput and latency, not disk. What grows, and what is purged:

Data Purged? When Window Setting Ingested tables (connector.t_*), RAG corpus (rag.chunk), run history never (no retention policy) when the connector is deleted, or by hand — — Event outbox yes, never past the slowest consumer daily 04:30 30 days LUMNIK_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS Audit trail yes daily 04:45 365 days (0 disables) LUMNIK_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS Webhook delivery journal (payloads and receiver responses) yes daily 05:00 90 days LUMNIK_WEBHOOKS_DELIVERY_RETENTION_DAYS

No disk metric ships (observability): supervise the PostgreSQL disk yourself. Check the database size from the repo root:

$ docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec postgres psql -U lumnik -d lumnik \
    -c "SELECT pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size('lumnik'))"
 pg_size_pretty
----------------
 11 MB
(1 row)
  • No growth multiplier is measured. The mirror is roughly your declared source tables plus system columns; rag.chunk adds the text and a 768-float vector per chunk.
  • Backups grow with the mirror; backup.sh --keep N bounds how many dumps you keep.

docs.title: Load tests — sizing the hub with k6
docs.text: Measure what a lumnik deployment can serve, find the knee of the curve, and turn it into an infrastructure sizing decision. Scenarios are k6 scripts; nothing to install — the runner uses the grafana/k6 Docker image.

docs.title: Quickstart (against a running self-host stack)
docs.text:
./loadtest/run.sh smoke.js                 # prove the harness: auth + routes, ~10 s
MAX_VUS=25 ./loadtest/run.sh read-mix.js   # the sizing ramp, ~2.5 min

run.sh mints the Bearer token as user integrator, with the password from the repo-root .env. For another stack, set K6_USER / K6_PASSWORD / KC_URL / BASE_URL.

docs.title: What is measured — and what is not
docs.text:
Measured: the hub's read surface, weighted like integrator usage — /api/platform/version, /api/platform/connectors, /api/platform/runs, /api/views, /api/workflows, /api/inbox, /api/entities/conflicts. Every one answers 200 even on an empty stack, and every request is authenticated and tenant-scoped.

Not measured:

  • ask / chat / RAG search — the model dominates their cost. Size the model on its own hardware.
  • Ingestion — a scheduled batch, not concurrent users; its cost is in the run reports.

docs.title: The sizing method
docs.text:
1. Run smoke.js first, twice (the first run warms the JVM). A failing smoke means the harness is wrong, not the hub.
  2. Ramp read-mix.js at increasing MAX_VUS (25 → 50 → 100 …) until p95 bends sharply upward or http_req_failed leaves zero. The last clean step is this deployment's capacity.
  3. Watch docker stats on the hub and PostgreSQL during the ramp. The knee is usually the database: pool saturation shows as latency, not errors.
  4. Record one line per run in the sizing table:
date hardware (CPU/RAM) stack MAX_VUS p95 worst endpoint failed verdict 2026-08-17 M1 Max / 64 GB selfhost compose (image 2026-07-12, ONLY 5 surfaces¹) 25 runs: 210 ms 0.00% clean 2026-08-17 M1 Max / 64 GB selfhost compose, full 7-surface mix 25 connectors: 50 ms 0.00% clean — ~51 rps 2026-08-17 M1 Max / 64 GB selfhost compose, full 7-surface mix 50 runs: 50 ms 0.00% clean — ~101 rps, p95 flat vs 25 VUs 2026-08-18 VPS, 4 vCPU / 16 GB / NVMe selfhost + TLS façade, via https² 25 runs: 10.6 ms 0.00% clean — ~56 rps 2026-08-18 VPS, 4 vCPU / 16 GB / NVMe selfhost + TLS façade, via https² 50 connectors: 10.9 ms 0.00% clean — ~112 rps, p95 flat vs 25 VUs

¹ that image did not have the workflows surface, hence ONLY.

² through the full public path (Caddy, TLS, the façade issuer), k6 running on the VM itself: client network excluded, TLS included.

docs.title: Search (PostgreSQL provider)
docs.text:
With the PostgreSQL Search provider, the index shares the database with ingestion. This scenario measures query latency per matching mode, ingestion speed, index catch-up time, and what each does to the other. It runs on its own throwaway stack (ports 18080/18180, own volumes, a hub built with -Psearch):

bash loadtest/search/stack.sh up                              # builds the hub with the provider the first time (slow); REBUILD=1 forces a rebuild
MIN_FREE_MB=8000 bash loadtest/search-sizing.sh --tiers 10000 # writes loadtest/search/results/<stamp>/summary.md
bash loadtest/search/stack.sh down                            # removes the stack and its volumes

The script refuses a tier when the Docker VM has less than MIN_FREE_MB free (default 15000); the image needs about 0.6 GB plus the database.

What a tier does. Four entities (sz_exact, sz_text, sz_fuzzy, sz_prefix) carry the same generated rows and differ only in their matching mode. N is rows per entity. Three phases run from the same starting point:

phase what runs what it answers A the query mix at 20 requests/s for 60 s latency with nothing else running B ingestion of N/10 more rows per entity, no search load ingestion speed and catch-up on their own C the same ingestion while the query mix keeps its rate, until the index has caught up what sharing the database costs both sides
  • B and C each start from the same saved copy of the database, so the comparison is contention, not extra volume.
  • The corpus comes from a fixed seed: 70 % canonical values, 15 % one-letter typos, 10 % abbreviations, 5 % phonetic variants.
  • Caught up means: for all four indexes, lag 0, document count equal to the rows ingested, and that count fresh. Lag 0 alone proves nothing — it reads 0 before projection starts.
  • Catch-up pace is set by LUMNIK_SEARCH_PROJECTION_CATCHUP_BUDGET (default 30 s per minute; see How fast an index catches up).

docs.title: Observed on one machine — an envelope, not a capacity
docs.text:
MacBook Pro M1 Max, 64 GB; Docker Desktop VM with 10 CPUs and 7.6 GB; hub and PostgreSQL in containers next to Keycloak; 2026-10-01. Rate 20 requests/s, catch-up budget 30 s. Each cell is run 1 / run 2, each on a fresh stack.

N = 10 000 rows per entity (40 000 in total, plus one seed row each):

phase exact p95 ms text p95 ms fuzzy p95 ms prefix p95 ms ingestion, rows/s (4 entities) catch-up s max lag during the load, s max lag to convergence, s A — search alone 61 / 71 34 / 39 60 / 77 35 / 39 — — — — B — ingestion alone — — — — 5 063 / 4 938 40 / 38 0 / 0 38 / 32 C — search during ingestion 70 / 72 46 / 41 70 / 79 44 / 39 3 540 / 4 444 52 / 47 0 / 0 47 / 41

N = 50 000 rows per entity (200 000 in total, plus one seed row each):

phase exact p95 ms text p95 ms fuzzy p95 ms prefix p95 ms ingestion, rows/s (4 entities) catch-up s max lag during the load, s max lag to convergence, s A — search alone 121 / 108 94 / 87 118 / 108 140 / 114 — — — — B — ingestion alone — — — — 13 699 / 18 018 54 / 66 0 / 0 38 / 43 C — search during ingestion 3 653 / 349 2 222 / 195 4 213 / 381 2 031 / 195 3 311 / 6 623 42 / 57 0 / 1 44 / 58 Finding Figures Search alone holds a 500 ms budget p95 87–140 ms at 50 000 rows (p99 ≤ 188 ms); runs agree within 25 % Search during ingestion at 50 000 rows is not settled run 2: 195–381 ms; run 1: 2.0–4.2 s (p50 ~100 ms in both) — no figure is claimed Contention at 10 000 rows is small p95 ≤ 79 ms; ingestion 10–30 % slower than alone Catch-up 1 000-row delta: 38–52 s; 5 000-row delta: 42–66 s, with or without search load Disk after phase B / C 10 000 rows: 79–81 / 51–52 MB; 50 000 rows: 271–273 / 195–199 MB (from 12 MB)
  • Ingestion lasts 0.8–6.0 s, timed from the hub's run reports: its rows/s is the least precise figure.
  • Lag during the load is 0 by construction (ingestion ends before projection drains); the figure that moves is the lag to convergence.
  • Not measured: 200 000 or 1 million rows per entity, the cluster provider, other hardware.

docs.title: Deciding for your own installation
docs.text: Replay this scenario on your hardware at the volume and rate you expect, then apply Choosing a provider. Rows per tenant is not a trigger: decide on the contention you observe and on your latency and freshness budgets.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• Localhost numbers size only localhost. Size on the target hardware, over the users' network.
  • Tokens from the bundled realm live 1 hour (accessTokenLifespan: 3600): enough for every scenario here except a long Search tier. The Search orchestrator renews its own token every 25 minutes (SZ_TOKEN_REFRESH_S lowers it); phase C's k6 load does not, so a catch-up over an hour ends in 401s and the phase is reported failed. No token-refresh loop ships for other soak tests.
  • Thresholds (P95_MS, default 500 ms) are regression gates, not SLOs; tune them per environment.
  • ONLY=name,name narrows the mix explicitly; the default is always the full mix, so a missing endpoint goes red.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
file role run.sh token minting + dockerised k6 invocation k6/lib.js endpoints, weights, auth params k6/smoke.js 1-VU harness check, CI-able k6/read-mix.js the ramping sizing scenario k6/search-mix.js the Search query mix at a constant arrival rate, per mode search-sizing.sh the Search sizing orchestrator (phases A, B and C per tier) search/stack.sh the throwaway -Psearch stack (up, down, token, psql, pgdump/pgrestore) search/snapshot.sh save and restore the stack's database, with a counts proof search/gen_corpus.py the deterministic corpus and query generator

The scenarios live in loadtest/; deploy first (self-host), then size.

docs.title: Upgrading the hub
docs.text: Migrations run forward-only at boot. The pre-upgrade backup is the only rollback.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. Take a backup — backup-restore.md. The backup is the rollback.

  2. Note the current schema versions:

    $ lm migration status
SCHEMA     VERSION  PENDING  LAST APPLIED
core       83       0        2026-10-25 07:04
identity   18       0        2026-10-24 21:55
rag        6        0        2026-10-24 21:55
search_pg  3        0        2026-10-25 00:13

    search_pg appears only on a hub built with Search.

  3. Point at the new image and restart:

    • selfhost: set LUMNIK_VERSION in .env (or leave it unset to track main), then deploy/selfhost/up.sh. It keeps the overlays the stack was started with (TLS proxy, Search). A stack with Search is rebuilt from source, not pulled: git pull first, as in Running from source.

    • Helm (cloud edition): bump hub.image.tag, then helm upgrade.

    • The hub migrates its database at boot, then reports healthy:
    Path Boot budget On timeout selfhost compose ~210 s (90 s grace + 12 × 10 s) the container shows unhealthy; it is not restarted Helm (cloud edition) ~150 s (startup probe) Kubernetes restarts the pod

    Follow the boot with ./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub. 5. Run lm migration status again: a higher VERSION and PENDING 0 on every schema means the migrations are done. 6. Apply each resolution: entity again with the same manifest, then run lm entity resolve NAME.

docs.title: Turning on the run queue
docs.text:
LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED=true (Helm: runQueue.enabled) makes manual connector runs and on-demand export runs wait in status Queued (connectors, exports).

Setting Default Effect LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED false queue manual and on-demand runs LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_MAX_AGE 1h a run still queued after this ends: Cancelled (connector), Failed (export) LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_POLL_INTERVAL 5s how often a waiting run is picked up LUMNIK_CONNECTOR_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS 4 how many endpoint runs one hub drives at once. Each takes up to two connections of the admin pool: raise quarkus.datasource."admin".jdbc.max-size with it

The setting is global to the deployment: upgrade every hub replica to the same release first, then turn it on. Turning it off again:

  • runs already queued still start, or end once they pass LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_MAX_AGE;
  • new manual and on-demand runs start at once, except where a run is still queued: there a new connector run is born Cancelled and a new export run answers 409, until the queued one drains;
  • nothing is left stuck.

docs.title: Release notes that need a gesture
docs.text: Some releases change what existing data means. Each section below says what you see after upgrading and what to do.

docs.title: A REST header reference must resolve
docs.text:
A REST connector header declared with value_env now reads like the auth fields: the lm secret entry first, then the hub's environment (REST § request headers).

  • A name that resolves nowhere fails the run, lm source rest test and lm source rest probe: Header X-Client-Id unavailable (env=CLIENT_ID). Before, the header was dropped and the request went out without it. Store the value (lm secret set CLIENT_ID), or remove the header from the manifest if the source does not need it.
  • An lm secret entry now outranks an environment variable of the same name for a header. If both exist with different values, the secret's value is sent: remove the one you do not want.

docs.title: Subscriptions are tenant-wide
docs.text:
Webhooks and email rules are refused to an admin bound to any scope:* role — see Outputs. Ones a bound admin created earlier keep firing. A tenant-wide admin lists them and removes what nobody owns:

$ lm notify list
ID    EVENTS            RECIPIENT        TEMPLATE            ENABLED
1000  decision.*        adv@example.com  decision-alert      true
1001  data.row.changed  ops@example.com  event-notification  true
$ lm integration list
ID    NAME            URL                        EVENTS                      ENABLED
1000  ops-automation  https://hooks.example.com  decision.*,connector.run.*  true
$ lm notify rm 1001
removed: 1001
$ lm notify list
ID    EVENTS      RECIPIENT        TEMPLATE        ENABLED
1000  decision.*  adv@example.com  decision-alert  true

A webhook goes the same way: lm integration rm <ID>.

docs.title: One local csv file is the table's state
docs.text:
A csv-file connector whose local path names one file (no * or ?) removes the rows the file no longer holds — see CSV § full refresh. Before the upgrade, the table kept every older version of a changed row. The first run that reads the file after upgrading (a file is read again only once it changes) counts those older versions as removed. Later runs count only the rows the file lost. On that first run:

  • up to 30 % of the table: they are removed;
  • beyond 30 %: the run fails, removes nothing and names the counts;
  • to keep them, point the connector at a folder (*.csv); to let them go, set refresh.max_removed: off for that run, then remove the line.

docs.title: A jdbc table holds one row per key
docs.text:
A jdbc-generic table holds one row per pk_columns value (JDBC § one row per key). The first run after upgrading keeps the newest row per key and removes the older versions, even when it reads nothing new:

$ lm connector run demo-invoices
run scheduled: 13629016-e970-4a1a-92b7-aed86627f3f8
$ lm run get 13629016
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
13629016  demo-invoices  invoices  Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-18 13:49  2026-10-18 13:49
• 2 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them

If one earlier run read the same key twice with two different values, the run fails naming pk_columns and removes nothing. Declare the source table's whole primary key, apply, run again.

docs.title: Running from source
docs.text:
git pull
make -C lm install                 # installs lm into ~/.local/bin (keep it on your PATH)
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build    # rebuilds and restarts the hub

Your data is kept; migrations run at the hub's next boot. On a TLS-proxy install, run its command again afterwards.

docs.title: Roll back
docs.text:
There is no down-migration. Rolling back is restoring the backup taken in step 1; writes made since are lost.

  1. Set LUMNIK_VERSION in .env back to the previous release.
  2. deploy/selfhost/up.sh: the hub comes back on the previous image.
  3. deploy/selfhost/restore.sh backups/<UTC-stamp>: the database as it was before the upgrade.

docs.title: If the boot fails mid-migration
docs.text:
The migration stops at the failing version; later migrations do not touch your data, and the hub does not become healthy.

  1. Save the log: docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs hub > hub-upgrade.log.
  2. Need service back now? Roll back.
  3. Report the failing version: the last Migrating schema … to version … line in the log.

docs.title: Changing the public address
docs.text: Do not change the hub's public address during an upgrade: every user would log in as a new one. Keep the same public address.

docs.title: Quickstart — the customer's data in minutes
docs.text:
Quickstart

Install lm, log in, load one export, show the rows, ask a question.

Before this page

The hub runs.

You need

One CSV export from the customer.

You get

Rows you can show, and a first answer in French or English (Pro).

Other sources

An API, an SFTP server, an S3 bucket: Other first sources.

docs.title: 1. Install lm
docs.text:
Take the archive for your platform from the Releases page. There are five: macOS (Intel, Apple Silicon), Linux (x86-64, arm64), Windows x86-64.

shasum -a 256 -c lm_<version>_checksums.txt --ignore-missing   # check the download first
tar -xzf lm_<version>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz                      # your platform's archive
install -d ~/.local/bin && install -m 0755 lm ~/.local/bin/lm
  • Windows: the archive is a .zip with lm.exe. Unpack it into a folder on your PATH.
  • From source (Go 1.26+): cd lm && make install.
  • The shell cannot find lm? Add ~/.local/bin to your PATH.

Check it:

$ lm version
lm version dev (commit 94ae18cc9667, built from 2026-10-19T05:34:15Z)

A downloaded binary prints its release number instead of dev. Put this line in a bug report.

docs.title: 2. Log in
docs.text:
lm config set-context selfhost --server http://localhost:8080 \
    --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context selfhost
lm login

lm login prints a link and a code, then waits. Open the link in a browser. Sign in as integrator: the password is INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env. The terminal then finishes:

$ lm login
To sign in, open:
  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik/device?user_code=EYQP-LLJN
and enter code: EYQP-LLJN

Waiting...
Logged in to lumnik Open Edition.

A Pro hub prints Logged in. Check the round trip. On a fresh hub, the table is empty:

$ lm connector list
NAME  TYPE  TENANT  SCHED  WINDOW  STATUS  LAST RUN

docs.title: 3. Load the export
docs.text:
The customer hands you stock.csv:

sku,label,qty,warehouse
PMP-100,Pompe doseuse,12,Lyon
VAN-200,Vanne papillon,0,Lyon
FLT-300,Filtre a cartouche,40,Grenoble

One command loads it, in a scope you name:

$ lm csv ingest stock.csv --scope retail --name stock-count
Ingested stock.csv into ext.stock_count
  • rows written:    3
  • promoted cols:   4
      - sku (text)
      - label (text)
      - qty (bigint)
      - warehouse (text)

  • askable:         scope 'retail' — try: lm ask --scope retail "how many rows are in ext.stock_count?"
A dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.
  • qty holds numbers only, so it lands as a number. The other columns land as text.

  • On lumnik Open, the last two lines read:

    A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat.
The rows are in ext.stock_count, and a dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

  • The load runs once. Nothing runs again on its own.

docs.title: 4. Ask a question (Pro)
docs.text:
Ask in the scope you named:

$ lm ask --scope retail "quels articles ont une quantité à zéro ?"
Les articles ayant une quantité à zéro sont :

- SKU : VAN-200
  Libellé : Vanne papillon

  SKU      LABEL
  VAN-200  Vanne papillon
  1 row returned

  SQL: SELECT "sku", "label"
FROM "ext"."stock_count"
WHERE "qty" = 0
LIMIT 500
  • The rows and the SQL always come with the answer. Show them to the customer.
  • Use the words of the data. « Quels articles sont en rupture de stock ? » is declined: no column says "rupture". « Quantité à zéro » names the column, and works.
  • Without --scope, the question goes to your default scope, where this file is not.
  • lm ask answers 404 on lumnik Open, and on Pro with the AI switched off.

Why Ask declines, and what to do: When Ask refuses.

docs.title: 5. Take it back off
docs.text:
$ lm connector delete stock_count --dry-run
Would delete connector stock_count (csv-file) — 3 rows of ext.stock_count, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)

Without --dry-run, lm asks you to type delete. Any other answer deletes nothing. A script passes --force.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Make it recurring: a csv-file connector reads the export on a schedule: CSV & files. Give it the registered name, here stock_count: lm turns every - of --name into _. Then lm connector resume stock_count.
  • Another source: Other first sources — an API, SFTP, S3.
  • The full demo, with two sources fused into one customer: The WOW.

docs.title: What makes a scope answerable
docs.text:
Ask needs to know a scope's tables. A connector run, a one-shot load or an entity apply tells it, with nothing to configure. See what Ask knows of a scope:

lm source schema --scope retail

Empty, or not found? Rebuild it with lm source rediscover --scope retail, then ask again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Do this 401 on every command Your session ended. Run lm login again. Error: access refused (403): scope not granted Your account holds scope: roles, and not this one. Use a scope you hold. Error: API error 404 (no details from the server) on lm ask lumnik Open, or the AI is off. See The two editions. Ask declines a question Rephrase it with the words of your columns. Check lm source schema --scope <tag>. A second connector appears after lm apply -f metadata.name differs from the registered name. Delete the duplicate, re-apply under the name lm connector list shows.

docs.title: Other first sources — an API, SFTP, S3
docs.text: The Quickstart loads one CSV. Here, three other first sources. Each one ends where the Quickstart does: rows you can show, then a question.

docs.title: Store the credential first
docs.text:
A password or a key never goes on the command line or in a manifest. Store it in the hub:

Gesture Use it for lm secret set NAME a password or a token. It prompts; nothing shows on screen or in your shell history. lm secret set NAME - a value on several lines, such as a private SSH key. Paste it, then Ctrl+D (PowerShell: Ctrl+Z, Enter). 
$ lm secret set SFTP_EXPORT_PASSWORD --description "nightly export server"
Value for SFTP_EXPORT_PASSWORD:
Created secret "SFTP_EXPORT_PASSWORD"
$ lm secret list
NAME                           ROTATED_AT                     DESCRIPTION
SFTP_EXPORT_PASSWORD           -                              nightly export server
  • No command prints a secret back. Lost it? Set it again.
  • Writing a secret needs the lm_admin role (roles).

docs.title: An API with an OpenAPI description
docs.text:
lm writes the connector manifest from the API's description:

lm secret set STRIPE_API_KEY
lm source rest from-openapi \
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/openapi/master/openapi/spec3.json \
    --name stripe --scope billing -o stripe.yaml

Open stripe.yaml before you apply it:

  • A big API gives a long manifest: one endpoint per GET path. Delete the ones the customer does not need. A path the draft cannot page correctly stays commented out, under a line that says what to declare.
  • Add spec.schedule (a cron) to run it every night. Nothing else schedules it.
lm validate -f stripe.yaml
lm apply -f stripe.yaml
lm connector run stripe          # apply declares it; this starts the first run
  • lm validate stops at the first envelope error. Fix it, run it again.
  • An endpoint's id comes from its whole path: /v1/charges is stripe/v1-charges. Silence one with lm endpoint disable stripe/v1-charges.

Then ask in the scope you declared (Pro), once the run is Completed:

lm ask --scope billing "how many charges above 1000?"

All the REST options: REST.

docs.title: A nightly SFTP export
docs.text:
The most common case: the ERP drops a file on an SFTP server every night.

ssh-keyscan sftp.acme.io | ssh-keygen -lf -    # read the server's SHA256:… fingerprint
lm secret set ACME_SFTP_KEY -                  # paste the private key, then Ctrl+D
lm csv ingest sftp://lumnik@sftp.acme.io/export/billing-latest.csv \
    --key-secret ACME_SFTP_KEY --host-key-fingerprint "SHA256:…" \
    --scope billing --name acme-billing
  • Without --host-key-fingerprint, the hub refuses to connect.
  • A server reached by password takes --password-secret NAME instead of --key-secret.

docs.title: Make it nightly
docs.text:
The one-shot leaves no manifest. Write a csv-file manifest under the name the one-shot registered. lm turns acme-billing into acme_billing: read it in lm connector list. Another name creates a second connector.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme_billing                  # the name lm connector list shows
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [billing]
spec:
  schedule: "0 6 * * *"
  transport:
    kind: sftp
    host: sftp.acme.io
    user: lumnik
    path: /export/*.csv
    key_env: ACME_SFTP_KEY
    host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:…"
  after_process: move
  archive_path: /archive/

lm validate -f acme-nightly.yaml
lm apply -f acme-nightly.yaml
lm connector resume acme_billing       # the one-shot left it dormant; apply does not wake it

All the file options: CSV & files.

docs.title: An S3 bucket
docs.text:
lm secret set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
lm secret set AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
lm csv ingest s3://acme-exports/billing/ \
    --region eu-west-3 --suffix .csv --scope billing
  • The S3 source reads these two secret names by default.
  • Other names? Pass --access-key-secret NAME --secret-key-secret NAME.
  • MinIO, Cloudflare R2, GCS in S3 mode: add --endpoint https://….

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: You see Do this Bearer token unavailable (env=STRIPE_API_KEY) The secret is missing. lm secret set STRIPE_API_KEY. apply failed: … (400) The hub refused the manifest. lm validate -f names the field. 429 Too Many Requests from the API Add default_rate_limit: 50/s under spec:, then lm apply -f again. WARN metadata.scopes — no scopes declared on validate Add scopes: [<scope>] under metadata. Without it, Ask cannot see the tables. An empty lm run list after a one-shot Expected: a one-shot records no run. A connector run does.

docs.title: Prerequisites — prepare the ground
docs.text:
What must be ready before the integrator arrives, in one checklist.

This list serves the guided path and any first self-host install. Items marked (real ingestion only) are not needed for the demo path itself.

On Windows, start elsewhere

Follow Deploy on Windows first — it installs WSL2 (admin rights + a restart, exactly what to get done before the integrator arrives) and says which window each command below goes in. Then come back to this checklist.

docs.title: The machine
docs.text: Item Requirement Notes Docker + Docker Compose v2 required a laptop or any cloud VM works Tools curl, python3, openssl, awk, jq up.sh refuses to start without the first four; the self-check below uses jq. Debian/Ubuntu: sudo apt install -y curl python3 openssl gawk jq Sizing 4 vCPU / 16 GB / SSD, measured for 50 concurrent users (sizing) the model needs its own budget — see below Free disk ~20 GB for a comfortable first install (images + models + data) the models alone are most of it Outbound network required during install: github.com (clone), the container registries, ollama.com (models) at runtime the AI layer is local by default (Models) Air-gapped install not supported no image pre-load or mirror tooling ships Go 1.26+ only to build lm from source — pre-built archives are on every release

docs.title: The AI layer (Ollama)
docs.text:
lumnik Pro only — the open edition does not use Ollama; skip this section. Chat, semantic search and ask need an Ollama the hub can reach. Install Ollama on the host (not in a container), then pull the three models:

ollama pull nomic-embed-text      # embeddings
ollama pull llama3.2              # conversational chat
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b     # text-to-SQL ask (4.7 GB — the analytic model)

Budget ~8 GB of downloads. No GPU is needed for the guided path.

docs.title: On a Linux host: let the hub reach Ollama
docs.text:
As installed, Ollama listens only on the host itself. The hub runs in a container and cannot reach it. Make Ollama listen on Docker's bridge:

sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
printf '[Service]\nEnvironment="OLLAMA_HOST=172.17.0.1:11434"\nEnvironment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1"\n' \
  | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ollama
  • Only containers can reach 172.17.0.1. Nothing is exposed outside.
  • OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 keeps the model loaded. Without it, the first question after a pause takes tens of seconds on a CPU-only box.
  • A host firewall must let the containers in: sudo ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 11434 proto tcp.
  • macOS and Windows (Docker Desktop) need none of this.

docs.title: Network & access
docs.text: Item Requirement Ports 8080 (hub) and 8180 (Keycloak) must be free on this machine; 11434 is Ollama's own (Pro). The stack binds them loopback-only — remote access goes through an SSH tunnel or the TLS proxy Source flow (real ingestion only) a network path hub → source database, and a SELECT-only account on the declared tables (JDBC → Connection) — nothing for the guided path: the demo embeds its own sources First-login accounts nothing to prepare: the realm ships hubadmin and integrator, whose passwords land in the generated .env at install time (Quickstart)

docs.title: The 60-second self-check
docs.text:
docker run --rm hello-world                                    # 1. Docker
curl -sI https://github.com | head -1                          # 2. network
go version                                                     # 3. Go (source build only)
python3 --version && openssl version                           # 4. tools up.sh needs
curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/tags | jq -r '.models[].name'  # 5. Ollama (Pro)
df -h ~                                                        # 6. disk
# Expected 1 Hello from Docker! — daemon up, permission, registry reachable 2 HTTP/2 200 — outbound network 3 go1.26 or later 4 two version lines 5 lists nomic-embed-text:latest, llama3.2:latest, qwen2.5-coder:7b 6 ~20 GB free where you'll clone

On a Linux host with the override above, ask the bridge instead: curl -s http://172.17.0.1:11434/api/tags.

All green? Start the guided path or go straight to Deploy.

docs.title: RAG over HTTP — the chat, search and scope API
docs.text:
The JSON contract behind lm ask, the TUI and the PWA — chat, search, scopes, corpora and the admin schema endpoints, with every guard refusal and every HTTP error shape a caller can hit.

lm ask, the TUI's :ask and the PWA call a few JSON endpoints on the hub. This page is the contract for calling them yourself, from a script or an app. The PWA's chat is one POST /api/rag/chat with mode: "analytic".

Requests and responses are application/json unless noted. The payloads below are real answers from the demo desk. Where an lm command does the same, it is named.

docs.title: Quickstart — one chat call with curl
docs.text:
Mint a token as in Test the API, then ask, the way the PWA does:

curl -s https://your-hub.example.com/api/rag/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"question": "Combien de clients GOLD sont à Lyon ?", "mode": "analytic", "scope": "desk", "lang": "fr"}'

The answer comes with its SQL and its rows: the analytic response. Read the SQL before you trust a zero.

docs.title: The two doors
docs.text:
The same chat lives behind two paths with different audiences:

Door Path Role User POST /api/rag/chat lm_user — the PWA's door Platform POST /api/platform/rag/chat + everything else under /api/platform/rag/* lm_integrator — lm, scripts, tooling

Both answer the same way, with the same scope binding and guards; only the role and the rate-limit bucket differ. An app for end users uses /api/rag/chat.

Four admin endpoints (status, reindex, schema, rediscover) also require lm_admin: the token must carry both lm_integrator and lm_admin.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Every call carries a Bearer JWT:

Authorization: Bearer <access-token>

Get one from your OIDC issuer: Test the API — mint a token. A token lasts one hour on the bundled realm: mint another when a call answers 401.

The tenant comes from the token, never from a header.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
POST /api/rag/chat              (lm_user)
POST /api/platform/rag/chat     (lm_integrator)

One endpoint, two modes, selected by the mode field:

Field Type Meaning Default question string the natural-language question — required (blank → 400) — mode string "analytic" (case-insensitive) = text-to-SQL over the ingested hub; anything else or absent = semantic retrieval + chat semantic scope string the data-scope tag. "all" = no specific scope; blank or absent = your default (lm scope set) if set, else none. Semantic: filters retrieval to chunks carrying the tag. Analytic: names the schema card to ask over — a scope-bound user must name, or default to, a granted scope (scopes). your default / system corpus string semantic only: restrict retrieval to one corpus (usually a connector source, see corpora) all corpora topK integer semantic only: how many chunks to retrieve as context, 1 to 50. Outside → 400 {"error":"topK must be between 1 and 50"} 10 lang string the answer language, a two-letter code ("fr"). The answer is written in it whatever the question's language — a terse question such as SO-000004 statut ? carries none. Absent = the question's own language. Any other value → 400 {"error":"lang must be a two-letter language code"}, in either mode. The PWA sends fr; lm ask sends --lang, else the language of LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG, in that order. the question's previous string analytic only: the question the last answer was given for, so that this one may continue it (« Et HAWARD ? »). See follow-up questions. Blank or absent = a standalone question. Over 1000 characters → 400 {"error":"previous must be at most 1000 characters"}. Sent in semantic mode → 400 {"error":"previous is only read in analytic mode"}. —

corpus and topK are silently ignored in analytic mode. Fixed sentences (abstentions, guard refusals) follow lang too, in French or English — see how refusals surface.

docs.title: Semantic response
docs.text:
The question is embedded, the top-K most similar chunks are retrieved (tenant-isolated, tag- and corpus-filtered), and the LLM answers from that context only, citing chunks inline with [row:hash] tags:

{
  "answer": "Les transitions autorisées pour une livraison correspondent à la transition d'état EN_ROUTE vers LIVREE.\n\nSelon les déclarations de workflow, seule cette transition est autorisée entre ces deux états.\n\n[No specific source is cited for the given context, but it can be inferred that it should follow a standard naming convention.",
  "citations": []
}

The semantic answer is the model's text, checked by no guard: here it ends with a stray sentence. Read it with care; for figures, use the analytic mode.

  • citations lists the row hashes of every retrieved chunk that is a row — the context the model saw. lm data row HASH shows the row behind one.
  • A kind: Workflow lifecycle chunk has no row hash: an answer drawn only from lifecycles has "citations": [].
  • The [row:hash] tags inside answer are the ones the model says it used.

docs.title: Analytic response (mode: "analytic")
docs.text:
The question is translated to a single read-only SELECT over the scope's declared schema, guarded, executed, and phrased back:

{
  "answer": "Il y a 2 clients GOLD à Lyon.",
  "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) \nFROM \"connector\".\"v_acmecustomer\" \nWHERE \"segment\" = 'GOLD' AND \"city\" = 'Lyon'\nLIMIT 500",
  "rowCount": 1,
  "rows": [
    {
      "count": 2
    }
  ],
  "dataAsOf": "2026-10-24T21:35:11.811114Z",
  "otherDoors": [
    "conflicts"
  ],
  "disputed": [
    {
      "key": "P-1008",
      "column": "city",
      "label": "Ville",
      "matched": "Lyon",
      "retained": "Lyon",
      "counted": true,
      "sources": [
        {
          "src": "t_acme_desk_erp",
          "value": "Lyon"
        },
        {
          "src": "t_acme_desk_crm",
          "value": "Villeurbanne"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "disputedTruncated": false,
  "abstained": false,
  "understoodAs": null
}

Every field is always present.

  • sql is the query that ran (or was refused).
  • disputed ([] when empty) names the fused records the answer filtered on while their sources disagree; disputedTruncated says more exist than the ten listed. When it is non-empty, otherDoors carries conflicts. When it appears: Disputed rows.
disputed[] field Meaning key the record's match key column, label the filtered column and its label matched the filter value at stake retained the value the fused record kept counted true: counted on a disputed value; false: left out while a source holds matched sources the _conflicts entries (src, value), in ledger order

lm ask -o json prints the same fields, plus columns.

  • rows is the raw result, one {column: value} map per row, at most 500 rows.
  • Execution is read-only, limited to your tenant, with a statement timeout.

docs.title: How refusals surface in the payload
docs.text:
A guard refusal arrives as a normal 200 analytic response: the refusal message as answer, rowCount: 0, rows: [], and sql holding the refused query ("" when the model abstained before writing any):

{
  "answer": "Je ne peux pas répondre à partir des données disponibles pour ce périmètre — la question ne correspond pas au schéma déclaré.",
  "sql": "",
  "rowCount": 0,
  "rows": [],
  "dataAsOf": null,
  "otherDoors": [],
  "disputed": [],
  "disputedTruncated": false,
  "abstained": true,
  "understoodAs": null
}

dataAsOf is the end of the scope's last completed run; null when there is none, and on refusals.

otherDoors names the doors that can answer when this one abstains, as tokens; [] otherwise:

Token The scope… Where to go next lifecycle declares a kind: Workflow, read by the semantic chat lm chat conflicts fuses an entity whose disagreements are in its ledger lm conflicts list

lm ask prints the command as a try: line — see Abstention exit.

  • The answer names no command: map each token to the gesture your surface has, and skip a token you do not recognise.
  • A token is offered only when the question is about what that door holds (sources that disagree; a lifecycle, its stages, a blocked document); an unrelated refusal carries none.

Branch on abstained, never on the words. The fixed sentences (abstentions, refusals, the zero-row caveat) follow lang, in English or French; anything else gets English. abstained is true when the door declined to answer:

  • the model's own "cannot answer", or a scope with no schema;
  • rejected SQL, or a table, column or value the scope does not declare;
  • a filter that matches several rows, or a query the database refused;
  • a query that returned no rows;
  • a phrased answer withheld for a figure the rows do not back;
  • a model that could not write the answer (the query ran: rows and sql are the result).

Treat rowCount: 0 as "read the answer text", never as "there are none".

Refusals that happen before the ask — a scope-bound user naming a scope they don't hold — are HTTP errors instead: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"} (see scopes).

docs.title: Follow-up questions
docs.text:
Send the previous question in previous; lm ask has no equivalent. The hub keeps nothing between calls: your client holds the thread, one sentence long. Send the response's understoodAs back as the next previous; when it is absent (a first question), send the question as asked.

Played on a hub whose scope catalogue holds eight articles (lm csv ingest ./articles.csv --scope catalogue). Only four fields of each response are shown:

$ curl -s https://your-hub.example.com/api/rag/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"question": "Et HAWARD ?", "previous": "Donne-moi les références dont la description contient Badu.",
         "mode": "analytic", "scope": "catalogue", "lang": "fr"}' | jq '{answer, sql, understoodAs, abstained}'
{
  "answer": "Il y a 2 références dont la description contient HAWARD :\n\n1. 4100.000.001\n2. 4100.000.002\n\nTotal de références : 2",
  "sql": "SELECT reference FROM \"ext\".\"articles\" WHERE description ILIKE '%HAWARD%'\nLIMIT 500",
  "understoodAs": "Donne-moi les références dont la description contient HAWARD.",
  "abstained": false
}
$ curl -s https://your-hub.example.com/api/rag/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"question": "Et seulement celles de la catégorie Pompes ?", "previous": "Donne-moi les références dont la description contient HAWARD.",
         "mode": "analytic", "scope": "catalogue", "lang": "fr"}' | jq '{answer, sql, understoodAs, abstained}'
{
  "answer": "Les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient HAWARD sont : 4100.000.001.",
  "sql": "SELECT reference \nFROM \"ext\".\"articles\" \nWHERE categorie = 'Pompes' AND description ILIKE '%HAWARD%'\nLIMIT 500",
  "understoodAs": "Donne-moi les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient HAWARD.",
  "abstained": false
}
$ curl -s https://your-hub.example.com/api/rag/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"question": "Et le deuxième, il coûte combien ?", "previous": "Donne-moi les références dont la description contient HAWARD.",
         "mode": "analytic", "scope": "catalogue", "lang": "fr"}' | jq '{answer, sql, understoodAs, abstained}'
{
  "answer": "Je n'ai pas pu rattacher cette question à la précédente. Posez-la en entier, avec la valeur ou le nom auquel elle renvoie.",
  "sql": "",
  "understoodAs": null,
  "abstained": true
}
  • understoodAs is present only when the question was resolved against previous. It is null for a standalone question and on that refusal. After a refusal, keep the previous you had: the user usually asks again in other words.
  • The answer is phrased for understoodAs, not for the follow-up alone. Every guard reads understoodAs.
  • understoodAs is never longer than 1000 characters, so it always fits the next previous.
  • A follow-up costs one more model call, except a bare « Et X ? » over a question holding one value, which the hub resolves itself. What a resolution may and may not do, and when it is refused: ask honesty.
  • A question may open by addressing the chat by name, « lumnik, combien d'articles… ? ». The address is removed before anything reads the question. A question that is nothing but the address (« lumnik, ») is kept as written.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
POST /api/platform/rag/search     (lm_integrator)        lm rag search QUERY --top-k N

The retrieval layer under the semantic chat: the nearest chunks, no model answer.

Field Type Meaning Default query string the search text — required (blank → 400) — topK integer number of hits, 1 to 50 (lm rag search asks for 5). Outside → 400 {"error":"topK must be between 1 and 50"} 10 corpus string restrict to one corpus (source) all scope string restrict to chunks carrying this scope tag; "all"/blank = no tag filter (for a scope-bound user, rewritten onto their granted set — never unfiltered) none 
{
  "results": [
    {
      "rowHash": null,
      "ref": "workflow/acme-order-lifecycle",
      "content": "Workflow acme-order-lifecycle — cycle de vie de la colonne status de la table connector.t_acme_desk_orders (declared by the integrator). États: BROUILLON (initial, « Brouillon »), EN_COURS (« En préparation », alias: en cours, encours), TERMINE (terminal, « Terminée », alias: fini), ANNULE (terminal, « Annulée »). Transitions autorisées: BROUILLON->EN_COURS, BROUILLON->ANNULE, EN_COURS->ANNULE, EN_COURS->TERMINE.",
      "similarity": 0.5389897637416403,
      "metadata": {
        "scope": "desk",
        "table": "connector.t_acme_desk_orders",
        "provenance": "declared"
      }
    }
  ]
}

One hit shown. rowHash is null on a workflow's chunk; on a row's chunk, lm data row HASH shows the row. similarity runs from 0 to 1. The same scope binding applies: a scope outside a bound user's grants → 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
GET /api/platform/rag/scopes      (lm_integrator)        lm scopes

The scopes with indexed chunks in this tenant (a scope is declared on the connector):

[
  {"scope":"demo","connectors":0,"chunks":1,"lastIndexed":"2026-10-24T19:59:25.582921Z"},
  {"scope":"desk","connectors":0,"chunks":2,"lastIndexed":"2026-10-24T21:35:19.934093Z"},
  {"scope":"retail","connectors":0,"chunks":1,"lastIndexed":"2026-10-24T19:55:42.964543Z"}
]

lastIndexed is an ISO instant, or "" if unknown. A scope-bound user sees only their granted scopes in this list.

docs.title: Your default scope
docs.text: GET / PUT /api/platform/users/me/scope (lm scope / lm scope set TAG) read and set the default the chat doors use when a request names no scope ({"defaultScope": "compta"}; empty string clears it). Both answer 404 {"error":"no user record on this hub for user_id N"} when your token names a hub user id that has no row on this hub (BYO IdP).

docs.title: Corpora
docs.text:
GET /api/platform/rag/corpora     (lm_integrator)

Lists the corpora with indexed chunks (no lm command; :corpus in lm chat picks one). A corpus is usually a connector source, but not always: applying a kind: Workflow indexes its declared lifecycle under workflow:<name>, which is backed by a manifest rather than an ingest run.

[
  {
    "name": "oneshot:ext.stock_count",
    "chunkCount": 1
  },
  {
    "name": "workflow:acme-delivery-lifecycle",
    "chunkCount": 1
  },
  {
    "name": "workflow:acme-order-lifecycle",
    "chunkCount": 1
  },
  {
    "name": "workflow:commande-lifecycle",
    "chunkCount": 1
  }
]

This listing is scope-bound too: a scope-bound user sees only corpora carrying at least one granted scope tag — and an untagged corpus belongs to no scope, so it is invisible to a bound user.

docs.title: Schema (admin)
docs.text:
GET  /api/platform/rag/schema?scope=<tag>        (lm_admin)    lm source schema --scope TAG
POST /api/platform/rag/rediscover?scope=<tag>    (lm_admin)    lm source rediscover --scope TAG

schema returns the scope's schema card — the exact tables/columns (with business labels, descriptions, examples and declared value-domains) the analytic mode is allowed to query. 404 if no card exists for the scope; run discovery first. rediscover rebuilds the card from the ingested tables and returns a summary:

{ "scope": "clients", "tableCount": 3, "columnCount": 41, "enriched": true, "sourceType": "connector" }

Both are served by the hub itself, so they exist in the Open edition and with the AI switched off.

docs.title: Status and reindex (admin)
docs.text:
GET  /api/platform/rag/status     (lm_admin)    lm rag status
POST /api/platform/rag/reindex    (lm_admin)    lm rag reindex

{"indexed": true, "chunks": 8, "indexedAt": "2026-10-24T21:32:45.842950Z", "provider": "ollama-nomic", "embeddingModel": "nomic-embed-text"}
  • provider and embeddingModel are the live embedding model's; "none" when there is none.
  • reindex rebuilds the platform corpus (manifests, API, hooks) and returns 202 {"status": "reindex_started"} at once; poll status. Chunks of ingested rows are not touched: they are written at ingestion and erased with their connector (GDPR → erasure).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Status Body When 400 {"error": "question is required"} (chat), {"error": "query is required"} (search), {"error": "scope is required"} (schema) missing/blank required field 400 {"error": "previous must be at most 1000 characters"}, {"error": "previous is only read in analytic mode"} a follow-up previous over the bound, or sent without mode: analytic 404 {"error": "Unable to find matching target resource method"} under /api/platform/rag/, {"error": "HTTP 404 Not Found"} on /api/rag/chat chat, search, scopes or corpora on lumnik Open: the hub has no such door. lm prints this hub's build has no Ask: … 404 no body the same doors on lumnik Pro with the AI switched off. lm prints this hub has Ask switched off (LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false): … 401 plain text authentication required + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header no/invalid token on /api/platform/* — note: not JSON 401 {"error": "no tenant in security context"} analytic ask/schema call whose token resolves no usable tenant 403 plain text missing role lm_integrator authenticated but not an integrator, on /api/platform/* 403 {"error": "scope not granted"} a scope-bound user asked outside their granted set — the uniform refusal across the whole read surface 404 {"error": "No schema card found for scope: ..."} GET .../schema on a scope with no discovered schema card yet 409 {"error": "no schema discovered for scope '...' — apply an entity or run discovery first", "hint": "lm entity apply registers a schema for the scope; ask again after it lands"} analytic ask on a scope with no schema card at all — a fresh install, or a scope with no kind: Entity applied yet 429 {"error": "rate limit exceeded"} + Retry-After: <seconds> header bucket exhausted — honor Retry-After before retrying 503 {"error": "...", "hint": "..."} the model or embedding service is missing or unreachable — a deployment problem, not a caller problem. (An analytic ask whose SQL already ran is not a 503 when only the answer could not be written: it is a 200 with abstained: true, the rows and the SQL.)

Rate limits are per (bucket, tenant) in a fixed 60-second window. The chat and search endpoints ride three buckets — user-chat, platform-chat, platform-search — each configurable via lumnik.ratelimit.<bucket>.rpm (fallback lumnik.ratelimit.default.rpm, code default 60; 0 disables). See rate limits.

docs.text:
