docs.title: Models — configuring the LLMs
docs.text: lumnik Pro. Three models do three jobs: the chat, the ask, the embeddings. Each one is an environment variable. The default provider is Ollama, on your machine: nothing leaves it unless you point it elsewhere.

docs.title: Which model does what
docs.text:
Job Default Variable Notes Chat: lm chat, answers from your indexed data llama3.2 RAG_CHAT_MODEL a conversational model; it writes no SQL Ask: lm ask, the PWA's Chat, lm view generate qwen2.5-coder:7b ASK_SQL_MODEL must write SQL: a coding model. ~4.7 GB Embeddings: indexing and semantic search nomic-embed-text RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL its dimension is load-bearing: below

The three ollama pull lines: Prerequisites. JUDGE_MODEL (gemma4) serves an offline evaluation only: a running hub never calls it. Skip it.

docs.title: The knobs
docs.text:
All are environment variables. Self-host: set them in the root .env, then re-run up.sh with your flags. Helm (cloud edition): the same names, prefixed LUMNIK_ when you run up.sh.

Variable Default Drives OLLAMA_BASE_URL http://host.docker.internal:11434 (self-host) where the hub finds Ollama — another machine RAG_CHAT_MODEL llama3.2 the chat ASK_SQL_MODEL qwen2.5-coder:7b the ask and view generation ASK_SQL_NUM_CTX 32768 the ask model's context, in tokens. Lower it on a host short of memory ASK_SQL_NUM_PREDICT 1024 the most tokens the ask model writes per call. Raise it if view generation or wide tables hit it LUMNIK_ASK_ANSWER_BUDGET_CHARS 6000 how many characters of rows the answer is written from (about fifty catalogue rows). Every row is still returned RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL nomic-embed-text the embeddings RAG_EMBEDDING_DIM 768 must match the embedding model — change it only with the migration
  • The ask model runs at temperature 0: the same question gets the same SQL, in practice.
  • A call that takes more than 120 seconds is reported, not retried: timeouts.
  • lm rag status shows the embedding provider and model the hub really uses.

docs.title: Swapping a model on Ollama
docs.text:
1. Pull it on the Ollama host: ollama pull mistral.
  2. Set RAG_CHAT_MODEL=mistral in the root .env. Edit the line if it exists: do not add a second.
  3. Re-run up.sh with the flags you installed with.

A misspelt variable is ignored without a word, and the old model keeps answering. Check:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec hub env | grep RAG_CHAT_MODEL

The same for ASK_SQL_MODEL. For RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL, see the dimension below.

docs.title: Switching the AI off
docs.text:
LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false turns off the chat, the ask, view generation and the embeddings, without changing the build. Absent means on. How to set it: Switch the AI off.

It must be exactly true or false; anything else (FALSE, no, 0) stops the hub at startup with a message naming the setting.

What you see once it is off:

  • The PWA has no Chat tab. The other tabs are untouched.
  • lm module list shows rag and llm as INACTIVE, reason disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled. In the Open edition they are not listed at all.
  • lm ask, lm rag search, lm scopes and a question in lm chat answer Error: API error 404 (no details from the server).
  • lm view generate answers that no chat model is available.
  • lm rag status says provider: none and indexed: false; lm rag reindex has nothing to index with.
  • lm csv ingest loads the file and no longer says it is askable.
  • Nothing calls a model and no embedding is computed.
$ lm ask --scope desk "combien de clients ?"
Error: API error 404 (no details from the server)
$ lm view generate desk "les clients"
Error: API error 400: generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one
$ lm rag status
indexed: false
chunks: 0
indexed_at: -
provider: none
embedding_model: none

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled

What does not change: the images and the data already indexed. Search does not depend on this setting.

Switching it back on brings back the data you had. What needed indexing while the AI was off (a workflow applied, a table ingested, a connector re-described) is absent: re-apply the workflow or the connector, or re-ingest the file. lm rag reindex rebuilds only the platform corpus.

docs.title: Embeddings — model and dimension travel together
docs.text:
nomic-embed-text writes 768-number vectors, and the index stores 768. A model with another dimension is a migration, not a variable flip. No lm command does it. Try it on a copy first.

  1. Back up: ./deploy/selfhost/backup.sh.

  2. As the database owner, empty the index and give it the new size <n>:

    DELETE FROM rag.chunk;
DROP INDEX rag.chunk_embedding_idx;
ALTER TABLE rag.chunk ALTER COLUMN embedding TYPE VECTOR(<n>);
CREATE INDEX chunk_embedding_idx ON rag.chunk USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

  3. Set RAG_EMBEDDING_MODEL and RAG_EMBEDDING_DIM=<n> in .env, then re-run up.sh.

  4. Index again: lm rag reindex, then run every connector, re-apply every workflow and reload every lm csv ingest file.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
Each model call times out at 120 seconds. Raise one for a slow model, in the hub's environment:

QUARKUS_LANGCHAIN4J_OLLAMA_ANALYTIC_TIMEOUT=300s     # the ask model; …_OLLAMA_TIMEOUT for the chat

The self-host compose passes only the variables it lists: add the line to the hub's environment: in docker-compose.selfhost.yml.

docs.title: Pointing at OpenAI
docs.text:
Not a variable: the provider is chosen when the hub is built.

  1. In lumnik-llm-langchain/src/main/resources/application.properties, switch the providers you want:

    quarkus.langchain4j.chat-model.provider=openai
quarkus.langchain4j.embedding-model.provider=openai
quarkus.langchain4j.analytic.chat-model.provider=openai

  2. Set quarkus.langchain4j.openai.api-key and the model names (quarkus.langchain4j.openai.*-model.model-name, …openai.analytic.*). Set temperature=0 on the analytic model: OpenAI's default is 1.0.

  3. Rebuild: ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build.
  4. OpenAI's embeddings have another dimension (1536 for text-embedding-3-small): migrate.
  5. Check with lm rag status: it names the provider and model in use.

You can mix providers: OpenAI for the chat, the local model for the SQL.

docs.text:
• Prerequisites — the AI layer: the ollama pulls.
  • When Ask refuses: what wraps the ask model's output.
  • Scopes: the boundary every model answers within.

docs.title: Scopes — business-data boundaries for Ask
docs.text:
A scope is declared on the connector — metadata.scopes — no object to create, no admin screen. By default it keeps every answer inside one declared scope; opt-in scope:<name> Keycloak roles turn it into a need-to-know boundary too.

Every lm ask example passes --scope. This page defines what a scope actually is, how one comes to exist, and what it guarantees.

docs.title: A scope is declared on the connector
docs.text:
There is no separate scope object to create or administer. A scope is a name a connector manifest declares about itself:

metadata:
  name: crm-customers
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [clients]     # ← this IS the scope
  • Every table and chunk the connector ingests carries its scopes. A tenant's scopes are those of its connectors and its fused entities.
  • metadata.scopes is the only place: metadata.tags or target.tags is refused at validate, with the line to paste instead.
  • A connector that declares none is valid but not askable in any scope; validation warns.
  • A scope name is lowercase, starts with a letter, then letters, digits, _ or -, at most 41 characters — the same rule on every door that writes one. It becomes the case-sensitive Keycloak role scope:<name>.

docs.title: Using scopes
docs.text:
lm scopes                       # list scopes in this tenant (chunks, connectors, last indexed)
lm ask --scope clients "how many customers in Lyon?"
lm scope                        # show your default scope (fallback: 'system')
lm scope set clients            # set your default; empty string clears it
lm ask "how many customers in Lyon?"   # no --scope: asks your default

$ lm scopes
SCOPE   CONNECTORS  CHUNKS  LAST INDEXED
demo    0           1       2026-10-24 21:59
desk    0           2       2026-10-24 23:35
retail  0           1       2026-10-24 21:55
$ lm scope set desk
default scope set: desk
$ lm ask "combien de clients à Lyon ?"
Il y a 2 clients à Lyon.
  data as of: 2026-10-24T21:35:11.811114Z (last completed run)
…
  SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "connector"."v_acmecustomer" WHERE "city" = 'Lyon'
LIMIT 500
  • lm scopes lists the scopes the chat has indexed content in. CHUNKS is what the chat can cite. CONNECTORS counts only connectors whose rows the chat indexed: it often reads 0.
  • lm connector scope ls <connector> shows a connector's declared scopes, run or not; lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what is askable.
  • Moving a connector to another scope moves its tables between the two scopes' schema cards at once (capture). Its indexed chat chunks keep their old scopes until lm connector scope sync.
  • The default is a preference, not a grant: a scope-bound user whose default names a scope they do not hold gets Error: access refused (403): scope not granted.

In the TUI the header shows the session scope — seeded from your default (TUI).

docs.title: What a scope guarantees — and what it doesn't
docs.text:
• Tenant isolation is beneath scopes, enforced by PostgreSQL Row-Level Security. A scope never crosses a tenant.
  • Within a tenant, the scope is the business-scope boundary on analytic SQL: the leak guard refuses any generated query that reads a table not declared in the scope (see the guard page for the refusal message).
  • By default a scope is a working boundary, not a security boundary between users: a user with no scope grants may ask any scope — scopes keep answers inside the selected data set. To make it a need-to-know boundary too, bind the user (next section).

docs.title: Binding users to scopes (opt-in)
docs.text:
A grant is a Keycloak realm role named scope:<name> — nothing else to create or administer.

  • A user with no scope:* roles is unscoped: tenant-wide access, exactly the default behavior above. (This is why admins need no special case — they simply carry no grants.)
  • A user with one or more scope:* roles is scope-bound:
  • asking or searching a scope they do not hold: Error: access refused (403): scope not granted;
  • lm ask needs a scope they hold: named with --scope, or set as their default. all is refused;
  • search and chat without a scope read only their scopes;
  • lm scopes lists only their granted scopes.

The boundary covers every read, not only the chat:

Surface A bound user sees views, entities, search only their scopes; another one answers scope not granted the inbox (lm inbox, Inbox) only decisions in their scopes; an id from another scope is a 404 workflows and their tape only workflows in their scopes connectors, runs, dead letters only connectors whose every scope they hold — the details

Writing is stricter than reading. A bound user may see a resource holding any one of its scopes, but may publish one (lm apply, lm entity apply) only while holding every scope it declares. A scopeless manifest is refused too. Here the caller holds scope:sales and the manifest declares scopes: [desk]:

$ lm apply -f docs/apps/demo/sources/10-erp.yaml
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted

Administering a connector follows the writing rule. A bound integrator sees, runs and changes only the connectors whose every scope they hold, and their runs and dead letters. The details, with captures: A scope-bound integrator.

Checking grants. lumnik does not store them: a grant is a Keycloak realm role, read from each request's token.

  • Your own: no lm command shows them; GET /api/bff/v1/me returns your tenant, roles (with your scope:<name> grants) and modules.
  • Someone else's: Keycloak's admin console — realm → Users → the user → Role mapping.

The same table can belong to several scopes: declare scopes: [achat, compta] on the connector and a scope:achat user sees it while a scope:stock user does not:

flowchart LR
  u0["no scope:* roles<br/>— unscoped"] -->|"tenant-wide"| all
  ua["scope:achat"] --> A
  ua --> AB
  ua -.->|"403 scope not granted"| S
  subgraph all["one tenant's data"]
    A[("scopes: [achat]")]
    AB[("scopes: [achat, compta]")]
    S[("scopes: [stock]")]
  end

docs.title: Scoping and the ladder
docs.text: The same scope name runs the whole ladder: a kind: View renders a scope's table, a kind: Process watches a scope's raw ingest table, and a kind: Workflow declares a lifecycle whose corpus chunk carries that same scope — so a bound user retrieves the declared graph only for the scopes they hold. One scope name, end to end.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• When Ask refuses
  • CSV & files / JDBC / REST manifests — every kind declares metadata.scopes the same way.
  • Role management — the three confusable 403s — scope not granted is one of three different-looking 403s; the table there tells them apart.

docs.title: Analyze the database directly
docs.text: Connect psql or a GUI (pgAdmin, IntelliJ, DBeaver) to the self-host PostgreSQL. To browse ingested rows without SQL: lm data tables, then :tables in lm ui (CLI reference).

docs.title: Three roles, three postures
docs.text:
The install creates three database roles:

Role Sees Can write Use it for lumnik_readonly schema connector only (your ingested data), one tenant at a time no — refused by PostgreSQL itself day-to-day analysis of ingested data lumnik_app one tenant at a time (RLS applies) yes reproducing the application's own posture lumnik_admin every schema, every tenant (bypasses RLS) yes, including DDL cross-tenant checks, the core and identity schemas — read only, unless you know why

Passwords live in your .env (LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD, LUMNIK_APP_DB_PASSWORD, LUMNIK_ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD) — generated per install, never shipped.

docs.title: Quick look, no tooling
docs.text:
The database publishes no port to your machine by default. From inside the container, psql connects without a password:

CID=$(docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps -q postgres)
docker exec -it $CID psql -U lumnik_readonly -d lumnik

docs.title: Connect a GUI (pgAdmin, IntelliJ, DBeaver…)
docs.text:
Give the database a TCP door on your machine only, via a compose override — the shipped file stays untouched:

# analyse-ports.yml (next to docker-compose.selfhost.yml)
services:
  postgres:
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:5433:5432"]

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f analyse-ports.yml up -d postgres

Then in your tool: host localhost, port 5433, database lumnik, one of the three roles above with its .env password. The 127.0.0.1: prefix matters — the database listens to your machine, not your network. To close the door, run the same command without the override file:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d postgres

Opening or closing the door recreates the database container: the hub loses its database for a few seconds.

docs.title: The one habit: name your tenant
docs.text:
Under lumnik_readonly or lumnik_app, row-level security filters every table by the current tenant — and until you name one, you see no rows at all. Start each session with:

SET app.current_tenant = '1';   -- your tenant id; a fresh install seeds tenant 1

In IntelliJ, put that line in the data source's startup script so every connection carries it. In pgAdmin, run it at the top of each Query Tool session.

Ingested data lands in schema connector as t_-prefixed tables, one per endpoint, each with the tenant_id column the isolation keys on. As lumnik_readonly:

lumnik=> select count(*) from connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
     0
(1 row)

lumnik=> SET app.current_tenant = '1';
SET
lumnik=> select count(*) from connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
     9
(1 row)

lumnik=> select count(*) from core.audit_event;
ERROR:  permission denied for table audit_event

\dn lists the schemas: connector, core, identity, platform, rag, public. Outside connector, connect as lumnik_admin; it sees every tenant without a SET.

docs.title: Diagnosing a failed run
docs.text:
A run went wrong — read the ledger, not the logs, first: lm run get and lm dlq tell you exactly which rows fell out and why before you go looking for a stack trace.

A run reports a failure, or fewer rows arrived than you expected. Follow this walk:

flowchart TB
  s["a run went wrong"] --> g["lm run get RUN_ID"]
  g -->|"the run itself failed —<br/>no ledger to read"| logs["the hub logs"]
  g -->|"dead-letters > 0"| dlq["lm dlq list --run RUN_ID"]
  g -->|"arithmetic clean, but<br/>expected rows absent"| cursor["the cursor"]
  dlq --> why["lm dlq get ID —<br/>the reason and the exact row"]
  why --> fix["fix by reason<br/>(table below)"]
  fix --> rerun["lm connector run NAME —<br/>then mark the entries handled"]

docs.title: 1. Read the run
docs.text:
lm run list --connector orders    # newest first — find yours
lm run get <RUN_ID>               # IN, OUT, SKIPPED, DEAD-LETTERS

The 8-character id from the table is enough. A run that failed outright:

$ lm run get 0c5618e6
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
0c5618e6  products   default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
✖ run failed: SFTP connect failed: DefaultConnectFuture[lumnik@sftp.example.internal/<unresolved>:22]: Failed (UnresolvedAddressException) to execute: null — UnresolvedAddressException.

It never read a row: the SFTP host name does not resolve. Fix the network or the manifest.

A run that completed but set rows aside:

$ lm run get 6e52921c
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
6e52921c  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
⚠ 2 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 6e52921c-4168-437c-81d6-55d8bcd2a24c

What lm run get tells you, and where to go next:

You see Meaning Next ✖ run failed: … (or • run cancelled: …) the run itself failed: connection, credentials, source gone read the message; if it is not enough, the hub logs ⚠ N rows quarantined rows were dead-lettered, each with a reason step 2 ⚠ N cell(s) a hook did not deliver as declared — the rows were still written a transformer left a value blank or changed; the row is there the table below • N row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them the source no longer holds those rows; the table shrank the source • N file(s) unchanged since they were last read — not read again the file did not change: IN 0 is normal to read it again: lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> • run partial: … the run stopped before the end of its source; the reason says why read it; the next run continues • N file(s) read but not archived … the rows are in; moving the file failed the archive folder's rights clean arithmetic, rows still missing an incremental connector only fetches past its cursor lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> — the next run reads everything again

A cell warning, as it appears:

$ lm run get 4aaff94f
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
4aaff94f  invoices   default   Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
⚠ 1 cell(s) a hook did not deliver as declared — the rows were still written

Here parse-date with format yyyy-MM-dd met 03/09/2026 and wrote the cell empty. The same count is cellErrors in lm run get -o json and cell_errors: in the TUI describe panel.

What each hook does with a value it cannot read: the reference.

To send such a row to the dead letters instead of writing it, declare on-error: dlq on its column.

docs.title: 2. Read the quarantine
docs.text:
lm dlq list --run <RUN_ID>    # every quarantined row: reason, attempts, resolution, message
lm dlq get <ID>               # the full detail — including the offending payload

Both take the 8-character ids from the tables.

$ lm dlq list --run 6e52921c
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  RESOLUTION  MESSAGE
9d07dd36  orders     6e52921c  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/orders.csv:9 — Record has 2 values but 5 column…
da3dc703  orders     6e52921c  MalformedSource  1                     /tmp/exports/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 c…

$ lm dlq get 9d07dd36
ID:        9d07dd36-53b3-406b-8fad-52dc769b5766
Connector: orders (ea9011bf-393d-4926-a405-8e3568d155a7)
Run:       6e52921c-4168-437c-81d6-55d8bcd2a24c
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   /tmp/exports/orders.csv:9 — Record has 2 values but 5 columns are declared
Detail:    {"file":"/tmp/exports/orders.csv","line":9,"message":"Record has 2 values but 5 columns are declared"}
Payload:   {"raw":["ORD-1008","C-006"],"file":"/tmp/exports/orders.csv","line":9}
Resolution: open

Line 9 stopped after two values. The payload is the row as the source sent it: the fix is in the export.

Reason What it means Where to look MalformedSource the source row itself is broken — encoding, truncated line the file or export; a transformer can often repair it at the door MappingFailed a hook could not read a value, on a column declared on-error: dlq the value the message names, in the row lm dlq get shows ValidationFailed the row broke a declared expectation the manifest's declaration against the data WriteFailed the database write failed the target table — types, drift; the hub logs have the SQL error

A hook that throws does not land here: it fails the run. Declared skips (Duplicate, PolicyExcluded) are counted in SKIPPED but never dead-lettered (Reading a run).

docs.title: 3. Fix, re-run, close the loop
docs.text:
Fix the source, then run the connector again. A jdbc or CSV run resumes on its cursor (how jdbc cursors resume); a REST run upserts on its key, so a re-run does not duplicate rows (REST storage).

$ lm connector run orders
run scheduled: 8778809f-36b6-45e8-bc62-717359e137a2

$ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
8778809f  orders     default   Completed  10  10   0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
6e52921c  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38

Then mark each entry handled — replayed by the new run, or not wanted:

$ lm dlq replayed 9d07dd36 --new-run-id 8778809f
marked replayed: 9d07dd36-53b3-406b-8fad-52dc769b5766

$ lm dlq discard da3dc703
discarded: da3dc703-b1b7-4a84-a2e1-6ee8ed241cf1
  • --new-run-id names the run that carried the row again. It must be a Completed run of the same connector, started after the row was set aside. Another run is refused, and the message says why.
  • A row no run carried again is closed with discard.
  • An entry is closed once. lm dlq get ID shows how, on its Resolution: line.

Handled entries stay in lm dlq list --run, their RESOLUTION filled in; lm dlq list --connector shows only the ones still pending:

$ lm dlq list --run 6e52921c
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  RESOLUTION  MESSAGE
9d07dd36  orders     6e52921c  MalformedSource  1         REPLAYED    /tmp/exports/orders.csv:9 — Record has 2 values but 5 column…
da3dc703  orders     6e52921c  MalformedSource  1         DISCARDED   /tmp/exports/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 c…

In the TUI: :runs and :dlq update live; on :dlq, ^R marks replayed and ^D discards.

docs.title: Reading the logs
docs.text:
Where each service's log lives — self-host or Kubernetes — how to shape a JSON log line into something readable, and when the answer isn't in the logs at all.

Not every failure lands in the hub's log. Look here first:

Symptom Look at the hub won't start, or 500s everywhere curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/health, then the hub log login fails, token rejected the keycloak log a run failed, rows are missing lm run get and lm dlq — not the logs a webhook never arrived lm outputs list https or certificate trouble the caddy log (TLS proxy) slow queries, connection refused the postgres log

/q/health names the failing check with DOWN: Observability. Which restart is safe: the on-call runbook.

docs.title: Self-host stack (Docker Compose)
docs.text:
The stack started by deploy/selfhost/up.sh has three services: hub, postgres, keycloak (plus caddy with the TLS proxy). Run these from the repo root:

# Follow the hub live (Ctrl-C stops following, not the hub)
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub

# Any docker compose logs flag: a time window, timestamps
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs --since 10m -t hub

# Another service: keycloak, postgres
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh keycloak

# Everything at once (noisy, but shows cross-service ordering)
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh

caddy lives in the TLS overlay file; name both files to reach it:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml logs -f caddy

docs.title: Kubernetes (cloud edition)
docs.text:
The chart names its workloads <release>-hub and <release>-keycloak; the default release is lumnik:

kubectl logs -f deploy/lumnik-hub          # follow the hub
kubectl logs --since=10m deploy/lumnik-hub # recent window only
kubectl logs --previous deploy/lumnik-hub  # the crashed container, after a restart
kubectl logs -f deploy/lumnik-keycloak     # auth trouble

Add -n <namespace> if you installed into one.

docs.title: Anatomy of a hub log line
docs.text:
The packaged hub (Docker, Kubernetes) writes one JSON object per line:

{"timestamp":"2026-08-18T09:41:24+02:00","level":"ERROR","loggerName":"io.lumnik.hub.connector…","threadName":"executor-thread-1","mdc":{"tenantId":"12","runId":"66541f10-0dc7-4534-85b0-942668020fb1"},"message":"chunk 4 failed: …"}
Field Meaning level ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG loggerName the component; ingestion lines start with io.lumnik.hub.connector mdc.tenantId the tenant the line belongs to mdc.runId the run id (as in lm run list) — on every line a run wrote, absent elsewhere

Slice the stream with jq (--no-log-prefix strips compose's hub-1 | prefix; fromjson? // empty skips any non-JSON line):

LOGS="docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs --no-log-prefix"

# Errors only, human-readable
$LOGS hub | jq -rR 'fromjson? // empty | select(.level=="ERROR") | "\(.timestamp) \(.message)"'

# One tenant's story
$LOGS hub | jq -rR 'fromjson? // empty | select(.mdc.tenantId=="12") | .message'

# One run's story, warnings included — the id comes from `lm run list`
$LOGS hub | jq -rR 'fromjson? // empty | select(.mdc.runId=="66541f10-0dc7-4534-85b0-942668020fb1") | "\(.level) \(.message)"'

No jq on the box? grep '"level":"ERROR"' still works on JSON lines.

docs.title: Turning up the volume
docs.text:
Env var Effect QUARKUS_LOG_CATEGORY__IO_LUMNIK__LEVEL=DEBUG debug for lumnik code only — the usual choice QUARKUS_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG debug for everything, frameworks included — a firehose

Self-host. A line in .env does not reach the hub: it only gets the variables docker-compose.selfhost.yml lists. Add a small override file next to it instead:

# debug.yml
services:
  hub:
    environment:
      QUARKUS_LOG_CATEGORY__IO_LUMNIK__LEVEL: DEBUG

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f debug.yml up -d hub

Also name every overlay file you started with (-f docker-compose.tls.yml), or the hub restarts without it. A later up.sh keeps debug.yml too. To turn it back down, run the same command without -f debug.yml.

Kubernetes (cloud edition).

kubectl set env deploy/lumnik-hub QUARKUS_LOG_CATEGORY__IO_LUMNIK__LEVEL=DEBUG

Turn it down with kubectl set env deploy/lumnik-hub QUARKUS_LOG_CATEGORY__IO_LUMNIK__LEVEL-.

Turn it back down

DEBUG is for the minutes you are actively looking. It drowns the signal, and the log may echo data you would rather not keep.

docs.title: When the answer is not in the logs
docs.text: Missing rows and failed runs are answered by the run ledger and the dead-letter queue, not by log lines: Diagnosing a failed run. Outbound deliveries: lm outputs list. In the TUI: :runs, :dlq and :outputs.

docs.title: Test the API — URLs, auth, Postman
docs.text:
Mint a token against the bundled realm and paste it into curl, Postman, or Swagger UI — every door the hub serves, listed with the role it requires.

Day-to-day work goes through lm; this page is for testing the HTTP API itself. URLs below are the self-host defaults. Behind the TLS proxy everything lives on one https origin, with Keycloak under /realms/*.

docs.title: The doors
docs.text:
URL Auth What it is http://localhost:8080/q/health none UP/DOWN with named checks — observability http://localhost:8080/q/metrics none Prometheus metrics (block /q/* at the proxy on a public origin) http://localhost:8080/q/openapi none the OpenAPI spec — what Postman imports http://localhost:8080/q/swagger-ui/ none the try-it console, shipped in the packaged hub http://localhost:8080/app/ browser login the PWA http://localhost:8080/api/rag/chat Bearer, lm_user the chat door — semantic or analytic, guards apply http://localhost:8080/api/entities/… Bearer: reads lm_user; apply and writes lm_admin fused entities, reads scope-bound — entities http://localhost:8080/api/views Bearer, lm_user saved-view discovery, scope-bound — views http://localhost:8080/api/platform/… Bearer, lm_integrator (some doors also lm_admin) the integrator surface: connectors, validator, runs, apply http://localhost:8080/scim/v2/… SCIM bearer token deprovisioning, Pro only — SCIM http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik — Keycloak: the issuer, and the token endpoint below

Roles ride in the JWT's groups claim; the catalog is on Roles & permissions. A scope-bound user gets the uniform 403 {"error":"scope not granted"} outside their granted scopes — a feature, not a failure.

docs.title: Mint a token
docs.text:
The bundled realm ships an integrator user (password: INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in the .env that up.sh generated) and a public CLI client, lm-cli, that allows the password grant. From the repo root, in curl:

INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD=$(grep '^INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

TOKEN=$(curl -s "http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
  -d grant_type=password -d client_id=lm-cli \
  -d username=integrator --data-urlencode password="$INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD" \
  | jq -r .access_token)

# First authenticated smoke test:
curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/platform/health -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

The reply lists every installed module (here a Pro hub with the AI switched off):

{"platform":"ok","modules":{"core":{"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0"},"identity":{"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0"},"rag":{"status":"inactive","version":"0.1.0","reason":"disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled"},"llm":{"status":"inactive","version":"0.1.0","reason":"disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled"}},"search":{"status":"not_installed","affectsReadiness":false,"error":null}}

Tokens from the bundled realm live one hour — mint again when a call starts answering 401. Your own IdP may be stricter.

docs.title: The same thing in Postman
docs.text:
On the collection's Authorization tab, choose OAuth 2.0 and fill:

Field Value Grant type Password Credentials Access Token URL http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik/protocol/openid-connect/token Client ID lm-cli Username / Password integrator / the INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD from .env

Get New Access Token → every request in the collection inherits the Bearer, and Postman re-mints it when it expires.

docs.title: Import the whole API
docs.text:
Postman → Import → URL → http://localhost:8080/q/openapi. Postman builds the collection from the running hub, every endpoint pre-filled. Set the collection auth as above.

Prefer a browser? http://localhost:8080/q/swagger-ui/ is the same spec with a try-it button — paste the token from Mint a token into its Authorize dialog.

Testing as a business user, not an integrator

Everything above authenticates as integrator. To see what a scope-bound user sees (the 403 scope not granted boundaries, the user chat door), mint the token with that user's credentials instead. Scopes explains the binding.

docs.title: Troubleshooting, by symptom
docs.text: Find your symptom; follow the link to the page that owns the fix.

docs.title: The stack won't cooperate
docs.text:
Which restart is safe, and what each one costs: the on-call runbook.

Symptom First move The hub won't start, or 500s everywhere curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/health (no lm command reads it), then the hub logs required variable LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY is missing a value when the stack starts the key is missing from .env — on a fresh install, generate one with openssl rand -base64 32; on an existing one, restore it from your backup (the master key) lumnik.secret.master-key is too short (< 16 chars) at boot the key is shorter than 16 characters — same fix First boot seems stuck migrations run at first boot — give it a minute, watch ./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub up.sh refuses to start, naming missing tools its preflight — the message shows the exact install line; run it, re-run up.sh (Windows walkthrough, step 3) !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token (check KEYCLOAK_ADMIN / KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env) at the end of up.sh — then logins fail either Keycloak was still starting: re-run up.sh; or KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env no longer matches the console's: set the same value in both. Still failing: ./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh keycloak Anything on a Windows PC the dedicated page: Deploy on Windows → Troubleshooting https / certificate trouble the TLS proxy — caddy logs, Deploy

docs.title: Login and identity
docs.text: Symptom First move 401 with tenant_id, subject/issuer or claim errors the claim wiring — BYO IdP troubleshooting has the full table 403 on every endpoint despite a valid login the groups claim doesn't carry lm_* role names — BYO IdP 403 {"error":"user is deactivated"} the identity was archived (SCIM departure) — SCIM Login broke after moving to TLS or a new hostname the issuer changed — Keep the same public address SCIM calls misbehave SCIM troubleshooting — the issuer-mismatch 404 is the classic lm prints API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server — your account may lack the required role (raw HTTP: 403 with an empty body) a required role is missing — Roles & permissions API error 403: missing role lm_integrator the /api/platform/* gate: the account lacks lm_integrator — same page

docs.title: Refusals that are features
docs.text:
Symptom What it is access refused (403): scope not granted (raw HTTP: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}) the business-scope boundary: your user holds scope roles and this resource is outside them. It covers every read surface (PWA lists, chat, views), so several going quiet at once points here. Scopes The chat says "I can't answer that…" or "I won't run this…" a guard refused rather than guess; the message says what to do next "The query returned no rows. That can mean…" an empty result — check the SQL shown before concluding there are none Error: API error 409: no schema discovered for scope '…' — apply an entity or run discovery first nothing was applied to the scope yet, or its last connector was deleted or moved — apply an entity (the message says so), then ask again The ask answers "I have no data declared for this scope yet…" although you ingested into that scope the scope's schema card declares no tables — see below 429 on chat, search, or view-generate — not a connector run the hub's own inbound limit — Rate limits. A vendor throttling a connector is the 429 under Ingestion

Look at the scope's schema card (needs lm_admin on top of lm_integrator):

lm source schema --scope <scope> prints Meaning Fix (no tables — run 'lm source rediscover --scope <scope>') the card exists but declares no tables run that lm source rediscover; it removes the empty card Error: API error 404: No schema card found for scope: <scope> no card at all — the 409 state above apply an entity to the scope

The ask is Pro only; lm source schema and rediscover exist on both editions.

docs.title: The ask and the model
docs.text: Symptom First move The ask/chat errors after ~20 s, with an opaque error id the model failed to load on the machine running Ollama — on Windows, update the NVIDIA drivers first, then the RAM note: Deploy on Windows, step 5 The very first ask after a restart is slow or times out the model loads on first use (tens of seconds on CPU) — ask again; on a server set OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1 in Ollama's own environment (Deploy) Chat/search return nothing, ask has no model Ollama isn't installed or reachable — install it (Windows: step 5) and check OLLAMA_BASE_URL (Models) Same, on a Linux host Ollama listens on 127.0.0.1, which the hub container cannot reach — bind it on the Docker bridge: Deploy → Linux host

docs.title: Ingestion
docs.text: Symptom First move A run failed, or rows are missing the dedicated recipe: Diagnosing a failed run run scheduled looked fine, but lm run list says Failed "scheduled" only means queued. Failed at 0/0 usually means the source did not answer — lm run get <id> prints why (Diagnosing a failed run) A run says Completed but IN=0 OUT=0 the connector found nothing to read — for file connectors, the path or mount does not exist where the hub looks (the WOW's ✔ checks catch it) lm entity apply errors naming a relation that does not exist a source connector never landed rows — check lm run list An applied entity never shows up in lm ask/chat the manifest declares no scopes: — Entities troubleshooting 429 Too Many Requests from a REST vendor lower default_rate_limit — REST troubleshooting SFTP auth, host-key, or S3 403 errors CSV & files troubleshooting Bearer token unavailable (env=…) — REST connectors only the secret was never set — lm secret set, quickstart table jdbc run fails: password_env '<NAME>' is neither in the server environment nor in lm secret lm secret set <NAME>, or set it in the hub's environment — JDBC troubleshooting A cursor seems stuck in the past lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint> — next run is a full refresh

docs.title: Outputs and apps
docs.text:
Symptom First move A webhook never arrived lm outputs list (failures first), then lm outputs replay <ID> — or ^R in the TUI :outputs (Outputs) The Records list on a phone looks empty see the table below The PWA shows an old version the service worker re-installs only when sw.js changes — the shell-cache note lm view -f v.yaml (the list), lm view KEY -f v.yaml (one record) or lm view apply refused a manifest field/column mismatch, or a missing scope role — Views troubleshooting lm process apply refused, or a declared process never fires a manifest/schema mismatch, or its trigger table broke at runtime — Processes troubleshooting lm workflow apply refused an unknown field, a lifecycle collision, or dormancy declared without on.key — Workflows troubleshooting A workflow alert didn't fire dormancy is observation-relative and needs on.key + dormancy.after — Workflows

An empty Records list on the phone:

You see Meaning Where to look an amber box with a message a refusal, with its reason: no view applied for the scope, or 403 scope not granted Views troubleshooting, Scopes grey "Aucune ligne" text the view rendered and found zero rows the source data

Still stuck? Reading the logs says where every component writes, and how to raise the volume for the minutes you need it.

docs.title: Querying Search
docs.text:
Ask the index you declared: one query, optional filters, ranked hits. lm search query is the terminal door; GET /api/search is the one an application calls.

Command lm search query "TEXT" [--entity E] [--facet field=value]… [--limit N] [--cursor C] Door GET /api/search Who lm_user, bounded by the entity's scopes Needs a Search provider built into the hub, and a declared and built kind: SearchIndex Not to be confused with lm ask: that one takes a question and counts or aggregates (and shows the SQL it ran). This one takes keywords and finds records, the same answer every time, with no model

docs.title: Quickstart — declare, build, ask
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the customers of the demo desk: fourteen fictional customers fused from an ERP export and a CRM export. Land the sources first (Landing the sources), then apply the entity, then declare the index. Search needs a provider in the hub — the published image has none, see Choosing a provider.

The index is the one from the declaration page: the customer's name matched with tolerance for typos, the code matched exactly, the city as words and as a filter, the segment as a filter.

apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1
kind: SearchIndex
metadata:
  name: customers
spec:
  entity: AcmeCustomer
  language: french
  fields:
    - name: name
      match: fuzzy
    - name: code
      match: exact
    - name: city
      match: text
      facet: true
    - name: segment
      facet: true

From the repository root:

$ lm entity apply -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml
Applied entity "AcmeCustomer" → connector."v_acmecustomer"

$ lm search apply -f docs/search/search-indexes/10-customers.yaml
Applied search index "customers" → entity AcmeCustomer (valid)

$ lm search rebuild customers --wait
Name              customers
Status            ready
Live generation   19
Documents         14
Lag               0s
Last rebuild      aa7b5014-3dbe-4f0d-8960-133950183b7c (ready)

The hub builds a new index on its own, within a minute. rebuild --wait builds it now, and returns when it answers. Without --wait, a query right away may get the answer for an index that is not built yet.

lm search status customers prints the same card at any time: status, documents, Lag behind the data, and the last error if the build failed. If the error shows only SQLSTATE …, the hub log has the full message, on the line naming the index.

Now ask. --entity narrows the search to one entity; without it, every entity you may read is searched and the hits of several entities come back mixed (the first column says which is which).

$ lm search query "hydraulique lyon" --entity AcmeCustomer
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.77   city=*Lyon* | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1010  0.41   city=Milano | code=P-1010 | name=Hydraulique Milano 1010 | segment=SILVER

facets:
city      Lyon (1)  Milano (1)
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

2 hits shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

docs.title: Reading a hit
docs.text: Column Meaning ENTITY, KEY what the hit is. The key is the entity's own — read the full record with it (lm entity get AcmeCustomer --filter code=P-1000) SCORE how close the hit is. Compare scores inside one answer only: they rank this answer, they do not measure anything across queries or indexes MATCH the fields the index declares for this hit — the fields that matched first, then the others alphabetically; an empty field is left out. Words found in a text field are between *stars* facets: for each filterable field, the values among all the matches and how many — not only the ones on this page as of how fresh the index is: it shows the data as of that moment. Trust it, not your clock

docs.title: What a query is
docs.text:
It is one argument, 1 to 200 characters, put in quotes when it contains spaces. The quotes are for your shell; they do not make a phrase search (there is none). Without them the shell hands over several arguments, and the command refuses rather than drop words:

$ lm search query hydraulique lyon --entity AcmeCustomer
Error: search query takes ONE argument — quote it when it has spaces, e.g. lm search query "hydraulique lyon" (got 2 arguments)

What a word does depends on the match mode the index gives the field it lands in (see Fields):

Mode What you can type Seen above fuzzy a name with a typo, a missing accent, a spelling variant Hydrolique finds Hydraulique, etancheite finds Étanchéité exact the whole code P-1008 — and the exact match scores highest text words, understood in the index's language (plurals, accents) Lyon on the city, shown between stars prefix the beginning of something typed not used by this index

A typo is absorbed by a fuzzy field:

$ lm search query Hydrolique --entity AcmeCustomer
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.32   city=Lyon | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD

facets:
city      Lyon (1)
segment   GOLD (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

and so is a missing accent:

$ lm search query etancheite --entity AcmeCustomer
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1004  0.48   city=Kraków | code=P-1004 | name=Étanchéité Kraków 1004 | segment=SILVER

facets:
city      Kraków (1)
segment   SILVER (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

A code that matches exactly comes first:

$ lm search query P-1008 --entity AcmeCustomer
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1008  1.23   city=Lyon | code=P-1008 | name=Filtration Lyon 1008 | segment=GOLD

facets:
city      Lyon (1)
segment   GOLD (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

A fuzzy field ranks by resemblance; it does not demand every word. The first screen of this page asked for "hydraulique lyon" and got two customers: the one that matches the name and the city first, and the other Hydraulique second. Read the score, not only the presence.

How several words combine depends on the provider:

  • PostgreSQL (these screens): on a text field, every word must be present. A word added narrows.
  • OpenSearch: any word may match. A word added can widen.

Check a query on the provider you run before relying on it. On PostgreSQL, two cities cannot both be a customer's city:

$ lm search query "lyon porto" --entity AcmeCustomer
0 hits

$ lm search query xyzzy --entity AcmeCustomer
0 hits

What a query does not have: no AND, OR or NOT, no phrase search, no field:value. A - or a quote is only punctuation. Here -hydraulique excludes nothing — the answer is the same two customers as above:

$ lm search query "lyon -hydraulique" --entity AcmeCustomer
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.77   city=*Lyon* | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1010  0.41   city=Milano | code=P-1010 | name=Hydraulique Milano 1010 | segment=SILVER

facets:
city      Lyon (1)  Milano (1)
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

2 hits shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

docs.title: Narrow with filters
docs.text:
--facet field=value keeps only the hits whose field has that value. It works on the fields the index declares facet: true (here city and segment) and can be repeated, one value per field.

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --facet segment=GOLD
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.55   city=Lyon | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD

facets:
city      Lyon (1)
segment   GOLD (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --facet segment=BRONZE
0 hits

A filter on a field the index does not declare as a facet is refused, naming the field:

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --facet code=P-1000
Error: API error 400: filters key 'code' is not a facet field on any eligible SearchIndex

docs.title: Pages and the cursor
docs.text:
--limit is 1 to 100 (the hub's default is 20). Outside that range the hub refuses and says so — the command never quietly changes the number you typed:

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --limit 0
Error: API error 400: limit must be between 1 and 100

When there is more, the answer ends with the exact command for the next page. Here with --limit 1 (note that the facets still count the whole match, not the page):

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --limit 1
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.55   city=Lyon | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD

facets:
city      Lyon (1)  Milano (1)
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48
more: lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --limit 1 --cursor eyJzY29yZSI6MC41NDU0NTQ1NjE3MTAzNTc3LCJzZWFyY2hJbmRleCI6ImN1c3RvbWVycyIsImRvY3VtZW50SWQiOiIxfDY6UC0xMDAwIiwiZmluZ2VycHJpbnQiOiJzaGEyNTY6MzllODY0N2M5N2NjMzFkMDQyMGJmZjNmM2U1MDcwN2YxMTU4ODYyMDJjODY5MWJlMTBkOTk4ZTc1MmZkZTBiMSIsImVsaWdpYmxlIjp7ImN1c3RvbWVycyI6MTZ9fQ

Paste that line — it carries the cursor — to get the next page:

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --limit 1 --cursor <cursor>
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1010  0.50   city=Milano | code=P-1010 | name=Hydraulique Milano 1010 | segment=SILVER

facets:
city      Lyon (1)  Milano (1)
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

1 hit shown · as of 2026-10-06 08:48

(The cursor is long; it is shortened to <cursor> here, nothing else is changed.)

A cursor is not a snapshot. If the indexes being searched change between two pages — one is rebuilt, one finishes building, one is removed — the hub refuses the old cursor rather than mix two states in one list. Run the search again without --cursor; the refusal says so:

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer --limit 1 --cursor <cursor>
Error: API error 400: eligible SearchIndex set changed since this cursor was issued; run the search again without cursor

A malformed cursor, or one from another search, gets the same advice.

docs.title: In a script
docs.text:
-o json (or -o yaml) prints the hub's answer. Standard output stays clean for the next tool: when the answer is empty, the explanation of why goes to standard error.

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer -o json | jq '{hits: [.hits[] | {code: .key.code, score}], facets, asOf}'
{
  "hits": [
    {
      "code": "P-1000",
      "score": 0.5454545617103577
    },
    {
      "code": "P-1010",
      "score": 0.5
    }
  ],
  "facets": {
    "city": [
      {
        "value": "Lyon",
        "count": 1
      },
      {
        "value": "Milano",
        "count": 1
      }
    ],
    "segment": [
      {
        "value": "GOLD",
        "count": 1
      },
      {
        "value": "SILVER",
        "count": 1
      }
    ]
  },
  "asOf": "2026-10-06T06:49:07.399715Z"
}

docs.title: When the answer is not "no results"
docs.text:
Several situations look like an empty answer and are not. lm search query tells them apart from a real "nothing matches" (which is a plain 0 hits, as for xyzzy above) and says what to do.

The index was deleted a moment ago. The old documents may still answer until the purge completes. Once it has:

$ lm search rm customers
Type 'delete' to delete search index customers over entity AcmeCustomer — its projected documents are purged: delete
search index customers deleted

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer
0 hits
no SearchIndex is declared over AcmeCustomer (that your scopes can read) — there is nothing to search. Declare one: lm search apply -f <manifest>

Nothing is declared over that entity — what the screen above says: declare an index (lm search apply -f).

The index is declared but not built. Declaring stores the declaration; building makes it answer:

$ lm search apply -f docs/search/search-indexes/10-customers.yaml
Applied search index "customers" → entity AcmeCustomer (valid)

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity AcmeCustomer
0 hits
SearchIndex "customers" over AcmeCustomer is declared but not built yet: lm search rebuild customers --wait

The build failed. lm search status NAME names the error, and the query says the last build failed rather than "not built yet". Quoted (… stands for the cause):

SearchIndex "customers" over AcmeCustomer has nothing built: its last build failed: entity 'AcmeCustomer' cannot be indexed: … — read it with `lm search status customers`, fix the cause, then lm search rebuild customers --wait

Three more answers:

You see It means Do search is not installed on this hub — no Search provider is built into it … the hub has no Search provider; this is not an empty result build the hub with one: deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search (PostgreSQL) or --search-cluster (OpenSearch), closed edition search is degraded: <reason> — retry in 60s the provider is installed but failing; the reason says how fix the backend; ingestion goes on meanwhile SearchIndex "NAME" over ENTITY is invalid: <reason> an entity was re-applied without a column the index declares fix the manifest and apply it again

Only an integrator is told not built or being built; any user is told the other cases.

docs.title: Over HTTP
docs.text:
For an application. The CLI sends one request:

Parameter Meaning q the query, 1 to 200 characters (required) entity one entity name; absent means every entity you may read limit 1 to 100, default 20; outside the range is refused with 400 cursor the nextCursor of the previous page facet.<field> a filter on a declared facet field; at most 10 fields, each once scope a business scope: keep only the entities that carry it, among those you may read (what the PWA sends). See below

scope= in detail:

  • absent: no narrowing; hits and facets are narrowed together when present;
  • empty, padded, repeated or not a lowercase identifier: 400;
  • a scope-bound user who does not hold it: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}; an unbound user may name any scope and is narrowed to it;
  • with entity, the entity must carry the scope, else the same 403.
$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    "$LUMNIK_URL/api/search?q=hydraulique&entity=AcmeCustomer&limit=1&scope=desk" | jq
{
  "hits": [
    {
      "entity": "AcmeCustomer",
      "title": null,
      "titleField": null,
      "key": {
        "code": "P-1000"
      },
      "score": 0.5454545617103577,
      "fields": {
        "city": "Lyon",
        "name": "Hydraulique Lyon 1000",
        "code": "P-1000",
        "segment": "GOLD"
      },
      "highlights": {
        "city": [
          "Lyon"
        ]
      },
      "canonicalLink": "/api/entities/AcmeCustomer?code=P-1000"
    }
  ],
  "fieldLabels": {
    "AcmeCustomer": {
      "code": "Code client",
      "name": "Raison sociale",
      "city": "Ville",
      "segment": "Segment",
      "credit_limit": "Encours autorisé",
      "email": "Email"
    }
  },
  "facets": {
    "city": [
      {
        "value": "Lyon",
        "count": 1
      },
      {
        "value": "Milano",
        "count": 1
      }
    ],
    "segment": [
      {
        "value": "GOLD",
        "count": 1
      },
      {
        "value": "SILVER",
        "count": 1
      }
    ]
  },
  "nextCursor": "eyJzY29yZSI6MC41NDU0NTQ1NjE3MTAzNTc3LCJzZWFyY2hJbmRleCI6ImN1c3RvbWVycyIsImRvY3VtZW50SWQiOiIxfDY6UC0xMDAwIiwiZmluZ2VycHJpbnQiOiJzaGEyNTY6MzllODY0N2M5N2NjMzFkMDQyMGJmZjNmM2U1MDcwN2YxMTU4ODYyMDJjODY5MWJlMTBkOTk4ZTc1MmZkZTBiMSIsImVsaWdpYmxlIjp7ImN1c3RvbWVycyI6MX19",
  "asOf": "2026-10-24T22:15:38.030639Z"
}
Field Meaning When absent or null hits[].key, score, fields, highlights the hit, as the CLI prints it — hits[].canonicalLink the record's address — hits[].title, titleField the business title and its field null unless the index declares one hits[].links field and url templates absent unless the index links to your ERP fieldLabels {entity: {column: label}}, the human names absent when none is labelled facets per facet field, values and counts over the whole match — nextCursor the next page's cursor null on the last page asOf the index's freshness — Status Meaning 400 what you sent is wrong; the message says what 403 {"error":"scope not granted"} an entity or scope you may not read 501 no provider installed 503 with a reason the provider is degraded

To check the engine without searching, ask for its capability (no lm command prints it):

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$LUMNIK_URL/api/search/capability"
{"state":"available","provider":"postgres","reason":null,"version":null}

docs.title: Who sees which hits
docs.text:
A hit is shown to whoever may read its entity: the index inherits the entity's scopes and they are checked when you ask, not when the index was built. A user bound to some scopes sees the entities where they hold at least one of them. An entity that does not exist and one you may not read answer the same 403 on purpose:

$ lm search query hydraulique --entity Unknown
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted

An app narrows this further: the PWA sends the app's own scope (scope= below), so a search opened from the stock app only ever shows the entities that carry stock, even to a user who holds other scopes too.

docs.title: In the PWA
docs.text: The PWA has a Search tab that calls this endpoint for the app's scope and shows the results to people who never open a terminal.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Search indexes — declaring them: the manifest, the match modes, the purge, choosing a provider.
  • CLI reference: every lm search command.
  • Ask your data: the other way in, for questions rather than keywords.

docs.title: kind: SearchIndex — declare what Search may see
docs.text:
A kind: SearchIndex manifest is an allowlist: the columns of one canonical entity that may leave PostgreSQL for an optional Search provider. No declaration, no indexing. Nothing is inferred from the data, and a column added to a source later never reaches the index on its own.

Kind SearchIndex (apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1, strictly checked) Source one entity, never a raw connector.t_* table Who may see a hit whoever may read the entity: its scopes, resolved at query time Apply / delete lm_integrator Status lm search status — lm_integrator Provider needed? to query, yes: choosing a provider. Without one, the declaration is kept

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1
kind: SearchIndex
metadata:
  name: customers
spec:
  entity: AcmeCustomer
  language: french
  fields:
    - name: name
      match: fuzzy
    - name: code
      match: exact
    - name: city
      match: text
      facet: true
    - name: segment
      facet: true

Apply it after the entity. The hub builds the index within a minute:

$ lm search apply -f docs/search/search-indexes/10-customers.yaml
Applied search index "customers" → entity AcmeCustomer (valid)
$ lm search status
NAME       STATUS    LAG(s)  DOCUMENTS  LAST REBUILD
customers  building  0
$ lm search status
NAME       STATUS  LAG(s)  DOCUMENTS  LAST REBUILD
customers  ready   20      14         ready
$ lm search query hydraulique
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.55   city=Lyon | code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1010  0.50   city=Milano | code=P-1010 | name=Hydraulique Milano 1010 | segment=SILVER

facets:
city      Lyon (1)  Milano (1)
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

2 hits shown · as of 2026-10-25 00:14

Fourteen customers indexed; two match hydraulique. city and segment are facets: counted values, to narrow with --facet segment=GOLD. Every way to query: Query it.

On a hub without a Search provider, nothing builds the index. Its status reads not_installed in lm search status and on the TUI's :search page. A query says why:

$ lm search status
NAME       STATUS         LAG(s)  DOCUMENTS  LAST REBUILD
customers  not_installed  0
$ lm search query hydraulique
Error: search is not installed on this hub — no Search provider is built into it, so there is nothing to query (this is not an empty result). The published hub image never carries one: build it from source with deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search (PostgreSQL) or --search-cluster (OpenSearch), both closed edition

docs.title: Fields: searchable, returned, faceted
docs.text:
Every declared field is returned with a hit. match also makes it searchable; facet: true also makes it a facet. So:

  • A searched or faceted field is always shown too.
  • A field without match is shown only: it rides along with the hit (a status, a date), and is never searched.
  • At least one field must be searchable.
apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1
kind: SearchIndex
metadata:
  name: orders
spec:
  entity: AcmeOrder
  fields:
    - name: order_no
      match: prefix
    - name: customer_name
      match: fuzzy
    - name: status
      facet: true
    - name: ordered_at
match Meant for exact codes, identifiers, closed values text free text, analysed in spec.language fuzzy names with typos, accents and spelling variants prefix autocomplete, order numbers typed partially

spec.language is one of simple (the default), english, french, german, italian, spanish, dutch, portuguese.

docs.title: Choosing a title
docs.text:
A hit shows the name of its entity as its heading, which tells a product from a customer but not one product from another. Name the field people recognise an item by, and the business app promotes it to the heading:

apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1
kind: SearchIndex
metadata:
  name: products
spec:
  entity: Product
  titleField: reference
  fields:
    - name: reference
      match: prefix
    - name: description
      match: text
    - name: family
      facet: true

$ lm search apply -f products.yaml
Applied search index "products" → entity Product (valid)

In the app, a result then reads:

2195.300.037
Product · product_id=1024944
description  Pompe Badu Resort 30 2cv Tri
family       Pompes
  • titleField is optional. Without it every result keeps the entity name as its heading, with the key under it.
  • It names one of the declared fields, searchable or return-only. Any other name is refused when you apply.
  • It is never guessed from the field order.
  • The entity stays visible under the heading, because one search may return several entities.
  • An item with no value in that field shows the entity name for that item only.

Declaring or changing a titleField is a re-apply. The heading changes at the next search when the field is already in the index; a title field added in the same apply shows once the index has caught up.

docs.title: Human names for fields
docs.text:
A result names its fields as the columns are called: credit_limit, category_description. Give a column a label in its entity's columns: block — the same label a view already shows — and Search uses it, with nothing to declare in the index:

columns:
  name:
    label: "Raison sociale"
  credit_limit:
    label: "Encours autorisé"

In the app, a result then reads:

Raison sociale  Acme Industries
Encours autorisé  50000
city  Lyon
  • The labels are the entity's. Change one by re-applying the entity; it shows at the next search once the hub has taken the new entity in.
  • A column without a label keeps its name (city above), so you can label what matters first.
  • They show in three places: on each result, in the record sheet it opens (every column of the record, not only those the index returns, and the columns reported as divergent), and on the filter chips offered with the results.
  • A filter chip is labelled only when the entities in the page agree. If two entities label the same column differently, the chip keeps the column name rather than pick one.
  • Labels are display names only: searching and filtering still use the column names.

docs.title: Linking a result to your ERP
docs.text:
To open the same item in the system that owns it, declare the address once, on the field people see:

apiVersion: search.lumnik.io/v1
kind: SearchIndex
metadata:
  name: products
spec:
  entity: Product
  titleField: reference
  fields:
    - name: reference
      match: prefix
    - name: description
      match: text
  links:
    - field: reference
      url: "https://erp.example.com/articles/{reference}"

$ lm search apply -f products.yaml
Applied search index "products" → entity Product (valid)

In the app, the reference of each result becomes a link: tapping it opens https://erp.example.com/articles/2195.300.037 in a new tab, and does not also open the record sheet. The rest of the card behaves as before.

  • {field} is the value of that field on the result. It must be one of this index's spec.fields, not necessarily the linked one. Literal text around it is kept. Nothing else is ever substituted.
  • One link per field, at most 16, each on a field the index declares. Nothing but field and url is allowed.
  • The address follows the same rules as a view's external link: https:// only, the host written out in full, the page opened in a new tab. Special characters in the value are made safe for the address. The other system receives the value — declare only systems you trust with it.
  • A result with no value for any {field} of the address has no link, and the field shows as plain text.
  • A link on the title field makes the heading itself the link.

A mistake is refused when you apply, naming the key — here an address that mentions {ghost}, which is not a field of the index:

$ lm search apply -f linked.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.links[0].url: {ghost} is not one of spec.fields

A new or changed link shows at the very next search, without waiting for the index to catch up.

docs.title: Columns joined from a lookup table
docs.text:
A joined column can be a field like any other, on a match: entity or on one that declares resolution:. The index follows the lookup table as it follows the entity's own sources:

  • the first lookup row for a key makes the rows holding that key appear with the joined value;
  • one more row of different content for the same key makes the key ambiguous: the joined value goes empty on those rows, it is never one of the two;
  • ingesting the same lookup row again changes nothing.

On an entity with resolution:, one result is one resolved customer. A row still undecided is not searchable yet.

docs.title: What is refused, and why
docs.text:
Refused Do instead spec.scope / spec.scopes nothing: an index takes its entity's scopes spec.table / spec.source index an entity, never a raw table a field that is not a column of the entity use the entity's column name, not the source's tenant_id, _conflicts, _entity_id… index business columns only a metadata.name that is not a lower-case slug, or apply rename it an entity whose scopes you do not all hold ask for the missing scope: role a second index over the same entity one index per entity: re-apply the first one, mixing match modes field by field 
$ lm search apply -f scoped.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.scopes: scopes are inherited from the entity and cannot be declared on a SearchIndex
$ lm search apply -f tenant.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.fields[0].name: 'tenant_id' is an internal column and cannot be indexed
$ lm search apply -f apply.yaml
Error: API error 400: metadata.name must be a URL-safe slug ([a-z0-9_-], starting with a letter or digit) and not one of [apply]
$ lm search apply -f second.yaml
Error: API error 409: entity 'AcmeCustomer' is already indexed by SearchIndex 'customers' — one SearchIndex per Entity: re-apply 'customers' to change it (match modes can be mixed field by field), or delete it first
  • A re-apply of an existing name needs every scope of the entity that name currently indexes.
  • To search one column two ways, give each field its own match mode inside the one index.

docs.title: Deleting — and the purge it leaves behind
docs.text:
lm search rm names the index and its entity and asks you to type delete (--force skips the question in a script):

$ lm search rm customers
Type 'delete' to delete search index customers over entity AcmeCustomer — its projected documents are purged: delete
search index customers deleted
  • Its results can show for a moment after the delete, never to someone who may not read them.
  • To change an index, re-apply it under the same name. Delete-then-recreate shows both for a while.

docs.title: Rows deleted directly in the database
docs.text:
A row deleted outside ingestion (a DELETE in the database, lm endpoint purge) stays searchable until the index is rebuilt. Rebuild, and wait for the end:

lm search rebuild customers --wait

Without --wait the command returns once the run is claimed, and a search right away can still return the deleted row. Only the ready outcome means it is gone (failed and cancelled are the others).

docs.title: When the entity changes
docs.text:
When an entity is re-applied without a column a SearchIndex uses, every tenant's SearchIndex over it turns invalid. The entity apply is never refused because of Search. An invalid index serves no query until it is re-applied successfully; restoring the column alone does not revalidate it.

lm search status says so in its STATUS column; what was built before stays under LAST REBUILD:

$ lm search status
NAME       STATUS   LAG(s)  DOCUMENTS  LAST REBUILD
customers  invalid  0       14         ready
$ lm search status customers
Name              customers
Status            invalid
Live generation   1
Documents         14
Lag               0s
Last rebuild      97641fed-1dd2-4f35-bd29-353763e0f249 (ready)
Invalid           spec.fields[2].name: 'city' is not a canonical column of entity 'AcmeCustomer'

A query no longer reaches the index's documents — neither their hits nor their facets — and the empty answer says why:

$ lm search query hydraulique
0 hits
SearchIndex "customers" over AcmeCustomer is invalid: spec.fields[2].name: 'city' is not a canonical column of entity 'AcmeCustomer' — fix the manifest and re-apply it: lm search apply -f <manifest>

To serve again, remove the column from the index and re-apply it. The index then reads withheld until a rebuild without the column has replaced its build; the section below shows that step.

docs.title: Removing a field from an index
docs.text:
Removing a field is how you stop exposing it. What a re-apply does to the index:

The re-apply… The index removes a field, or stops searching or faceting on one withheld: answers no query until rebuilt changes a field's match mode, the language or the entity withheld until rebuilt only adds (a field, a field newly searched or faceted) keeps answering from its current build; the addition appears after the rebuild

The hub starts the rebuild on its own at its next pass; lm search rebuild NAME --wait starts it now and returns when it is done. A withheld index stays withheld until that rebuild, even if you put the field back.

$ lm search apply -f customers.yaml
Applied search index "customers" → entity AcmeCustomer (valid)
$ lm search query hydraulique
0 hits
SearchIndex "customers" over AcmeCustomer is withheld: a re-apply removed or changed what its build still serves — it answers again once rebuilt: lm search rebuild customers --wait
$ lm search status
NAME       STATUS    LAG(s)  DOCUMENTS  LAST REBUILD
customers  withheld  0       14         ready
$ lm search status customers
Name              customers
Status            withheld
Live generation   3
Documents         14
Lag               0s
Last rebuild      fe1e7ee9-2d01-472b-a397-60f0b7e4ba84 (ready)
Withheld          a re-apply removed or changed what its build serves; it answers nothing until rebuilt: lm search rebuild customers --wait
$ lm search rebuild customers --wait
Name              customers
Status            ready
Live generation   4
Documents         14
Lag               0s
Last rebuild      fe72138f-9a9c-4ae7-8a3c-7c274fe5e559 (ready)
$ lm search query hydraulique
ENTITY        KEY          SCORE  MATCH
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1000  0.55   code=P-1000 | name=Hydraulique Lyon 1000 | segment=GOLD
AcmeCustomer  code=P-1010  0.50   code=P-1010 | name=Hydraulique Milano 1010 | segment=SILVER

facets:
segment   GOLD (1)  SILVER (1)

2 hits shown · as of 2026-10-18 22:13

Here customers.yaml is the quickstart manifest without its city field.

docs.title: How fast an index catches up
docs.text:
After a bulk load the index trails the data. lm search status shows how far behind, in LAG(s). The hub catches up about once a minute, on its own. To have it now: lm search rebuild NAME --wait.

Tuning the catch-up Setting Default Effect LUMNIK_SEARCH_PROJECTION_CATCHUP_BUDGET 30s time per minute for extra batches on indexes still behind LUMNIK_SEARCH_PROJECTION_REBUILD_BACKLOG_THRESHOLD 5000 pending changes above which the index is rebuilt instead

The lag is a metric too: Observability.

A document the provider refuses leaves the index degraded, with the provider's message in lm search status NAME; the other documents carry on. Then:

  • the source row is the cause: correct it and ingest it again;
  • the declaration is the cause: correct it, lm search apply -f <manifest>, then lm search rebuild NAME --wait.

docs.title: Choosing a provider
docs.text:
Search needs a provider, chosen when the hub is built (lumnik Pro). The published hub image carries neither.

Provider Self-host Where the index lives PostgreSQL deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search the database you already run OpenSearch / Elasticsearch deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search-cluster an OpenSearch 2.x/3.x cluster, or your Elasticsearch 8.x/9.x
  • The two are alternatives: up.sh refuses --search and --search-cluster together.
  • --search-cluster starts an OpenSearch container with security on and writes two passwords into .env: the cluster admin's, and that of a lumnik user confined to the lumnik-* indexes.
  • The hub reads the cluster from LUMNIK_SEARCH_OPENSEARCH_URL, …_USERNAME, …_PASSWORD and, for a private CA, …_TLS_CA_FILE.

When to move to the cluster provider: when searches slow down while connectors run. Measured numbers: Sizing.

Once an index is built, query it — the full guide:

lm search query "hydraulique lyon" --entity AcmeCustomer --facet segment=GOLD

Is there a provider? lm search query and the TUI's :search page say not installed, and every index's status reads not_installed. No lm command prints the raw state; over HTTP:

$ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$LUMNIK_URL/api/search/capability"
{"state":"unavailable","provider":null,"reason":"not_installed","version":null}
state Meaning available a provider answers degraded a provider is installed but impaired; reason is backend_unreachable, backend_auth_failed, backend_error, unsupported_distribution or cluster_red unavailable no provider in this hub (reason: not_installed)

A cluster outage never stops ingestion and never turns into an empty answer.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Self-hosted, read-only towards your sources, tenant isolation enforced by PostgreSQL itself. This page is for the person who signs off: what holds, how to check it in five minutes, and what is not built yet.

Self-hosted

The hub, the database, the model runtime: all on your infrastructure. There is no lumnik cloud.

Read-only mirror

Ingestion reads your ERP and never writes back. The source stays the system of record.

Isolated by RLS

Row-Level Security on every tenanted table. The request-path role cannot bypass it.

Read-only role under LLM SQL

Generated queries run as lumnik_readonly: SELECT only, one statement, LIMIT 500.

docs.title: Before you expose the hub
docs.text:
Two doors that answer without a login

  • /q/metrics, /q/openapi, /q/swagger-ui need no token, and /q/metrics names your connectors. The TLS proxy forwards them. On a public address, block /q/* at your proxy or firewall.
  • A Helm install set to auth.mode=dev-bypass (cloud edition): the hub checks no token, every caller is superadmin and picks any tenant. The chart defaults to oidc and renders dev-bypass only with auth.iUnderstandNoAuth=true as well. Never expose such a hub. The self-host stack (up.sh) always requires a login.

docs.title: The trust boundaries
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  idp["your IdP<br/>OIDC token"] -.-> edge["TLS edge<br/>Caddy proxy · your proxy · k8s Gateway"]
  edge -->|"HTTP"| jwt
  subgraph hub["hub · plain HTTP behind the edge"]
    direction TB
    jwt["token checked<br/>aud · tenant_id · roles · scopes"]
    app["lumnik_app<br/>RLS"]
    ro["lumnik_readonly<br/>RLS · SELECT only"]
    adm["lumnik_admin<br/>BYPASSRLS"]
    jwt -->|"API · views · ingestion"| app
    jwt -->|"LLM-generated SQL"| ro
  end
  app --> pg[("PostgreSQL<br/>tenant policy on<br/>every tenanted table")]
  ro --> pg
  adm -->|"migrations · DDL · purge"| pg
  hub -.- llm["Ollama<br/>local by default"]
Boundary What holds Details The token aud = lumnik-backend; tenant_id picks the tenant; groups carries lm_* roles and scope:<tag> grants; optional user_id. A malformed claim is refused. Bring your own IdP The database roles lumnik_admin owns every table and alone bypasses RLS. lumnik_app owns nothing. RLS & database roles TLS Stops at the edge. Hub↔PostgreSQL, hub↔Ollama and proxy↔hub are plain on your internal network. Where TLS stops Scopes A scope:<tag> role narrows chat, search, views, entity reads and the decision inbox to one data scope: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}. Scopes

PostgreSQL enforces the tenant. Inside a tenant, the business-scope boundary on generated SQL is the leak guard (tables outside the scope's card are refused), not a database policy.

docs.title: Verify it yourself, in five minutes
docs.text:
Run these on the self-host stack, from the clone directory.

No tenant set means zero rows. Open a session as the request-path role:

$ docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec postgres psql -U lumnik -d lumnik
lumnik=# SET ROLE lumnik_app;
lumnik=> SELECT count(*) FROM connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
     0
lumnik=> BEGIN;
lumnik=*> SET LOCAL app.current_tenant = '1';
lumnik=*> SELECT count(*) FROM connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
    10
lumnik=*> COMMIT;
lumnik=> BEGIN;
lumnik=*> SET LOCAL app.current_tenant = '2';
lumnik=*> SELECT count(*) FROM connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
     0
lumnik=*> COMMIT;

The role under LLM-generated SQL cannot write, and reads only the tenant set:

lumnik=> SET ROLE lumnik_readonly;
lumnik=> INSERT INTO connector.t_orders DEFAULT VALUES;
ERROR:  permission denied for table t_orders
lumnik=> BEGIN;
lumnik=*> SET LOCAL app.current_tenant = '2';
lumnik=*> SELECT count(*) FROM connector.t_orders;
 count
-------
     0

A stored secret is ciphertext (pgcrypto, AES-256):

$ lm secret list
NAME                           ROTATED_AT                     DESCRIPTION
ACME_API_KEY                   -
ACME_BASIC_PW                  -
SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD              -

lumnik=# SELECT name, left(encode(value_encrypted, 'hex'), 32) || '…' AS value_encrypted
         FROM platform.secret ORDER BY name LIMIT 2;
     name      |          value_encrypted
---------------+-----------------------------------
 ACME_API_KEY  | c30d04090302ab5278c2332e2a006cd2…
 ACME_BASIC_PW | c30d040903020d2a00713ded0a517fd2…

No token, no answer:

$ curl -si http://localhost:8080/api/platform/health | head -1
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized

A user token does not open the provisioning surface. SCIM has its own bearer tokens:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/scim/v2/Users -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],"detail":"invalid SCIM token","status":"401"}

docs.title: Which build is this?
docs.text:
$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
